title: All AFC, NFC North teams could emerge from Week 6 above .500
summary: One of the basic realities of life in the NFL is that each team is assigned to a division with three other teams, permanently.
full_text: One of the basic realities of life in the NFL is that each team is assigned to a division with three other teams, permanently. (Until there's a reason to realign, which last happened in 2002.) And whether a team is in a good division or a bad division controls much of a team's success, or not, in a given year. Of the 17 games played, six of them are determined by the division to which it is assigned. If the other teams are really good, it makes it harder for an otherwise good team to be as good as it can be. If the other teams aren't very good, it's easier. The fact that this is so obvious shows how fundamentally unfair it is. It can give some lesser teams a shot at hosting a playoff game. It can give the one good team in an otherwise bad division a chance to win enough games to emerge as the top seed in a conference (for example, the Patriots throughout most of the 2010s). This year, the teams of the AFC and NFC North will each have a tougher road to whatever their best-case scenario could be, based simply on membership in a predetermined division. All of them are over .500 through five weeks. Via NBC Sports research, a full division has been above .500 after six weeks only three times since 2002 (the 2025 NFC North, the 2024 NFC North, and the 2005 NFC East). Depending on how this weekend goes, both the AFC North and NFC North can turn that list of three into five. The Vikings, Lions, and Bengals are off, so the six-week hay is in the barn as to each of them. To complete the feat, the 3-2 Browns need to beat the 4-1 Ravens, the 3-2 Bears need to beat the Falcons, the 3-2 Packers need to beat the Cowboys, and the 3-2 Steelers need to beat the Buccaneers. If the Bears and Packers win, it'll be the third straight year that every team in the NFC North is above .500 through six weeks. Which will make it harder for each of them to get to wherever they want to be. That will likely change when the NFL expands the regular season to 18 games and seeds the playoff tree without regard to whether a team has won its division. That still won't solve the problem, and it will bolster the argument that there should be no divisions at all. Or, alternatively, that the two games per year against each of the other teams in the division should become one game per year. The point for now is that each of the four teams in the AFC North and NFC North could end up being objectively playoff-worthy in 2026, but playing six games against those other teams will make it harder to qualify. Meanwhile, someone from the NFC South will be winning the division and hosting a playoff game — even if (like last year) none of them ends up at or above .500. The entire approach makes it harder for the NFL to honor sports' most basic, longstanding message: "May the best team win." Given the way the NFL arranges its teams, the best team could end up with roadblocks that the not-best team won't have to navigate. Which could make it easier for the not-best team to win the Super Bowl.
author: Mike Florio

title: Panthers' JJ Jansen to play his 282nd game, most ever for a long snapper
summary: Carolina's JJ Jansen will become the NFL's all-time record holder for games played by a long snapper on Sunday.
full_text: Carolina's JJ Jansen will become the NFL's all-time record holder for games played by a long snapper on Sunday. The Panthers-Eagles game will be Jansen's 282nd, breaking a tie with Trey Junkin for the most games played at long snapper in NFL history. The 40-year-old Jansen long snapped at Notre Dame and then signed with the Packers as an undrafted free agent in 2008 but played only in the preseason, spending the regular season on injured reserve. In 2009 the Panthers needed a long snapper, so they traded a conditional 2011 draft pick for Jansen. He's been their long snapper ever since. Long snapping is a skill that few players ever learn, and most who do have a story of a football mentor who taught them the technique that can earn playing time on the varsity high school team, a college scholarship for some, and NFL riches for a select few. For Jansen, that mentor was his father, who had been a high school long snapper. "I still remember we practiced in the same way every single time," Jansen told Darin Gantt of Panthers.com. "We had like a square piece of grass that was probably 20 yards by 20 yards. I'd stand at one end in front of a tree that was right in the middle. My dad would stand at 15 yards away, and I would snap it . We'd have those legendary long nights where you're good, and then you stink, and then you're good, and you stink, and you're mad at yourself because you stink, so you yell at your dad, and he's yelling back at you and, there's this whole, you know, boys and their fathers moments." Jansen has played the second-most games of any active player, behind only Ravens defensive end Calais Campbell, who has played 283 games. If both Campbell and Jansen play all 17 games this season, at the end of the year Campbell will have played 295 games, tying him with Darrell Green for the 16th-most in NFL history, and Jansen will have played 294, good for 18th-most in NFL history. All 281 of Jansen's games have been with the Panthers. Former Lions kicker Jason Hanson has the NFL record for most games played with one team, at 327. If Jansen keeps playing every game in Carolina, he'll move ahead of Hanson in the final game of the 2028 season. Jansen is showing no signs of slowing down.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Chiefs nose tackle Khyiris Tonga is playing almost as much offense as Travis Hunter
summary: Jaguars cornerback/wide receiver Travis Hunter has been much-hyped for his status as a two-way player, first as a Heisman Trophy winner at Colorado and now in the NFL.
full_text: Jaguars cornerback/wide receiver Travis Hunter has been much-hyped for his status as a two-way player, first as a Heisman Trophy winner at Colorado and now in the NFL. But there's another two-way player in the NFL this season who hasn't received as much hype: Chiefs nose tackle and fullback Khyiris Tonga. Like Hunter, Tonga has started every game on defense this season. Like Hunter, Tonga has played only limited offensive snaps this season. Tonga has two carries; Hunter has two catches. Both have picked up one first down. Hunter plays a little bit more on offense, but not much more: Hunter has played 6.8 percent of the Jaguars' offensive snaps, while Tonga has played 4.2 percent of the Chiefs' offensive snaps. The Jaguars have said Hunter is capable of being a full-time player at both wide receiver and cornerback, while the Chiefs consider Tonga only a situational short-yardage fullback in addition to his duties as a starter on the defensive line. But as far as their usage this season, both players are comparable. Patriots coach Mike Vrabel, himself a former defensive player who occasionally lined up on offense as well, started using Tonga as a blocking fullback last season, when Tonga played 14 snaps on offense in New England. This year, Tonga signed a three-year, $21 million free agent contract with the Chiefs, and the Chiefs have increased his role on offense, including not just blocking but also running the ball. Tonga said on the Chiefs’ YouTube channel that it was a thrill the first time he went into the offensive huddle with quarterback Patrick Mahomes and running back Kenneth Walker. "It was super cool," Tonga said. "Being in the offensive huddle is amazing, especially having the players we have, to share the huddle with them. The only thing in my mind was, Don't mess it up. I just went out there to have fun. It makes it easy blocking for a guy like K9." Tonga even ran a route on a fourth-and-goal touchdown pass to Jalen Royals in Week 2, and Tonga said he was prepared to catch it if Mahomes threw to him but was a little relieved when Mahomes looked past him and threw to Royals. "I was just making sure I didn't drop it. Look it in if it came to me. It went past me, so it was OK," Tonga said. Could Tonga do anything else in Andy Reid's offense? He said he'd even be up for throwing the ball on a trick play if that gets called. "Having a guy like 15, I hope they don't make me throw the ball, but if we have to I'm ready," Tonga said. Tonga, who has also played 19 snaps on special teams this season, is willing to do whatever he has to do to help his team win.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Titans CEO Burke Nihill: Our organization believes in coach Robert Saleh, GM Mike Borgonzi
summary: The Titans have fired a head coach or GM each of the last four years, but they say they're going to be patient with their current coach and GM.
full_text: The Titans are 0-5 in head coach Robert Saleh's first season, and 3-19 five games into General Manager Mike Borgonzi's second season. But Titans CEO Burke Nihill says the franchise believes the right leadership is in place. "I personally feel a sense of stability," Nihill told ESPN on Friday. "I believe that Mike Borgonzi and Robert Saleh are ultimately going to get this team out of the woods and restore it to competitive football. The train is on the tracks. It just hasn't picked up momentum, but it will. I can confidently say this organization is in a place where there is organizational belief in Mike, in Robert, and they absolutely have all the support they need to get this train moving and moving faster." Those comments would mean more coming directly from Titans owner Amy Adams-Strunk, but the ESPN report says Nihill is empowered to speak for her. Nihill says the organization knows the fans are frustrated. "The first thing I would say back to the fans is just that we're sorry," Nihill said. "There's nobody in this building that doesn't feel . . . a sense of grief about it, because not only are we fans of the team as well, but we feel the sense of responsibility to deliver. And we've let our fans down because football is supposed to be fun. I think it starts on the field and the state of the franchise. We're 0-5, and that's not nearly good enough. It hasn't been for a while." The Titans fired General Manager Jon Robinson during the 2022 season, fired head coach Mike Vrabel after the 2023 season, fired General Manager Ran Carthon after the 2024 season and fired head coach Brian Callahan during the 2025 season. All those firings haven't turned the franchise around. Now they're pledging patience with Borgonzi and Saleh.
author: Michael David Smith

title: 19.8 million watched Bills-Rams on Monday night
summary: The Monday night instant classic between the Bills and the Rams nevertheless failed to crack the 20 million viewer threshold on the various Disney networks.
full_text: The Monday night instant classic between the Bills and the Rams nevertheless failed to crack the 20 million viewer threshold on the various Disney networks. Via ESPN, the final game of Week 5, broadcast by ABC, ESPN, ESPN2, ESPN Deportes, and NFL Network, generated 19.8 million viewers . It's the second most-watched Week 5 Monday night game since ESPN assumed the package in 2026; last year's Chiefs-Jaguars game holds the Week 5 record. ESPN also announced that the alternate broadcasts on ESPN2 (the ManningCast ) and NFL Network (a NextGen Stats production) attracted 1.1 million viewers, without specifying the audiences on either network. That approach could be a precursor to the upcoming Pat McAfee alt casts on ESPN2; if ESPN2 and NFL Network audiences are lumped together, there won't be a clear, apples-to-apples comparison between the ManningCast and the McAfeeFest. In the end, none of the Week 5 prime-time games surpassed 20 million. Bills-Rams arguably was the best candidate to get there, given the Super Bowl preview sizzle associated with the game, and the involvement of the last two NFL MVPs (Bills quarterback Josh Allen and Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford).
author: Mike Florio

title: Troy Aikman's role with the Dolphins hovers over his broadcasting future
summary: Why would any network with options opt for someone who works for one of the NFL's teams?
full_text: '' Troy Aikman's contract with ESPN expires after the 2026 season, which culminates in the four-letter network's first ever Super Bowl. Absent an extension, which Aikman currently doesn't expect, he'll become a broadcasting free agent. His separate relationship with the Dolphins hovers over Aikman's future on TV. Via Mark Maske of Front Office Sports , Aikman does not have a “ formal and ongoing agreement ” to serve as a consultant with the Dolphins. This means that he's working for the team on an at-will basis, and that he (or the team) can end the relationship at any time. It could be in Aikman's best interests to end the relationship with the Dolphins now. If ESPN (or CBS or Prime Video) will be paying $20 million or more for its top NFL analyst gig, why would any of them hire someone who has both restrictions on his access and a cloud over his objectivity, thanks to having an employment relationship with one of its teams. Last month, Aikman " called bullshit " on the idea that other broadcasters don't have conflicts of interest. That misses the point. Aikman is employed by the Dolphins. That relationship prevents him from entering team facilities or attending practices — and it creates avoidable complications when it comes to games involving the team that employs him. When ESPN's Jason Kelce refers to the Eagles as "we," it's because he used to play for the team. (And ESPN is trying to get him to knock it off .) When Aikman talks about the Dolphins, "we" is technically accurate; he works for the team. For networks with options, why would any network opt for someone who is employed by one of the teams? Beyond Tom Brady (who owns a piece of the Raiders and has an even more obvious conflict of interest, even if Fox doesn't care), none of the other candidates for the biggest jobs in NFL broadcasting bring such baggage with them. As to Aikman, the right decision is obvious if he hopes to get another high-profile broadcasting job. He should end his relationship with the Dolphins as soon as possible.
author: Mike Florio

title: Terrion Arnold remains on paid leave
summary: The NFL's decision to reinstate Packers running back Josh Jacobs and Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper from the Commissioner Exempt list carried with it a conspicuous omission.
full_text: The NFL's decision to reinstate Packers running back Josh Jacobs and Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper from the Commissioner Exempt list carried with it a conspicuous omission. Seahawks cornerback Terrion Arnold remains on paid leave. All three landed on paid leave on Sunday, August 30. Both Jacobs and Cooper are returning after six games. Arnold will continue to wait. The distinction highlights the evolution of paid leave. Now, the NFL uses it as a way to pre-suspend a player with pay for the number of games he's likely to miss once officially suspended under the Personal Conduct Policy. The player receives credit once he's suspended without pay for the games missed while on paid leave. As to Arnold, who faces a potential sentence of life in prison due to eight felonies arising from an alleged armed robbery and kidnapping, it makes sense for the league to wait for the criminal case against him to be resolved. While the standard punishment for a case of domestic battery is six games, the claims against Arnold could trigger something longer — especially in light of the potential criminal penalties. Frankly, the NFL may never have to convert Arnold's paid leave into an unpaid suspension. If he ends up behind bars for the practical balance of his career, the length of the suspension won't matter.
author: Mike Florio

title: Lions put OL Ben Bartch, WR Tom Kennedy, LB Devin White on injured reserve
summary: The Lions took care of some roster business during their bye week.
full_text: The Lions took care of some roster business during their bye week. They announced that they have placed offensive lineman Ben Bartch, wide receiver Tom Kennedy, and linebacker Devin White on the injured reserve list. All three players will have to miss at least four games before they'll have a chance to return. Bartch was inactive in Week 5 due to a foot injury and White broke his forearm in that game. Kennedy is expected to miss the rest of the season with an MCL injury that requires surgery. The Lions now have three open roster spots to fill. Safety Brian Branch and center Cade Mays have designated for return from injured reserve, so they could take two of those slots.
author: Josh Alper

title: KC Concepcion on Minkah Fitzpatrick's hit: It was a football play; it wasn't dirty
summary: Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick's hit on KC Concepcion on Sunday knocked out the Browns wide receiver.
full_text: ' Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick's hit on KC Concepcion on Sunday knocked out the Browns wide receiver. Concepcion was diagnosed with his first concussion. Fitzpatrick will appeal a fine from the NFL, calling the hit just a " football play " despite a 15-yard unnecessary roughness penalty. Concepcion agrees with Fitzpatrick's assessment. “I know the game that I signed up to play,” Concepcion said Friday, via Mary Kay Cabot of cleveland.com. “This game is a very physical game. To me, it wasn’t a dirty hit. It was just a football play .” The rookie first-round pick cleared concussion protocol on Friday and will play Sunday. “I thank the Lord, just for him allowing me to get back up and be able to walk off the field,” Concepcion said. “I’m like this all the time, smiling, dancing, cracking jokes. [But] I would say that I am glad that I was able to get up and be able to play again.”
author: Charean Williams

title: Chris Olave returns to practice, listed as questionable for Sunday
summary: Saints wide receiver Chris Olave was back on the practice field Friday, but his status for Sunday's road game against the Giants remains up in the air.
full_text: Saints wide receiver Chris Olave was back on the practice field Friday, but his status for Sunday's road game against the Giants remains up in the air. Olave missed practice on Wednesday and Thursday due to an illness, so his return for a limited workout on Friday would seem to have him pointing in the right direction to play in Week 6. Olave has 39 catches for 537 yards and a touchdown through the first five weeks of the season. Running back Alvin Kamara (back) is also listed as questionable. He was limited in practice all week. Defensive lineman Nathan Shepherd (illness), defensive back Lorenzo Styles (knee), and long snapper Zach Wood are the other questionable players for New Orleans. Linebackers Kaden Elliss (calf) and Anfernee Jennings (knee) have been ruled out.

title: Bills WR DJ Moore, DL Ed Oliver are questionable

full_text: The Bills did not rule anyone out for Sunday's game against the Raiders. They do, however, list five players as questionable. title: Stephen Jones says Joey Porter Jr. is "all-in" with the Cowboys
summary: Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr. did not play in four games with the Steelers.
full_text: ' Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr. did not play in four games with the Steelers. He was inactive due to his on-again, off-again back issue, which wasn't an issue after the trade to the Cowboys. Porter, though, has had an ankle injury and an illness, playing one of two possible games in Dallas. He is questionable for Sunday's game against the Packers. Porter was unhappy with the Steelers after not getting a desired long-term contract extension before the season. The Cowboys made clear after the trade that they aren't negotiating with Porter this season. Cowboys executive vice president Stephen Jones was asked on 105.3 The Fan whether he had concerns about a hold-in from Porter. “Oh, absolutely, I think he’s all in," Jones said on his radio show Friday, via Jon Machota of TheAthletic.com. "He wants to be out there. He was sick [in Week 5 against the Bucs]. He couldn’t play last week with the flu. But he obviously played in our [Week 4 game against the Texans], and I think he’s fired up about what he can do to help us win against the Packers.” Porter said earlier this week that he expects to have a full-time role in the defense against the Packers.
author: Charean Williams

title: Trent McDuffie, Kam Curl questionable for Rams-Cardinals
summary: Two of the Rams defensive backs are uncertain to play Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
full_text: Two of the Rams defensive backs are uncertain to play Sunday's game against the Cardinals. Trent McDuffie (groin) and safety Kam Curl (ankle) are both listed as questionable. Head coach Sean McVay told reporters that Trent McDuffie felt something in his groin at the end of Thursday’s session, so the team held him out of Friday’s practice out of an abundance of caution. McDuffie has registered seven passes defensed and an interception so far in 2026. The rest of the Rams are good to go, including tight end Davis Allen (foot) who missed the first two days of the practice week. He was limited in Friday’s session. Receiver/returner Alex Bachman (wrist), linebacker Nate Landman (wrist/shoulder), tight end Colby Parkinson (shoulder), linebacker Omar Speights (knee), offensive lineman Keagan Trost (hamstring), and cornerback Josh Wallace (shoulder) are the other players who are off the injury report.
author: Myles Simmons

title: John Lynch: George Kittle asked me if we're trying to trade for Khalil Mack
summary: The trade deadline was a topic of conversation for General Manager John Lynch on Friday.
full_text: '' The trade deadline was a topic of conversation for General Manager John Lynch on Friday. Lynch was a guest on KNBR and he was asked if calls are picking up with the November 10 deadline drawing closer. Lynch said that the calls have picked up of late and that the team has made its own "just to kind of see where the market's at" right now. Lynch was also asked specifically about interest in Chargers pass rusher Khalil Mack. "I can’t tell you that ," Lynch said, via 49ersWebzone.com. "A lot of people ask me that. We seem to be connected to everyone, and I don't know where that comes from. I had a player ask me that yesterday." Lynch eventually named tight end George Kittle as the inquisitive player, which isn't surprising "because he asks about everything." Kittle's interest in the prospect makes sense, however. The 49ers are 5-0 and should feel good enough about their chances to make a run that they'd be willing to bolster the roster ahead of the deadline. On the other hand, the Chargers are 0-5 and should be considering picking up assets for the future with this season headed off the rails.
author: Josh Alper

title: Colts add Tyler Warren to injury report, list him as questionable

title: NFL removes Broncos OLB Jonathon Cooper from Commissioner's Exempt List
summary: The NFL has announced it has removed Broncos outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper from the Commissioner's Exempt List.
full_text: The NFL has announced it has removed Broncos outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper from the Commissioner's Exempt List. Cooper is eligible to play in the team's next game on Oct. 25 after missing six games. The NFL placed Cooper on paid leave on Aug. 30 following domestic-related charges involving two incidents with his former girlfriend in June. Cooper's motion hearing was continued on Monday at the request of the district attorney’s office. He is now scheduled for a motion hearing on Feb. 23 and a jury trial the week of March 2. The NFL season ends with Super Bowl LXI on Feb. 14. Cooper is facing five charges after two disputes with his ex-girlfriend that began with a fight over a cell phone. The most serious charge is felony second-degree assault/strangulation. He participated in the team's training camp and three preseason games after pleading not guilty to all charges. Cooper lost $180,000 in per-game roster bonuses but was able to keep his six weekly game checks of $676,471 each while on leave. In its statement, the league said it will continue to investigate and monitor Cooper's legal matter until a resolution.
author: Charean Williams

title: Josh Jacobs will be removed from paid leave on Monday
summary: NFL leaves door open for further discipline.
full_text: The efforts of Packers running back Josh Jacobs to keep the NFL from seeing the video of the altercation that resulted in his no-contest plea for battery has worked. For now. The NFL has announced that Jacobs will be reinstated from the Commissioner Exempt list on Monday. The timing isn't coincidental. With the baseline punishment for domestic battery under the Personal Conduct Policy set at six games, the move allows the league to pre-suspend a player whose internal investigation is still pending. Then, if/when a suspension is imposed, he'll get credit for the games missed while on paid leave — and he'll forfeit the pay he received during the games in which he didn't play. Although paid leave technically isn't discipline (even though, as a practical matter, it is), the missed games become part of the eventual discipline. And the league's decision to reserve the right to add additional games ties directly to the video that it wants to review before it closes his case. It's a risky move for the NFL. Until it sees the video, it won't know whether the video contains images that would justify a much more significant punishment than a six-game suspension. The better play, given Jacobs's efforts to keep the league from seeing the video, would be to tell him that he won't play at all until the league sees the video. If, in the end, the video is as shocking as the Ray Rice video from 2014 was, the NFL will have another P.R. mess on its hands. Maybe, after 12 years, the memory of extent of the Ray Rice situation has faded. Either way, the safest approach would have been to tell Jacobs that, until the video is seen by the league, his stay on paid leave will continue.

title: David Blough takes responsibility for clock debacle
summary: When a soldier is captured by the enemy, he knows to say only three things: Name, rank, and serial number.
full_text: When a soldier is captured by the enemy, he knows to say only three things: Name, rank, and serial number. As to the Commanders' overtime clock debacle against the Giants, a similar three-step formula has emerged. It's my responsibility. I take accountability. It won't happen again. Offensive coordinator David Blough completed the fault trifecta on Friday , in his first comments to reporters since the Week 5 game ended in a tie, thanks to a stunning failure to find a way to attempt a field goal in the final 55 seconds of the extra 10-minute period, Blough repeatedly expressed a very basic, general message of responsibility, acceptance of accountability, and determination to not let the situation repeat itself. The reporters tried to get more (any) details from him about how it transpired. He continued to retreat to a combination of words and phrases that eventually seemed to be the product of talking points that had been prepared and memorized at some point this week. Ultimately, there has been no real insight from coach Dan Quinn, quarterback Jayden Daniels, or Blough into how it happened. And none of them has been asked the one question that may have yielded the most revealing answer: Did the quarterback and the rest of the offense realize that the game would end when the 10 minutes expired? At this point, with a new slate of Sunday games looming (and with the Commanders facing the 49ers on Monday night), the incident will become a footnote to the 2026 season. And we'll never know precisely how it happened. We know what happened — they screwed up, royally. But we'll never know how it happened, why it happened, and, ultimately, who bears the bulk of the blame. Yes, it's everyone. Still, there's someone who deserves more blame than others. And there's a specific explanation (beyond "shit happens") as to how it came to be. That explanation, through multiple press availabilities, never emerged.

title: NFL Week 6 injury report: Lamar Jackson, Jalen Hurts sidelined; Caleb Williams could return
summary: Tyler Huntley and Tanner McKee will start in place of Jackson and Hurts, while Michael Penix Jr. is cleared to face Chicago
full_text:
The NFL keeps chugging along, and as with every upcoming slate, injuries have become a central focus. Unlike previous weeks, where it feels like it's been more about who is out of the lineup rather than who is in it, Week 6 is more of a mixed bag on the injury front, which can be looked at as a glass half full.
However, if you're a Ravens fan, you're certainly not ecstatic about the latest injury developments as Lamar Jackson is slated to miss his second-straight game due to an ankle injury. That means Tyler Huntley will get another start after defeating the Falcons last Sunday night. Meanwhile, the Eagles are drowning in injury news and will also be starting a backup quarterback in Tanner McKee . This comes after the revelation that starter Jalen Hurts is dealing with a blood clot in his calf. He headlines what is a CVS receipt-sized injury list for Philadelphia this season.
But, as we mentioned, it's not all doom and gloom from an injury standpoint. Michael Penix Jr . (rib) has the green light to play for the Falcons, while it's not out of the realm of possibility that Caleb Williams makes his return to the Bears or A.J. Brown reinserts himself into the Patriots offense this week, either.
Below, we'll run through every injury report across the league as we barrel towards Week 6.
Note : Cincinnati, Detroit, Miami, and Minnesota are on the bye in Week 6.
David Montgomery did not make the trip to London and has since officially been ruled out. That means backup Woody Marks will see the lion's share of the touches out of the Texans' backfield. Meanwhile, safety Jalen Pitre did not practice all week with a shoulder injury, so it's not surprising to see him ruled out. As for Ingram and To'oTo'o, they both practiced fully on both Thursday and Friday and seem more on the probable side of the questionable designation.
The Jaguars will once again be without their top long snapper as they ruled out Ross Matiscik due to a shoulder injury he suffered last week against the Eagles. However, they did have some reinforcements after signing Jacob Bobenmoyer .
Caleb Williams was a full participant throughout the week of practice, but is officially questionable to make his return in Week 6. On Thursday, Williams told reporters he does "not know if I'm playing yet."
Michael Penix Jr. (ribs) was a full participant in practice on Friday and carries no injury designation, so the Falcons starter will play in Week 6 against Chicago. Atlanta won't have corner C.J. Henderson, however, as he's still dealing with a groin injury he suffered in Week 5 against the Ravens.
Baltimore will be without Lamar Jackson for the second straight week as he continues to deal with an ankle injury. The two-time NFL MVP has yet to practice since suffering the injury, and his absence will thrust backup Tyler Huntley into the starting role yet again. Meanwhile, Jurgens will miss Sunday's divisional matchup as he is still in concussion protocol. That'll likely result in Vega Ioane starting at center. On the bright side, Zay Flowers is good to go as he carries no injury designation after being limited on Thursday and Friday with a toe injury.
Cleveland saw Mason Graham, Quinshon Judkins, and Carson Schwesinger all return to practice on Friday in a limited capacity after missing the start of the week due to injury. They are each questionable to play, but that return to the field does leave the door open for them to play in Week 6.

title: Josh Jacobs, Jonathon Cooper to come off NFL commissioner exempt list, eligible to return in Week 7
summary: Both players will become eligible for Week 7, although their teams must determine whether they are ready to play
full_text:
The league announced two players will be removed from the NFL's Commissioner Exempt list in the coming days. Denver Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper will be removed on Friday, and Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs on Monday.
Cooper is eligible to play in Denver's Week 7 game against the Arizona Cardinals , and Jacobs is expected to be eligible to play in Green Bay's Week 7 game against the Detroit Lions , according to ESPN.
"The league's review of both the Josh Jacobs and Jonathon Cooper situations 'remains ongoing' and is not affected by the change to either player's status," the report states.
Players on the commissioner's exempt list continue to be paid. If the NFL later suspends either player, the league could credit the games missed on the exempt list toward the suspension and seek repayment of salary earned during that period. Being on the list means players cannot attend practice or games.
Cooper was dismissed from minicamp and was placed on the list ahead of the season following two arrests involving an alleged domestic violence incident with his ex-girlfriend in June. He faces five charges, including second-degree felony assault. His trial was moved from mid-November to early March.
Cooper has spent his entire career thus far with the Broncos, who drafted him in the seventh round of the 2021 NFL Draft.
Jacobs was charged with two misdemeanors, battery and damage to property, from an arrest in May. Jacobs filed an action seeking to prevent the public release of evidence related to the case, including alleged video of the incident. Jacobs' attorney released a statement saying he "accepts responsibility for his actions" and says he is "excited to get back on the field with his teammates."
Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs’ legal team of Clarence F. Duchac III, David Z. Chesnoff and Richard A. Sconfield release the following statement on Jacobs being removed from the commissioner’s exempt list. Jacobs is now eligible to return to the team in Week 7. pic.twitter.com/BuiPIR93VZ
Jacobs signed a four-year, $48 million deal with the Packers heading into the 2024 season and he is now in his third year with the team. The All-Pro was selected by the Las Vegas Raiders at No. 24 overall in the 2019 NFL Draft.
In his absence, RB Marshawn Lloyd has led the team with just 112 rushing yards and two touchdowns. Kaleb Johnson is second on the team with 106 yards.
While both players will be eligible to return in Week 7, that decision is ultimately up to the coaches and players involved.
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: Jaylen Waddle trade revisited: Bo Nix, Broncos struggling to integrate speedy WR who's also dropping passes
summary: Neither the Denver passing offense nor Waddle are playing well
full_text:
In Bo Nix's preseason debut this year -- his first football game since breaking his ankle -- he rifled a ball to Jaylen Waddle , who had won on a vertical route up the middle of the field. Waddle caught it and sped away from his defender, a 35-yard gain. The Denver crowd erupted, even for a preseason game . This is what they had wanted so badly, the missing piece for a team that was on the doorstep of a Super Bowl berth last year.
Welcome to Denver, @D1__JW ‼️ 📺: 9NEWS pic.twitter.com/qvxiByZBAl
Denver needed explosiveness. Waddle brought it in bunches. This was the start of a beautiful marriage.
After another eyesore offensive performance from Denver in which Waddle was hardly involved (four catches, 24 yards), we revisit the deal this offseason that came with seemingly so much promise ... and wonder if Waddle and Nix can get on track.
The Dolphins were in the midst of a massive teardown that included the release of Tyreek Hill, Tua Tagovailoa and Bradley Chubb . Miami, 27, was neither as old as Hill or Chubb nor as costly as Tagovailoa, but Miami opted to wipe the slate as clean as possible, and Denver seemed to be the perfect home.
Adding the speed and explosiveness of Waddle to a group that included a big-bodied possession receiver (Sutton) and several ancillary pieces was going to unlock Nix, the Broncos thought.
The supposed "perfect combination" has actually been, for the most part early this season, very little combination. Through six games, Waddle has 22 catches for 228 yards and one touchdown. His 10.4 yards per reception are on pace to be his worst number since his rookie year.
Waddle has played a large role in that last line. He has four drops already this season after three all of last year. He came to Denver with a 6.1% career drop rate (which already wasn't great), but he is at a very bad 10.8% this year.
The preseason wasn't the only false hope. After a brutal Week 1 in which pretty much everything went wrong for Denver, Waddle caught eight of 10 targets for 138 yards against the Jaguars , showing off his full skill set. He caught a 49-yarder downfield. He made catches on in-breaking routes, something he did so well in Miami. He showed off his YAC ability, and he absolutely roasted Jourdan Lewis for a crucial third-down conversion. Sean Payton talked up the need to get him the football. It seemed like all was on track.
Jaylen Waddle showed out in his first home game with Denver 8 REC, 138 YDS, 17.3 AVG on 10 TGT vs. Jacksonville After a quiet Broncos debut, Waddle helped Denver erase a 10 point deficit and grab its first win. https://t.co/qmZR0HioXM pic.twitter.com/DxVPCl9Mi1
Outside of the Jaguars game, Waddle's longest catch is 13 yards. Three of his five targets 20+ yards downfield came in the Jaguars game; the other two are an underthrow and a near-interception into double coverage. And the frustration spilled over in Week 5, when Nix checked into a run play on third and long.
Pay attention to Jaylen Waddle and Bo Nix after this run😭 pic.twitter.com/21feUnewVR
Nix's passing tendencies have bordered on playing not to lose, rather than playing to win. His average throw travels 4.9 yards downfield, not only the shortest in the NFL this season but also the shortest by any quarterback through six games in the last 20 years. He simply is not even attempting to hit Waddle in the intermediate and deep areas where Waddle thrives.
Furthermore, it's not as if Waddle hasn't been open. According to NFL Next Gen Stats , Waddle has an average separation of 3.9 yards, the 11th-highest rate in the league and much higher than his mark last year (2.7).
Remember all those fun downfield routes Waddle got against the Jaguars? Here's what his seven targeted routes looked like Thursday.
Free Jaylen Waddle pic.twitter.com/DpQUCJNGeM
Of course, this was on a short week and just the second week since Sean Payton took playcalling duties back from Davis Webb . But there is a clear disconnect between what Waddle provides, what Nix wants to throw and what the coaching staff trusts Nix to do. One clip going around is Nix opting against firing a downfield throw to Waddle to instead throw a dump-off that gets knocked down. Like in Week 4, Waddle is not happy after the play.
3rd & 8, First Down ends the game... Watch 17. Could Nix rip this in? Also... watch Waddle after the play from the second angle... not happy #BroncosCountry pic.twitter.com/vuI3TF15Tv
It's not like the work is being funneled elsewhere. The entire passing attack is bad. Waddle leads all Broncos with 228 receiving yards and is nearly 100 yards ahead of the next-closest wide receiver ( Pat Bryant , 133).
At some point, Nix has to push the ball downfield. It will take a combination of his willingness and the staff scheming more downfield throws Nix is comfortable with -- his comfort level is clearly very low right now -- but this isn't close to the Waddle anyone expected. There's blame to share.
It's also not worth writing off 100%. Waddle's drops are at a career-worst rate. Nix's downfield throwing is at a career-worst rate. We'd like to see more chances for Waddle on in-breaking routes -- he has just four receptions on ins, crossers, slants and posts -- and a greater willingness for Nix to throw them. The play-calling has been mixed, and Nix still doesn't look like himself. Maybe more time removed from the ankle injury, which sapped much of his offseason, will help. It's been concerning, but the season is only one-third of the way done.
Just like it's early for Denver, it's early for Miami. In the grand scheme, it's much, much earlier, even. The Dolphins aren't likely to contend for ... a while. Assessing how they did in this trade will take ... a while.
Miami and its youngsters are taking their lumps this season, as expected, but they have shown some good signs. Chris Johnson is PFF's No. 21-graded cornerback, just behind some bigger names such as Devon Witherspoon , Quinyon Mitchell and Travis Hunter .
Johnson's 6.1 yards per attempt allowed as primary defender ranks 24th out of 74 defensive backs targeted at least 20 times, and his 8.6 yards per completion allowed is 11th. There is a lot to like here.
It's even earlier for Chris Bell, an explosive wide receiver with borderline first-round talent who fell to the third round after a torn ACL. He has just five catches on 16 routes, but those five catches have gone for 92 yards. Again, patience is required.
Chris Bell showing off his speed 💨 @KCvsMIA on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/tNbGIYPEGf
Moore unfortunately suffered an ankle injury in the preseason and had to undergo surgery. He is still on IR.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Mike Macdonald shuts down potential Seahawks quarterback change, sticking with Sam Darnold
summary: Darnold has thrown an NFL-high seven interceptions, but Macdonald stands behind his starter
full_text:
It hasn't been the best season for Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold . He suffered a gluteal injury during the team's season opener and has struggled quite a bit since returning from it. Darnold has completed only 60.4% of his passes at an average of just 6.9 yards per attempt, and he's thrown for seven touchdowns against an NFL-high seven interceptions. He seemingly hit a nadir on Thursday night against the Broncos , completing 52.9% of his passes at 5.5 yards per attempt and throwing two picks, including one that led to Denver's game-winning field goal.
Despite those struggles, Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald is not considering a change under center.
"No, no," Macdonald said during a radio appearance when asked about a potential switch from Darnold to backup Drew Lock .
Macdonald stated that the Seahawks have a starter-quality backup in Lock, but that the offense can find its way with Darnold under center.
"Sam's played great football for us this year the majority of the time," he said. "There's other times he needs to take care of the football but I think these are solutions we can find with Sam as our QB. I believe that."
Lock played most of two games in place of Darnold (all but the first drive of the opener against the Patriots , and Week 2 against the Cardinals ), completing 35 of 48 passes for 422 yards and four touchdowns. That performance was mostly out of line with what he's put on tape throughout his career, though, so it's not that surprising that the Seahawks aren't considering a change just yet.
Even while he led the Seahawks to a Super Bowl victory, Darnold also struggled with turnovers last season, throwing 14 interceptions — but he was much more efficient in the passing game to make up for it. He completed 67.7% of his passes at an average of 8.2 yards per attempt. The Seahawks are breaking in a new offensive coordinator this year: Brian Fleury, who replaced the departed Klint Kubiak, now the head coach of the Raiders .
Macdonald acknowledged that Fleury has some things to figure out during the mini-bye before the Seahawks take on the undefeated Chiefs in Week 7.
"Brian is well prepared. He's incredibly smart," Macdonald said, via Seattle Sports . "But as an offense, we need to really look at what we're doing, how we're doing it, what we're asking certain people to do. We need to look at all of those things right now."
That process should probably involve looking at what they're asking Darnold to do and deciding exactly how it needs to be tweaked so he can rediscover some of what made him more effective for most of last season.
author: Jared Dubin

title: The Broncos have a Bo Nix problem, and their Super Bowl window may force a tough decision
summary: Bo Nix keeps winning, but the Broncos can't ignore what the numbers say
full_text:
Bo Nix is 28-12 through his first 40 NFL starts, more victories than John Elway and Peyton Manning had over that same stretch. Among active quarterbacks, only Patrick Mahomes and Lamar Jackson had better records at this point in their careers.
There's just one problem: Nix is directing one of the NFL's least productive offenses, and his individual numbers are getting worse. So what exactly should we make of all that success?
Thursday night's 17-14 overtime victory against Seattle might have been the most extreme example yet. Denver managed 168 yards of offense, averaged 2.9 yards per play and gained a grand total of 38 yards on 25 plays after halftime. Nix finished with 107 passing yards, averaging exactly four yards per attempt.
Former NFL quarterback Ryan Fitzpatrick wasn't nearly as forgiving. During Amazon's postgame show, he ripped Nix's performance, saying, "He's not playing competitive football right now," and later calling it " almost disrespectful to the quarterback position ."
So, yeah … the Broncos improved to 4-2 and extended their streak of one-score victories to 14 games. Their defense dominated for long stretches, forcing turnovers and capitalizing on Seattle's mistakes. And it's not a stretch to suggest they accomplished all this in spite of, not because of Bo Nix.
Denver has a defense capable of carrying this team to the Super Bowl . But if Nix can't give the Broncos more than he has through the first six games, none of that matters. Put more bluntly: How much longer are they willing to wait for him to figure it out?
It's easy to look at Nix's 2026 numbers, throw your hands up and conclude that he's suddenly fallen apart. The third-year quarterback has undoubtedly gotten worse this season, but some of the problems have been there all along.
Nix threw 29 touchdowns and 12 interceptions as a rookie in 2024 and helped Denver reach the playoffs. He followed that with another winning season, and through his first 39 starts, he'd thrown 60 touchdowns, completed 64.2% of his passes and piled up 8,648 passing yards.
Those aren't bad numbers, and Nix, at times, has looked comfortable running Sean Payton's offense. Enough to give Denver reason to believe it had found its long-term answer. But look a little deeper, and the picture starts to change.
Nix's efficiency -- how consistently he moves the ball, creates big plays and avoids negative ones -- doesn't quite match his impressive record, according to TruMedia. To put that into perspective, we compared him to a sample of 74 other quarterbacks drafted since 2008, looking at how each performed through his first 39 starts over his first three NFL seasons.
Nix excelled at avoiding sacks, getting the ball out quickly and keeping Denver out of trouble. But there was a tradeoff: He wasn't making nearly enough big plays through the air, and his 6.4 yards per attempt ranked 59th among the 75 quarterbacks in our sample.
In other words, Nix was good at avoiding mistakes, but not nearly as good at making plays that could change a game. And through six games in 2026, even that formula has started to fall apart.
Nix isn't just throwing shorter passes. He's taking fewer chances downfield, making more turnover-worthy plays and struggling to move the offense. And when he does drop back, he's getting less out of those opportunities than at any point in his career.
Consider how his numbers have changed since his rookie season.
There was genuine progress in 2025. Nix's EPA per dropback increased, his big-time throw rate improved and he did a better job of avoiding sacks when pressured. That's meaningful, and it offers at least some evidence that he was improving.
But through six games in 2026, those gains have largely disappeared. His big-time throw rate has been cut in half, his turnover-worthy play rate has nearly doubled from last season and his EPA per dropback has turned negative.
And while his accuracy rate has remained stable, he's generating fewer first downs, explosive plays and touchdowns. And he's putting the ball in harm's way more often.
There's also the ankle injury to consider. Nix underwent surgery after fracturing his right ankle in January's playoff win over Buffalo, but he has repeatedly insisted he's fully healthy. Asked directly after Denver's Week 4 loss to San Francisco whether the injury was affecting his play, he offered a one-word answer: "No."
It's certainly fair to wonder, based on what we've all witnessed this season, if that's not entirely true.  There's also the fact that Payton has commandeered play-calling duties from offensive coordinator Davis Webb , hoping to jump-start an offense that had struggled through its first four games.
So far, it hasn't helped. Denver managed just 224 yards against the Chargers in Week 5 and 168 against Seattle, and the Broncos now rank 31st in yards per game and last in yards per play. Payton helped Nix develop over his first two seasons, but the last two weeks have only raised more questions about whether he'll ever become the quarterback Denver envisioned when they drafted him.
Nix was the 12th overall pick, and the sixth quarterback taken in the 2024 NFL Draft , behind Caleb Williams , Jayden Daniels , Drake Maye , Michael Penix Jr . and JJ McCarthy .
Some two-and-a-half seasons later, how does Nix stack up against his classmates?
Maye helped lead the Patriots to the Super Bowl in Year 2, while Daniels took Washington to the NFC Championship Game as a rookie. Williams made significant strides under Ben Johnson in 2025, leading Chicago to a division title and a playoff victory, and Penix has been surprisingly impressive this season. Even with injuries complicating the comparisons, there's enough evidence to suggest every quarterback in this class not named Nix or McCarthy is developing into the player their teams envisioned.
2024 first-round QB class: NFL passing production, 2024-26
Nix has started more games than anyone in the group, and unlike several of his classmates, he's had the same coach and offensive system since arriving in the NFL. That stability should have helped his development, and for a while, it appeared to. But through six games in '26, Nix is heading in the wrong direction.
That doesn't mean Denver should give up and move on. But after 40 starts, his struggles raise a bigger question: How much longer should the Broncos expect to wait for a breakthrough?
So what happens to quarterbacks whose numbers look like Nix's after some 40 starts? Do they figure it out, or is three seasons enough to know what you have?
The good news for Denver is that some quarterbacks do turn things around. The bad news? Most don't suddenly become stars. There's a big difference between improving enough to keep your job and becoming the guy who can carry a team to the Super Bowl.
We used TruMedia data to look at 24 quarterbacks whose early-career efficiency resembled Nix's, then compared their first 39 starts with their next 21. Nine improved their EPA per dropback by at least 0.05. But just four reached +0.10 or better, and as it turns out, even that didn't guarantee long-term success.
What happened to quarterbacks who started their careers like Bo Nix?
Josh Allen and Dak Prescott give Denver some hope. Both started with numbers similar to Nix's, took major steps forward over their next 21 starts and continued to produce at a high level over the following 20 games. Andy Dalton, stylistically a much closer comp to Nix than Allen or Prescott, needed a little longer, making his biggest leap between starts 61 and 80.
Others followed a different path. Tua Tagovailoa, Jared Goff and Baker Mayfield initially improved, only to see their numbers fall off during the next 20 starts. Derek Carr and Blake Bortles also made gains before regressing, while Mitch Trubisky and Mark Sanchez, both top-5 picks in their respective draft classes, never made much progress. Of course, Goff and Mayfield eventually turned their careers around, which shows that development is…
author: Ryan Wilson

title: What's wrong with Bo Nix and Sam Darnold, and can either one of them figure it out?
summary: Nix managed just 107 passing yards, and Darnold threw two interceptions
full_text:
"No way to sugarcoat it. That one sucked."
That was how Sam Darnold opened his postgame press conference Thursday night after a 17-14 overtime loss to the Broncos . He was talking about his performance, but he could have been talking about everything offensively from both sides ... and, from a neutral viewer's perspective, the game as a whole.
The Broncos won despite 168 yards of offense, the fewest in an overtime win in NFL history. The Seahawks generated 353 yards of offense but wasted much of it with three turnovers and a missed field goal.
Both Nix and Darnold are going through major struggles of very different types this season. Darnold is tied with Justin Herbert with seven interceptions this year, and that's despite him missing most of the season opener and all of Week 2 with a leg injury.
Nix, meanwhile, is averaging an NFL-low 5.6 yards per attempt, and he's not really exploring trying to raise that rate. His 4.9 air yards per attempt is not just the lowest in the NFL this season, but the lowest by any quarterback through six games in the last 20 seasons. After the game Thursday, Amazon Prime analyst and former NFL quarterback Ryan Fitzpatrick ripped into Nix for "not playing competitive football."
If there's one thing bonding both teams -- and both quarterbacks -- it's that the mini-bye comes at a very good time to evaluate, re-evaluate and make changes. It's not as if the world is crashing down: Seattle is 3-3, Denver 4-2. But it's clear neither is operating at a Super Bowl-winning level or close to it, and given the high expectations of both, that isn't good enough.
"They're incredibly valuable," Mike Macdonald said about the extra three days. "Yes, incredibly valuable. So the responsibility, or onus, is on us to go make it come to life. So that's what we intend to do."
But can either quarterback actually do it?
All turnovers are bad, but not all are equally bad. Both of Darnold's turnovers Thursday were of the "really bad" variety. In the fourth quarter, down 14-11, the Seahawks faced a third-and-1 at the Denver 39-yard line. It was in Jason Myers ' field goal range, and if Seattle wanted to get aggressive, they could have gone for it on fourth down. Instead, Darnold did this:
BRONCOS INTERCEPT SAM DARNOLD WITH 1:25 LEFT IN THE GAME SEAvsDEN on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/7vK2rjBe1k
Then, after leading a really impressive drive to force overtime, Darnold did this on the third play of the extra session:
Ja'Quan McMillian read this PERFECTLY. SEAvsDEN on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/1igvuDtROG
You simply cannot take points off the board and hand points to the other team, especially in games like this, where points are at a premium.
And it's not just this loss. It's every loss so far. The Seahawks have 12 turnovers this year, second-most in the NFL behind only the hapless Chargers . Ten of those 12 have come in losses. In Week 3 against the Commanders , Darnold threw two picks, including a late pick-six. Last week against the 49ers , Darnold threw two more picks, and a terrible George Holani fumble while Seattle was simply trying to run the clock out in the first half resulted in a San Francisco touchdown.
The Seahawks' three losses are by a combined eight points. Those turnovers loom really, really large. They're also canceling out games Seattle largely controls. The Seahawks have already lost two games in which they out-gained their opponent by 150+ yards. The rest of the NFL combined only has two such games.
Darnold has always been a wildcard (at best) when it comes to ball security. He led the NFL with 20 turnovers last year, and he's on pace to have roughly the same number this year. His 4.7% interception rate is on track to be a career high, though it's probably due to regression a bit.
The issue is that Darnold isn't offsetting those turnovers with good play, as he did last year. His numbers across the board are down.
Three things are coming into play here, and they're all related. First, the Seahawks can't run the ball. They're 26th in rushing success rate and 31st in rushing expected points added.
This is where they really miss Kenneth Walker III , who wasn't the most consistent back down-to-down but provided so much explosiveness to make up for it. Just look at what he's doing in Kansas City.
If defenses don't need to worry about the run as much, they don't have to respect play action as much, either. In fact, Kirk Herbstreit pointed out on the broadcast Thursday that the Broncos' linebackers weren't even taking a step down to stop the potential for a run on play action.
Darnold was one of the NFL's best play-action passers this year. He hasn't been the same this year.
Sam Darnold ranks on play action
That middle column is key. The downfield elements of the play-action passing attack aren't there. Seattle is also running into a chicken-or-egg issue under new offensive coordinator Brian Fleury. Darnold has been under center on just 44% of his snaps this year, down from 54% last year. But is that because the opponents aren't respecting the under-center play actions? Either way, the drop-off has been steep.
And finally, Darnold's protection has not been good. Again, it's related. Is the protection not good because the play action isn't good, because the run game isn't good? Regardless, Darnold is being pressured on 45% of his dropbacks, up from 35% last year.
"You could say it's on the offensive line," Macdonald said postgame. "It's on our offense. You know, it's both. So, it's how efficient we can run the ball and we can move the ball other ways. So, but the quarterback is getting hit way too much. So everybody sees that."
Verdict: There are fixable elements here, but it really starts with Darnold not turning the ball over. Zach Charbonnet's return could help, but relying on an already not-explosive runner coming off a torn ACL to fix everything is unreasonable. Rather, Fleury will have to find creative solutions, and Seattle will have to run the ball better to make everything easier for Darnold. As it turns out, Klint Kubiak and Kenneth Walker III were really good at their jobs.
Nix's deepest completion Thursday was 8 yards downfield. He did try three deeper throws, but all three were incomplete: a deep shot to Marvin Mims Jr. that got broken up, an underthrow intended for Jaylen Waddle and a crosser to Courtland Sutton that got broken up by a big hit.
It's clear that Nix not only doesn't want to throw downfield, but that the Broncos don't trust him to make any plays downfield.
Nix has 13 plays on third down Thursday night. He went 4 for 11 for 32 yards with one sack and one 0-yard run. He gained just two first downs on the 13 plays overall, and he threw short of the sticks on nine of his 11 passes.
The final two failures particularly peeved Fitzpatrick from a competitiveness standpoint. The first came with 1:25 left in regulation and the Broncos up 14-11. The screen wasn't open, so Nix threw the ball into the dirt, stopping the clock, too. The Seahawks saved their last timeout and tied the game on the ensuing drive. Then in overtime, Nix got stuffed on a designed run. Afterward, Fitzpatrick implored Nix to "make somebody miss and get a first down for your football team."
Ryan Fitzpatrick gave his thoughts after the Broncos' overtime victory #TNFonPrime pic.twitter.com/AQ5wuThFjc
Denver is looking more "Checkdown City" than "Mile High City," too. Nix is targeting his running backs on 24.3% of his throws, the highest rate in the NFL among players with at least 120 dropbacks.
That's not necessarily a bad thing -- Brock Purdy is right behind him at 23.2% -- but you can't target running backs a ton and never push the ball downfield. Purdy is averaging 7.8 yards per attempt, an average number. Nix, again, is at an NFL-low 4.9. From CBS Sports researcher Doug Clawson:
There are 701 qualified QB seasons through 6 games in the past 20 years 2026 Bo Nix ranks 701st out of 701 in average pass length…
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Eagles steal QB from Cowboys: Joe Milton expected to sign with Philadelphia after injury to Jalen Hurts
summary: Joe Milton joins Tanner McKee and rookie Cole Payton in Philadelphia, a move that raises the possibility of Jalen Hurts eventually landing on injured reserve
full_text:
With Jalen Hurts out this week due to a blood clot , the Philadelphia Eagles ended up stealing a player from the Dallas Cowboys . The Eagles are going to sign Joe Milton off of the Cowboys' practice squad, according to multiple reports . Under NFL rules, if you sign a player off another team's practice squad, that player has to be placed on your 53-man roster, so Milton won't be a practice squad player in Philadelphia; he'll be on the actual roster.
With the addition of Milton, that means the Eagles will have three quarterbacks heading into Sunday's game against Carolina. Milton will join Tanner McKee and rookie Cole Payton . Hurts has already been ruled out due to a blood clot in his calf and it's unknown when he can return to the field.
For Sunday, the Eagles will hand the starting job over to McKee , but clearly, they weren't comfortable with only having a rookie behind him, which is why they went out and added Milton. There was some speculation that the Eagles might look to bring Andy Dalton back to Philadelphia, but in the end, the team decided to go with Milton.
The Eagles offense is at its best when a mobile quarterback is under center, and that's why the decision to add Milton certainly makes some sense. Although he's never started a game before, he does come with some serious mobility, but he is inexperienced.
Milton is now on his third team in three seasons and he's thrown just 53 passes in that span. He started his career with the Patriots after New England selected him in the sixth round of the 2024 NFL Draft. After one year of sitting behind Drake Maye (and Jacoby Brissett ), he was traded to the Cowboys in April 2025. During the 2025 season, he saw action in four different games while backing up Dak Prescott .
During the 2026 offseason, the Cowboys made a trade for Sam Howell , and he ended up beating Milton out for the backup QB job. The Cowboys ended up cutting Milton after the preseason in a move that seemed to blindside the 26-year-old QB.
"It was shocking. But it's life. You got to be able to live with it and deliver blows back when it's time," Milton said at the time . "I'm still the best quarterback in my eyes.  It is what it is. It's something you got to live with and take to the chin."
The Cowboys signed Milton to their practice squad and that's where he's spent the past five weeks until the Eagles made their move on Friday.
The fact that the Eagles are adding a quarterback likely signifies that Hurts will be out for more than one game. If they thought he was only going to be out for a week, they probably would have been comfortable with Payton as the backup for just one game, but if Hurts is going to miss an extended amount of time, then it certainly makes sense to add another quarterback, which is what Philly ended up doing.
The Eagles didn't go into detail about the nature of the clot that Hurts is dealing with, but ESPN has reported that he'll be out indefinitely "until this situation is solved." At this point, it seems like almost a given that the Eagles will end up putting Hurts on injured reserve. If they DON'T go that route, that means they'd have to carry four quarterbacks on their 53-man roster, which wouldn't make sense for a team that currently has 24 players on its injury report.
Also, if the Eagles put him on IR now, that would give Hurts five weeks to heal. After facing the Panthers this week, the Eagles will have three divisional games with the Cowboys (Week 7), Commanders (Week 8) and Giants (Week 9) before getting a bye in Week 10. So putting Hurts on IR would give him more than a month to recover. The Eagles first game after their bye is on Nov. 22 against the Steelers .
author: John Breech

title: NFL Week 6 picks: Our experts face off on Ravens at Browns, Packers vs. Cowboys and more
summary: CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict Week 6's top games
full_text:
We are already in Week 6 of the NFL regular season! Can you believe it? This weekend, two AFC South rivals in the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars will battle in London, while Caleb Williams looks to return to the lineup against the Atlanta Falcons after missing the last three games.
We also have an intriguing matchup in the NFC on Sunday night between the Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers , while the Washington Commanders will look to get back on track against the 49ers in San Francisco following their embarrassing tie with the New York Giants . Dan Quinn needs to find a way to get his team to refocus after they completely forgot about the clock in overtime.
Which teams should you pick in Week 6, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 13 over at DraftKings Sportsbook.
Dajani (Texans +3): The Jaguars have established themselves as one of the best teams in the AFC. While that's objectively true, they certainly aren't perfect. They probably should have dominated a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles team last week, yet didn't. Additionally, there are some questions about the offensive operation. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone last week, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, they are coming off their first win of the season against the lowly Tennessee Titans . I predict they keep that momentum going and score an upset victory across the pond. DeMeco Ryans is calling defensive plays again, and C.J. Stroud is actually playing good football. He's tied for the most 20-yard completions (21) in the NFL this season. Houston is also 14-2 SU and 11-4-1 ATS in its last 16 divisional games away from home.  … Prediction: Texans 21, Jaguars 18
Dubin (Jaguars -3): I think it's a real advantage that the Jaguars have already been in London for a week while the Texans haven't yet traveled across the pond. Jacksonville, as Dajani mentioned, has established itself as one of the best teams in the AFC. The offense has been efficient and explosive, and the defense has looked good as well. I know the Jags struggled with the Eagles for a bit of last week's game and probably should have lost, but Houston has only beaten a Tennessee team that is barely functional. It's not like the Texans have looked good at any point. Their defense has disappointed, and they can't run the ball whatsoever. … Prediction: Jaguars 24, Texans 20
Dajani (Falcons +3): It looks like Caleb Williams is going to return to the lineup after missing three games with his hamstring injury, and it also looks like Michael Penix Jr . will play after missing the very end of "Sunday Night Football" with his rib injury. The Chicago Bears have racked up their most rushing yards per contest (173.2) through five games since 1988, but keep an eye on the status of Kyle Monangai , who missed Week 5 with a toe injury. Last week's loss to the Packers was concerning from a defensive standpoint. The Bears have actually allowed 30 points over three straight road games (dating back to last year), which is tied for the longest streak in TEAM HISTORY. I'm going to take the points with the home team, and take Bijan Robinson and Co. to bounce back.  … Prediction: Falcons 30, Bears 27
Dubin (Bears -3): The impending return of Caleb Williams has me leaning toward Chicago here. In the one non-monsoon game that Williams played, the Bears dropped 59 points on the Panthers . They ran the ball at will and created explosive plays in the passing game. Their defense was exposed a bit by the Packers last week, and the Falcons could get going offensively here ... if Michael Penix Jr. actually plays through the rib injury he suffered last week. At least some of this pick is thinking Tua Tagovailoa could start under center for Atlanta.  … Prediction: Bears 23, Falcons 17
Dajani ( Ravens -4.5): I'm not going to bash the Cleveland Browns for their loss to the New York Jets in that gross weather, where punter Corey Bojorquez missed a snap and granted the Jets 34 yards of field position to set up the game-winning touchdown. But I am nervous about Cleveland's injuries with guys like Carson Schwesinger , Mason Graham , Mike Hall Jr., Tytus Howard , Quinshon Judkins and KC Concepcion banged up. I think it's fair to say that Lamar Jackson is expected back this week after sitting one game with his ankle injury, but I was wildly impressed with this Ravens defense and their ability to shut down what was statistically the hottest offense in the NFL since Michael Penix Jr. returned. Bijan Robinson rushed for 86 yards on Sunday night. He was averaging about 170 rushing yards per game with Penix under center. If it weren't for all the walking wounded in Cleveland, I would probably side with the home dogs. Not this time. … Prediction: Ravens 26, Browns 20
Dubin (Ravens -4.5): I can't tell if this line is assuming the return of Lamar Jackson or not, but r ecent reporting suggests he has a chance to return to action . If he does, I think the Ravens win this game by a lot. The Browns might be 3-2, but they have not played like an above .500 team so far. Each of their wins required a game-winning drive late in the fourth quarter, and that's not at all sustainable. I don't trust that their offense can get anything going given the various injuries to the skill-position players, and if Jackson is back, I don't think the Ravens' offense can be stopped.  … Prediction: Ravens 31, Browns 14
Dajani (Panthers +1.5): CBS Sports legend John Breech pointed out that the Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has ever been able to overcome. Philly is, of course, coming off an international game and facing a team that is coming off its bye. This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 SU and 0-3-1 ATS. That's pretty fascinating. The Eagles have covered the spread just once all season, while the last time the Panthers were on the field, they registered an impressive victory against the Detroit Lions . Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns, Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns and Tet McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and -- you guessed it -- two touchdowns. I have some legitimate concerns about the Panthers defense, but I'll take the upset in Philly. … Prediction: Panthers 23, Eagles 21
Dubin (Eagles -1.5): I don't feel good about this one at all. I'm basically just throwing my hands in the air and saying, well, the Eagles can't lose again , can they? … Prediction: Eagles 20, Panthers 17
Dajani (Packers -1.5): I told you the Packers were going to upset the Bears last week, and that something "weird" was going to happen. The "weird" came in the form of a 31-7 beatdown of Tyson Bagent . It's tough to trust Dallas after watching an undrafted rookie quarterback making his second career start come into AT&T Stadium and drop 419 yards of total offense on the Cowboys' head in prime time. Now, they have to go to Lambeau Field and try to stop a quarterback in Jordan Love , who is clearly finding his rhythm, having just thrown for 367 yards and two touchdowns. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are definitely a fun duo, but so are Christian Watson and Matthew Golden . Heck, let's make it a trio with tight end Tucker Kraft .   … Prediction: Packers 27, Cowboys 24
Dubin (Packers -1.5): The Dallas defense is just too bad for me to feel comfortable picking the Cowboys against a team that has an offensive pulse. The Packers showed last week that they are capable of throwing the ball all over the yard even if their running game can't get going. Even with the return of Joey Porter Jr. , I expect that Green Bay will get one or all of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft going down the field. Dallas should put up points, too, because the Packers'…

title: Christian Parker contradicts Jerry Jones, to stay on sideline as Cowboys defense seeks answers
summary: Parker says he will "most likely" remain on the sideline, but the addition of Mike Pettine underscores the urgency in Dallas
full_text:
FRISCO, Texas -- Any football fan knows that when a coach or coordinator is moved up to the booth, it's the start of a performance improvement plan that typically does not end well.
Jerry Jones said Tuesday on 105.3 The Fan that Christian Parker would move upstairs for Week 6. Parker himself pushed back on that notion on Thursday, saying he will "most likely" remain down on the sideline. "There's advantages of both for sure, but I've always been a guy that's usually been down on the field," Parker said.
A day later, Schottenheimer confirmed during a radio interview that Parker will remain on the sideline.
Parker also received the dreaded vote of confidence from Brian Schottenheimer amid his struggling defense's performance in the Cowboys' 2-3 start to the 2026 season. That came in the wake of Dallas hiring former Cleveland Browns coach Mike Pettine as a senior assistant . Pettine actually gave Parker his first job in the NFL when he was Green Bay's defensive coordinator in 2019.
"Christian Parker is our defensive coordinator and everything, all decisions, will run through him," Schottenheimer said Wednesday. "We're supporting him. I support him. I believe so strongly in the guy. I do. I think the guy's an incredible football coach. We have to coach better. We got to play better. I think our players will be the first ones to say there's things that they need to do better. There's things I need to do better.
"And so no one is sitting here pointing fingers at Christian Parker. But as the head coach, you have to make decisions that you think helps you win games. That's not just adding a Mike Pettine, it's some of the personnel adjustments that I know you guys are dying to know about that are being worked on behind the scenes and communicated to the players."
Schottenheimer said Friday that Pettine will be in the coaching booth on Sundays, but that observers likely won't see him at all that many practices because he will be in the film room instead.
"You're not gonna see him on the field a whole lot," Schottenheimer said. "He's in there just driving and grinding through film. He actually loves that part of it. That's kind of the way the thing is set up. He's certainly allowed on the field any time he wants, but he's maximizing his time kind of getting caught up with what we're doing as he's only been here a couple days."
Dallas knows that being the league's 31st-ranked total defense (395.4 total yards per game allowed), last-place run defense (168.4 rushing yards per game allowed) and worst third-down defense (52.6% third-down conversion rate allowed) won't cut it.
How fixable are the issues?
"Very fixable because they're under our control," Parker said. "Very fixable."
The level of urgency Parker and his players have shown through five weeks is far from an overreaction. Matt Eberflus, Parker's predecessor in 2025, had the Dallas defense looking very similar through five weeks. The only significant difference is that Eberflus' unit was the league's worst against the pass, while Parker's is the league's worst against the run.
Completion percentage allowed
One guaranteed personnel adjustment is to make new Dallas cornerback Joey Porter Jr . a full-time starter now that his stomach bug is behind him . He played in 48.1% (25 of 52) of the Cowboys' defensive snaps in their 34-30 road win over the Houston Texans . He and the team were ramping up for him to be a full-time starter after being on the roster for a week, but he was scratched shortly before kickoff in Week 5 because he couldn't stop throwing up. Losing his No. 1 corner that close to kickoff was something Parker called "not ideal." However, he and Porter Jr. are ready for him to have a "heavily increased" workload against the Green Bay Packers.
Look for rookie first-round edge rusher Malachi Lawrence to get more involved. Lawrence racked up his first career sack as well as a pass defensed in Week 5 against the Buccaneers. His quarterback pressure rate of 14.3% ranks fourth among qualified rookies, according to Pro Football Focus. He trails only David Bailey (16.4%), Sonny Styles (15%) and Cashius Howell (14.8%). Through five weeks, Lawrence co-leads the Cowboys in sacks with 1.0 despite playing significantly fewer pass rush snaps than some of Dallas' other edge rushers and defensive linemen.
"Played very well," Schottenheimer said. "I think he's starting to show the flash and the acceleration and the ability to rush the passer that we knew we were getting when we drafted him. And I thought he had a very, very good game against Tampa Bay and you'll see him get more opps [opportunities]."
They'll need Lawrence to beat Packers left tackle Jordan Morgan with regularity to have any hope of slowing down Green Bay quarterback Jordan Love and his top two speedy receivers, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden . Dallas sees facing a high-powered Packers passing attack as an opportunity rather than a challenge.
"I see that we have a lot of opportunities to make plays on the ball, so I know we're all excited for that," Porter Jr. said. "We really have to rally to the ball and make plays when they call on us to."
