title: NFL trade deadline proposals: One move for each of eight Super Bowl contenders
summary: Brian Thomas Jr., Khalil Mack and Budda Baker headline our proposed moves for the NFL's leading championship contenders
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is less than a month away, which means the hot stove is about to really heat up. Two major trades have already gone down, with Joey Porter Jr . heading to Dallas and Marvin Harrison Jr . heading to Houston. Several more will take place before the Nov. 10 deadline.
The most likely teams to make trades, of course, are the Super Bowl contenders. Everyone wants to make the move that solidifies their position or puts them over the top. So, we're here today to identify one move that each of the contenders should make.
To denote the Super Bowl contenders, we're going to use the top eight teams in Super Bowl odds over at DraftKings , all of whom have shorter than +2000 odds to hoist the Lombardi Trophy: the 49ers , Rams , Bills , Ravens , Chiefs , Seahawks , Jaguars and Bengals .
Things didn't end on the best of terms for Jennings and the 49ers, admittedly. He wasn't happy about his contract situation. There was at least one sideline argument with Kyle Shanahan. But the Niners are hemorrhaging wide receivers, Jennings has a ton of familiarity with the system and Jennings isn't seeing the ball or even the field as often as he would probably like to in Minnesota. Why not bring him back to hold down the fort until guys like Deebo Samuel and/or De'Zhaun Stribling are ready to return?
The Rams are going to get a lift from Myles Garrett's return, so the idea of trading for another defensive lineman doesn't make much sense. Their biggest issue outside of that is probably at tackle, where Alaric Jackson has already been suspended for one game and has a domestic violence case hanging over him, and Warren McClendon is probably the weakest link on the offense. The issue here is with identifying a specific tackle to trade for. Teams don't just trade quality tackles willy-nilly. They keep them around. You'd probably have to try to buy low on someone who has fallen out of favor or isn't playing well, like an Austin Jackson in Miami. And how attractive is that proposition?
The Bills definitely need help in the defensive backfield, and the slot is the most obvious place for an upgrade. They're playing Dee Alford there, for the most part, and according to Pro Football Focus, he's allowed opponents to complete 12 of 17 passes for 197 yards when throwing his way lined up inside. Still has lined up both outside and in the slot for the Chargers and played well in both roles, but especially when kicked inside. Opponents are just 7 of 12 for 53 scoreless yards targeting him there. With the Chargers struggling, maybe they're willing to part with him for a draft pick.
The Ravens signed Trey Hendrickson to upgrade their pass rush, but right now, they still check in with a below-average pressure rate of just 35.1% (20th in the NFL), according to Tru Media. Baltimore is never afraid to double down and turn a relative weakness into a strength, and with the Chargers' aforementioned struggles, Mack could probably be had at a reasonable price.
The Chiefs are in desperate need of wide receiver help — especially (and I can't believe I'm saying this) after they lost Tyquan Thornton to a potentially season-ending injury. They have Rashee Rice to work the underneath zones, but nobody to beat defenses down the field or even truly threaten them deep to open things up for Rice and the run game. When Thomas is at his best, as we saw during his rookie season, that's what he does. The Jaguars probably don't want to trade him, but he seems to be falling out of favor and even out of the lineup with Josh Cameron 's recent emergence; he hasn't played more than 62% of snaps in any game this year. If Marvin Harrison Jr. can be traded, so can Thomas.
The Seahawks cannot run the ball at all, as we have seen throughout this season and that was on full display on Thursday night against the Broncos . Pollard is no great shakes, but he's got 1,000 yards in four consecutive seasons and is at least a professional runner who can get what's blocked and a bit more. The Seahawks should be getting Zach Charbonnet back fairly soon, but we don't know if or when Jadarian Price will return. Pollard would be an upgrade over Emanuel Wilson and/or George Holani as a complement to Charbs. It's not the sexiest deal in the world and might not even be the best possible use of resources, but the Seahawks do need help in the backfield.
This is the best fake trade target of the bunch. The Jaguars have a good defense, but the weak link is at safety. The Cardinals probably aren't going anywhere any time soon, and Baker has just this year and next year left on his contract. Inserting Baker into the back end of the Jaguars' defense would just take things to another level and solidify them as one of the favorites in the AFC.
The Bengals got better up front defensively with the additions of Dexter Lawrence , Jonathan Allen , Boye Mafe and second-round pick Cashius Howell . They added Bryan Cook to upgrade the safety slot. They have DJ Turner II holding down one side of the field at corner, but they could use an upgrade over DJ Ivey , or at least someone to provide depth behind him. Someone like Zyon McCollum in Tampa or KeiSean Nixon in Green Bay could be an interesting target.
author: Jared Dubin

title: Ryan Fitzpatrick rips Broncos' Bo Nix after ugly 'TNF' game: 'He's not playing competitive football right now'
summary: Fitzpatrick called it 'almost disrespectful to the quarterback position'
full_text:
After another ugly outing from Bo Nix , Amazon Prime analyst and former NFL quarterback Ryan Fitzpatrick ripped the Broncos ' quarterback, calling his performance "almost disrespectful to the quarterback position" and "not playing competitive football." The rant, which came after a 17-14 Denver win over Seattle, clearly caught fellow analysts Tony Gonzalez, Andrew Whitworth and Richard Sherman by surprise.
Ryan Fitzpatrick gave his thoughts after the Broncos' overtime victory #TNFonPrime pic.twitter.com/AQ5wuThFjc
Nix went 17 for 27 for 107 yards, an average of 4.0 yards per attempt. He did not throw a touchdown or have a turnover.  The zero turnovers were key, considering the Seahawks had three, including two Sam Darnold interceptions, one of which set up Wil Lutz's game-winning field goal in overtime. Still, it was ugly.
"Now they're in the locker room right now, they're excited, they won -- he's not playing competitive football right now," Fitzpatrick said, his voice rising.
"I can only imagine how Sean Payton feels," he continued. "Sean Payton, Davis Webb , everybody that blocks for him. He's not competing right now, and that's something he's hung his hat for the last two years. I don't know if he's still injured, I don't know what's going on, but it's not good enough. It's effort."
For what it's worth, Payton's locker room speech included praise for the team for finding a way to win and avoiding turnovers.
"Just promise ourselves we're still improving." Sean Payton speaks to the victorious @Broncos locker room! #TNFonPrime pic.twitter.com/a8cma9VZjt
The Broncos finished with a measly 168 yards, their fewest in a win since Week 1, 1983 -- John Elway's first start. Denver is currently 31st in yards per game and 32nd in yards per play this season but has a 4-2 record after Thursday's win, a remarkable testament to the defense.
Fitzpatrick specifically pointed to two issues with Nix's performance.
"First of he guy doesn't want to throw the ball," Fitzpatrick said. "He's throwing to the flats, he's throwing behind [the line of scrimmage]. That's fine. But he has no trust from his coach, he calls a screen play on third and 8. Just run up and let the clock keep going. What does he do? He throws it away, Seattle gets the ball, they have a timeout."
Nix's average pass went 3.0 yards downfield Thursday, a stunningly low number. His furthest completion downfield was 8 yards, and he's averaging 4.9 air yards per attempt. That's not just the lowest in the NFL; it's the lowest by any player through six games in the last 20 years.
Fitzpatrick's other issue -- and the one where the competitiveness comes in -- came in overtime.
"He's got two chances to be competitive, the last one being a designed run for him to run, make somebody miss and get a first down for your football team," Fitzpatrick said, his voice rising to a yell.
After Darnold's interception, the Broncos ran RJ Harvey (5 yards) before a Nix scramble (3 yards) and then the Nix keeper, where he gained nothing. Luckily for Nix, Lutz drilled the 53-yarder. It will go down as a game-winning drive for Nix. But much like the rest of the night, in Fitzpatrick's opinion, Nix's performance overshadowed the final result.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Marvin Harrison Jr. set for Texans debut as C.J. Stroud defends former Ohio State teammate
summary: After a quiet start to his second season in Arizona, Harrison will begin a new chapter alongside his former college quarterback
full_text:
Marvin Harrison Jr . will suit up and is expected to play for the Houston Texans in Sunday's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars , one week after he was acquired in a trade with the Arizona Cardinals for a 2027 second-round pick.
A fading weapon in Arizona, Harrison only had five catches for 85 yards through four games and drew harsh criticisms surrounding his regression as a former first-year selection out of Ohio State. Texans quarterback and former Buckeyes teammate C.J. Stroud defended Harrison, saying his internal perspective is all that matters as he battles detractors.
"I don't think anybody ever is a finished product. You're always learning ways to get better," Stroud said . You're always learning ways to get better at what you're already good at. I think there are two different types of perspectives you can look from. You can look from the world's perspective of who people think you are or yourself.
"I think that's where I've learned that it doesn't really matter what people say. They can't really stop or start what you have going on. Then you have your perspective of who you think you are, who you believe you can be. I think that's more important. For Marvin, he knows that. He's a heck of a player."
Over 16 starts as a rookie, Harrison recorded 62 receptions for 885 yards and eight touchdowns before his production dwindled during his second campaign, part of that due to a concussion suffered last season.
"I don't agree with some of the things that are being said about him," Stroud said. "At the end of the day, that's what people who are on the outside are saying. I'm a firm believer of really focus on what you can control and then whatever other people say or have their opinions, kudos to them.
"They have platforms and things that they can say on, but that doesn't really affect you unless you make it. I think he'll be fine. I try to just be [a resource] to him if I need to. He's a confident dude. He'll be fine."
The deal had been in the works for weeks behind the scenes, according to Texans general manager Nick Caserio, who said this week it was Cardinals general manager Monti Ossenfort's call to wait until the conclusion of last week's games to reveal Harrison's destination.
"The deal was basically done Friday night, we kind of had an agreement in place. I gave him my word, he gave me his word, that's how you do business," Caserio said during an interview on 95.7 The Fan , "That's how he and I do business, but he wanted to handle it a certain way as it pertains to the communication and some of the other things, so we certainly didn't have a problem with that at all."
author: Brad Crawford

title: Ranking NFL's best and worst divisions: New leader emerges entering Week 6
summary: The AFC North claims the top spot with four winning teams, while the NFC North and former No. 1 NFC West round out the leading contenders
full_text:
What makes a great division? It starts with good teams and good players. It also needs to be competitive, ideally from top to bottom. The NFC West once again checks most of those boxes, but the 49ers' early lead, coupled with the Rams' sluggish start, has made the division less exciting, at least for the time being. It's also opened the door for a new division to take the title as the NFL's best. Below are the updated rankings for each division entering Week 6.
This division was not decided until the last play of the regular season in 2025. With each team sporting a winning record, it appears that we might be heading for a similar finish in 2026. If the Bengals stay healthy, it should be a three-team race for coming down the stretch (sorry, Browns fans).
Baltimore is off to a strong start under new coach Jesse Minter. The Ravens showed resolve last week when they rallied to defeat the Falcons in Atlanta with backup Tyler Huntley under center. The defense remains suspect, however, and it could prevent Baltimore from being a legitimate Super Bowl contender.
Cincinnati shook off two consecutive losses with a win last Sunday in Miami. As expected, the Bengals have been led by Joe Burrow , receivers Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase , and a resurgent defense that is 10th in the NFL in points allowed and third in red zone efficiency. The running game, which hasn't quite been the same since Joe Mixon's departure, continues to be a non-factor, though.
Inconsistent is a good word to sum up the Steelers, who won this division in 2025. Pittsburgh has rotated wins and losses each week, entering this weekend's game in Tampa. One emerging bright spot for Pittsburgh has been Jaylen Warren , who leads the Steelers in both rushing and receiving. Aaron Rodgers has largely been good in his farewell season. He just became the first Steelers quarterback since Terry Bradshaw to throw three touchdown passes in three consecutive games.
The Browns have been one of the league's surprise success stories, but it doesn't appear to be sustainable. Cleveland's offense is one of the league's worst on third down and in the red zone. That needs to quickly change if the Browns want to hang around.
The AFC North is more competitive from a win-loss standpoint, but the NFC North might be harder, as each team has a legitimate shot at winning the division. The irony is that the division's top team at the moment has the biggest question mark: quarterback.
Kyler Murray is 4-0 as Minnesota's starting quarterback, but he has left a lot to be desired. He isn't losing games for Minnesota, but he isn't winning them, either. While that has worked out for the Vikings to this point, Murray will need to elevate his game (at least in the weighty moments) if Minnesota is going to keep this up. A healthy Justin Jefferson would help, too.
Green Bay, after a 1-2 start, has quieted some of the outside noise with two consecutive wins, including last week's blowout over the Caleb Williams-less Bears. Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are emerging as a lethal dynamic duo, and the Packers' defense -- which is getting closer to welcoming back Micah Parsons -- has forced seven turnovers during Green Bay's current winning streak. The running game, however, continues to be an issue, averaging just 60.4 yards per game.
The Bears, a trendy preseason pick to win the division, have been held back by Williams' injury. While Williams' absence is hurting them now, it could benefit them in the long run because of the emergence of running backs D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai (who is currently dealing with a thumb injury). The Bears are currently tops in the NFL in rushing yards gained (866), second in touchdown runs (10) and seventh in yards-per-carry average (4.7).
As was the case last year, the Lions have an elite, championship-level offense but a subpar defense. Unless the Lions can acquire some defensive reinforcements by the trade deadline, Detroit will probably be spending another season fighting for a wild-card spot.
The NFC West is the NFL's most fascinating division.
Let's start with San Francisco, which has built an early cushion over Seattle and Los Angeles despite their ongoing injury issues. Making the 49ers' start even more impressive is that it includes road wins over the Rams (in Australia) and the Seahawks. The 49ers are getting MVP-level play from Brock Purdy . Los Angeles can take some solace in the fact that each of their losses was against top-tier teams. Two of those losses were winnable games. They would have won last Monday night's game if their special teams didn't let them down again.
They dug a hole for themselves, but the Rams have the talent to still make a run at the division. They have the reigning league MVP in Matthew Stafford , a dynamic duo in receivers Davante Adams and Puka Nacua and a defense that will welcome back reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett sometime in the next month.
And don't forget about Seattle; the defending Super Bowl champions are .500 after losing Thursday night's rock fight in Denver. Turnovers once again plagued the Seahawks, who forced overtime before Sam Darnold threw an interception that set up the Broncos ' game-winning field goal.
Seattle has a nasty defense and the league's best receiver in Jaxon Smith-Njigba , but they continue to struggle to consistently run the ball, which puts Darnold in too many third-and-long situations. Darnold is also taking way too many hits.
This division was supposed to be more compelling, but the Chargers haven't followed the script. Instead, Jim Harbaugh is presiding over a dumpster fire that is almost as bad as the one he left behind at Michigan.
Kansas City looks like they've rediscovered their championship touch. A big reason for that is the addition of Kenneth Walker III , who is currently on pace to obliterate Eric Dickerson's single-season rushing record. Health and durability appear to be the Chiefs' biggest question, especially Walker's, after he averaged 25 touches per game during the season's first month.
Like the Browns, the Raiders' fast start also looks like fool's gold. Their defense is 22nd in points allowed, and their running game might be the league's worst. Las Vegas also faces a daunting schedule with upcoming games against the Rams, 49ers, Seahawks and Broncos.
Speaking of Denver, the Broncos improved to 4-2 following Thursday's overtime win over the Seahawks. Denver's defense (which played without Patrick Surtain II and Talanoa Hufanga ) had another impressive night, but it was another ugly game for Bo Nix , who threw for just 107 yards and averaged only 3.96 yards per pass attempt.
Denver has a great defense, but as long as Nix continues to play like this, they shouldn't be considered a serious Super Bowl contender, let alone a threat to overtake Kansas City in the West.
The Jets are hanging around (for now), but the reality is that this is a two-team race. Buffalo had a chance to run away from the field, but the Patriots were able to upset the Bills on their own turf in Week 4. The Patriots then moved over .500 with an impressive win over the Raiders.
With the Patriots gaining ground, the Bills responded with a gutsy overtime win over the Rams this past Monday night. After a few so-so games, Josh Allen showed why he is the front-runner to win his second MVP. He literally put the Bills' offense on his back with 121 yards and a touchdown on 10 carries.
Similar to the Broncos, the Patriots have a nasty defense but a suspect offense. But unlike Denver, New England's quarterback, Drake Maye , is finding his stride after a slow start to the season.
Why is the NFL's only division without a winning team not ranked last? Because every team in this division is capable of winning it. That's been the theme of this division for a while, and it continues to be the case this season.

full_text:
This is an article version of the CBS Sports HQ AM Newsletter, the ultimate guide to every day in sports. You can sign up to get it in your inbox every weekday morning here .
If you enjoyed college football's Week 6, then buckle up for Week 7. This slate is simply loaded with high-impact games that will leave an indelible mark on the College Football Playoff race. Speaking of the playoff, it's hard to discount No. 6 Alabama too much following last week's loss to No. 1 Georgia . It will get even better if the Tide bounces back with a win over rival No. 14 Tennessee on the Third Saturday in October. The Volunteers will trot out George MacIntyre at quarterback again, and he has Alabama on upset alert as an 8.5-point underdog -- even if our experts are in near consensus about the Crimson Tide covering the spread.
While we're giving out picks, let's check in with Tom Fornelli for his Lock of the Week .
And here are our picks for every other marquee matchup in Week 7:
The Texans finally earned their first win of 2026 last week, and the parallels to 2025 are striking. It was a blowout win over the Titans last year that snapped a dreadful stretch to open the season and sparked a victory streak. What if Houston catches fire again this year? The Jaguars should be on notice in their second consecutive game in London, because the Texans might be fixed. Fire up the upset alert sirens .
Our Jordan Dajani likes the Texans to win outright across the pond.
"That's not a real upset! They're only three-point underdogs," you might say. OK, then. How about the Titans? They're seven-point underdogs to the Colts , yet our Tyler Sullivan says it would not surprise him if they secure their first win of the season.

title: Week 6 bold predictions: Packers run wild on Cowboys, Marvin Harrison Jr. has stellar debut for Texans, more
summary: Harrison Jr. shines in his Texans debut with C.J. Stroud, Green Bay gets its ground game rolling against Dallas, and Justin Herbert breaks out of an ugly slump
full_text:
Anything can happen in the NFL , and the start to Week 6 of the 2026 season certainly hammered home that fact.
In the Denver Broncos (4-2) 17-14 "Thursday Night Football" overtime win over the Seattle Seahawks , they triumphed at home despite averaging 2.9 yards per play. That's the fewest in Sean Payton's 318-game head-coaching career, and Denver's 168 total yards of offense ranked as their fewest in a victory since Pro Football Hall of Fame quarterback John Elway's first start as a rookie in 1983.
Quarterback Bo Nix , who ranks dead last in the NFL in yards per pass attempt at 5.6, improved to a 13-3 career record in games when he averages six yards per pass attempt or fewer, the best of all-time minimum 15 starts per CBS Sports Research, after averaging 4.0 yards per pass attempt on Thursday. All other active quarterbacks have a combined .283 winning percentage in starts where they average six yards per pass attempt or fewer. That's absolutely unfathomable.
What other hijinks   could take place across the rest of the NFL's Week 6 slate? Here is a look at five bold predictions.
The Green Bay Packers are back above .500 after quarterback Jordan Love's laser show (367 yards and 2 passing touchdowns while completing 25 of his 31 throws) in a 31-7 beatdown of the Chicago Bears at Lambeau Field in Week 5.
Now that they have a winning record, they're now the owners of the third-fewest rushing yards per game (60.4) by any team above .500 through five games of a season in league history, per CBS Sports Research. Green Bay's NFL-worst rushing offense also ranks as the fewest rushing yards per game through games of any season in the Packers' 106-season franchise history. Some of that has to do with the absence of running back Josh Jacobs , who is on the commissioner's exempt list after being charged with two misdemeanors, and some of that has to do with the team's beat-up offensive line.
However, the offensive line has stabilized with veterans Laken Tomlinson and Travis Glover stabilizing the team's guard play. That's one of the reasons why the Packers will run for over 100 yards as a team for the first time in 2026 against the Dallas Cowboys on "Sunday Night Football."
The others are that Green Bay running back MarShawn Lloyd is a freight train at 5 feet 9 inches tall and 220 pounds, and the Cowboys have the league's worst run defense (168.4 rushing yards allowed per game). Dallas allowed the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to go off for 241 yards rushing, their most in a game since 2024, on "Thursday Night Football" in Week 5. Facing a leaky defense like that and Lloyd fresh off running through Bears cornerback Jaylon Johnson's face for a touchdown in Week 5, Lloyd and the Packers cross the century mark on the ground for the first time this season.
Marshawn Lloyd trucks a guy on his way to the end zone 😤 @CHIvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/NNcSwQfTOU
Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud is quietly playing efficient football: he has the fifth-most passing attempts without an interception (185) through five games in NFL history while throwing for the fourth-most passing yards in the NFL (1,402) this season.
The Texans (1-4) have a high-volume passing offense this season because of their struggling rushing offense, and that will lead to Houston's newest player, 2024 fourth overall pick wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. , thriving in his team debut against the AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars (4-1). How much will he soar in his first game back with his former Ohio State Buckeyes teammate in Stroud?
Harrison Jr. will produce his first 100-yard receiving game since his rookie year in 2024 and just the third overall 100-yard receiving game of his young career on Sunday. He and Stroud were Ohio State teammates for two seasons from 2021 to 2022, and Harrison Jr.'s 14 receiving touchdowns when Stroud was the starting quarterback in 2022 are tied for the third most in a single season in Buckeyes' history.  Harrison Jr. also set or tied career-highs in catches (77), receiving yards (1,263) and receiving touchdowns (14) in that 2022 season with Stroud. Houston will be celebrating their newest trade acquisition's 100-yard game when the clock hits zero at Wembley Stadium on Sunday.
The Los Angeles Chargers are injury-plagued and riding the struggle bus at 0-5 to start 2026. Pro Bowl quarterback Justin Herbert is tied for the most interceptions (seven) and turnovers (nine) in the NFL this season, and he has a couple of ugly streaks going against him. He has five consecutive games with a fourth-quarter turnover, making him the first quarterback since Charlie Frye in 2006 to do that. Herbert also hasn't thrown for multiple passing touchdowns in a game in his last seven games, the longest such streak of his career.
However, he will play a clean fourth quarter and throw multiple touchdown passes against the 4-0 Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead on Sunday. The last time the Chiefs were on the field in Week 4, 38-year-old Kirk Cousins threw for 365 yards, 2 touchdowns and an interception on 31 of 52 passes in a narrow 30-27 Chiefs win. Herbert will snap out of his funk and raise his level to go toe-to-toe with Mahomes by having a clean fourth quarter and throwing multiple touchdowns for the first time in a while.
Geno Smith is on an incredible public relations campaign in 2026 with the New York Jets . After leading the NFL with 17 interceptions as a Las Vegas Raider in 2025, he hasn't thrown any through five games this season. Smith has six passing touchdowns to no interceptions this season, a stark contrast from his touchdown-to-interception ratio at this time a year ago when he had the same number of touchdown passes (six) but with nine interceptions. He is only the second quarterback in NFL history with no interceptions through five starts, after leading the league in interceptions the previous season, and is tied with Vinny Testaverde, also with the Jets, back in 2001, per CBS Sports Research.
However, Smith will throw his first interception of the season in Week 6 at the New England Patriots . Patriots All-Pro cornerback Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) is on track to return this week, fully practicing on Thursday after being limited on Wednesday. In his first game back after a two-game absence, Gonzalez will intercept Smith for the veteran's first interception of 2026.
Yes, your eyes don't deceive you. According to DraftKings Sportsbook , the 1-4 New Orleans Saints are favored by 1.5 points over the 3-1-1 New York Giants on the road at MetLife Stadium. Perhaps the ugliness of the NFC East leader's 27-27 tie at the Washington Commanders in Week 5 is pushing the spread in favor of the Saints. Maybe it's the allure of New Orleans quarterback Tyler Shough , whose 1,299 passing yards rank as the seventh-most in the NFL.
Regardless, that positions the Saints to win on Sunday, as they have covered in seven consecutive road games, the longest active road cover streak in the entire NFL, per CBS Sports Research. However, the Saints' road cover streak will be broken on Sunday because Jameis Winston plays a more efficient brand of football than Shough.
Sure, Winston's 57.6% is the second-worst in the NFL among 31 qualified quarterbacks in 2026, but he is starting to turn a corner and find a groove as an NFL starting quarterback once again. He is the first Giants quarterback with three-plus passing touchdowns in consecutive games since Eli Manning in 2016, and Winston didn't throw a single interception after having two in Week 4 against the Arizona Cardinals a couple of weeks ago.
On the other hand, Shough has a turnover problem: his eight this season are the third-most in the league. Winston will outduel Shough and prevent a Saints road cover for the eighth consecutive such game.
author: Garrett Podell

title: Week 6 breakdown: Josh Allen vs. Maxx Crosby and the keys to pivotal AFC clash
summary: The Raiders may have to abandon their usual four-man rush and turn up the pressure to slow Allen and Buffalo's play-action attack
full_text:
Josh Allen is fresh off making NFL history in Buffalo's 37-34 overtime win over the Los Angeles Rams in Week 5. He became the first quarterback to average 10-plus yards per pass attempt (11.1) and 10 yards per carry (12.1), and he stuffed the statsheet with 210 yards passing 121 yards rushing and two total touchdowns.
So what will he do in the Bills' (3-2) return to action the Raiders ? That depends on the success rate he has when Buffalo runs their deadly under-center play action game, featuring himself and James Cook, against five-time Pro Bowl edge rusher Maxx Crosby .
Entering Week 6, Allen is utilizing under-center play action on 25.5% of his dropbacks in 2026, the second-highest rate in the NFL, trailing only Sam Darnold (25.5%), according to the NFL's Next Gen Stats. On those plays, Allen is completing 64.5% of his throws, just below the league average rate of 65.2%, while averaging 9.0 yards per attempt, the eighth-most in the NFL. The greater danger arises when he takes matters into his own hands with his legs. When he has tucked the ball and run, Allen has scrambled six times for 65 yards and a touchdown. When combining the passing and the rushing, Allen has a 57.1% success rate on under-center play-action dropbacks, the fifth-highest in the NFL entering Week 6, per the league's Next Gen Stats.
How has the Raiders' defense handled defending under-center play-action this season? Not great, allowing a 75% completion percentage (15 of 20) and two touchdowns on under-center play-action passes while giving a single scramble for 36 yards (fifth-most allowed on such scrambles.
So, how can Las Vegas tilt the scale back in its favor? Turning up the heat with the blitz. Allen has been around league average overall when blitzed this season, with a 93.2 passer rating against the blitz, 15th in the NFL. When blitzed in under center play-action scenarios, the efficiency is relatively the same among his peers: Allen has a 115.5 passer rating, which ranks 13th in the league.
The problem is the Raiders' defense is using a standard four-man pass rush on 76.6% of opponents' dropbacks this season, the second-highest rate in the league, while creating a 32.2% pressure rate when sending four or fewer, just under the average around the NFL entering Week 6 (33.1%), according to the NFL's Next Gen Stats. When they actually blitz, their pressure rate increases to 63.4%, the highest in the NFL, per TruMedia. Las Vegas defensive coordinator Rob Leonard breaking his tendencies and channeling his inner Brian Flores will be crucial come Sunday.
No matter what Buffalo is running, they'll certainly look to avoid Crosby. He has played on 85.3% of defensive snaps, the second-highest rate among edge defenders, trailing only Detroit Lions Pro Bowler Aidan Hutchinson (89.1%), per the NFL's Next Gen Stats. No matter who the Raiders play, opposing offenses have schemed up 70.3% of their designed runs away from his side of the field, the highest rate among 73 edge defenders on the field for at least 50 designed runs, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats.
So where will Crosby be on Sunday? Odds are across the Bills' right tackle: Crosby has aligned on the left edge, offensive right edge, on 78.6% of his snaps this season. Opponents are double-teaming or chipping Crosby at the second-highest rate among edge defenders with at least 50 pass rushes from the left edge (34.6%), but he has still generated 20 pressures, including a sack, tied with two other players for the second-most from that specific spot, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats. Despite teams chipping and doubling him, Crosby is still racking up big numbers this season. He has two sacks in five games to go along with 30 quarterback pressures, tied for the fourth-most in the NFL with Houston Texans All-Pro edge rusher Will Anderson Jr .
The Bills have one of the NFL's best-blocking right tackles in Spencer Brown , who has allowed a 6.3% pressure rate, the sixth-lowest among right tackles, but he left Week 5 with a back injury after just 15 snaps on Monday. Tylan Grable , his substitute, struggled. Grable surrendered four quarterback pressures on 20 pass blocks the rest of the night for a 20% quarterback pressure rate allowed, the highest by any Bills offensive lineman in a game this season, according to the NFL's Next Gen Stats. The good news for Buffalo is that Brown practiced fully on Thursday after being limited on Wednesday, indicating he is likely to be active in Week 6.
How successful the Bills are with their under-center, play-action passing game and how wild Crosby is able to roam will likely decide the victor in this AFC clash Sunday afternoon at 4:25 pm EST on CBS.

title: NFL Week 6 best bets: Texans to shine against Jaguars in London, two anytime TD scorers for Bears-Falcons

full_text:
We are definitely moving in the right direction with our best bets. After a tough start, we hit three out of five each of the last two weeks, but there's one I'm particularly proud of -- and, for your sakes, hoping you'll jump on board.
I put Jacoby Brissett 2+ passing touchdowns AND 1+ interceptions out into the world last week, and he came through: three touchdowns, one interception. We cashed out with +230 odds. And now I must re-emphasize this:
Jacoby Brissett has thrown 2+ passing touchdowns AND 1+ interceptions in seven of his last 11 starts. And you can still get it at major plus odds!
We also nailed the Texans covering against the Titans and Davante Adams as an anytime touchdown scorer. We missed on the Bears , who got stomped by the Packers , and on a Drake Maye rushing prop; the blowout really hurt there.
But overall, it was another good week. Let's keep stacking.
As always, all betting odds are courtesy of DraftKings .
I was pretty surprised to see this line. The Jets are coming off a win over the Browns , yes, but it was a 17-12 affair in the rain in which the Jets managed a measly 4.2 yards per play and basically won because Deshaun Watson was incompetent.
Drake Maye has had some rough stretches this year but is really hitting his stride. Over the past two weeks, Maye leads the NFL in passing touchdowns and passer rating and is third in yards per attempt. He's taken just two sacks after taking nine from Weeks 1-3. The big play is back in a major way, a huge part of Maye at his best.
The defense has also come around, too, even with Christian Gonzalez out. Now, it's looking like he'll be back to augment a unit that already ranks fifth in yards per game allowed. Also, Zak Kuhr is dialing up some impressive pressure looks, and Geno Smith has taken the third-most sacks in the NFL this year.
I am downright scared about what this Houston defensive line could do to a Jaguars offensive line that just lost Anton Harrison and already wasn't in the best shape. Last week, Jalen Carter absolutely dominated Jacksonville's interior o-line; this week, it will be Will Anderson Jr . and Danielle Hunter on the edges.
Furthermore, C.J. Stroud has played some really, really good ball this season. In the three games Nico Collins has played, Stroud is completing 70.9% of his passes, averaging 8.6 yards per attempt, and posting 0.24 EPA per dropback. Extended to the whole season, that would rank second, fourth and sixth, respectively. He hasn't thrown a single interception all season, either.
Finally, while the Jaguars are down arguably their best lineman, the Texans theirs, Braden Smith , back. Marvin Harrison Jr . is also expected to make his Houston debut. I anticipate a big day for Collins and the Texans, with a crucial win coming home.
The Giants are coming off a game in which they gave up four catches and 60 receiving yards to Chig Okonkwo. Now they face another receiving-first tight end in Juwan Johnson . Johnson had been consistently productive this year -- at least three catches and at least 50 yards in every game -- before facing the Vikings ' excellent defense. He had just 16 yards last week. But the Giants' defense is not the Vikings' defense, and it's not close. I like Johnson to have a solid day against a linebacking unit that has had major ups and downs in coverage.
How about another tight end? The Cowboys ' high-powered offense and porous defense make for a shootout, and Tucker Kraft should be a beneficiary. There was always going to be a bit of a ramp-up for the excellent tight end coming off a torn ACL, but over the past two weeks, he's had 11 catches for 104 yards. Now he faces a Cowboys defense that can't seem to stop anyone.
A healthy Joey Porter Jr . should help against Christian Watson and/or Matthew Golden , but defending tight ends has been a major issue for Dallas. The Cowboys have allowed 9.0 yards per attempt when opponents target tight ends, the fifth-highest rate in the NFL through five weeks. And it's not as if they've faced a ton of good receiving tight ends, either; the best was probably Isaiah Likely in Week 1, and Likely had eight catches for 78 yards and two touchdowns.
It's looking like no Kyle Monangai again this week for the Bears, so backing D'Andre Swift to find the endzone (-175) makes sense by itself. He scored last week against the Packers, and though he had just one touch after halftime and Ben Johnson saying he doesn't want to overuse any running back, a major deficit certainly didn't help. If that game had been closer, I doubt Swift would have only had one carry in the second half. Having Caleb Williams back should help this offense big time, and even if he's not back, I think Swift scores. He has four touchdowns on the season and has been stopped at the 1-yard line an NFL-high seven times.
Drake London is due for some major regression. He has usually dominated with Michael Penix Jr . on the field, and that's holding up this year: 21 catches for 408 yards in the past three weeks, all Penix starts. It sounds like Penix will be good to go Sunday, and that means it's time for London to find the end zone. His 27 receptions and 488 receiving yards this season are both by far the most of anyone without a touchdown. Regression is coming, and it starts against a leaky Chicago secondary.

title: Three underrated NFL Week 6 games that could help shape the playoff race
summary: A desperate Eagles team, two elite rushing offenses and an unpredictable division leader highlight three games that should be on your radar
full_text:
Week 6 of the NFL is sure to bring drama. The Kansas City Chiefs are the only unbeaten team remaining in the AFC, and the two NFC undefeated teams are the San Francisco 49ers and the Minnesota Vikings. At the opposite end of the spectrum, the AFC contains all three of the league's goose-egg teams. The Miami Dolphins, Tennessee Titans and Los Angeles Chargers are all still looking for their first win at 0-5.
There are some obvious stand-out games, but there are also some under-the-radar matchups that you should have circled. Here are the three you shouldn't miss.
The Philadelphia Eagles' season may actually be cursed. They sit at 2-3 and are on a three-game losing streak, but what may be worse than all that is that they will be without quarterback Jalen Hurts, ruled out due to a superficial blood clot. Add the hamstring injuries to running back Saquon Barkley and wide receiver DeVonta Smith and things look rough.
Carolina quarterback Bryce Young has been playing well, so the difference in quarterback situation is major.
Head coach Nick Sirianni is going to find himself in the hot seat very soon, and his job is officially on watch with their offense looking stale. The Eagles are entering desperation mode, especially if they fall to 2-4, so I am interested to see what Philly prepares as the situation heads towards dire.
The Panthers have been an interesting watch for me this season. They're in a loss, win, loss, win pattern this year, so pinpointing them as a team hasn't been easy. A team coming off a bye has never lost to a team coming off an international game, so based on that, the Panthers have the edge. From quarterback to schedule to trajectory, these teams appear headed in opposite directions.
The Bears could get quarterback Caleb Williams back this week, which makes this a game to watch. Williams was a full participant on Wednesday and Thursday as he looks to return from the hamstring injury that has sidelined him for the last three weeks.
The Bears are coming off a blowout loss to the Packers, while the Falcons are coming off their first loss since quarterback Michael Penix returned.
This run game intrigues me.
Chicago ranks first in the league in rushing yards with 866, and Atlanta is right behind the Bears. The Bears are second in the league in touchdowns on the ground with 10, and the Falcons are fourth in that category with eight. I am excited to see who can outrun the other, especially with each team's run defense being strong so far this year.
The Giants got lucky last week with a tie against the Washington Commanders and are also lucky to be sitting at 3-1-1 despite the injury to quarterback Jaxson Dart. The Giants are atop the NFC East for the first time since 2015 and with the rest of the division struggling, they really could end the regular season with hats and t-shirts.
New York isn't without their struggles, though, and the quarterback situation has a chance to change at some point this season. Jameis Winston is not consistent.
The Saints sit at 1-4, and, as their schedule suggests, they have their fair share of problems. As they look for their second win, the unreliable Giants are a team they could beat. While New York is in the best spot they've been in recent history, they're not a sure bet, and the Saints could take advantage of that.
Even with the better record, the Giants come in as underdogs, and I'm looking forward to seeing how this one shapes out, how it impacts two rocky divisions, and whether it will lead to different quarterback decisions.

An update for a contender here, a shedding of a veteran for a rebuilding/retooling team there, and viola, the trade deadline has passed. Last year was an exception, with the Jets ' fire sale of Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams representing two of the biggest midseason trades ever.
On the other hand, Jakobi Meyers being traded from the Raiders to the Jaguars looked very much like a run-of-the-mill trade deadline swap. Meyers was expected to add reliability to a thin receiver room dealing with injuries, and the 2-6 Raiders had no reason to keep a disgruntled vet. Nothing too earth-shattering one way or another. In fact, in our trade grades , we gave Las Vegas the higher mark.
Now, though, it's clear this wasn't just a sensible add for Jacksonville, but a crucial one. Who knew a solid-but-unspectacular wide receiver — Meyers has never been a Pro Bowler and has one 1,000-yard season — could completely change an offense?
Apparently, Jacksonville did.
Meyers set career highs with 87 receptions and 1,027 yards in 2024, but absent a contract extension, he requested a trade right before the 2025 season. He doubled down on that request in late October, shortly before the deadline, and the Jaguars made his wish for a new home come true two weeks later. (They'd extend him shortly thereafter, taking care of that wish, too.)
For the Jaguars, adding Meyers was a way to boost Lawrence's surroundings. At the time, Brian Thomas Jr . was in the midst of a tough 2025 season after a terrific 2024 rookie campaign. Travis Hunter was hurt. Parker Washington was showing encouraging signs, but his breakout was still weeks away.
On the day of the Meyers trade, Thomas led the Jaguars with 30 catches. That number ranked tied for 55th in the league. Liam Coen clearly needed another player —one who was reliable and had, as Liam Neeson says in "Taken," a very particular set of skills.
Meyers is a very well-rounded player — not necessarily elite at one specific skill, but good to very good at a lot of them. When the team acquired Meyers, GM James Gladstone said Meyers' "superpower" was not dropping the football . That may sound silly, but at the time of the trade, the Jaguars had 30 drops, tied for the most by any team through eight games since 2000. Meyers has one drop (none this year) since joining Jacksonville.
Meyers' other superpower is winning over the middle of the field, the area where Lawrence has become arguably the best passer in the NFL.
Lawrence to Meyers, between numbers, 10+ yards downfield
Most on team since Meyers arrived?
As I wrote in my breakdown of Lawrence's rise late last year, Meyers is really good in the areas of the field where Lawrence is really good. That's a really good combo.
Meyers' numbers aren't anything special this year (15 catches, 202 yards, two touchdowns across five games), but he's still excelling in that over-the-middle area.
Trevor Lawrence zips it in to Jakobi Meyers for 6️⃣ @NEvsJAX on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/bM92cePTMS
Much of Meyers' importance this season isn't seen in the numbers, though. He really helps all the other wide receivers fit into place. Washington, for example, has run nearly half of his routes from the slot since Meyers' arrival; that number was under 35% in 2025 before Meyers arrived. Tight end Brenton Strange has also taken a huge leap. Thomas Jr. is now more of a vertical piece.
Meyers is also an excellent, willing blocker. He is 12th in PFF's wide receiver run-blocking grades, and watch him usher Tariq Woolen out of the way on Washington's first touchdown of Week 5.
51-YARD TOUCHDOWN FOR PARKER WASHINGTON @PHIvsJAX on NFL Network Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Gf38EGe1Qr
But really, it all comes back to Lawrence. By any measure, he has played like a top-10 quarterback with Meyers on the field, and in many stats, he's been in the top five. The Jaguars were looking for a guy who wouldn't let Lawrence down. Instead, they found a guy who lifted him up.
Thanks to Spotrac , we can track both picks the Raiders got in the Meyers deal. The fourth-round pick (No. 117) was packaged with a second-round pick and sent to the Texans for a later second-round pick and a third-round pick. The Raiders added safety Treydan Stukes and offensive lineman Trey Zuhn III , respectively, with those picks.
The sixth-round pick got sent to Buffalo for Taron Johnson and a seventh-round pick, the latter of which was sent to the Jets alongside Geno Smith for a sixth-rounder. The Raiders then used that sixth-rounder and a fourth-rounder to trade up for running back Mike Washington Jr .
Even with all the good that Meyers has done in Jacksonville, Las Vegas made the right choice. The team was a mess last year, and it wasn't going to extend Meyers. It also shows how valuable getting multiple picks can be. The Raiders have been able to infuse their roster with intriguing young talent, an ability enhanced in part by this deal. Teams wheel and deal constantly during the NFL Draft . The ability to do so with extra picks under their control is a major advantage.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: NFL Week 6 picks, odds, best bets: Panthers capitalize on Eagles' troubles, Rams dominate Cardinals

full_text:
It was finally a great week, going 9-6 against the spread, 11-4-1 straight up and 3-2 on best bets. Maybe you don't consider that a "great week," but this season has been tough. The 9-6 record was actually tied for the best mark at CBS Sports last week, and the 37-41-1 overall ATS record ranks third . A lot of time to bounce back.
Last week, we knew the Pittsburgh Steelers would easily cover against the Indianapolis Colts , the Cincinnati Bengals took care of business against the Miami Dolphins and the New York Giants covered 3.5 points in a weird tie with the Washington Commanders . However, the Cleveland Browns let us down in a gross matchup dominated by bad weather, while the Jacksonville Jaguars struggled against a short-handed Philadelphia Eagles squad. Don't overlook that result.
Here's a look at what I'm thinking this week. As always, credit to the CBS Sports research team for making me sound smart.
Odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook
Top five picks ATS record: 13-12 Overall ATS record: 37-41-1 Straight-up record: 46-32-1
Sunday, 9:30 a.m. ET ( NFL Network, Stream: Fubo , try for free)
The Houston Texans finally got that elusive first victory against the lowly Tennessee Titans , and then scored another victory directly after the game by trading for Arizona Cardinals wideout Marvin Harrison Jr . -- reuniting him with his college quarterback, C.J. Stroud .
I'm calling my shot here: Take the Texans to build on their momentum against the Jaguars in London. The Jaguars are one of the best teams in the NFL, but it's hard to ignore last week's struggles. Jacksonville went 0-3 in the red zone against the Eagles, including two trips where the Jags failed to score any points from the one-yard line. As for the Texans, maybe this defense tightens up with DeMeco Ryans calling the plays again. Houston is also 14-2 straight up and 11-4-1 against the spread in its last 16 divisional games away from home.
The pick: Texans +2.5 Projected score: Texans 21-18
Sunday, 1 p.m. ET (CBS, Stream on Paramount+ )
The reports of the New England Patriots ' demise have been greatly exaggerated. They destroyed a previously one-loss Las Vegas Raiders team, 45-17, on Sunday, and get the New York Jets at home. The Patriots are 10-1 in their past 11 home games, 6-1 in their past seven AFC East games, and 11-0 under Mike Vrabel vs. teams entering the matchup with a losing record. New England is also 9-2 SU and ATS in its last 11 vs. the Jets -- who haven't covered the spread vs. an AFC East opponent under head coach Aaron Glenn.
Drake Maye has scored eight total touchdowns with two turnovers over the past two games, after scoring one touchdown with seven turnovers over the first three games of the season. Plus, this Patriots defensive front has really impressed. I mentioned this earlier in the week: the football world isn't talking enough about the impact rookie Gabe Jacas and Elijah Ponder have had on Vrabel's defensive line. This Ponder guy has 4.5 sacks over the last four games!
The pick: Patriots -7.5 Projected score: Patriots 28-20
Sunday, 1 p.m. ET (CBS, Stream on Paramount+ )
I planned to make this a top pick before Jalen Hurts ' unfortunate blood clot .
CBS Sports' John Breech pointed out that the Eagles are facing a scheduling disadvantage this week that no team has EVER overcome.
The Eagles are coming off an international game and are facing the Carolina Panthers, who are coming off the ir bye . This has only happened four times, but the team coming off the international game is 0-4 straight up and 0-3-1 against the spread.
Philly really botched that game against the Jaguars last Sunday morning, and Nick Sirianni just put himself that much more on the hot seat with his decision to keep the final kickoff in play. The Eagles still have some serious injury issues with Saquon Barkley , DeVonta Smith and Drew Kendall working through various issues. Plus, Philly has covered the spread just once all season!
The last time the Panthers took the field, they scored an impressive victory against the Detroit Lions . Bryce Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns, Chuba Hubbard rushed for 122 yards and two touchdowns and Tet McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and two scores.
The pick: Panthers -3.5 Projected score: Panthers 24-20
Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free)
I think people see this line and say, "OK, it's a massive number for a divisional game with the favorite coming off a tough loss on Monday night. Let's auto-bet the dogs to cover." Sometimes I do that, but not in this situation.
I think Sean McVay and the Los Angeles Rams are seeing red after Week 5. McVay got too conservative in overtime after his offense had scored THREE STRAIGHT touchdowns to end the fourth quarter, while the special teams unit as a whole disappointed again. Now, the preseason Super Bowl favorites have a losing record through five weeks. It's time to get back on track.
The Rams are 10-1 SU and 11-0 ATS in their last 11 games following an ATS loss. That's pretty remarkable. The Cardinals are also 1-6-1 ATS in their last eight games as a double-digit road underdog. I genuinely believed they would cover the spread against the Lions last week, but Jacoby Brissett's offense didn't have the success I expected. Arizona was out-scored, 24-7, in the first half, and that was it. Give me the Rams, big.
The pick: Rams -12.5 Projected score: Rams 30-17
Monday, 8:15 p.m. ET (ESPN, Stream: Fubo , try for free)
Go ahead and believe I'm being dramatic here, but I really do wonder how the locker room and the coaching staff is feeling after the Commanders ran out the clock on themselves in overtime. I became more bewildered the more I looked into it. Because offensive coordinator David Blough called a play with motion as those precious seconds continued to tick off the clock, while quarterback Jayden Daniels simply forgot about the situation. As a quarterback, you're looking at the clock and the play clock before every snap. For him to take a dive in that spot was just absolutely insane.
As for the San Francisco 49ers , they have been pretty trustworthy from a gambling perspective. They are 4-1 ATS this year, and 10-4 ATS in their last 14 primetime games when favored by at least three points. I think it's possible Washington could rally and Daniels puts together a magnificent game. After all, he did rush for 103 yards and two touchdowns on Sunday. But with the Commanders being publicly shamed all week and then having to fly across the country to face the best team in the NFL, I'm not sure they get a cover here.
The pick: 49ers -7.5 Projected score: 49ers 28-20

title: What to know about Falcons – Bears in Week 6
summary: The Falcons just a heartbreaker in overtime to the Ravens. The Bears got absolutely drubbed by a divisional rival. Both of these teams are looking for a win, but naturally, only one can get it. Will it be the Falcons? That’s a question with a lot of moving parts. If the Bears don’t start Caleb […]
full_text: Sep 10, 2017; Chicago, IL, USA; A view of the line of scrimmages during a game between the Chicago Bears and the Atlanta Falcons at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: Patrick Gorski-USA TODAY Sports | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Falcons just a heartbreaker in overtime to the Ravens. The Bears got absolutely drubbed by a divisional rival. Both of these teams are looking for a win, but naturally, only one can get it. Will it be the Falcons? That’s a question with a lot of moving parts. If the Bears don’t start Caleb Williams, my instinct is that yes, a Chicago team with a backup quarterback and no Kyle Monangai is quite gettable for Atlanta. If Williams is back in action and Monangai is too, this offense is incredibly formidable, and that looks to be the way things are trending for the Bears. That makes the task much harder, even if the shaky Bears defense also provides real opportunities. How will this one go? That remains to be seen, but here’s what you need to know for Week 6. Team rankings Team Record Points Scored Yardage Passing Yards Rushing Yards Points Against Yardage Against Passing Yards Against Rushing Yardage Against Turnovers Created Turnovers Surrendered Falcons 2-3 13 10 21 2 21 16 27 4 27 25 Bears 3-2 13 7 18 1 5 9 12 9 17 29 The Bears are one of those teams that look extremely impressive on paper and are very talented, but have more weaknesses than these surface level metrics might indicate. The passing attack is lesser without Caleb Williams, the rushing attack is incredible but may be missing sledgehammer back Kyle Monangai this week. The defense, meanwhile, has struggled against good offenses and been lights out against bad ones, and is also dealing with injuries. The have one of the brightest offensive minds in football and a very good team top to bottom when they’re fully healthy, but they are not fully healthy. Atlanta’s been up-and-down but is settling into roughly the shape I think we’ll see this season, which is a very good offense with an effective defense that isn’t quite good enough to stop elite passing games or rushing attacks. The injuries in the secondary and attrition up front have combined to make the sledding tougher and they’re not forcing enough turnovers, but overall this looks like a team that should be comfortably league average or better across these high level categories. They just need to settle into a consistent level of play. How the Bears have changed in 2026 They returned a ton of talent from last year, and notably traded Gervon Dexter to the Falcons and re-united him with ex-Bears assistant general manager Ian Cunningham, who is now running the show in Atlanta. They sought to bolster the defense in particular with signings like safety Coby Bryant, defensive tackles Kentavius Street and Neville Gallimore, and linebacker Devin Bush. Their draft brought in promising safety Dillon Thieneman, center Logan Jones, and some interesting depth. Overall, though, this was not a transformative offseason and was not intended to be, as the Bears built a solid foundation of talent and were betting on good coaching and some truly outstanding potential on offense to push them over the top this year. What to know for Week 6 The Bears are an incredibly dangerous offense paired with a defense that is worse than its underlying metrics suggest. That offers up a recipe for a real shootout in Atlanta. It’s tough to get a read on the actual abilities of this Bears team, but the offense was at full strength in Week 1 in favorable conditions and boatraced the Panthers, putting up 552 yards en route to a 59-37 win. The following week, they played the Vikings in the rain and Brian Flores befuddled Chicago, which lost 9-3 and lost Williams for multiple weeks. It’s been difficult to get a true sense of the offense from there because they’ve had Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent under center and have had running back injuries, as well, but Ben Johnson did dismantle the Eagles 27-7 in Week 3 with Keenum. With Williams set to return, a world of possibilities opens up for Chicago again. He’s simply one of the most gifted quarterbacks in league, and if the results can be a bit inconsistent, Williams’ ability to make nearly any throw while backpedaling away from pressure, scrambling, or otherwise just being wildly off-balance makes defending him extraordinarily difficult. The fact that the Falcons have not yet faced him adds a little difficulty to the mix, as does the fact that he can be a lethal scrambler. Williams has plenty of weapons to throw to. While they take turns popping off, Luther Burden, Rome Odunze, and Kalif Raymond offer plenty of speed and big play potential; tight ends Colston Loveland and Cole Kmet are both capable pass catchers as well. Ben Johnson is a mad scientist who marries that varied passing attack to a very strong ground game featuring D’Andre Swift—who is banged up—and bowling ball with legs Kyle Monangai, who seems likely to miss this game. Teams that can’t account for all these threats tend to have a tough time, and the Falcons are a bit banged up in the secondary. Pressure is the best way to solve this. This is not a Tyler Huntley game, where the Falcons leaned heavily on the blitz and paid for it against the Ravens backup, who has the third-best completion percentage when pressured in the NFL this year. Williams is 22nd in the NFL in completion percentage under pressure, plummeting 30 percentage points when the rush is getting to him, though he remains a threat to break a long run. Williams does not take many sacks, but you’ll live with that if you can force him into bad throws. If that puts extra pressure on a ground game that’s much less effective with a banged-up Swift and without Monangai, so much the better. The Falcons defense will have its work cut out for it regardless, but what about the Falcons offense? That’s a little more straightforward, despite Chicago being statistically top ten thus far through five weeks. What do I mean by that? Chicago has faced two capable offenses thus far and allowed over 30 points to both; the Panthers scored 37 in a shootout and the Packers easily set a new season high with 31 points last week. They held the Jets, Vikings, and Eagles in check, but all three of those teams are struggling with personnel troubles and dysfunction, so that’s not an achievement that deserves sustained applause. The splits here are also reflected in passing yardage, where Bryce Young and Jordan Love picked them apart for over 300 yards apiece, while Geno Smith, Carson Wentz, and Jalen Hurts in whatever nightmare box the Eagles are putting in all scuffled. The Bears have a run defense that looks better in raw yardage than in DVOA, and they have yet to face a back as good as Bijan Robinson (and arguably not even as good as Brian Robinson Jr., for that matter). They can rush the passer well and have a knack for authoring big plays, but they also lost leading sack artists Montez Sweat and Dayo Odeyingbo for this week alongside linebacker TJ Edwards, leaving them thinner and less capable up front. As long as Michael Penix Jr. is good to go, this offense is more than capable of attacking this Chicago defense deep and with a diet of the Robinsons, which is likely to bear real fruit. The bigger question is whether this Falcons defense can bottle up a very capable, creative Bears offense and, failing that, whether the offense can keep up with what the Bears are capable of doing. I would be very surprised if this doesn’t turn into a shootout, unless Williams or Penix suffers an unexpected setback and don’t play Sunday. The Falcons badly need to get back on track after that sour Sunday night and have a real chance to do so against yet another depleted team. If they can’t get the job done against a much less effective defense and a team that might be working without one of its top backs and with a limited or absent version of their star young quarterback, it’s going to be time to worry.
author: Dave Choate

title: NFL predictions: Falcons must win trenches against the Bears
summary: The Falcons fell to the Ravens in overtime on Sunday Night Football in Week 5, breaking a two-game winning streak where the offense averaged a blazing 40 points per game. Atlanta came back down to earth against an injured but still extremely well-coached Baltimore team, falling to 2-3 with the most difficult stretch of the […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - DECEMBER 31: Chicago Bears defenders tackle Drake London #5 of the Atlanta Falcons during the first quarter at Soldier Field on December 31, 2023 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Quinn Harris/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Falcons fell to the Ravens in overtime on Sunday Night Football in Week 5, breaking a two-game winning streak where the offense averaged a blazing 40 points per game. Atlanta came back down to earth against an injured but still extremely well-coached Baltimore team, falling to 2-3 with the most difficult stretch of the schedule still to come. It’s a disappointing result for the Falcons, but hopefully a learning experience for the new coaching staff. Attention now shifts to Week 6’s matchup with the Bears, who possess one of the league’s most fearsome offenses. Chicago is the only team in the NFL that has rushed for more yards than Atlanta, and should see starting quarterback Caleb Williams return to the lineup after a three-week absence. This is likely to be the toughest test yet for the Falcons defense, who are very shorthanded at cornerback and edge rusher. Unlike the Ravens, however, the Bears defense is quite vulnerable to both the run and pass. Despite Williams’ return and the Bears offensive prowess, the Falcons are just 1.5-point home underdogs in Week 6. The over/under of 51.5 suggests an offensive showcase, and Atlanta is going to need to put up points and control the clock to keep pace with Chicago. Falcons vs Bears Week 6 predictions This matchup presents a major opportunity for the Falcons to step up and win the trenches on both sides of the ball—similar to how they dominated both the Packers and Saints earlier in the season. The Bears have a good offensive line, but are likely to be missing bruising running back Kyle Monangai for the game. D’Andre Swift is a good runner himself, but Chicago has been most effective with the two-headed attack of Swift and Monangai—who is responsible for nearly as many yards and TDs as Swift. Caleb Williams will also factor in as a runner, but there’s no telling how he’ll perform in his first game back from injury. On the other side of the ball, the Bears will be without top edge rusher Montez Sweat due to a PED suspension. Veteran Dayo Odeyingbo is also in danger of missing the game with a quad injury. At linebacker, starter T.J. Edwards and reserve Keyshaun Elliott also missed practice for most of the week. That’s a lot of injuries piling up the in front seven against a Falcons team who would love nothing more than to run the ball. While former Falcons Grady Jarrett and Kentavius Street are performing well as pass rushers, neither has been an impact run defender. If Atlanta’s offensive line can bounce back and dominate the way they did back in Weeks 3 and 4, that’s a pathway to success for the Falcons. We all know this offense is a lot better when Bijan and Brian Robinson and getting chunk yardage on the ground, and that’ll be the most important thing to establish early in the game. Long sustained drives will also help keep Chicago’s offense off the field and the defense fresher over the long haul. On defense, this is another big test for a Falcons front that got beat up by the Ravens. I think Atlanta can get pressure, but they’ll have to also play disciplined football against the rushing threat of Caleb Williams. I’d expect a different approach this week than what we saw against Baltimore, perhaps with a QB spy involved on the majority of plays. It’ll be significantly easier to defend just D’Andre Swift versus Swift and Monangai, so that could also be a boon for the Falcons. At the end of the day, Atlanta’s depleted secondary presents some issues. I expect the Bears to have success in the passing game, and that means this could turn into a shootout. In that scenario, it’ll be hard for the Falcons to keep pace with Chicago. This will be the offense’s biggest test yet, as it might require a more pass-heavy approach from Penix throughout the game. All that being said, I think the Bears with Caleb Williams at the helm are possibly the most dangerous offense in football. Atlanta goes back and forth with Chicago throughout the game, but the defense can’t stop Chicago enough thanks to their secondary injuries. The Falcons fall to Chicago, 31-27, but do show some really nice things in the process. Rise up with Falcons fans on the SB Nation app! Pittsburgh is coming off a 12-point home win over the Indianapolis Colts, marking their first double-digit margin of […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - NOVEMBER 16: Mark Andrews #89 of the Baltimore Ravens scores a touchdown against the Cleveland Browns during the fourth quarter at Huntington Bank Field on November 16, 2025 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images Updated Standings : Baltimore Ravens 4-1 Cleveland Browns 3-2 Pittsburgh Steelers 3-2 Cincinnati Bengals 3-2 Pittsburgh Steelers Matchup: @ Tampa Bay Buccaneers, 1:00 pm EST The Steelers will look to string together consecutive wins for the first time this season after continuing to alternate victories and losses through five games. Pittsburgh is coming off a 12-point home win over the Indianapolis Colts, marking their first double-digit margin of victory so far in 2026. The Steelers showed more continued signs of offensive life, particularly in the run game led by Jaylen Warren (188 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns). Their opponent this week, the Buccaneers, have a much stingier run defense — allowing only 72.8 rushing yards per game (No. 2 in the NFL). Tampa Bay also ranks Top 10 in passing yards given up as well and, despite their 1-4 overall record, are coming off a strong win last Thursday night over the Dallas Cowboys. The Buccaneers will have a rest advantage and home-field advantage, so the Steelers will have their work cut out for them despite being favored to win. If the Steelers are stymied on the ground, the onus will turn to Aaron Rodgers and company in the passing attack. Rodgers has three passing touchdowns in three straight games. Pittsburgh’s defense will be facing undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels, making his third start in-place of the injured Baker Mayfield. Daniels has been inconsistent as a passer and has thrown three interceptions but is a dynamic athlete. The Steelers will have to account for him in the run game in addition to running back Bucky Irving, who ran for 165 yards on 21 carries in Week 5. If the Steelers can key in on Irving in the backfield and force Daniels to beat them through the air, their defense should hold up well. Baltimore Ravens Matchup: @ Cleveland Browns, 1:00pm EST The Ravens are coming off a third straight win, all by one possession, after securing a 30-23 overtime victory last Sunday night. Backup quarterback Tyler Huntley, starting in place of Lamar Jackson (ankle) led two consecutive touchdown drives late in the game to erase an eight-point deficit. Huntley is set to start again this Sunday as the Ravens look to start 1-0 in the division with a win over the Browns. Baltimore has won three straight meetings against the Browns, two of which were 20+ point victories. However, the Browns have often played them tough, especially in Cleveland, so this won’t be a cakewalk by any means — especially without Jackson under center. Huntley will need to have another mistake-free performance and handle blitz packages well. The Browns will likely crowd the line of scrimmage and try to take away underneath passing routes, forcing Huntley to beat them with downfield throws. The Ravens are expected to get rookie wide receiver Ja’Kobi Lane back from injury in this game, which will provide another pass-catching weapon. Defensively, the Ravens will need to buckle down and limit points again. They allowed only 16 offensive points in last week’s win over the Atlanta Falcons. Quarterback Deshaun Watson has been at his best this season when blitzed and struggled more versus calmer pressure. That creates an interesting strategy dilemma for Jesse Minter. Regardless, the Ravens have done a good job limiting big plays in the passing game this year, which will come in handy against talented rookie wide receiver Denzel Boston. The Browns have other young playmakers that call for defensive attention as well. Cleveland Browns Matchup: vs. Baltimore Ravens, 1:00pm EST The Browns’ winning streak came to a conclusion last week after they dropped a 17-12 contest against the New York Jets. It was a sloppy offensive performance from both sides, but the Browns were in position to win after taking a lead in the fourth quarter, which they failed to retain or recoup. With the loss, the Browns dropped out of first place in the division, a spot they’ll look to get back by beating the Ravens this Sunday. This will be Todd Monken’s first game coaching against his former team, giving the Browns another source of extra motivation to win. Monken will look to attack a Ravens’ defense that ranks middle-of-the-pack in yardage and points allowed but is set to return a key piece in edge rusher Trey Hendrickson. The Browns’ offense has largely struggled this season, scoring the fifth-least points per game at just 18.6. Some of their most successful moments have come out of structure with Watson evading pressure and scrambling. Cleveland’s defense will be facing Huntley instead of Jackson, making for a much easier matchup. However, the Ravens scored 30 points last week, proving that their offense is still capable of producing with Huntley under center. The key for the Browns will be limiting Derrick Henry’s damage on the ground and taking away short-yardage throws. Huntley has rarely connected on deep throws in his career. The Browns will also need to find a way to keep the ball out of Zay Flowers’ hands as much as possible.

Head coach Jesse Minter said that the decision was made in Jackson’s “best interest.” The 29-year-old quarterback has not practiced for the last two weeks due to an ankle injury suffered against the Tennessee Titans in Week 4. Tyler ‘Snoop’ Huntley will get another start after leading the Ravens to an overtime win in Atlanta in Week 5. Jurgens, who arrived in Baltimore via trade from the Eagles last week, could not clear concussion protocol in time to play on Sunday. Rookie offensive lineman Vega Ioane will stay at center for one more game with a major question mark at right guard, where both potential starters – Andrew Vorhees and Emery Jones Jr. – are listed as questionable. If neither can go, the Ravens could start Kyle Hergel, who signed in Baltimore after Jovaughn Gwyn and Ethan Pocic were injured in Week 3. Also missing Sunday’s game are veteran defensive tackle Broderick Washington, who missed practice on Thursday and Friday, and rookie tight end Matthew Hibner, who suffered a hand injury against the Falcons. Hibner left the game and returned in a blocking-only capacity; Minter said that he would miss “maybe a week” and should not land on injured reserve.
