title: Bills game-day food: Buffalo Hardtack for Week 6 at Las Vegas Raiders
summary: How the heck long have I been doing this anyway? It doesn’t matter; the mad-kitchen scientist is back for another season of recipes to make your Buffalo Bills game days even more memorable. For those of you new to this, it’s pretty simple. We love the Bills. We love food. Every week, you’ll get a […]
full_text: How the heck long have I been doing this anyway? It doesn’t matter; the mad-kitchen scientist is back for another season of recipes to make your Buffalo Bills game days even more memorable. For those of you new to this, it’s pretty simple. We love the Bills. We love food. Every week, you’ll get a themed recipe based on the Bills and their opponent. Hardtack So last week I deviated things a bit and the theme started with a nod to the mascot (then worked in the city). I had fun with that, and with the Las Vegas Raiders game up I asked the question we all want the answer to this week. What did pirates eat? Well kids, on long sea voyages you needed food that wouldn’t spoil, had high calorie density, and you could easily make and store. Hardtack is exactly that. Used for long voyages and as a survival food, hardtack is made from flour, water, and sometimes a little salt. Not to be confused with a cracker or type of actual bread, hardtack is more like concrete that will keep you alive. Intended to be dipped and softened before consuming, traditional hardtack is mostly flavorless. Not mine. You still NEED to dip it/dunk it, but it should enhance what you’re pairing it with not just absorb it. Buffalo Hardtack Makes: About a dozen biscuits Active time: 20 min Total time: About 3 hours Ingredients 3 cups all-purpose flour, divided 1/3 cup hot sauce (see below) 2/3 cup water 1 tsp honey 1/4 tsp cumin 1/2 tsp onion powder 1/2 tsp garlic power Essentials: Measuring cup and spoons, mixing bowl, rolling pin, baking sheets, pizza cutter, fork, a love of adventure and long journeys Preheat oven to 250ºF Thoroughly combine 2 cups flour, hot sauce, water, honey, cumin, onion and garlic powder in mixing bowl. If the dough is still sticky, continue adding flour (about 2 tablespoons at a time) until no longer sticky (very slight tacky is OK); you might not need all three cups. Dust counter or other surface with flour; roll out dough to about 1/4-inch thickness. Segment dough into 3-inch by 3-inch squares using pizza cutter, if you want to be traditional (but smaller is fine too). Poke holes into dough with fork (see below); place dough segments onto baking sheet. Bake in preheated oven for about 3 hours, flipping every 30 min. Remove from oven and allow to cool; serve with some sort of liquid, such as soup. Wingin’ It tips Hardtack recipes typically call for thicker dough as it’s better for long-term storage. If you’re actually planning to do so, some recipes call for 1/2-inch thickness. The thinner version makes it a little easier to soften and eat. I even experimented with really thin to make crackers for adding into soup and the like. How long will this keep if you want to store it? If you’re a purist and use just water, flour, and salt; apparently there is Civil War-era hardtack on display at a few museums still believed to be not be spoiled. I chose ingredients that should retain shelf stability in that they can be dehydrated well. For the hot sauce, avoid anything with pulp. The standard sauce for wings is Frank’s, and that’s an excellent choice for this. The seasoning is already powdered, and honey is also known for shelf stability. That said, because I don’t want anyone to run with this and do something foolish, store this in an airtight container and I wouldn’t personally keep it around longer than a few weeks. As for tips, I did add food coloring to mine to add a little flair. If you look closely you can see a little swirl of pink. Speaking of coloration, because of the hot sauce and food coloring, the top the “biscuits” or “slabs” as I think of them got real pale, real quick. The bottom stayed a salmon pink with a little browning toward the end. Research indicates this is pretty normal. Here’s a picture gallery to give some idea of the process in case you’re a visual learner. And scope out the two I made with special shapes for the occasion. For my final thoughts; I want to express exactly what the hardtack experience is using the bread continuum, as it’s technically a type of bread. Have you ever dipped a slice of bread into soup? You know how you have to dip real quick and take it out so it doesn’t disintegrate? Yeah, that’s not this. You know with croutons in soup how you might put them in a few at a time so they don’t dissolve over time? That’s not this. Have you ever crumbled crackers into soup and they’re mushy kinda quick but hold together? Yeah, still not there. What about a whole cracker? Have you ever dropped one in and it gets floppy after a minute and falls apart? Yeah, that’s not hardtack. No. With this stuff (and remember mine is half the thickness most recipes call for); I put a “biscuit” into an entire bowl of soup right at the beginning. It was the last thing I ate. I could break it with my spoon. It was not floppy. It did not crumble. I still had to chew carefully. That said. It was delicious. Just more like flavorful concrete than a true bread. Give me money. Money me. Money now. Me a money needing a lot now ! Skarekrow likes certain products. Skarekrow likes money. title: NFL predictions: 3 bold takes for Bills-Raiders Week 6 game
summary: The Buffalo Bills have taken their show on the road out west, already winning a thriller against the Los Angeles Rams in primetime last Monday ahead of Week 6 at the Las Vegas Raiders. After sleepwalking through a first half in SoFi Stadium where quarterback Josh Allen and the Bills’ could do nothing to move […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 17: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills runs the ball and gets tackled by Maxx Crosby #98 of the Las Vegas Raiders during a game at Highmark Stadium on September 17, 2023 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills have taken their show on the road out west, already winning a thriller against the Los Angeles Rams in primetime last Monday ahead of Week 6 at the Las Vegas Raiders. After sleepwalking through a first half in SoFi Stadium where quarterback Josh Allen and the Bills’ could do nothing to move the football, the offense came alive late in action to break a winless overtime curse that spanned seven previous attempts. The catalyst for that surge was of course Allen himself, and he took over the game like few others can do against an NFL defense. Given Buffalo’s challenges on defense and its inability to stop almost any passing attack, Allen’s had to elevate his game to another level in 2026. That means there’s very little from Allen’s game that should come as a surprise. The man knows how to wear a cape and he’s done so with aplomb since taking over the reigns as QB1 for the Bills. That’s especially true early this season, partially out of necessity due to a defense unable to stop most opponents. With that in mind, how does one lay claim to a bold prediction about Josh Allen, if it’s not one that speaks to a lack of production? Well, I might have one idea to offer. Let’s dive in, starting with a bold take on Allen, well… at least leading off with a spicy take . Spoiler alert: There’ll be no bold claims made below of Buffalo’s defense. Without any intent to take away from all that outside linebacker Greg Rousseau has accomplished, it’s pretty obvious that we need to see it before believing most things true of the defense. Josh Allen stops fighting mechanics … and allows Josh Allen to be Josh Allen. Discussing his play after Monday Night Football , Allen’s self-reflection offered a glimpse at what might have been holding him back: “Early on, just didn’t feel like I was in a rhythm — wasn’t taking some of the underneath stuff. You know, fighting, mechanically, some stuff right now that I’m working on. But I felt like in that second half I got into a rhythm.” Allen is already discussed as among the greatest quarterback to play professional football, yet his statement about “ fighting, mechanically, some stuff ” is revealing. It’s also a perhaps a teaching moment for outsiders, as one that offers a pretty good alibi for his play in the first half against the Rams. It’s evident that second half in Los Angeles featured a more lock-in version of Allen, someone who was playing more instinctual football that allowed him to operate in better rhythm unsaddled by any critical focus on mechanics. Allen would later refute the idea that it’s unusual for him to be battling mechanics in-season , stating that it’s likely something “every quarterback fights throughout the year — it could be as simple as one thing.” In recent weeks, Allen’s decision making has come under a bit of fire thanks to a pair of ill-advised arm punts. One doomed a shot at winning, while another ended hope of putting up points before halftime. Were those decisions borne out of being hyper-focused on mechanics, or the result of throwing caution to the wind, mechanical flaws be damned? It’s possible both things are true, but many people will tell you that the most dangerous version of Allen is the one where he’s in a zone, playing instinctual football. Almost no one can touch him, figuratively and literally. Allen fueled almost exclusively by instincts may carry a turnover or two, but there’s a far better chance he’s scoring four or more touchdowns in such a state. I believe this is the version of Allen we see in Week 6. He may very well spend quite a bit of time on mechanics during the lead up in-week, but it’s a practice that should be put to bed at kickoff. This isn’t a situation akin to Tim Tebow’s, where he had major fundamental flaws as a passer. The amazing thing about Allen is his ability to make incredible things happen out of thin air, where other quarterbacks often fail due to mechanical breakdowns or otherwise. Allen has made incredible strides as a quarterback, thanks to the work he puts in to improve. We’ve seen what efficiency brings to his game, especially when there’s a talent void at wide receiver. His feeling the need to focus acutely on mechanics may be limiting Allen’s play. Instead, refusing to fight mechanics should allow Allen to play more free. It likely keeps Allen out of a headspace that binds him up while also playing voodoo with his internal clock. Allen himself will tell you the only thing that matters is getting a win. His play late against the Rams is all the evidence you need to understand that a fire-breathing unicorn is at its best when unbridled . Sunday feels like a “get right with himself” game for Allen. Look for Allen to play with less restraint early in Las Vegas, but don’t go in expecting him to detrimentally throw caution to the wind. In two games against the Raiders, Allen has played well. In two wins, Allen’s completed 55-of-71 passes for 562 yards with five touchdown passes and no interceptions. Where he hasn’t made as much impact is as a rusher, gaining just six yards on six carries. The oddsmakers at FanDuel Sportsbook aren’t bothered by that stat, currently listing Allen with the best odds (-175) of scoring a rushing touchdown at any point in the game. He’s also the current co-leader with running back James Cook III (+350) as odds-on-favorites to score two-plus rushing (or receiving) touchdowns. Which leads to my next point… Keon Coleman excels as featured WR Under head coach Joe Brady, the Bills want to play high-level football where they’re constantly in pursuit of points and attacking a defense from the start. We’ve seen that in Brady’s preference for starting on offense when winning the coin toss. “Put the ball down” is this years mantra, fit for an oval car magnet. Brady wants the team to take the ball and score at every opportunity, and to stress defenses with a deadly and complete passing attack. Yet since Week 3, the long pass has been a struggle. Well, at least passes traveling a ton of distance in the air. Much of that has to do with wide receiver DJ Moore’s shoulder injury and the way defenses are playing tight end Dalton Kincaid. Where early on Moore and Kincaid helped fuel each other’s success thanks to the honesty teams had to utilize in covering both players, now Kincaid seems to have disappeared alongside Moore. To add insult to injury, now wide receiver Joshua Palmer is dealing with his own shoulder injury. Despite that, the Bills deploy the most explosive offense in the last decade . A key part of that fact is due to the emergence of wide receiver Keon Coleman. Once thought of as a potential trade candidate, Coleman has blossomed in year three. He continues making “wow” catches despite added coverage cheating his way with Moore sidelined. There’s plenty of meat on the bone still for Coleman to steal, and I expect him to be deployed as a true WR1 against the Raiders. Buffalo must figure things out with Kincaid, and the coaches should play it safe with Moore. They should also continue involving Shakir early, which could help calm the tsunami known as Maxx Crosby. All of those things should happen while trying to establish Coleman as the top target in the downfield passing attack. Through five games, Coleman has made 15 catches on 18 targets for 224 yards and two touchdowns. That’s a highly efficient stat line, which is made more impressive by his 11 catches for a first down. Coleman has proven to be reliable and an important part of the passing game in 2026. Last week he saw just two targets, with his lone catch going for seven yards and a touchdown. Expect to see Coleman worked into the plans well before crunch time on Sunday, even if…
author: Matt Byham

title: 5 Buffalo Bills to watch at Las Vegas Raiders
summary: The Buffalo Bills are set to take on the Las Vegas Raiders for just the second time in their history in the state of Nevada. In the first matchup between these two teams in Las Vegas, the Bills beat the Raiders 30-23 in an empty Allegiant Stadium thanks to COVID regulations in place for the […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills are set to take on the Las Vegas Raiders for just the second time in their history in the state of Nevada. In the first matchup between these two teams in Las Vegas, the Bills beat the Raiders 30-23 in an empty Allegiant Stadium thanks to COVID regulations in place for the 2020 season. The stadium will be far from empty come Sunday, as the Bills will face a resurgent Raiders squad that’s off to a better start than anticipated. The team won its first three games this season before dropping contests to the Kansas City Chiefs and New England Patriots in consecutive weeks. Can the Bills make it a three-game losing streak for the Raiders? There will be plenty of factors leading towards Buffalo’s ultimate success or failure in that endeavor, but one thing is certain: The Bills would love to enter their bye week at 5-1. Here are five players to watch this week as they attempt to attain that goal. _____________________________________________________________________________ James Cook III At the risk of beating a proverbial dead horse, this is a big week for Cook given his case of fumblitis he’s developed over the last 23 games. Cook has nearly as many fumbles (4) as he does touchdowns (5) this season, and he’s averaging a fumble on every 44 touches since the start of the 2025 regular season. When asked earlier this week, head coach Joe Brady said that, eventually, Cook needs to start protecting the football if he expects to play the snap share and maintain the carry share that he has over the last calendar year. Cook is obviously a dynamic runner—he’s averaging 5.6 yards per carry and already has 15 rushing attempts of ten yards or more this season—but his turnover rate is a tremendous concern. Will the fumbles be in his head? The Raiders will clearly have scouting information about the success of “Peanut Punches” on Cook, so they’ll likely be ripping and punching at the ball every time he touches it. Another thing I’m interested in watching is what happens to Cook if he does put the ball on the ground again. Will Brady follow through on his threat to limit Cook’s touches and snaps if it happens? TE Dalton Kincaid Where is he? Obviously, opposing teams are going to bracket him, especially if wideout DJ Moore isn’t on the field. That’s a pretty common tactic for any defense against any opposing player’s best receiving option. My concern is just how easily Buffalo, and Kincaid, allow their top receiver to be removed from the game. Joe Brady has to scheme some easy-button targets for Kincaid early to give him some rhythm and flow for the game. Just look at how badly the Buffalo passing attack struggled last week against the Los Angeles Rams in the early moments of the game as an example. It will help quarterback Josh Allen to settle into the contest if he can find some easy completions early. Kincaid is his best option. The Bills can’t let him be entirely erased like he has been for the last two games. DL T.J. Sanders The big fella made his presence felt in his 2026 season debut, and it’s pretty clear that the coaching staff views him as an important part of the defensive line rotation given his heavy usage. Sanders played on 51 snaps last week, trailing only Deone Walker (63) in playing time among Buffalo defensive linemen. Sanders rewarded the coaches by notching five tackles, adding a sack to thwart a two-point conversion attempt that might not appear on the stat record, but it does go down as an absolutely massive play in the game. Sanders looked strong, quick, elusive—all the things the Bills wanted from him when they traded up to select him at No. 41 overall in the 2025 NFL Draft. With Ed Oliver likely sitting again this week, expect a heavy dose of Sanders again against the Raiders. Inside Linebackers My goodness, can somebody just make a play? Dorian Williams looks fine on run downs and lost on passing plays. Terrel Bernard is a step slow and constantly involved in some sort of communication snafu with safeties and slot corners in coverage. I know that the coaching staff has said repeatedly that the linebackers are playing their assignments , but there’s no way that Brady and defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard can watch the games and the film, and then still say that the middle level of the defense is performing well. The Bills were absolutely smoked in the intermediate levels last week, and while we could point at Puka Nacua and his incredible ability as a reason for that, the assignment isn’t easier this week. Tight end Brock Bowers is a stud, and fellow tight end Michael Mayer isn’t a slouch, either. One of Buffalo’s two veteran ILBs needs to start doing something on the field, or else they’re likely going to start watching someone like rookie Kaleb Elarms-Orr take their place. CB Dee Alford Will he play this week? Given that the Bills released Anthony Kendall, who was signed from the practice squad and manned the slot last week, I assume that Alford will be ready to roll this Sunday. Kendall, for what it’s worth, looked no worse than the Bills’ other options in the slot so far this season, so it’s good that the team was able to re-sign him back to the practice squad. Alford started to look more comfortable against the New England Patriots before an ankle injury caused him to miss last week’s matchup. He’s probably have to deal with some big bodies in the aforementioned tight ends this week, but he also may find himself matched up against a speedster in Tre Tucker. He doesn’t operate much from the slot, but it’s a way that the Raiders can manipulate matchups and take Tucker away from someone like Christian Benford this week. If Alford is good to go, it helps Buffalo’s defensive depth. If he can play well on top of it, it will help the defensive unit tremendously.

title: James Cook is going to need the bye week after facing Las Vegas Raiders
summary: The Buffalo Bills will be taking on the Las Vegas Raiders this Sunday, after which they’ll be able to reset during the bye week before hosting the Baltimore Ravens. The bye is a bit early but that’s not a bad thing with a rookie head coach, a shaky defense, and an offense that’s had some […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills will be taking on the Las Vegas Raiders this Sunday, after which they’ll be able to reset during the bye week before hosting the Baltimore Ravens. The bye is a bit early but that’s not a bad thing with a rookie head coach, a shaky defense, and an offense that’s had some stumbles despite their elite status. For one player in particular though, the Raiders will likely wind up making him extra grateful for the bye. Based on the current stats, James Cook is going to need the extra rest. James Cook might be really exhausted… The Raiders are 3 – 2, they’ve been within striking distance of taking down Kansas City, and should be respected as such. That said, their run defense has been terrible. By the time James Cook is done running this Sunday, it’s possible he won’t need a flight home to Buffalo. Hyperbole aside, on paper this is an insanely lopsided matchup. The Raiders are currently allowing 140.6 yards per game, nearly 30 more than league average and the fifth worst in the league. That’s not due to teams tossing a ton of extra attempts their way either. On a per play basis, Las Vegas is second worst in the league and allows 5.21 yards per rushing attempt. Shockingly, the Raiders have only allowed one rusher to break 100 yards, but man was that spectacular. Kenneth Walker III ran for 177 in Week 4. On the other hand, allowing running back committees to go wild isn’t really any better than a single person doing it. Buffalo’s run game, if you weren’t aware, is in elite territory. In fact, there’s only one team ahead of the Bills when it comes to rushing efficiency. Kansas City. While it was their second best effort this season, Kansas City’s totals were buoyed by the aforementioned spectacular performance by Walker. The Bills are averaging 5.37 yards per carry as a team. James Cook is personally at 5.6 yards per rush. He has three 100-yard games already this season. About the only concern is that the Raiders have recovered six fumbles this season, which leads the league. Let’s watch a few plays to see if they look like something James Cook might be able to do… pic.twitter.com/MrUVgBn1rX — Kuebiko (@Kuebiko_Kami) October 16, 2026 Did you play the game? What was your answer? Was it “yes?” Then you WIN! Great job!

title: 5 Las Vegas Raiders to watch vs. Buffalo Bills
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders host the Buffalo Bills this week in what is their third of four straight games against top-flight competition. After winning three games against against bottom-dwellers to start the season (the Miami Dolphins and Los Angeles Chargers are winless, while the New Orleans Saints are 1-4), the Raiders have dropped consecutive contests […]
full_text: The Las Vegas Raiders host the Buffalo Bills this week in what is their third of four straight games against top-flight competition. After winning three games against against bottom-dwellers to start the season (the Miami Dolphins and Los Angeles Chargers are winless, while the New Orleans Saints are 1-4), the Raiders have dropped consecutive contests against the Kansas City Chiefs and New England Patriots. Their schedule isn’t any easier this week or next, as they face off against the Bills before taking on the Los Angeles Rams on October 25. Are the Raiders for real? Is their 3-2 start a product of an easy schedule? Given the talent they have on offense combined with the Bills’ defensive woes, this isn’t a game that anyone should feel comfortable filing into the win column before it’s played. If the Bills want to earn their way to a 5-1 record heading into their bye week, they’ll need to take care of business against a solid Raiders squad. Here are five Raiders we’re watching this weekend against the Bills. _____________________________________________________________________________ QB Kirk Cousins For the second consecutive week, Buffalo faces a veteran quarterback with tremendous accuracy. The plan this week has to be the same as it was for Matthew Stafford, at least as it relates to the pass rush. If Buffalo can blitz Cousins and force him to make off-platform throws, they’ll be able to help their struggling defensive secondary. For at least a half of football, Buffalo was able to bend without breaking against the Rams. Cousins isn’t quite on the level of Stafford, but he’s accurate enough to beat them repeatedly if he’s given time to work in the pocket. If Buffalo can create pressure, they can keep him from picking them apart. I think adding an extra rusher on occasion early will speed him up, which should let the Bills flow into more simulated pressure looks later in the contest that will lead to a turnover. WR Tre Tucker Vegas’ tight ends steal much of the press, but the speedy Tucker is a very good receiver in his own right. Buffalo hasn’t exactly been competent in pass defense this season—and that’s putting it lightly, as the team is currently 31st in passing yards allowed—so any team’s top receiving options should be viewed as threats. While the Raiders might also have a strong running back in Aston Jeanty, the Bills have been fine against the run, ranking fifteenth in yards allowed there. The pass defense is what gives me the most digestive discomfort, and Tucker has the speed to beat the Bills at multiple levels of the defense. If he’s working in the slot, something he does just around 18% of the time this season, he’s especially dangerous. In those situations, he’d be matched up against Dee Alford, or a linebacker, or a safety. If he’s outside, Christian Benford will likely see plenty of reps against Tucker, and that’s a matchup I like for the Bills. Davison Igbinosun and Maxwell Hairston will have to avoid penalties and excess separation, respectively, if they want to limit the Raiders’ top deep threat. TE Brock Bowers Bowers is arguably the best tight end in football, so there isn’t a team in the league who’s happy to face him. For a Buffalo pass defense that couldn’t cover a tray of lasagna with Reynolds Wrap of late, this is a matchup nightmare. Honestly, Buffalo might want to watch film of other teams and their bracket coverages against Dalton Kincaid for some ideas about how to limit Bowers. Kincaid has been absolutely erased over the last few weeks, and while I don’t think Buffalo has the defensive talent in the secondary to do that to Bowers, they need to try something to make anyone other than him beat them in the passing game on Sunday. On Monday night, it seemed like Buffalo was intent on making anyone other than Davante Adams beating them, and Puka Nacua caught 17 passes on an absurd 24 targets. The Bills need to make it difficult to target Bowers on Sunday. They can’t let him operate in the middle of the field like they allowed Nacua to operate last week. DE Maxx Crosby Crosby sure would look good in a Bills uniform, but for now, Buffalo will have to figure out a way to keep him off of quarterback Josh Allen for the week. Crosby has two sacks this season to go with 13 quarterback hits. He looks to be fully healthy after dealing with a knee issue last season. While the Bills’ offensive line has been excellent in run blocking, they haven’t been as good in pass protection this season. Last week, they held up well against a tough Los Angeles Rams front even with Tylan Grable playing right tackle in place of starter Spencer Brown for much of the game. Brown is likely to return this week, but he and Dion Dawkins will have their hands full with Crosby on Sunday. LB Nakobe Dean Dean is a tackling machine, but he’s also been abysmal in coverage this season. According to Pro Football Reference , he’s allowed 13-of-15 passes to be completed when he’s the closest player in coverage. Those passes have gone for 114 yards and a touchdown. Dalton Kincaid, Dawson Knox, Khalil Shakir, Ty Johnson—the Bills have plenty of receiving options to stress the intermediate and short areas of the field where Dean will likely be the closest man in coverage. After designing a screen game that worked beautifully against the Los Angeles Rams, it seems that the Bills have a plan to exploit that area that doesn’t involve the ways they’ve done it in the past, where they ran crossers and “mesh” concepts ad nauseum. Dean is a great player, and he’s forced three fumbles this season already, which should put James Cook III on high alert, but he can be exploited in coverage.

title: Exploring Las Vegas Raiders tendencies ahead of Week 6’s game against Buffalo Bills
summary: The Raiders are 3-2 entering Week 6 and average a narrow defeat at the hands of the Chiefs at home, they were throttled by the Patriots a week ago. Let’s dive into those Las Vegas’ tendencies before the Bills trip to Allegiant Stadium for on Sunday. Raiders offense Motion Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak, who […]
full_text: The Raiders are 3-2 entering Week 6 and average a narrow defeat at the hands of the Chiefs at home, they were throttled by the Patriots a week ago. Let’s dive into those Las Vegas’ tendencies before the Bills trip to Allegiant Stadium for on Sunday. Raiders offense Motion Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak, who rose to prominence in Seattle last season coordinating the Seahawks Super Bowl winning offense, is of course calling the plays in Las Vegas, and he’s hardly utilized motion through five games. In fact, the Raiders 26.3% motion rate on run and pass plays is, far and way, the lowest figure in the league, per FTN Fantasy Data via SFdata9ers on Twitter/X . Another TE-based offense As I wrote earlier today , Brock Bowers is, in my estimation, the best receiving tight end in football. And Las Vegas recently gave Michael Mayer a contract extension. So it’s only natural that Kubiak deploys multiple tight ends frequently. How frequently to be exact? The Raiders have utilized some type of multiple tight-end set — either 12, 13, or 22 personnel — on 60.2% of their offensive snaps to date, the second-highest figure in the NFL, per Football Insights . Buffalo must be prepared to cover Bowers and Mayer in this one. Kirk Cousins in the pocket Only Jared Goff has traveled outside the pocket on a lower percentage 0f throws than Cousins entering this game. He’s sitting just under 15% in that category right now, per Jrfortgang on Twitter/X . Interestingly enough, after this game, the Bills will have faced three quarterbacks who make up the bottom trio of the non-pocket throw percentages right now — Goff, Stafford, and Cousins. Raiders defense Problems up front Crosby is a superstar. Former University at Buffalo star Malcolm Koonce is one of the better No. 2 edge rushers in football. But, collectively, the Raiders defensive line has gotten gashed on the ground against opposing offensive lines entering this game. This might be the biggest mismatch I've ever seen: Buffalo's OLine vs. Las Vegas' DLine Best Run-Blocking Offensive Lines by RB Yards Before Contact per Attempt [Since 2021] 1. 2026 Bills (3.65) —[big gap]— 2. 2025 Ravens (3.09) 3. 2024 Eagles (3.07) Worst Run-Defending… pic.twitter.com/JISfXpDkYb — Scott Barrett (@ScottBarrettDFB) October 15, 2026 NFL games are not played on paper. But the analytics do absolutely favor Buffalo’s rushing attack in this matchup with the Raiders. Let’s see if the Bills can take advantage with James Cook and Co. …about Malcolm Koonce The veteran outside rusher has 16 pressures on 100 pass-rush snaps through Week 5. And he’s actually winning his individual reps at a high rate too. Check where he is on this chart… slightly ahead of Greg Rousseau currently in pass-rush win rate. Edge rusher pass rush win rate and double team rate (per PFF) – min 100 pass rush snaps pic.twitter.com/uRaDq0vpR4 — Shaun Newkirk (@Shauncore) October 13, 2026 The initial blocking emphasis needs to be put on limiting Crosby. But Koonce is certainly no slouch on the other side of the Raiders defensive front in passing situations. Blitzing and Cover 0 The Raiders are currently blitzing at the third-highest rate among all defenses, at just under 55% of the time. And what tracks with that — they’re third in Cover 0 (man coverage, no safety help over the top) at 8.2%, behind only the Giants at 11.0% and the Patriots at 8.2%. Las Vegas won’t be shy about dialing up blitz packages in this contest.

title: Bills vs. Raiders history: Playoff wins, comebacks, and Josh Allen
summary: The Buffalo Bills and Las Vegas Raiders have been playing football against each other since 1960, and after more than six decades, the series is about as close as it can get. Buffalo holds a narrow 22–21 advantage, but there’s a catch. The Raiders actually lead the regular-season series 21–20. It’s a pair of postseason […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills and Las Vegas Raiders have been playing football against each other since 1960, and after more than six decades, the series is about as close as it can get. Buffalo holds a narrow 22–21 advantage, but there’s a catch. The Raiders actually lead the regular-season series 21–20. It’s a pair of postseason victories that put the Bills on top. So, rather than going all the way back to the AFL days, we’re going to fast-forward to January 1991 and open our time capsule when the Bills and Raiders met with a trip to the Super Bowl on the line. _____________________________________________________________________________ 1991: The one that sent Buffalo to its first Super Bowl The Raiders were still playing in Los Angeles when they traveled to Buffalo for the AFC Championship Game on Jan. 20, 1991. The Bills were coming off a 13–3 regular season and had already beaten Miami in the divisional round. All that stood between them and their first Super Bowl appearance was a Raiders team that had finished the season 12–4. As it turned out, Los Angeles wasn’t much of an obstacle. Jim Kelly connected with James Lofton for a touchdown on Buffalo’s opening possession, and the Bills never looked back. Thurman Thomas added a rushing touchdown, Darryl Talley returned an interception 27 yards for another score, and Buffalo was already up 21–3 by the end of the first quarter. Things didn’t get any better for the Raiders in the second. Kenneth Davis ran for two touchdowns, Kelly found Lofton again, and the Bills went into halftime leading 41–3. Yes, 41–3 at halftime . Buffalo eventually won 51–3, with Kelly throwing for 300 yards, Thomas rushing for 138, and the Bills’ defense intercepting Raiders quarterback Jay Schroeder five times. The Bills were headed to their first Super Bowl, and the Raiders were headed home. _____________________________________________________________________________ 1994: The one that kept the streak alive Three years later, the Raiders returned to Rich Stadium for another playoff game. This time, however, they made Buffalo work for the win. It was Jan. 15, 1994, and the Bills were trying to reach their fourth consecutive Super Bowl. Los Angeles had other plans, jumping out to a 17–6 lead in the second quarter before Thomas scored to cut the deficit to four at halftime. Kelly found Bill Brooks for a touchdown in the third quarter, and a Steve Christie field goal put Buffalo ahead 22–17. But the Raiders answered with an 86-yard touchdown pass from Jeff Hostetler to Tim Brown, taking a 23–22 lead into the fourth quarter. Kelly and Brooks connected again, this time for a 22-yard touchdown, and the Bills held on for the 29–23 win. They were headed back to the AFC Championship Game, and eventually to their fourth straight Super Bowl. _____________________________________________________________________________ 2011: The one nobody saw coming Of course, not every memorable Bills-Raiders game has involved the playoffs. There’s another one worth pulling out of our time capsule, especially for anyone who enjoys thrillers. On Sept. 18, 2011, the Oakland Raiders came to Buffalo and spent the first half making things miserable for the home team. The Bills trailed 21–3 at halftime, and there wasn’t much reason to think things were about to get better. But Fred Jackson opened the second half with a 43-yard touchdown run, and suddenly Buffalo had some hope. Ryan Fitzpatrick and the Bills went on to score touchdowns on all five of their second-half possessions, turning what had looked like an easy Raiders win into a back-and-forth game. The lead changed hands five times in the fourth quarter alone. With Oakland ahead 35–31 and time running out, Fitzpatrick led one final drive, finding David Nelson for a six-yard touchdown with just 14 seconds remaining. Buffalo won 38–35, and Fitz became a Buffalo legend. _____________________________________________________________________________ 2020 & 2023: The ones Josh Allen played That brings us to the Josh Allen era, where the Bills have continued to have the upper hand against the Raiders. Allen has faced the Raiders twice, and he’s won both games. The first came in 2020, when Buffalo traveled to Las Vegas and came away with a 30–23 win in the teams’ first meeting since the Raiders left Oakland. The most recent meeting between the two teams came Sept. 17, 2023, in Orchard Park. It wasn’t nearly as exciting as some of the games we’ve revisited. Allen threw for 274 yards and three touchdowns, Buffalo’s defense kept the Raiders’ offense under control, and the Bills cruised to a 38–10 win. _____________________________________________________________________________ It’s been three years since the Bills and Raiders last shared a football field, and even longer since Buffalo made the trip to Las Vegas. Allen is 2–0 against the Raiders, and the Bills have won the last three meetings. On Sunday, they’ll have a chance to add another win to both records — and give themselves a little more breathing room in a series that’s been neck and neck for more than six decades.
author: Rachel Auberger

title: Bills record book watch: Dawson Knox, Josh Allen eye Week 6 records
summary: The Buffalo Bills are headed to Las Vegas for a Sunday afternoon matchup with the Raiders, and we’re bringing the record book, and some pencils, along for the trip.  We’ve got a couple of players who have been knocking on the door of their next spot in franchise history, a few who could move up with a good afternoon, […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills are headed to Las Vegas for a Sunday afternoon matchup with the Raiders, and we’re bringing the record book, and some pencils, along for the trip. We’ve got a couple of players who have been knocking on the door of their next spot in franchise history, a few who could move up with a good afternoon, and some possibilities that would require the kind of performance that makes us reach for a calculator. As always, we’ve divided our record book into four chapters: Sure Things, A Good Bet, Not Impossible, and Superhuman. _____________________________________________________________________________ WEEK 6 — October 18, 2026 Chapter 1: Sure Things Nothing to write in ink just yet. That doesn’t mean we won’t find something to add before the weekend is over. _____________________________________________________________________________ Chapter 2: A Good Bet • Josh Allen rushing touchdowns Five games. Eight rushing touchdowns. Five straight games with at least one trip into the end zone on the ground. Allen has already established the NFL record for consecutive games with a rushing touchdown to start a season by a quarterback. Now he has a chance to extend it – making it harder for anyone to write their name above his in the future. Considering Allen has scored at least once on the ground in every game this season, we’re feeling pretty good about his chances of keeping that streak alive against the Raiders. • Greg Rousseau career sacks Rousseau came flying out of the gate this season, piling up six sacks in Buffalo’s first three games. Since then? Nothing. He’s been sitting on 38 career sacks for two weeks, just half a sack away from moving past Darryl Talley on Buffalo’s all-time list. This will be his third attempt to get that next sack. Surely he’s due? • Dawson Knox receiving yards Knox has been hanging around James Lofton on Buffalo’s all-time receiving yards list, and he couldn’t have gotten much closer Monday night without actually catching him. His six receiving yards against the Rams brought him to 2,730 for his career. Lofton finished his time in Buffalo with 2,736. That means Knox needs six yards to tie Lofton and seven to pass him for 16th place in the franchise record book. Considering Knox caught a six-yard pass Monday, we’re hoping Allen can find him again this week – but at least a yard farther down field. _____________________________________________________________________________ Chapter 3: Not Impossible • Dawson Knox receiving touchdowns While we’re watching Knox climb the receiving yards list, there’s another opportunity worth keeping an eye on. Knox has 28 career receiving touchdowns, putting him in a tie with Gabe Davis and Stevie Johnson for seventh place in franchise history. Jerry Butler is next with 29. One touchdown against the Raiders would move Knox into a tie with Butler for sixth place. Two would put him ahead of Butler outright. Of course, Knox hasn’t been finding the end zone very often this season, but there’s nothing stopping him from changing that Sunday – unless it’s Josh Allen trying to get all the records himself. • Khalil Shakir receiving yards Shakir has an opportunity to do a little rearranging of Buffalo’s all-time receiving yards list this week. With 2,568 career receiving yards, he’s sitting in 21st place, but the next three players are all within 74 yards. Shakir needs 64 yards to pass J.D. Hill, 73 to pass Fred Jackson, and 74 to pass Haven Moses. He had 80 yards against the Rams on Monday night, so it’s defintely within reach. _____________________________________________________________________________ Chapter 4: Superhuman • Josh Allen rushing touchdowns Allen already owns the NFL record for rushing touchdowns by a quarterback, but his climb up the all-time list — which includes players at every position — is far from finished. With 87 career rushing touchdowns, Allen sits in 16th place. Eric Dickerson and Curtis Martin are tied for 14th with 90 apiece. Three rushing touchdowns against Las Vegas would put Allen in a three-way tie with Dickerson and Martin. Four would move him past both. That’s asking a lot, even from Allen. But three rushing touchdowns in one game isn’t something we’ve never seen him do, so have those erasers handy. • James Cook rushing yards Look who’s back. We’ve been watching Cook chase Allen on Buffalo’s all-time rushing yards list, and Monday night didn’t do him any favors. Cook ran for 111 yards against the Rams – a great game by most standards. But Allen ran for 121. Instead of closing the gap, Cook actually lost another 10 yards to his quarterback. For Cook to move past Allen on Sunday, he’ll need to outgain him by at least 170 rushing yards. It’s a pretty tall order – especially considering Allen doesn’t seem particularly interested in slowing down his own rushing production. • Greg Rousseau single-season sacks We’re still waiting for Rousseau to get that next sack, but if he decides to make up for the last two weeks all at once, there’s another possibility. Rousseau has six sacks this season, and his personal best is eight, set in 2022. Two sacks against Las Vegas would tie that mark. Three would give him nine and establish a new single-season career high — with plenty of football still left to play. Now, we’re not expecting three sacks every Sunday. At this point, we’d be happy to see him get the first one out of the way. • Dalton Kincaid receptions and receiving yards Kincaid could make some serious moves in Buffalo’s tight end record book if he puts together a big game against the Raiders. He currently has 172 career receptions, putting him sixth among Bills tight ends. Charles Clay is fifth with 178, and Scott Chandler is fourth with 182. Seven catches Sunday would move Kincaid past Clay, while 11 would put him ahead of both Clay and Chandler for fourth place. And if those catches add up to a whole lot of yards, there’s another possibility for the Buffalo tight end. Kincaid has 1,969 career receiving yards, leaving him 152 yards away from passing Chandler’s 2,120 for fourth place among Buffalo tight ends. Kincaid already had a 130-yard game against Houston earlier this season, so we know he can put up big numbers. Asking for 152 yards and 11 catches in the same afternoon is another matter entirely. But that’s why this one belongs in the Superhuman chapter. _____________________________________________________________________________ That’s our list for Week 6. Some of these records could change with a single play. Others would require the kind of afternoon we’d be talking about for years. Either way, we’ll have the record book open, the pencils sharpened, and the erasers on hand Sunday as the Bills take on the Raiders.

Tomorrow we’ll see if they are awake and healthy enough to contend with a Panthers squad that should be freshly rested from their early bye week. To see […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - OCTOBER 04: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Tanner McKee #16 looks on during the game between the Los Angeles Rams and the Philadelphia Eagles on October 4, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA.(Photo by Andy Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Panthers are back and they’re facing what’s left of the shockingly 2-3 Eagles as they return from a game in London just six days ago now. Tomorrow we’ll see if they are awake and healthy enough to contend with a Panthers squad that should be freshly rested from their early bye week. To see what other storylines and shenanigans we should be on the lookout for this week, I spoke with Brandon Lee Gowton of Bleeding Green Nation to get the inside scoop on the Eagles quarterback, running back, wide receiver, and edge injuries, among other concerns. It really does sound like only one team is going to walk into this game on two feet and that may surprisingly be the Carolina Panthers. Here’s what Brandon had to say. With Jalen Hurts out for the game, what’s next for the Eagles at quarterback? Tanner McKee will start against the Panthers. It’s been a pretty weird run for him dating back to Week 18 of last season. Prior to that regular season finale, there was optimism about McKee’s outlook. He had previously shined in preseason settings; so much so that the Eagles decided to rest him after their first preseason game last year. With the Eagles deciding to rest starters in Week 18, McKee got the start and there was hope that he might be able to beat the Washington Commanders. He looked good early on in the game before DeVonta Smith left … but then much less so afterwards. It seems like this performance shook the team’s confidence in him because they went out and acquired Andy Dalton from your Carolina Panthers. (Great deal by Dan Morgan.) It was originally thought that Dalton was only being brought in to be QB3 behind Jalen Hurts and McKee … but in OTAs it became apparent that there was a real QB2 battle going on. With neither candidate making a strong case over the other, that battle continued into the lead up of the Eagles’ Week 1 game. Dalton was Hurts’ backup for the first three weeks before his sole passing attempt with the team was intercepted in the end zone during the Eagles’ Week 3 loss. The Eagles then demoted Dalton to QB3 before cutting him. And that’s how we got to McKee becoming No. 2 again. It’s hard to predict how much time Hurts is going to miss due to his blood clot. McKee figures to be the starter until Hurts is back, if he even returns this season. Though it would seem like the Eagles could pivot to intriguing rookie Cole Payton at some point if they get knocked out of the playoff picture. Then again, the NFC East is looking so bad that the Eagles might hang around longer than expected. As for what Panthers fans can expect from McKee, I’m really not sure. He looked the worst I’ve ever seen him play during offseason practices and preseaosn games. He’s also going to be operating behind the Eagles’ patch-work offensive line while missing some key skill players. I can’t say I’m very confident that he’s going to play well. But I don’t want to write him off entirely until we see him in some regular season action because he has shown signs of promise in the past. UPDATE! As I was answering this question, the Eagles reportedly signed Dallas Cowboys practice squad quarterback Joe Milton to their roster. Guessing he’s the emergency third quarterback this week behind McKee and Payton? Your running back position looks about as injured as the Panthers’ [insert position here]. With the signing of training camp/practice squad running back Ja’Quinden Jackson, what do you expect the Eagles ground attack to look like on Sunday? Funny enough, they didn’t even sign Jackson (despite reporting that suggested otherwise after hosting him on a visit)! Not as of me typing this sentence, at least. They added Ian Wheeler to the practice squad instead. But, yeah, the Eagles are really thin at running back. It looks like their top three options are going to be out: 1) Saquon Barkley, 2) Tank Bigsby (on injured reserve, and 3) Will Shipley. That leaves the team with Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele, who were both called up from the practice squad last week. They also have Jaydon Blue and the aforementioned Wheeler on the practice squad now. The Eagles managed to gain just 22 yards on 18 carries in Week 5. Give the Jags’ run defense, which has been stingy this season (fewest yards per carry allowed), for being stout. But it’s hard to expect the Eagles to be awesome on the ground when their offensive line is dealing with a lot of key absences and they’re down to RB4 and RB5. I’m expecting the ground game to look a little better against the Panthers because … how much worse could it get than Week 5? That was the fewest rushing yards the Eagles have had in a game since Week 2 of the 2015 season. But there’s no good reason to expect it to fully click until we actually see it happen. Perhaps Panthers fans feel differently since Carolina is allowing the most yards per carry in the league. Speaking of injuries, the Panthers early season has so far been defined by them. Where are the Eagles hurting the most right now, besides running back, and how will that affect their game? The Eagles have 24 players listed on their injury report this week. Not ideal! Here are the key positions to monitor (outside of running back): WIDE RECEIVER — It sounds like DeVonta Smith might be able to play after being upgraded to limited in Thursday’s practice. But with Dontayvion Wicks being downgraded to not practicing, the Eagles might be without another starter as they’re getting their top target back. OFFENSIVE LINE — Lane Johnson retired and the Eagles traded Cam Jurgens, who was struggling anyway. The Eagles opened Landon Dickerson’s practice window to return from IR but they don’t seem to be in a rush to activate him. Drew Kendall, who was brought in from the bench to play center after Dickerson got hurt and they moved Jurgens to left guard, returned to practice on Thursday in a limited capacity. If he’s healthy, he’ll probably start at center. If not, look for Jake Majors — who made his NFL regular debut last week after being called up from the practice squad — to get the nod instead. Starting right guard Tyler Steen is banged up but it seems like he might be play. The Eagles’ projected starting offensive line for Sunday: LT Jordan Mailata (pretty good starter), LG Willie Lampkin (fan-favorite undersized blocker who struggled in pass pro making his first regular season start last week), C Jake Majors (fringe roster player), RG Tyler Steen (cromulent starter now playing at less than 100%), and RT Markel Bell (massive player who is playing like a third-round rookie, which he is). EDGE RUSHER — Starter Jalyx Hunt is out. He leads the Eagles in quarterback hits so far this season. The Eagles’ pass rush has already been lacking, so, missing him isn’t great. The Eagles are hoping Jonathan Greenard, who was limited in practice on Wednesday and Thursday, can return from an ankle injury. Rotational rusher A.J. Epenesa could also miss this week’s game. Arnold Ebiketie is also on the injury report, albeit as a full participant. The only Eagles edge rusher NOT on the injury report this week is Nolan Smith. There are loud rumbles from columnists and fans alike that the Eagles should consider “punting” on the still young 2026 season. What’s been wrong so far and might the Eagles be eyeing the wounded Panthers as a get-right game? I think a win here would be a pretty nice feeling for an Eagles team that’s endured a lot of chaos through the first six weeks of the season. Especially after nearly having the Los Angeles Rams beat in Week 4 and the Jacksonville Jaguars beat in Week 5. But I struggle to give this team the benefit of the doubt. While they’re not far off from being 4-1, they would be…

title: Panthers Injury Report & Transactions – Week 6
summary: The Carolina Panthers front office is busy throughout the season with transactions, roster moves, and injury updates. Here’s what’s happening at Mint Street this week. Injuries Finally, some good news on the injury front! Through their 2-2 start this year the Panthers have distinguished themselves as the most injured team in the NFL and it’s […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - SEPTEMBER 13: Keith Cooper Jr. #97 of the Miami Dolphins leaves the field after warmups against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Raiders defeated the Dolphins 27-13. (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Carolina Panthers front office is busy throughout the season with transactions, roster moves, and injury updates. Here’s what’s happening at Mint Street this week. Injuries Finally, some good news on the injury front! Through their 2-2 start this year the Panthers have distinguished themselves as the most injured team in the NFL and it’s impressive Carolina is playing .500 ball. Young stud wide receiver Jalen Coker is back after missing the Panthers last game. Running back Trevor Etienne has yet to make his 2026 debut and he is also listed as questionable after fully participating this week in practice. The biggest impact could be on the offensive line. Stalwart right tackle Taylor Moton has yet to play in 2026 due to blood clots and is listed as questionable after being a full participant in this week’s practices. Veteran guard Damien Lewis missed Carolina’s last game and is listed as questionable for Sunday but was a full participant in Friday’s practice. Also hoping to make his 2026 debut is veteran defensive tackle Tershawn Wharton who is now questionable with a neck injury. The Panthers bye last week gave other guys who have been dinged up to get some rest, including outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips and tight ends Tommy Tremble and Darren Waller. Right tackle Monroe Freeling is doubtful while running back AJ Dillon is out for Sunday. Transactions Signed DT Keith Cooper to the practice squad Cooper was a 2025 undrafted free agent who was signed by the Cleveland Browns and appeared in one game as a rookie with no stats. Earlier this year he joined the Miami Dolphins and has played in three games in 2026 with one tackle. Cooper played 29 defensive snaps and 16 on special teams for the Dolphins before he was released and signed this week by the Panthers. Released OLB Cam Gill from the practice squad Gill has been in and out of Carolina going back to 2024. Between 2020 and 2023 he appeared in 40 games for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers with 29 tackles and 2.5 sacks. In 2024 he came to Carolina and played in 10 games for the Panthers, registering a solid 22 tackles. That year he played 221 defensive snaps for the Panthers and 172 on special teams. He didn’t play in the NFL last year and has bounced around Carolina’s practice squad in 2026 without yet taking the field. Released DT Anthony Goodlow from the practice squad Goodlow was originally signed to the Panthers practice squad on September 1, 2026 and had managed to survive up to this point without getting waived then re-signed. But, here we are. The 26-year-old undrafted player spent most of 2024 on the Cardinals practice squad without playing in a game. Last year he had three tackles in three games for Arizona before coming to Carolina this year. He’s now once again on the move.

title: Brian Answers: Eagles woes, Panthers offensive gameplan, Bryce Young extension, and more!
summary: Hello CSR! Welcome to Brian Answers, part two of your weekly Panthers fan mailbag for everyone! We’re right back into Panthers football with a very winnable matchup on Sunday, albeit due to many injuries in Philadelphia. But the game keeps rolling and the cards keep getting dealt, all we can do is enjoy the fun […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 4: Bryce Young #9 of the Carolina Panthers celebrates after defeating the Detroit Lions following an NFL football game on October 4, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hello CSR! Welcome to Brian Answers, part two of your weekly Panthers fan mailbag for everyone! We’re right back into Panthers football with a very winnable matchup on Sunday, albeit due to many injuries in Philadelphia. But the game keeps rolling and the cards keep getting dealt, all we can do is enjoy the fun of the regular season. Let’s dive into your questions! JoshuaTreeTD: Do you think Dave and Brad will continue to switch up the offensive play style to attack any given opponents weakness from week to week? It felt like the Lions were not expecting such heavy RPO plays and it caught them fully off guard and Bryce executed it almost perfectly. What would you predict the play style will be to attack Philly? The Panthers have definitely been adaptive on offense. I think the formula of mixing in some deep shots with their usual run approach will continue, but I definitely see them running a lot of RPO this week against a pretty good Eagles front seven. This offense has been aggressive as far as trying to score points, so I do think I agree that they’ll have a unique game plan for each team they face. And that seemed to be the vision when they brought in Dave Canales. schrodingersblackcat: Will Bryce be the one to finally break our black jersey curse? I didn’t feel great about this game, but then Jalen Hurts was ruled out with a blood clot. Which, by the way, from one fan base to another, I hope he recovers in short order and has no complications. These types of things make you realize there’s more to life than the next week of football, and I hope Hurts gets all the treatment he needs and doesn’t have any negative impact on his life as a person. That said, this is definitely a game where the Panthers should have every chance to win it, in convincing fashion. And knowing their recent history as a franchise, they might drop the ball and lose this game. Cause Panthers fans can never have nice things. Aleins4u: If you had a offensive oriented head coach, would you rather: Have a good, but not great DC, who frequently gets HC interviews but never gets the job A series of great DCs, but each only lasts 2 years before getting poached for a HC job And same question, except a defensive oriented head coach and OCs. The core of the question is, would you rather a good quality, consistent approach on the side of the ball the HC has less knowledge about, or a constantly but shifting great approach that might require different player types. I’m all for having coordinators on both sides of the ball that are so good that they move on to higher positions. I think you have to maximize every coach you have, because they can be poached at any moment. I would rather have coordinators that prove themselves worthy of going off to make more money and take on more responsibility, because the best franchises in the NFL tend to expect this and try to give development reps to the guys they have in the trenches behind them. I’d much rather have a coordinator that helps this team win a Super Bowl than someone who isn’t excellent enough to get them there, but still sticks around because other teams don’t feel he can take them to the next level. The name of the game is winning in this league, win the championship and figure out the repercussions after the fact. Mozzie11: The NFC South has been the worst division for years with winners having losing records at times. This year the NFC East is throwing their hat the ring for worst. Panthers and Eagles is just part of the epic battle. Which division ‘wins’ the title this year? I do think the NFC South will continue its recent history of getting the least deserving team a playoff berth. The Panthers have been very good, but they are still up and down. The Falcons are on an upward trajectory. The Saints are 2-3 unexpected wins away from joining them at the top of the division. The NFC East is certainly in the same playing field, but I think one of those teams will jump far ahead of the rest. Which team that is at this juncture, I don’t know. @WTMealey: Are we eyeballing the entire NFC playoff picture now or just the South? Like is it silly to be glad the Rams lost last night? BTW do we have rivalry with them now? But really are we rooting for AFC teams to beat top 10 NFC teams to help our likelihood of having 2 home playoff games or ….? Is it too soon? I think bolshy in the comments answered this better than I could: “I wouldn’t eyeball anything but Philly right now”. This Panthers team is showing a great deal if promise, but I’d be more concerned with the games they win than other contenders losing. They may change that mindset in the coming weeks, but I’m not ready to do that right now. I’ve been hurt too many times. Brazilian Panther: Pick one between the OG movie Carrie from 76, the remake with Chloe Grace Moretz from 2013 or Mike Flanagan’s 2026 mini series on Prime Video Brian. I just watched the series this past weekend and I really liked what they came up with. Cheers To be fully transparent, I haven’t watched even a little of the new mini-series. So I can’t make a ruling on that, but I’ve heard nothing but good things about it. Sound off down below in the comments if you have, and what your thoughts on it. I’m very much a fan of the original, but I liked both of the first two iterations. casualpanthersfan: The panthers are currently averaging 30.3 point per game. Would you take the over or under on the panthers point total this week? I will always preface these questions with the same statement; I do not bet real money on the Panthers because they always do the opposite of what I think. And if I think they’ll do the opposite of what the regular media thinks they’ll do, I also lose most of the time. Don’t bet on the Panthers, your mental health will thank you. But gun to my head, this is still a strong Eagles defense. I think it will be an ugly low scoring game. Bruce Guild: Brian, we’re giving up 5.4 yards a carry so far, but Philly just lost Lane Johnson to retirement, traded Jurgens, has Dickerson on IR, and ran for only 22 yards in London without Saquon. Is this the week Evero’s front finally gets right against the run, or does our run D get exposed anyway? And with both starting corners on IR, do they load the box, make Hurts beat them throwing, and trust Will Lee and Evans one-on-one? This week will be interesting, and thank you for the Grok question . Jalen Hurts suddenly being out changes the whole dynamic of this game, and I’m not sure if Saquon Barkley or Devonta Smith ends up playing given this development. They are both banged up and the Eagles might elect to just rest them both because of the dire situation. But if the Eagles do come out aggressive, I expect Ejiro Evero to be very aggressive blitzing like he has been this season. And if Saquon plays I expect the focus will be to contain him, just like the focus against the Lions and Gibbs. Bull123: Injuries…who plays on OL?…Coker?…Phillips? Are we stuck with Evans? Seems like Taylor Moton could be back, but I think the coaching staff plays it safe with him after his health issues. Monroe Freeling is still dealing with his knee issue in week 4, and while he got a limited practice on Thursday I don’t know where he’s at. So we might be seeing Stone Forsythe starting just to not rush anyone back. I expect the guard situation on the OL to remain the same. Jalen Coker is all go for Sunday. We’ll have to wait on Jaelan Phillips but he’s logged two limited practices this week. I assume you’re referring to Akayleb Evans with the last part, and I don’t expect his role to change too much. The Panthers seem to be wading out this period of having their top 2 CBs hurt until mid season. LouWillVille: Once Moton and Freeling…

title: Chicago Bears Week 6 Flashbacks: A meltdown, a milestone, and a breakout
summary: 1. 2006, Bears @ Cardinals: They Are Who We Thought They Were! October 16, 2006 | Bears win 24-23 There are weird wins, and then there is what happened in Arizona on Monday Night Football in 2006. The Bears entered Week 6 undefeated at 5-0 and looking like one of the best teams in football. […]
full_text: A Jay Cutler pass to Matt Forte with 18 seconds left in the game put the Chicago Bears ahead 18-17 on Sunday, Oct. 11, 2015, at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Mo. (Keith Myers/Kansas City Star/Tribune News Service via Getty Images) 1. 2006, Bears @ Cardinals: They Are Who We Thought They Were! October 16, 2006 | Bears win 24-23 There are weird wins, and then there is what happened in Arizona on Monday Night Football in 2006. The Bears entered Week 6 undefeated at 5-0 and looking like one of the best teams in football. By halftime, none of that seemed to matter. Arizona had built a 20-0 lead while Rex Grossman and the Chicago offense completely unraveled. Grossman eventually finished just 14-of-37 for 144 yards, four interceptions and two lost fumbles. The Bears offense never scored a touchdown. Somehow, Chicago still won. The comeback began when Mark Anderson stripped Matt Leinart and Mike Brown recovered the fumble for a touchdown. Later, Brian Urlacher ripped the football away from Edgerrin James, allowing Charles Tillman to scoop it up and race 40 yards for another defensive score. That still left the Bears trailing 23-17 with under three minutes remaining. Enter Devin Hester. Hester fielded a punt at his own 17-yard line, found daylight and took it 83 yards for the go-ahead touchdown, completing one of the most ridiculous comebacks in franchise history. Arizona still had a chance to win, but Neil Rackers missed a 40-yard field goal in the closing seconds, allowing Chicago to escape with a 24-23 victory. The numbers make the result even harder to believe. The Bears committed six turnovers, gained only 168 yards and did not score an offensive touchdown. Urlacher finished with 19 tackles and forced the fumble that completely changed the game. Of course, the night became even more memorable after Cardinals coach Dennis Green stepped to the podium and delivered one of the most famous postgame rants in NFL history. “They are who we thought they were!” He wasn’t wrong. The Bears were 6-0. 2. 2014, Bears @ Falcons: Cutler leads Chicago to its 750th victory October 12, 2014 | Bears win 27-13 The Bears entered Week 6 desperately needing to get things moving in the right direction. Back-to-back losses had dropped Chicago to 2-3, and a road trip to Atlanta presented another difficult challenge against Matt Ryan and a dangerous Falcons offense. Instead, Jay Cutler put together one of his best performances in a Bears uniform. Cutler completed 26-of-38 passes for 381 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions, setting what would stand as his highest single-game passing total during his time in Chicago. He had plenty of help from his receivers. Alshon Jeffery caught five passes for 136 yards, while Brandon Marshall added six receptions for 113. Matt Forte once again did a little bit of everything, finishing with 80 rushing yards, 77 receiving yards and two touchdowns. Chicago led 13-3 at halftime, but Atlanta erased that advantage with 10 unanswered points in the third quarter. With the game tied at 13, Cutler delivered the play that swung momentum back toward the Bears. Facing third-and-long, he launched a deep ball down the sideline to Jeffery, who hauled it in for a 74-yard gain. Forte scored a touchdown shortly afterward, and Chicago never trailed again. The Bears defense shut Atlanta out in the fourth quarter, while Forte added another touchdown to finish off a 27-13 victory. Cutler’s performance and the win itself were already noteworthy, but the afternoon also carried some franchise history. The victory was the 750th regular-season win in Chicago Bears history, making them the first NFL franchise to reach that mark. A big road win, Cutler throwing for nearly 400 yards, and another number added to one of the league’s oldest franchises. Not a bad afternoon in Atlanta. 3. 2024, Bears vs. Jaguars: Caleb Williams shines in London October 13, 2024 | Bears win 35-16 The Bears traveled across the Atlantic in Week 6 of Caleb Williams’ rookie season with some momentum beginning to build. By the time they left London, that momentum had turned into one of Williams’ first real statement performances as an NFL quarterback. Jacksonville actually struck first and held a 3-0 lead after the opening quarter, but Chicago quickly took control. Williams found Cole Kmet for a 31-yard touchdown early in the second quarter before connecting with him again from two yards out just before halftime. The Bears went into the locker room leading 14-3 and never really looked back. Williams continued spreading the football around after halftime, this time finding Keenan Allen for a pair of touchdowns as Chicago’s lead continued to grow. He finished the afternoon 23-of-29 for 226 yards, four touchdowns and one interception, while also causing problems with his legs by rushing for another 56 yards. It was the first four-touchdown passing game of Williams’ young career. Kmet caught five passes for 70 yards and two touchdowns, Allen added two scores of his own, and D’Andre Swift rushed for 91 yards and another touchdown as Chicago rolled to a 35-16 victory. Kmet’s afternoon deserves a little extra appreciation as well. When long snapper Scott Daly suffered a knee injury, Kmet suddenly found himself pulling double duty. Not only did he lead the Bears in receiving and catch two touchdowns, he also stepped in as Chicago’s emergency long snapper. Because apparently catching touchdowns in London wasn’t enough. The win moved Chicago to 4-2 and gave the Bears their third straight victory, while Williams walked away with the first four-touchdown game of hit young career. For Bears fans watching from back home, waking up early turned out to be worth it. Gary Baugher Jr. is a second year contributor to WCG, bringing football insight backed by over 16 years of experience in organized football and more than 30 years as a passionate fan of the game. You can follow him on Twitter at @iamcogs .

title: NFL predictions: Bears will bounce back big against the Falcons
summary: I know some Chicago Bears fans are down after that loss to the Green Bay Packers, but was Week 1 really that long ago? Are we letting the game in the pouring rain and three straight starts by backup quarterbacks cloud our outlook for the Bears? After an offseason of real hope, hype, and anticipation, […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - SEPTEMBER 13: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears reacts after a touchdown is scored during the first quarter against the Carolina Panthers of the game at Bank of America Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) | Getty Images I know some Chicago Bears fans are down after that loss to the Green Bay Packers, but was Week 1 really that long ago? Are we letting the game in the pouring rain and three straight starts by backup quarterbacks cloud our outlook for the Bears? After an offseason of real hope, hype, and anticipation, Caleb Williams and the Chicago offense dropped 59 points in a road game to kick off the year. Sure, the defense was exposed a bit, but the Bears were the talk of the NFL. After that Week 1 performance, the offseason buzz around Williams as a dark-horse Most Valuable Player candidate ramped up even more, as a bunch of money poured in on him to win MVP, thus lowering the odds. Then a tough battle against an aggressive Minnesota Vikings defense came in a downpour, and Williams was carted off. Most thought the season was doomed, but the injury wasn’t season-ending, and the Bears regrouped to go 2-1 in Caleb’s absence. Week 6 for the Bears is a road game against the Atlanta Falcons, and our partners at FanDuel Sportsbook currently have the Bears at -1.5, with the over/under at 51.5. A road favorite with some uncertainty at quarterback is exactly what the Bears were one week ago, and we all remember how that one turned out. But this time, the talk is positive about Caleb starting for the first time since Week 2. He practiced on Thursday, said he could do everything, had another practice today, and was full again, presumably with no setbacks. Assuming he plays*, I like the Bears to win and cover the 1.5 points. I also like the over on the total because Atlanta’s offense will get theirs. I also like the over on Williams’ passing yards, set at 225.5 by FanDuel. There’s still plenty of season left, so if you think Caleb can get his MVP case back on track, those odds are at +10,000. Not gonna lie, a few bucks on that at those odds could be a fun one to monitor. *If the Williams doesn’t play, I still like the Bears to win and cover, but I’d stay away from the total. title: Bears at Falcons: 3 Props to Play
summary: We are back with 3 props to consider playing this week as the Bears head to Atlanta to take on the Falcons. Last week we had an unfortunate 1-2 record, which dropped our season record to 7-8. Certainly not taking names like we have the last two years, but we still have plenty of time […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 04: Colston Loveland #84 of the Chicago Bears prepares for a play during the fourth quarter against the New York Jets at Soldier Field on October 04, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Jessie Alcheh/Getty Images) | Getty Images We are back with 3 props to consider playing this week as the Bears head to Atlanta to take on the Falcons. Last week we had an unfortunate 1-2 record, which dropped our season record to 7-8. Certainly not taking names like we have the last two years, but we still have plenty of time to turn this one around. Caleb Williams is set to return, which should be a boost to the offense, but the Bears defense is banged up, which could open the door for some big gains on the Falcons side of the ball. Here are this week’s plays. As always, odds courtesy of FanDuel. Bijan Robinson OVER 90.5 Rushing Yards -114 I hate putting this one in the article, but how can I not? The Bears’ run defense hasn’t been overly stout this year. Even when the defense was playing better, now we have a situation where Montez Sweat, TJ Edwards, and Dayo Odeyingbo are going to miss this game. The Bears’ front seven is definitely hurting, and it just feels like Robinson is destined to have a big game. Colston Loveland OVER 36.5 Receiving Yards -114 The Colston Loveland breakout game has to be coming, so why not have it come against the Falcons? After having only 3 receiving yards in his first two games. It’s not like Loveland has been on fire, but he does have 107 yards over his last three games, which averages out to 35.8 yards per game. With Caleb Williams getting back behind center, it feels like this is where Loveland could break out and put some bigger numbers on the board. I’m not sure if he’s cracking 100 yards or anything, but I feel like he should easily get north of 50 or 60 yards this week, and there’s a good chance he finds the endzone. Kalif Raymond OVER 24.5 Receiving Yards -114 When Kalif Raymond played with Caleb Williams and Case Keenum, he had games of 90, 84, and 40 yards. When he played with Tyson Bagent, he had two games where he had a total of 5 catches for 12 yards. For whatever reason, Bagent couldn’t work the ball to Raymond. But Caleb Williams should be back, and if he is, how can you not like Caleb working the ball back to Raymond? I’m not saying Raymond has a massive game, but it feels like he can comfortably go over 40 or 50 yards this week.

title: Is Chicago Bears’ secondary the team’s biggest concern?

title: Bears vs. Falcons Injury Report: Caleb Williams is Questionable
summary: The Chicago Bears and the Atlanta Falcons have released their game-day injury reports, and there’s good news for both starting quarterbacks. Chicago’s Caleb Williams (hamstring) logged a third straight full practice, while Atlanta’s Michael Penix Jr. also practiced fully all week after leaving his last game with a rib injury. However, the Bears list Williams […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 20: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears stands on the sideline during the national anthem prior to the game against the Minnesota Vikings at Soldier Field on September 20, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears and the Atlanta Falcons have released their game-day injury reports, and there’s good news for both starting quarterbacks. Chicago’s Caleb Williams (hamstring) logged a third straight full practice, while Atlanta’s Michael Penix Jr. also practiced fully all week after leaving his last game with a rib injury. However, the Bears list Williams as questionable, while Penix has no injury designation for Sunday’s game and is expected to start. At his pre-practice press conference, head coach Ben Johnson didn’t address whether Williams was starting or not, and he said, “I’m hopeful we’ll have more clarity at the end of the day today. He (Williams) looked good yesterday for one practice, but we’ve got to be able to stack a few back to back.” Assuming there were no setbacks, and given the full practice, Williams seems in line to start, but they’ll have a walk-through tomorrow to make sure there are no lingering effects from the injury. Also questionable for the Bears are corners Tyrique Stevenson (hip) and Kyler Gordon (calf), who is still on the PUP list. Stevenson was limited all week, while Gordon was full. If Gordon isn’t activated for Atlanta’s game, he’ll need to be activated next week when his 21-day practice window expires. The Bears have ruled out linebackers T.J. Edwards (hamstring) and Keyshaun Elliott (quadricep), running back Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe), and defensive lineman Dayo Odeyingbo (quadricep), Johnson also said there’s a chance that left tackle Ozzy Trapilo could make his season debut on Sunday, adding, “We think he’s really close.” The Falcons only have two players on their injury report: starting cornerback C.J. Henderson (groin) is out, and veteran defensive end Za’Darius Smith (neck) is questionable and was limited at today’s practice.
