title: Bears at Falcons Q&A: Caleb back? Can the Bears stop Bijan and Drake?
summary: We are back with our 5-question series, and this time we spoke with a real person! Last week, of course, our friends at ACME Packing Company couldn’t be reached to participate in a Q&A, so we did one with AI. This week, the Bears head to Atlanta to face the Falcons. This week, we spoke […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - OCTOBER 05: Bijan Robinson #7 of the Atlanta Falcons runs the ball for to score a 59 yard touchdown against the New Orleans Saints during the first quarter of the game at Caesars Superdome on October 05, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Morgan Simmons/Getty Images) | Getty Images We are back with our 5-question series, and this time we spoke with a real person! Last week, of course, our friends at ACME Packing Company couldn’t be reached to participate in a Q&A, so we did one with AI. This week, the Bears head to Atlanta to face the Falcons. This week, we spoke with Jeanna Kelley of The Falconholic (SB Nation’s Atlanta Falcons site) to get you ready for the matchup. Here’s that Q&A. 1. When Michael Penix was out, the Falcons looked like one of the worst teams in the league, but with Penix, it’s an entirely different team that could potentially win the South. Is Penix that much better, or are the other three QBs that horrible? You know that old saying, if you have two quarterbacks, you have no quarterbacks? Well, apparently in Atlanta, if you have four quarterbacks on the 53-man roster, you actually have ONE quarterback. Michael Penix Jr., in my opinion, is the only starting-caliber QB on the roster. Cooper Rush has a ton of experience as a backup, and his game experience made him the best choice when Penix wasn’t physically ready and Tua Tagovailoa hurt his oblique right before Week 1. But there’s a reason Rush has a ton of experience as a backup and not a starter. Jack Strand, the rookie undrafted free agent out of Minnesota Moorhead who showed real promise in the preseason, is on the active roster because the Falcons believe he has potential and they don’t want him poached off the practice squad, but he needs plenty of development before he can be considered a viable option. If you were watching Sunday Night Football last week when the Falcons lost to the Ravens, you saw how the game ended when Penix left the game with a rib injury, and Tua finished things out in overtime with a pick that handed the win to Baltimore. My biggest concern with Tua is his concussion history, because I want him to have a long, happy, and healthy life outside of football. But I also have real questions about whether he’s physically able to play at a high level at this point of his career. 2. Bijan Robinson and Drake London seem to be decent players. If the Bears are going to try and contain them at all, what is the best way for Dennis Allen’s defense to approach that? I think the Bears have to expect that both Bijan Robinson and Drake London will make plays. They’re exceptional athletes, and containing them is hard even for extremely talented defenders. Penix can process through his reads quickly, but the blitz—which the Bears use often—can disrupt him. It might be a little trickier with Montez Sweat out, but I do think the Bears D will be able to shake him up a little bit, which will impact his ability to get the ball out to London/other receivers. While I do think Penix is healthy enough to play after speaking with him Wednesday, I’m not certain the rib injury won’t impact him at all on Sunday. With the run game, my ongoing concern is the predictability with only two guys on the depth chart. Bijan is ridiculous, but he is human. He’s such a focal point in Atlanta’s offense that if teams are able to key in on him and slow him down, it can throw the entire game plan off. 3. When the Bears decided to trade Gervon Dexter to Atlanta, most Bears fans weren’t pleased. He may not have been in Chicago’s long-term plans, but he was one of their better defensive lineman. From afar, he seems like he’s played well thus far. How has he looked? Falcons players, coaches, media, and fans all LOVE Gervon Dexter Sr., and we’re delighted the team already extended him. He’s been excellent for Atlanta. PFF has him graded at 81.9 so far for the season, which ranks him fourth in the league among interior DL players — PFF grades never tell the whole story, but those numbers match the eye test. He’s been really generous with his time for the media and seems very grateful to be here. My favorite story from him came after his extension — he got the call as he was driving his son somewhere, and his son immediately started thinking of all the toys his dad could spend that money on. Dexter has been complimentary about his time with the Bears, and has mentioned the fact that Ian Cunningham wanted him here and what that means to him, and he also mentioned how happy Grady Jarrett was for him when he was traded to the Falcons. It seems like a really good fit for him and for the team. 4. This has nothing to do with the game, but it was a hot topic for us Bears fans in the spring, so I want to ask… Did Falcons fans feel that the Bears should have received two comp picks for the hiring of Ian Cunningham? I know the rule is “top football executive,” which is technically Matt Ryan, but we all know that Cunningham is the guy making the calls. I enthusiastically agree with Bears fans that Chicago deserved compensatory picks for losing Ian Cunningham. Matt Ryan is highly intelligent, is a fast learner, and I believe he is doing an outstanding job as President, and I’m delighted to have him back in the building, but Ian has the experience and the success in an executive role, and Matt Ryan is learning from him. I personally think it’s shady as hell that the Bears didn’t get comp picks for Ian, and I think it’s disrespectful to Ian and the Bears. 5. How do you think this one plays out on Sunday? This is always the most difficult question to answer about the Atlanta Falcons. I have this one penciled in as a loss for Atlanta, but I think it will be close. 28-24 Bears.

title: Bears-Falcons: Offensive fireworks key to Chicago victory
summary: The Chicago Bears are hitting the road for the second straight week. On Sunday, they will face the Atlanta Falcons. The Falcons have unlocked their offense with the return of quarterback Michael Penix. He has the offense humming with the help of playmakers Bijan Robinson and Drake London. It will be a game of draftmates. […]
full_text: Aug 14, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Atlanta Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa (1) and quarterback Michael Penix Jr. (9) warm up before a game against the Denver Broncos at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Chicago Bears are hitting the road for the second straight week. On Sunday, they will face the Atlanta Falcons. The Falcons have unlocked their offense with the return of quarterback Michael Penix. He has the offense humming with the help of playmakers Bijan Robinson and Drake London. It will be a game of draftmates. Penix was selected seven spots after Caleb Williams. But unlike when the Bears play the Patriots next week or if they were to face Washington again, this matchup seems to be flying under the radar a bit. What is it going to take for the Bears to bounce back from their bad loss and get the win on the road? Points… Our crew weighs in. Sam: The home/road splits from the defense are obvious going back to last year. Containing Bijan Robinson and Drake London is paramount to the Bears staying in this game. Having Caleb back would be great, but don’t forget there’s a Thursday night short week looming. Hopefully, getting Monangai and Swift healthy enough to keep the TOP on Chicago’s side will keep Atlanta’s weapons sidelined and the defense fresh. ECD: Offense – Let Caleb cook (if cleared) and balance out his return with a good effort on the ground. If Caleb is not cleared… put Case Keenum in. We don’t need to see Tyson Bagent again unless it’s for a ceremonial kneel-down. Defense – Do… something. Anything positive on the road would be a win. And make a trade for a difference maker while you’re at it. Special Teams – Let’s see what we have in Zavion Thomas as both a punt and kick returner. He’s been gradually improving his average and had a big one against the Packers. Josh: The basic key to the game is Chicago needs to stop trying to make fetch happen. Tyson Bagent is not a starter, and the defense is not a unit that can stop the run and defend the pass at the same time. If Caleb Williams can start, then Ben just needs to let 18 do his thing while DA stacks the box to limit Robinson. Iceman can win a passing duel for Chicago so long as Roush and Thomas aren’t forced into the rotation instead of actual good players. If it’s Keenum, then Ben will need to lean on Kmet, Raymond, and Burden more. DGooch – Keys to the Game – defend the back third of the field. Don’t turn the ball over. Limit, to the extent possible, Bijan’s impact (yes, stack the box). But truly, the key to the game is to get Caleb back, healthy, and playing up to his potential. Do that, and find someone other than Roschon Johnson to run the ball, and the Bears have a good chance to get the taste of that last game out of our collective mouths. Jeff Berckes: Manufacture pressure on Michael Penix if he starts. He’ll be carrying a rib injury from last Sunday and he’s already uncomfortable when heated up. If it’s Tua, well, same story and watch the turnovers roll in. Don’t give either time to pick you apart. On offense, can we get a wellness check on Colston Loveland? This might be the time for Caleb to show off that arm talent early and often. What do you think it will take to beat the Falcons? Let us know in the comments.

title: A Possible Approach to the NFL Trade Deadline for the Chicago Bears
summary: Introduction The Chicago Bears need to pursue a number of aggressive trades to build up the defense and the run game before the November trade deadline. To be clear, this is not because trading premium picks for defenders is a smart team-building strategy. It usually is not, as indicated by a number of recent trades […]
full_text: Introduction The Chicago Bears need to pursue a number of aggressive trades to build up the defense and the run game before the November trade deadline. To be clear, this is not because trading premium picks for defenders is a smart team-building strategy. It usually is not, as indicated by a number of recent trades where teams sent away valuable assets to gain players in pursuit of “a playoff push” only to have injury or misfortune derail a season (or two). No, the fundamental reason the Bears need to pursue such trades is that Ryan Poles cannot be allowed to pick in the third and fourth rounds of the NFL Draft again. This is illustrated by his selections of Velus Jones, Zacch Pickens, Roschon Johnson, Tyler Scott, Tory Taylor, Ruben Hyppolyte II, Sam Roush, and Zavion Thomas. Against this there is Malik Muhammad, who is very promising, but the odds are simply against trusting Poles with these selections. Additionally, he should not be allowed to pick defensive players in the second round of the draft, as proven by Kyler Gordon (who is beginning to resemble the Easter Bunny and Sasquatch at this point), Jaquan Brisker (no longer on the team), Tyrique Stevenson (unfortunately still on the team), Gervon Dexter (no longer on the team), and Shemar Turner (Schrodinger’s Bear – both on and off the team). An argument could be made that he should be allowed to make selections in the first round of the draft, because so far that has gone relatively well. Unfortunately, though, allowing Poles access to a first-round pick would give him the potential to trade down into the second round or worse, the dreaded third round. Therefore, those picks must also be sent away. This means that while the following suggestions have the benefit of improving the defense, the goal is keeping Poles from making more poor selections that fans will have to face, tolerate, justify, or debate depending on their preferences. 2027 Round 1 Selection Reflexively, it makes sense to trade this selection for a defensive tackle. For example, the Titans are struggling, and while they are likely committed to Cam Ward for 2027, it seems obvious that they will need a backup plan in place for 2028. Could Chicago make Mike Borgonzi an offer too good to refuse in an attempt to land Jeffery Simmons? If the Titans were a well-run organization, yes. However, there is no sign that the team will be willing to part with their $105million All-Pro. This means, then, that Chicago needs to deal with a more practical and ruthless general manager. Enter Howie Roseman of the Philadelphia Eagles. Cooper DeJean was arguably the best defensive player in the 2024 NFL Draft, and he has already helped the Eagles win a Super Bowl. There are two years left on his rookie contract, and he’s been elite. Still, Roseman has proven time and again that he is willing to take the long-term view to team building. He has already seen his elite right tackle retire (and has to keep him on the roster for cap purposes) while also sending away his starting center. Now it’s time to make it easier for him to replace Lane Johnson while solving one of Chicago’s biggest weaknesses. Chicago Sends: 2027 CHI R1 + 2028 CHI R2 Chicago Receives: CB Cooper DeJean + 2028 PHI R5 2027 Round 2 Selection The Chargers are in a tailspin and Joe Hortiz is going to have to make decisions about the team’s future before he has that opportunity taken away from him. In some ways, the emotionally satisfying move is for Chicago to offer a 4th-round pick in exchange for the last half-season (more or less) of Khalil Mack’s current contract. That’s high compared to recent estimates, but Chicago has also been put in a tight spot by Montez Sweat’s PED suspension and other GMs know it. A more appealing option is for the Bears to make an offer for Tuli Tuipulotu, in the last year of his contract and at a negotiations dead end with the team that drafted him. Tuipulotu could command a similar deal to what the Commanders received for Montez Sweat when he was traded to Chicago, but remember that a 2nd-rounder from Chicago in 2024 was far earlier than one in 2027 will hopefully be, and Tuipolotu already has a Pro Bowl and a 13-sack season under his belt. Therefore, this proposal adds a sweetener by exchanging a pesky 3rd-round pick in 2028 for a much more palatable 5th-rounder. Remember that the Bears have multiple players who can be cut to free up cap space, even leaving aside restructures, if such a trade were to happen and an extension would be needed. Chicago Sends: 2027 CHI R2 + 2028 CHI R3 Chicago Receives: Tuli Tuipulotu + 2028 LAC R5 2027 Round 3 Selection The Bears need a powerful run game, and Roschon Johnson (notably a 4th-round selection) is not able to provide the extra depth they need. Already, an injury to Kyle Monangai has revealed how thin the Bears are at halfback. Therefore, it’s finally time to reach out to the Tennessee Titans. Supposedly, the Titans are not interested in trading Tony Pollard and it would take a strong offer to move them off of that position. However, Chicago is in a position to make that kind of strong offer for the former 4th-round pick. Pollard has been able to amass at least a thousand yards from scrimmage for the last five seasons, and if Chicago needs three tight ends, it certainly needs three running backs. Chicago Sends: CHI 2027 R3 Chicago Receives: Tony Pollard 2027 Round 4 Selection So far, this proposal has done nothing to improve the interior of the defensive line, which is arguably the greatest weakness of the team. Fortunately, there are many struggling teams in the NFL. Grady Jarrett is currently 6th in ESPN’s pass rush win rate and 2nd in run stop win rate, but he is the only member of the defensive line consistently delivering at a high level. Enter the Washington Commanders, coming off of the most mind-numbing tie game imaginable and in need for a reset. Daron Payne is in the last year of his contract, and he arguably would need a new contract. However, it’s possible to leave any such move for later. Instead, Chicago could simply take on Payne and see how the season plays out for the 29-year-old. If he plays closer to his in-season performance (with a 1.6-yard depth-of-tackle and a 10+% pressure rate), he might earn an extension. If he’s closer to 2025 (with a sub 9% pressure rate and just over 2 yards allowed before a tackle on average), then the Bears can let him walk. To sweeten the deal for both sides, a pick-swap in 2028 rounds out the proposal of a 4th-rounder. Chicago Sends: CHI 2027 R4 + CHI 2028 R4 Chicago Receives: Daron Payne + WAS 2028 R5 Conclusions As should be obvious, with a small amount of grinding it is possible to make sure that Ryan Poles will not be able to make a draft selection in the second, third, or fourth round of 2027. This same approach also gets rid of the native second-, third-, and fourth-round selections of Chicago in 2028 while strengthening their draft power in the vital fifth round there (the “Braxton Jones/Austin Booker” zone, as it were). This has to be considered a victory for the Bears. It also addresses three key needs on defense and strengthens a vital aspect of the offense. The alternative to this sort of action is to believe that a team that is 3-2 this season and 14-8 since the arrival of the new head coach will figure it out, and that the limitations of the general manager will resolve without such dramatic action. The team went 2-1 with backup quarterbacks and is tied for the fifth-fewest points allowed on the season. It might be too early to panic and to functionally trade away multiple drafts. But where’s the fun in that?

title: Prospects of interest for the Bengals in the Ohio State vs. Indiana game
summary: With the Bengals on a bye week this week, and Ohio State traveling to face the defending National Champion Indiana Hoosiers, it feels like a good time to sneak a little draft talk into the mix. There are a ton of talented skill position players in this game, including Heisman favorite Jeremiah Smith. However, the […]
full_text: With the Bengals on a bye week this week, and Ohio State traveling to face the defending National Champion Indiana Hoosiers, it feels like a good time to sneak a little draft talk into the mix. There are a ton of talented skill position players in this game, including Heisman favorite Jeremiah Smith. However, the Bengals are not going to be in the market for a first round wide receiver. Even if they were, they are not going to be in a position to take Smith. Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh are ultra-talented receiver prospects for the Hoosiers, but enough about the skill players. Austin Siereveld Siereveld has played all over the line for the Buckeyes the last few seasons. He has experience playing everywhere but center for Ohio State. Ultimately, his best position may be at guard at the next level. The Bengals Dalton Risner is playing good football, but is scheduled to be a free agent after the season. The Bengals drafted Brian Parker II in the sixth round, and he will have an opportunity to be a future starter somewhere on the Bengals line. When you want to compete for Super Bowls, you will need depth on the offensive line regardless. A player like Siereveld with his versatility should be of interest to every team in the league. Austin Siereveld (#67) Ohio State ✅ Positional versatility ✅ Leg drive as a run blocker ✅ Plays with good technique ✅ 83.3 run blocking grade in 2025 ✅ Allowed 15 pressures and 0 sacks during the 2025 season pic.twitter.com/WKtFnM7ZPk — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) June 4, 2026 Amare Ferrell Jordan Battle is coming off a really solid performance against Miami. However, that doesn’t take away from some of his early-season struggles in the secondary this season. Battle still misses too many tackles and is scheduled to be a free agent after the season. The Bengals could decide to bring in another day two safety to fill his spot. Amare Ferrell is an experienced safety prospect for the Hoosiers, having already eclipsed 2,000 snaps during his career. He has good enough size for the position at 6’2” and 205 pounds. He possesses impressive ball skills with 8 interceptions over the previous two seasons. Ferrell is a player to keep an eye on at safety. The Buckeyes have a couple of players at the position that could be mid-round draft selections also. Those guys are Earl Little Jr. and Jaylen McClain. Amare Ferrell will be entering his 3rd season as a starter. He has 8 interceptions over the last two seasons. He has a high football IQ, good size at 6’2” and 210 pounds, and an 82.8 coverage grade in 2025. pic.twitter.com/8D1qL7oS85 — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) May 3, 2026 Jermaine Mathews Mathews is another experienced defensive back. He has played over 1,600 career snaps earlier at corner. He has the flexibility to play in the slot or on the outside. He currently has a 76.0 coverage grade during the 2026 season. He played pretty well going up against the Texas Longhorns’ talented receivers during week two. This week will be another big test for Mathews against Becker and Marsh. Mathews doesn’t have the greatest size at around 5’11” and 195 pounds, but he is a physical player. Mathews is a more than willing tackler, instinctive in zone coverage, and should test fairly well at the combine this year. The Bengals will have a decision to make at corner with both DJ Turner and Dax Hill scheduled to hit free agency after the season. Even if they bring both of those guys back, you can never have too much depth at the corner position. I would expect an early-round investment at the position come April. title: Bengals Bye Week Awards: Unsung Hero
summary: We’re continuing our Cincinnati Bengals Bye Week Awards with a look at who’s been the team’s unsung hero through five games. The MVP debates get the headlines. full_text: We’re continuing our Cincinnati Bengals Bye Week Awards with a look at who’s been the team’s unsung hero through five games. The MVP debates get the headlines. This one’s for the guys who stepped in when Colbie Young went down on the first play in Pittsburgh, when Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins both left the Jacksonville game, and when the safety room got thin. Here are the nominees who keep showing up without anyone noticing. Samaje Perine, RB : 27 carries for 110 yards (4.1 per carry, best among the backs), seven catches for 61 yards and a touchdown. In Miami, he led the team with 68 rushing yards and caught a touchdown out of the backfield. Joe Burrow called him “Mr. Reliable” after the game and said he “doesn’t get enough credit.” That’s the definition of this award. Dohnte Meyers, WR/KR : 13 catches for 141 yards as the next man up in a receiver room dealing with injuries to Young, Chase and Higgins. He also opened the Miami game with an 81-yard kickoff return that set up the first touchdown 52 seconds in. Evan McPherson, K : Named AFC Special Teams Player of the Month and given a game ball after the Miami win. Kickers only get noticed when they miss. “Money Mac” hasn’t given anyone a reason to notice. Jonathan Allen, DE : Eight tackles, three sacks, one forced fumble. Allen has been a great addition to this defensive line and is quietly tied for the team lead in sacks (three) and has the third-most pressures (16). Who’s the player you think nobody’s talking about? Offensive line, special teams, a backup DB? Make your case.

title: Bengals Bye Week Awards: Most Improved Returning Player
summary: With the bye week here, it’s time for some awards for the Cincinnati Bengals through the first five games of the 2026 season, starting with the most improved player. The 2025 defense gave up 28.9 points a game, ranking 30th in the NFL. Through five games in 2026, it’s allowing 21.8 points per game, which […]
full_text: With the bye week here, it’s time for some awards for the Cincinnati Bengals through the first five games of the 2026 season, starting with the most improved player. The 2025 defense gave up 28.9 points a game, ranking 30th in the NFL. Through five games in 2026, it’s allowing 21.8 points per game, which ranks 11th. A lot of that is the new additions up front, but some of the guys who were here last year have grown up, too. Only players who were on the 2025 roster qualify for this one. Barrett Carter, LB 2025: 106 tackles, zero sacks, one tackle for loss in 17 games. 2026: 41 tackles, 1.5 sacks, four tackles for loss and a forced fumble in five. He already has four times last season’s TFL total in less than a third of the games, and he’s playing more like a three-down linebacker. Dax Hill, CB 2025: one interception, 11 passes defensed, no forced fumbles in 17 games. 2026: five passes defensed and a forced fumble in five games. That’s a pace of 17 passes defensed. The coaches keep calling Hill a guy who “can do whatever you ask,” and they’ve been asking a lot with the secondary banged up. Kris Jenkins, DT 2025: 1.5 sacks in 14 games. 2026: two sacks in five games, as part of the rotation behind Dexter Lawrence and Jonathan Allen. Mike Gesicki, TE 2025: 28 catches, 307 yards, two touchdowns in 13 games. 2026: 12 catches, 159 yards, four touchdowns in five. He’s already doubled last year’s touchdown total. Jordan Battle, S 2025: 125 tackles, four interceptions. He had four interceptions in all of 2025 and has three already. There are still some tackling issues, but his turnovers have been big momentum-swingers. Demetrius Knight, LB 2025: 106 tackles, three sacks, two interceptions. Knight has shown improvement thus far and currently has an 81.2 run defense grade from Pro Football Focus , ranking sixth among all linebackers. And to further the discussion, who’s the returning player you expected to take a leap who hasn’t yet? Shemar Stewart? Myles Murphy? Make your case in the comments!

title: Bengals Film Room: Joe Burrow has season-best performance vs. Miami Dolphins
summary: For the first time this season, we saw peak Joe Burrow as he led the Cincinnati Bengals to a 31-24 win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 5. The passing numbers a week prior against Jacksonville showed 428 yards passing with 1 passing touchdown and 2 interceptions. While he played pretty well overall, the turnovers […]
full_text: For the first time this season, we saw peak Joe Burrow as he led the Cincinnati Bengals to a 31-24 win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 5. The passing numbers a week prior against Jacksonville showed 428 yards passing with 1 passing touchdown and 2 interceptions. While he played pretty well overall, the turnovers played a big part in the Bengals coming up short against the Jaguars. This week against Miami, Burrow threw for just 190 yards on the day. To me, it was a better performance than the week before. Mainly, the reason for that is that he didn’t have a single turnover. When the Bengals can win the turnover battle, they are going to win a lot of games. They were also able to have more balance with the running game this week, getting 117 rushing yards on Sunday. Burrow finished the game against Miami completing 23/32 passes on the day for a 71.9% completion rate. He also was able to throw for 4 touchdown passes, with three of those coming in the first half. He threw those three touchdowns to Mike Gesicki, Samaje Perine, and Tanner Hudson. All three of those scores came inside the red zone. Finding ways to finish with touchdowns instead of field goals in the red zone is going to continue being a critical component of how successful this team is on a weekly basis. Mike Gesicki’s 4th receiving touchdown of the season pic.twitter.com/RVRfPn7mKT — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 12, 2026 Samaje Perine with the Bengals second touchdown of the game pic.twitter.com/H4rPkCWdhB — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 12, 2026 Burrow’s third touchdown pass of the first half was to Tanner Hudson. pic.twitter.com/14IgAZmTyv — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 12, 2026 Burrow was able to spread the wealth on Miami, with nine different players catching a pass this week. While that is always beneficial, it is still nice to have Ja’Marr Chase back on the field. Chase missed a good chunk of the previous game with a concussion, but was able to get cleared and showed no signs of that slowing him down against the Dolphins. Burrow did a masterful job maneuvering in the pocket for his final touchdown pass. This time finding Ja’Marr Chase for a 45-yard touchdown score. Chase was able to pin the ball up by his shoulder with one hand. Joe Burrow to Ja’Marr Chase for the 45-yard touchdown 🥶 pic.twitter.com/yk57XwXcUV — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 12, 2026 The Burrow to Chase connection is alive and well, and they will need it to be on point after the bye week. The Bengals will travel to division leading Baltimore on October 25th. An efficient Joe Burrow could help the Bengals secure a huge divisional road win that day.

title: Does Samaje Perine deserve a larger role at running back over Chase Brown?
summary: Samaje Perine was the Cincinnati Bengals’ leading rusher on Sunday against the Miami Dolphins, and he provided a spark that this ground game hasn’t had enough of so far this year. The veteran running back logged 14 carries for 68 yards during the game. That 4.9 yards per carry is the highest number for a […]
full_text: Samaje Perine was the Cincinnati Bengals ’ leading rusher on Sunday against the Miami Dolphins , and he provided a spark that this ground game hasn’t had enough of so far this year. The veteran running back logged 14 carries for 68 yards during the game. That 4.9 yards per carry is the highest number for a Bengals running back this season. Perine also added 2 receptions for 10 yards, and found the end zone for Joe Burrow’s second touchdown pass of the game. Chase Brown has not been able to get fully going consistently this year in the running game. He had 20 carries for 80 yards against Houston, and followed that up with a respectable 13 carries for 61 yards in Pittsburgh. Against Jacksonville in Week 4, he only ran the ball 9 times for a total of 10 yards. This week he ran the ball 13 times for 39 yards. One thing I still like about what Brown brings to the table is being a receiving threat out of the backfield for the Bengals. He hauled in three receptions for 21 yards against the Dolphins. One of those came on a play with Perine in the backfield, and a play-action fake to get Brown the ball out in the flat. He was able to make a guy miss and picked up the first down. Bengals are under-center, play-action to Perine, and they get the pass out in the flat to Brown who makes a guy miss for the 1st down. pic.twitter.com/2KYmfk8hM4 — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 12, 2026 Perine, on the other hand, is never going to wow anyone with his speed or elusiveness ( except for the Chiefs in the 2021-22 AFC Championship ), but he is a dependable player who consistently moves the chains when given opportunities. His 14 carries on Sunday actually outnumbered the 13 carries he had during the first four games of the season. I think getting the two players closer to a 60-40 split on carries each game makes sense going forward. With that split, you can afford to give either guy closer to the 60% based on who has the hotter hand during that particular game. Do you think Samaje Perine deserves a larger role in the offense moving forward? Sound off in the comments. Samaje Perine vs. Miami 14 carries for 68 yards (4.9 YPC) 2 catches for 10 yards and a TD 1 magnificent beard pic.twitter.com/DESX3nT5WB — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) October 13, 2026

Bengals News 10 Stats to Know From First Five Weeks of 2026 As a team, the Bengals have pressured opposing quarterbacks on 40.4% of their dropbacks, the eighth-highest rate in the NFL, per NGS. full_text: (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns will try to get back to their winning ways on Sunday as they host the Baltimore Ravens in downtown Cleveland. This was looking to be a spicy meeting of first-place teams before the Browns stumbled last week in a loss to the New York Jets. But a win would still propel the Browns into first place in the AFC North Division, as they would hold the current tiebreaker over both the Ravens and Pittsburgh Steelers by virtue of wins against both teams. The Ravens come into the tilt riding a three-game winning streak thanks to last week’s overtime win against Atlanta that was orchestrated by backup quarterback Tyler Huntley, who will get the start again this week as quarterback Lamar Jackson is still sidelined with an ankle injury. Huntley has won three consecutive games in place of Jackson, with the Ravens averaging 33.7 points per game, so Cleveland’s defense may not be catching a break on Sunday. Speaking of Cleveland’s defense, they still have some key pieces ailing as defensive tackles Kalia Davis and Mike Hall Jr. will both miss the game, while defensive end Derek Barnett, defensive tackle Mason Graham, and linebacker Carson Schwesinger are all questionable. title: Can the Browns defeat the Ravens? How about like this!
summary: The Cleveland Browns and Baltimore Ravens square off this weekend in a key AFC North Division contest. Currently, every team in the division has a positive record, with Baltimore on top with a 4-1-0 record. A Cleveland win would tie the Browns for the division lead. The Pittsburgh Steelers are on the road against the […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns and Baltimore Ravens square off this weekend in a key AFC North Division contest . Currently, every team in the division has a positive record, with Baltimore on top with a 4-1-0 record. A Cleveland win would tie the Browns for the division lead. The Pittsburgh Steelers are on the road against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers while the Cincinnati Bengals are on their bye week. RELATED: BROWNS, RAVENS LIST OF 36 INJURED PLAYERS Cleveland has done well hosting Baltimore in the past five years, going 3-2-0. So far this year, the Browns have not defeated a single team considered to be one of the league’s best teams, and essentially, the two contests against the Ravens are their only difficult challenges. Cleveland is playing the league’s “last-place schedule,” being pitted against the majority of division cellar-dwellers from last year. A split with Baltimore will become an advantage later in the season. The Ravens feature their usual ground-and-pound running game, featuring Derrick Henry, who is ranked #5 it total rushing yards this year. The Browns haven’t done well as far as stopping the run, so this may set up what this game is truly about. According to FOX Sports, Cleveland is ranked #18 against the run. Can the Browns defeat the Ravens? Here are a few ideas: Monken’s familiarity and the Browns’ receivers Cleveland head coach Todd Monken had run Baltimore’s offense for the past three years successfully. He knows every nook and cranny of this side of the ball. He understands the advantage of Henry running the ball, and that WR Zay Flowers is a league menace. But Monken has a few new tricks he can deploy. The Browns have a strong (enough) armed QB in Deshaun Watson. Baltimore’s defensive backfield can be beaten long, or spin the ball into intermediate zones quickly. The Ravens have given up 16 plays of 20+ yards and one that went for over 40 yards. Monken has a trio of very good receivers that are able to stretch the field, plus tight end Harold Fannin. Test the Ravens’ defensive backs early and often. A quick note: Watson is 2-0 against Baltimore at home. Ravens’ injury list Hate to see a team win by default, but this may become a reality with the Ravens. Currently, they have 19 players on their first injury report going into Week 6, according to Nikhil Mehta of Baltimore Beatdown . That is an army of players. The key players listed that remain questionable to play are QB Lamar Jackson, C Cam Jurgens, CB Marlon Humphrey, LT Ronnie Stanley, DT Calais Campbell, OG Andrew Vorhees, and LB Trenton Simpson. They added a few more on Thursday . Not great for Baltimore, but will take it. Last week, backup QB and former Brown Tyler Huntley played decently in Baltimore’s 30-23 win over the Atlanta Falcons. Home field advantage For whatever reason, the Ravens struggle playing in Cleveland. Even in victory games, things just happen. Baltimore has a history of getting involved in unpredictable and sloppy games when they should dominate the Browns. Strange things tend to happen. The “Factory of Sadness” is a real thing. Baltimore players getting hurt, defenders dropping interceptions, dropped passes, losing good leads going into the fourth quarter, and ugly losses. Not to mention, the Browns fans get up for Baltimore because they realize they are always in the division title mix. In 2024, Cleveland went 3-14-0, but beat the Ravens at home 29-24. The 33-31 win over Baltimore at home in 2023 became the 11 th win, which secured a playoff seed. A 7-10-0 record in 2022 included beating the Ravens 13-3 at home, just like the year before when Baltimore came into FirstEnergy Stadium and left town with a 24-22 late loss. Do you think these 3 factors will lead to a Browns win over the Ravens in Week 6? Join the conversation! summary: Where is this team headed? Can’t fire the head coach, can’t fire the defensive coordinator, could fire the special teams guy, but won’t. full_text: Photo by Stephen Dunn/Getty Images | Getty Images Where is this team headed? Can’t fire the head coach, can’t fire the defensive coordinator, could fire the special teams guy, but won’t. They could bring in some consultants like a defensive consultant (which they kind of did), a special teams consultant, or a game-planning consultant, but probably won’t be doing that either. That pretty much leaves scheme and personnel. If your players can’t communicate, understand, and execute your scheme, you need a new scheme or you need to simplify, simplify, simplify. If your player personnel isn’t good enough, then you’ve got to think about redistributing snaps away from the underperformers towards other players. Five games in, that last point is going to be our focus today, as we look at positional rankings (or percentile rankings) to identify which players elevated their performance more than others and players whose play has deteriorated. We’ve covered positional rankings extensively this offseason, go here if you need a quick primer . The idea is that instead of using a player’s raw PFF Grade, we look at where a given player is ranked relative to the other players in the league at his position, just as we did last week. Based on the overall ranking scale provided by PFF, the results can be split into quintiles, which delivers the following positional ranking groups: body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table { border: 1px solid #000 !important; border-collapse: collapse !important; } body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th { padding: 0px 6px !important; } Positional Ranking Description 100-80 Blue-Chip Performance 79-60 NFL starter quality performance 59-40 Slightly above or below average 39-20 Underperformance 19-0 Red Flag performance Today, we’ll compare the cumulative 2026 rankings with the 2025 rankings using a snap-adjusted positional index (or SNAPI for short). (This post was initially drafted on Friday and Saturday of last week, and contains data for Weeks 1-5 for Cowboys and Texans, Weeks 1-4 for all others. The results shouldn’t change too much after a full Week 5, so we’re sticking with that original data set.) For individual players, we’ll use their positional ranking. For groups and units, we’ll use SNAPI, which adjusts for playing time and provides a better measure than a simple average. Offensive Line – Finally Trending Up What a great start it’s been for Tyler Guyton. After starting out as the problem child in training camp (and very briefly in a two-man competition for the LT spot), he is now ranked 16th out of 94 tackles by PFF. Brandon Thorn pointed out on Twitter that Guyton “is an All-Pro caliber talent with ascending but unrefined skill, partly due to being inexperienced (25 career starts with 14 career college starts)“ – and most of those college starts were at right tackle. Four of the five offensive linemen now grade as NFL-starter quality or better, with three reaching the blue-chip tier. body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table { border: 1px solid #000 !important; border-collapse: collapse !important; } body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th { padding: 0px 6px !important; } Offensive Line 2025 2026 Player POS Snaps Pos. Bass G 352 71 265 36 108 67 NEW: Broderick Jones T 632 29 9 78 95 18 Terence Steele T 1,163 47 324 80 95 16 SNAPI 60.2 68.1 Moving up from a SNAPI of 60.2 to 68.1 is already quite an achievement, and it’s very encouraging to see three blue-chip performances here. But Terence Steele is dragging the total unit performance down quite a bit with a positional rank of 16 (80th out of 95 tackles). The team needs to figure out how to address this. Perhaps try out T.J. Bass at right tackle, maybe give Broderick Jones more than nine snaps, or throw one of the other backups out there and see what happens. But inactivity is not a solution. Skill Positions – Shaking off the rust The skill position players are not quite where they were last. Their combined SNAPI dropped 77.2 last year to just 68.2 this year. body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table { border: 1px solid #000 !important; border-collapse: collapse !important; } body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th { padding: 0px 6px !important; } Skill Position 2025 2026 Player POS Snaps Pos. For Flournoy, it’s simply matter of opportunity: Flournoy’s 2025 data is heavily buoyed by two massive 100-yard performances. When the game plan called on him to run a full route tree, he responded. But for Jake Ferguson, the situation is different. YPRR is a football metric that measures a pass catcher’s efficiency by dividing their total receiving yards by the number of passing routes they ran, essentially giving us the average number of receiving yards a player makes every time he runs a route. His yards per catch fell drastically from 10.7 yards in 2023 down to just 6.8 yards this year. Catching passes closer and closer to the line of scrimmage structurally caps how many yards a player can generate per route. That “catch compression” may have also triggered an alarming drop in Yards after Catch (YAC), but what if that drop isn’t just a product of scheme deployment? Ferguson is only 27, but perhaps an age-related decline is behind what some observers described as a lack of burst…

Mike Pettine is the new senior defensive assistant for the Dallas Cowboys, and the hope is that his experience brings some hope to a struggling unit. Cowboys could have new plan for rookie Caleb Downs ahead of Sunday’s showdown vs. Packers – Joseph Hoyt, Dallas Morning News The Cowboys have adjusted how they’ve used Caleb Downs over the last few games due to players being banged up. However, a change back to his original usage could be coming. FRISCO — The Cowboys have used rookie first-round pick Caleb Downs mostly at safety over the last two games due to injuries in the team’s secondary. “That’s not the design for Caleb,” Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said this week. “We want Caleb down near the line of scrimmage.” That could be the design against the Packers on Sunday Pettine ready to lend support, experience to Cowboys’ defense – Todd Archer, ESPN Mike Pettine is now in Dallas after he planned on being away from the league for a while. His mission is to give everything he’s got for his close friend Christian Parker as a senior defensive assistant. The subject of joining the staff was first broached in the winter, but Pettine had recently announced his retirement. Pettine visited the Cowboys in the spring and was with the coaches for a few days. Pettine will be in the coaches booth during games while Parker will remain on the sideline. “I’m just obviously trying to hit the ground running here,” Pettine said. “I feel like I’m trying to sip water from a firehose but trying to get caught up on all the film and make observations here and there. title: Cowboys at Packers: 3 causes for concern in Week 6
summary: After a 10-day mini bye week, the Dallas Cowboys return to action on Sunday night, facing off against the Green Bay Packers. While it’s still very early in the season, this feels like a game the Cowboys need to win if they want any shot at winning the NFC East. Before the two teams square […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images After a 10-day mini bye week, the Dallas Cowboys return to action on Sunday night, facing off against the Green Bay Packers. While it’s still very early in the season, this feels like a game the Cowboys need to win if they want any shot at winning the NFC East. Before the two teams square off, here are three causes for concern in this matchup. 1) Matthew Golden and Christian Watson’s big-play ability Last week against the division rival Chicago Bears, the Green Bay Packers offense came alive. For the first time since Week 1, the Packers recorded 400+ yards of total offense, reaching 428 total yards to go with 31 points in their victory over the Bears. The biggest reason for Green Bay’s success on offense was their ability to lean on their explosive offensive weapons to record chunk plays. In the game, the Packers recorded three separate receptions of 45 or more yards, including two of 50 or more yards from Matthew Golden and Christian Watson. While Golden and Watson may not have the stats of some of the NFL’s elite receiving duos, both have excellent speed and are two of the most explosive deep threats in the entire league. Last week, for the first time all year, the Packers got both of them going in the same game, leading to the duo wreaking havoc on Chicago’s defense. Golden and Watson combined for 12 catches for 266 yards and two touchdowns in the matchup, each averaging over 20 Y/R. If the Cowboys want any chance of walking out of Green Bay with a win, they’ll absolutely need to limit the big plays by Golden and Watson. That will be easier said than done for this struggling Cowboys’ defense. 2) Packers’ defense forcing turnovers Another big factor in their blowout victory last week was the ability of Green Bay’s defense to register takeaways. The Packers totaled a season-high five takeaways against the Bears, recording three interceptions to go with two fumble recoveries. Since their Week 3 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons, the Packers’ defense has excelled at taking the ball away. They have recorded at least one takeaway in each of their last three games, taking them up to nine on the year, the fourth-most of any team in the league. Talented safety Xavier McKinney has been the catalyst for the Packers’ defense in this department, recording three interceptions in Green Bay’s last three matchups. With all the problems Dallas is having on the defensive side of the ball, the last thing they need in this game is for their offense to turn the ball over. If McKinney and the rest of the Packers’ defense are able to continue and take the ball away, it could be a long night for the Cowboys. 3) Cowboys’ recent history against Green Bay This may sound hard to believe, but Friday, October 16th marks exactly 10 years since the last Cowboys victory over the Packers. Since that 2016 win in Lambeau, Dallas has lost five of their last six matchups against Green Bay, with the only non-loss being the tie last season. If you look back a little further, Dallas is 1-10-1 in the two teams’ last 12 matchups, including a 1-5 record in games at Lambeau Field. While year-over-year trends don’t amount to much in the NFL, it’s hard to look at Dallas’ recent track record against the Packers and not be a bit concerned. Let’s hope the Cowboys flip the script on Sunday.

Skyy Moore (Ankle), Javon Hargrave (Achilles), and Benjamin St. Juste (Hamstring) were ruled out Friday. It comes as no surprise as each player has not practiced this week. Keisean Nixon (Groin) does not have an injury designation and Savion Williams (Ankle) has been listed as questionable. Finally, edge rusher Lukas Van Ness (Shoulder) carries no injury designation entering the game.

title: Cowboys looking for first complete game of season to win at Packers
summary: The Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers. Lambeau Field at night in primetime in mid-October. This week’s looming Sunday Night Football matchup has deeply rooted, historic reasons to be epic, but right now only the home team fanbase is in this kind of hopeful mood. Cowboys fans are more so dreading the task at hand […]
full_text: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers. Lambeau Field at night in primetime in mid-October. This week’s looming Sunday Night Football matchup has deeply rooted, historic reasons to be epic, but right now only the home team fanbase is in this kind of hopeful mood. Cowboys fans are more so dreading the task at hand of trying to defend well enough in this game to not drop a second straight game, and fall to 2-4 on a season that was supposed to be so much more. The Cowboys can’t count on the divine intervention of seeing all three other teams in their division lose or tie head-to-head like last week. They need to get in the win column. The Packers can’t afford to take their foot off the gas even a little bit – they are in a three way tie at 3-2 with the Detroit Lions and Chicago Bears, all looking up at the undefeated Minnesota Vikings. With that, it’s time to get to our weekly win/loss scenarios for the Cowboys in their second road appearance on SNF this season. The Dallas Cowboys will beat the Green Bay Packers if… …they knock Jordan Love off his spot, and run the ball well. We don’t often go with a two-fer across both main phases of the game for these scenarios, but in a way maybe that speaks to the desperation mode the Cowboys are in after two bad losses in 12 days prior. Starting with the defense, there is no way to sugarcoat how lopsided of a matchup the Packers receivers against the Cowboys secondary, specifically the safeties, is in this game. There really is no conceivable way for the Cowboys to “win” this matchup. Malik Hooker and Markquese Bell played a lot of safety snaps against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers for a defense still without P.J. Locke or Jalen Thompson, and neither is good enough at sustaining deep coverage or plastering receivers downfield to be relied on against Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. This is why the focus shifts to the Dallas pass rush instead. Both Watson and Golden had over 120 yards in the Packers’ 31-7 win against the Bears, with Watson having two touchdowns. The second-best receiver duo in the league when it comes to yardage output (the first being George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb for the Cowboys) tore up the Bears without a whole lot of route creativity whatsoever. Just good old-fashioned getting behind the defense, something the Cowboys were susceptible to in all of the crunch-time moments of the game against the Bucs. The Cowboys’ best chance to not allow this to happen to them is to not even let these types of routes develop downfield by not giving Jordan Love the time to throw them. This will be the first game the Cowboys have Mike Pettine assisting their defensive coaching alongside coordinator Christian Parker. It may be a bit fantasy football-ish to expect anything immediately tangible to come of this, but Pettine’s area of expertise is indeed getting pressure in the front seven. The Cowboys have teased personnel changes coming off their mini-bye, and have rookie edge rusher Malachi Lawrence coming on stronger each week, as well as James Houston on the bench awaiting more opportunity. Pettine’s most recent job was with the Vikings from 2022-25, working alongside the most blitz happy coordinator in the league Brian Flores. He’ll have experience to bank on coaching against this Packers offense specifically. From @SamHoppen #Vikings !!! #Cowboys !!! pic.twitter.com/hjkDqCexuQ — Matt Williamson (@WilliamsonNFL) October 15, 2026 All of this doesn’t need to show up in a massive way in the stat sheet when it comes to sacks, but this is absolutely not a game where Jordan Love can be comfortable in the pocket all night. On offense, the greatest band-aid of all is and always has been the run game. The Packers have been beaten badly on the ground in a few games this season, mainly by teams that had more than one back they could rely on though. The Cowboys have nothing even resembling a threat out of the backfield beyond Javonte Williams right now, but after the Tampa Bay loss, simply remembering they can lean on Williams as a bell cow would be a welcome sign. When the Cowboys are forced into a high-volume of passes, the likelihood of the negative plays that have called into question Brian Schottenheimer’s play-calling and scheming rearing their ugly head skyrockets. The pass game still needs to shine in this game and the Cowboys need to finish the majority of their drives with seven points, but if the backbone of these drives are the run game, the Cowboys will be in the best position to win they can ask for. The Dallas Cowboys will lose to the Green Bay Packers if… …they don’t win on third down. Only the Detroit Lions and Denver Broncos have given up more third-down conversions this season than the Packers defense, and no team has converted less than the Packers offense. Before getting ahead of ourselves in thinking this is a big area the Cowboys can exploit, their own defense had had the fourth most third down attempts against them this season. If the eye test compared to this showed that the Cowboys were playing stout defense and getting off the field, that would be great, but we know this is more a result of not even being able to get teams into third downs via giving up big plays on earlier downs. Offensively, the Cowboys have faced virtually the same number of third downs as the Packers. The Packers offense delivered the kill shot on the very first drive of the second half last week, turning a 14-7 lead into 21-7 with a 3rd-and-22 touchdown of 53 yards to Watson. This was an insurmountable lead for the Tyson Bagent-led Bears offense, one that served as a bit of a “get right” opponent for the Packers defense, who held the Bears to 4-14 third down conversions. The Cowboys defense had gaffes on similar third and long situations against the Bucs, and those simply cannot happen against much stiffer competition on the road this time out. They also punted on offense at a higher rate they had going all the way back to last year, making sustaining drives more of a focus area against the Packers. This offense is simply too talented to be leaving third and shorts on the field instead of using them as opportunity to play the game on their terms. The money down is going to be a deciding factor as always in this game, and if the Cowboys can’t find a way to win with some margin here, it could be a long night. Another thing to watch for along these lines is the fact the Packers have the third most penalties in the league this season. The Cowboys were handed a golden opportunity to look more convincing the last two weeks, when the Texans committed 13 penalties against them but Dallas only won by four, and the Bucs beat them in Jerryworld despite 14 penalties. This is not a good forecast at all, but a chance to right this wrong in time to save the season is still in sight for the Cowboys at Lambeau.
author: Sean Martin

title: Digging into the numbers to predict Cowboys at Packers
summary: Every week, we’ll examine the numbers behind the next opponent on the schedule. Looking at the recent numbers and trends for each team, we’ll add it all up to see which squad may have the edge. This week, the Cowboys travel to Lambeau on Sunday Night Football to face the Green Bay Packers. Cowboys key […]
full_text: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images Every week, we’ll examine the numbers behind the next opponent on the schedule. Looking at the recent numbers and trends for each team, we’ll add it all up to see which squad may have the edge. This week, the Cowboys travel to Lambeau on Sunday Night Football to face the Green Bay Packers. Cowboys key stats from last week Dak Prescott threw for 316 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions against the Buccaneers. Both interceptions came after tipped balls off the hands of receivers. He finished with a 69.1 quarterback rating. Javonte Williams finished the day with just 45 yards on 12 carries. He also scored a touchdown on the first drive of the game. Dallas largely abandoned the run early after the first drive. The leading receiver for the Cowboys on the day was George Pickens. The receiver had his biggest game of the season, catching nine passes for 130 yards and a touchdown. The Dallas defense collapsed against Tampa Bay. They allowed 241 yards on the ground and 189 passing yards to rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels. More importantly, they forced zero turnovers, despite Daniels gifting them a pick six. The Cowboys get the stop on 3rd down and almost had a whole lot more 😳 @TBvsDAL on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/HgO8WEcEFh — NFL (@NFL) October 9, 2026 Packers key stats from last week The Packers dismantled the backup QB-led Bears last week, winning 31-7 . Quarterback Jordan Love threw for 367 yards, two touchdowns, and finished with a 137.5 passer rating. The leading receiver on the day was Christian Watson, snagging six catches for 143 yards and two touchdowns. Matthew Golden wasn’t too far behind, finishing with six catches as well and 123 yards. These two receivers accounted for 266 out of the 428 total yards on the day for the offense. The Packers had three players with receptions of over 45 yards versus the Bears. The big play potential will be a factor in the matchup this week. Surviving the explosives It’s no secret – Jordan Love loves to throw the ball down the field to his explosive play makers. The Packers currently rank ninth in deep ball percentage at nearly 15% (SumerSports). Wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden both rank in the top ten for receiving yards. They’re going to air the ball out. Dallas, on the other hand, lost last week because of 14 points coming from a pair of explosive plays in the third quarter. They currently rank 28th in average depth of target, allowing teams to throw the ball downfield routinely. This sounds like a potential disaster, right? The hope for Cowboys fans lives in newly acquired Joey Porter Jr. Unable to go last week due to illness, the star cornerback will play at Lambeau. His ability to limit receivers on the outside certainly helps Christian Parker, who can now be more aggressive with blitzes and disguises, knowing that he has a cornerback that’s able to play press man coverage at a high level. And with the signing of Mike Pettine to help on the defensive staff, the signs point to enhanced aggression from the play-caller. But will it be enough against such a potent offense? CHRISTIAN WATSON WHAT A CATCH @CHIvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/z0TbC7WaQe — NFL (@NFL) October 11, 2026 What do the numbers mean? On paper, this doesn’t look great for Dallas. The largest weakness in the matchup between the two teams is clear: Packers passing offense vs Cowboys defense. This defensive unit has shown little-to-no ability in getting after the passer on a consistent basis. The backend has been plagued with injury and underperformance. And this is a receiving corps for the Packers that is not to be trifled with On the other side, however, this could be a week where Dallas needs to stick with their run game. The Packers are the 22nd ranked team in rush success against, meaning this could be a get right week for Javonte Williams and the offensive line. The benefit of running the ball this week, of course, is keeping Jordan Love and his receivers off the field. Dallas should gameplan around long, methodical drives to help keep their defense off the field. And when the Packers start to cheat up and commit resources to the box, that’s when Dak Prescott strikes George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb with dagger shots downfield. The gameplan sounds good coming from a writer on a random weekday, but can Dallas actually commit to the run and execute it well? That could be the determining factor this week. As it sits right now, the Packers are 1.5 point favorites. The numbers and the mismatch against the Cowboys defense gives the feeling that this game favors Green Bay more than what essentially equates to a coin toss in Vegas. But if Dallas can get their ground game going against a vulnerable Packers rush defense, that could be the great equalizer in this one.

title: Brian Schottenheimer: Christian Parker will be on sideline, Mike Pettine in booth
summary: This has been an interesting week for the Dallas Cowboys to say the least. Technically it has been longer than that. Dallas lost to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers last Thursday night and as they were heavy favorites in that game (both literally and figuratively) the fallout from getting waxed has made things rather tense. Fallout […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect This has been an interesting week for the Dallas Cowboys to say the least. Technically it has been longer than that. Dallas lost to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers last Thursday night and as they were heavy favorites in that game (both literally and figuratively) the fallout from getting waxed has made things rather tense. Fallout has been particularly intense on the defensive side of the ball. Rookie defensive coordinator Christian Parker has struggled, and head coach Brian Schottenheimer pledged to use the mini bye following the Thursday game to figure out how to address those issues as well as others across the team at large. Unfortunately, in true Cowboys fashion, some of the work on defense has played out in the public which mas made things rather confusing. In order: Monday: The Cowboys hired Mike Pettine to serve as an advisor to the defensive staff Tuesday: Jerry Jones said on 105.3 The Fan that Christian Parker would be moving from the sideline to the booth Wednesday: Brian Schottenheimer said that nothing had been decided on Parker’s in-game location Thursday: Parker himself said that he would “most likely” be on the sideline Friday: Schottenheimer confirmed that Parker would remain on the sideline and that Pettine would be in the booth You can hear Schottenheimer offering the last bit in the clip below. You can also here at the beginning that he is asked who Pettine reports to and he says directly to him, not to Christian Parker. Brian Schottenheimer tells @1053SS , @rjchoppy and @BobbyBeltTX that Mike Pettine reports "directly to me." pic.twitter.com/xIlagovD27 — 105.3 The FAN (@1053thefan) October 16, 2026 On one hand, a very obvious one, it makes full and total sense for Pettine to report to Schottenheimer given that Schottenheimer is the team’s head coach. Nothing is unfair or illogical about that. On the other hand though, it is obvious that the narrative surrounding Christian Parker has been rather not great so far this season and at this particular moment. Putting that information out into the ether through a public vehicle is at the very least stirring the pot, even if unintentionally. Maybe Schottenheimer wants that. Perhaps he doesn’t realize that that’s part of what’s happening. Whatever the case, so ends one of the weirder sagas to follow the Cowboys in recent memory. At least for now.

title: Dallas Cowboys offensive line vs. Green Bay Packers defense
summary: The Dallas Cowboys need a get-right game against the Green Bay Packers. One of the biggest keys to making that happen is the work of the offensive line. Let’s see how they match up with the Packers. Trench Dashboard Here are the Cowboys offensive line metrics for the 2026 season so far.  Pass Block Win […]
full_text: Photo by Matthew Pearce/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys need a get-right game against the Green Bay Packers. One of the biggest keys to making that happen is the work of the offensive line. Let’s see how they match up with the Packers. Trench Dashboard Here are the Cowboys offensive line metrics for the 2026 season so far. Pass Block Win Rate – 50% (17th) Run Block Win Rate – 69% (31st) Pressure rate allowed – 27% (10th) Sacks allowed – 6 (2nd) Last three-week trend: Pass protection steady, run blocking fading The pressure point Every opponent will look at the Cowboys offensive line and ask, where can we break it? Here’s what to watch for. PRESSURE POINT: Green Bay’s blitzes are more dangerous than its four-man rush There is an unusual split in Green Bay’s defensive numbers. The Packers have 14 sacks, seventh-most in the NFL, yet their Passs Rush Win Rate ranks 29th (see below). That tells us Green Bay is not consistently dominating offensive linemen one-on-one. Instead, defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon has been willing to create pressure with extra rushers and disguise. Through the first four games, Green Bay has blitzed a healthy amount, something to expect this week against Dallas. That matters after what happened against Tampa Bay. The Buccaneers repeatedly confused Dallas with blitzes and different pressure looks. Dak Prescott was officially sacked zero times, but the offense struggled to consistently identify where pressure was coming from and never developed a comfortable rhythm. Tampa Bay controlled possession for more than 39 minutes and Dallas produced only 16 points. That means Cooper Beebe has to identify those looks before the snap. Tyler Smith and Tyler Booker also have to communicate when defenders cross over each other or linebackers arrive late. Dallas protected Prescott well statistically against Tampa Bay. The next step is protecting him without the offense becoming uncomfortable every time a defense threatens to blitz. PRESSURE POINT: Devonte Wyatt is now the main interior threat Micah Parsons was hoping to return against his former team, but Green Bay head coach Matt LaFleur said the Packers are still waiting for medical clearance, and Parsons is not expected to return this week. That removes the biggest possible matchup nightmare from Dallas’ preparation. But Devonte Wyatt cannot be ignored. Wyatt produced two sacks against Chicago last week, giving Green Bay an explosive interior pass-rush option. Interior pressure can be particularly damaging because Prescott cannot simply step forward away from an edge rusher. If Wyatt gets through the middle, the pocket disappears directly in front of the quarterback. Where to attack Every defensive line has a weakness, here are the Packers soft spots where the Cowboys offensive line should attack. GREEN LIGHT: Run directly at Green Bay’s depleted middle Green Bay’s 27% Run Stop Win Rate ranks 28th in the NFL. Opponents have already rushed for 638 yards and eight touchdowns at 4.1 yards per carry. The Packers have also suffered two enormous injury losses. Linebacker Edgerrin Cooper is out for the season after tearing his Achilles, that’s a huge loss. Cooper had 30 tackles and six tackles for loss before the injury and was becoming one of Green Bay’s most important defensive players. Then defensive tackle Javon Hargrave suffered an Achilles injury against Chicago and is also expected to miss the remainder of the season. That is exactly where Dallas needs to attack. Booker’s 80.0 PFF run-blocking grade ranks ninth among guards, while Smith gives Dallas its most powerful offensive lineman back on the opposite side. Dallas should use double teams inside and make Green Bay’s replacement linebackers come downhill to make tackles. GREEN LIGHT: Make Green Bay prove it can win with four rushers The Packers’ sack total looks intimidating, but there’s a way to show these numbers are wonky. Green Bay’s poor Pass Rush Win Rate combined with an equally bad 25% in defensive pressure rate that ranks 24th in the league, means their blitz game is how they generate sacks. If Green Bay only sends four defenders, it’s safe to say Dak can trust the offensive line. Tyler Guyton has been one of the biggest positives of the Cowboys season. Among tackles in the league he’s near the top in most statistical categories and PFF blocking grades. If Guyton and Terence Steele can hold up against Green Bay’s edge rushers, Dallas can release Jake Ferguson and the running backs into routes instead of constantly keeping extra blockers beside the tackles. If Green Bay responds by blitzing, Prescott needs immediate answers and everything boils down to the interior. The Chaos Report Here’s the Green Bay Packers defensive trends for this season at the defensive line. Sack Total – 14 (7th) Pass Rush Win Rate – 43% (29th) Run Stop Win Rate – 27% (28th) QB Pressure Rate – 25% (24th) Last three-week trend: Sacks climbing, injuries mounting Matchup of the week Tyler Booker vs. Devonte Wyatt For the first time in a few weeks, the key matchup is inside rather than at offensive tackle. Wyatt showed why against Chicago. He finished with two sacks and a forced fumble, creating pressure directly through the middle of the Bears offensive line. Booker is the Cowboy best equipped to stop him. Dallas’ second-year guard has become arguably its most dependable run blocker. His PFF blocking grades rank highly among guards, and he has surrendered only six total pressures without allowing a sack this season. This matchup matters in both directions. When Dallas throws, Booker has to stop Wyatt from collapsing the pocket into Prescott. When Dallas runs, Booker needs to move Wyatt backwards and create space for Javonte Williams. With Hargrave unavailable, Green Bay has lost one of the players who could rotate inside and keep its defensive tackles fresh. That gives Dallas another reason to keep pounding away. Best route to success: Make Green Bay stop the run before worrying about its blitzes. Dallas rushed for only 50 yards last week and now ranks 29th in the league in rushing production and 31st in Run Block Win Rate. However, Green Bay ranks 28th in Run Stop Win Rate. The Packers have lost Cooper and Hargrave, and Parsons is not expected to return, all this is major this week. Dallas needs to attack the middle, stay ahead of the chains and prevent Green Bay from reaching the situations where the Packers can unleash its pressure packages. If the Cowboys are constantly facing second-and-five and third-and-two, the Packers have to respect everything and defend the entirety of the Cowboys offense. Injury updates: The Cowboys offensive line is at full strength. Green Bay has much bigger problems and are dangerously thin on the defensive line. With the names already mentioned, Jordon Riley is slowly returning from an Achilles injury he sustained in Week 17 of last season, so watch his name. Colin Oliver and Warren Brinson have both gone to IR, and Anthony Campbell is questionable so watch for his name on the practice report as well.

title: Denver Broncos are 4-2 and in excellent position for a stretch run
summary: Back in May when the NFL released the Denver Broncos 2026 schedule, I saw a brutal first six games for Denver and questioned how they could come out of that stretch above .500. In fact, my snap analysis was exactly this: “Frankly, if Denver can get through this stretch of games at or above .500 […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - OCTOBER 15: Jaylen Waddle #17 of the Denver Broncos reacts to a call against the Seattle Seahawks during the second quarter of the game at Empower Field At Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Andrew Wevers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Back in May when the NFL released the Denver Broncos 2026 schedule , I saw a brutal first six games for Denver and questioned how they could come out of that stretch above .500. In fact, my snap analysis was exactly this: “Frankly, if Denver can get through this stretch of games at or above .500 then we have to chalk that up as a major win.” Here they are at 4-2 and it feels like around Broncos County that we’re reacting to an 0-6 team right now. We need to a little perspective. And yes, Bo Nix and the offense need to get better. They need to find a better running game. They need better interior pass protection. They need wide receivers to get better separation. Bo needs to get through his reads on scheduled. All of this has been said ad nauseum. But here’s the thing, they are 4-2 and nowhere near playing good offensive football. And 4-2 against mostly playoff contenders (ChargersLOL). Denver has gotten through the worst part of their schedule with a winning record and have a chance to reset the whole season. Road games against the Arizona Cardinals and Carolina Panthers with a home game against the Kansas City Chiefs in between. Punch the Chiefs in the mouth and make them doubt Week 1 happened and go into the Bye Week at 7-2. This is far more possible in my mind than what they just did to get to 4-2 through the first six games. So let’s F-in go! There is a lot of discussion around the Broncos today. title: Broncos OLB Jonathon Cooper has been removed from the Commissioner’s exempt list
summary: According to 9NEWS Denver’s Mike Klis, the NFL has removed Denver Broncos edge rusher Jonathon Cooper from the Commissioner’s exempt list. The Broncos veteran starting edge rusher will be eligible to play vs. the Cardinals next week. Earlier this week, it was reported that Cooper’s trial date was pushed back to March, instead of in […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - AUGUST 21: Denver Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper (0) and linebacker Nik Bonitto (15) celebrate after a defensive play in the first quarter during a preseason game between the Green Bay Packers and the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on August 21, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images According to 9NEWS Denver’s Mike Klis, the NFL has removed Denver Broncos edge rusher Jonathon Cooper from the Commissioner’s exempt list. The Broncos veteran starting edge rusher will be eligible to play vs. the Cardinals next week. Per source, the NFL removed Jonathon Cooper from the Commissioner Exempt List. The Broncos OLB will be eligible to play in the Broncos’ Week 7 game on Oct. 25 after missing six games. The NFL initiated an investigation under the Personal Conduct Policy following Cooper’s… — MikeKlis9NEWS (@mikeklis9news) October 16, 2026 Earlier this week, it was reported that Cooper’s trial date was pushed back to March, instead of in November during the season, which opened up the possibility of Cooper being removed from the Commissioner’s Exempt list . The league placed him there before the start of the season due to his ongoing felony assault case, and he was sidelined for 6 weeks before now being removed from this list and being eligible to play starting next week vs. the Arizona Cardinals. The NFL released a statement announcing their decision, but also added that the league’s review of the matter remains ongoing and will not be affected by this change to his roster status. The National Football League today removed Jonathon Cooper of the Denver Broncos from the Commissioner Exempt List. He will be eligible to play in the Broncos’ Week 7 game on Oct. 25 after missing six games. The NFL initiated an investigation under the Personal Conduct Policy following Cooper’s arrests in June. The league’s review remains ongoing and is not affected by this change to Cooper’s roster status. Cooper was placed on the Commissioner Exempt List on Aug. 30. Cooper also released a statement on his personal Instagram account where he stated that over the last several months, he has spent a lot of time working to better himself. He added that work will continue and that playing in the NFL and representing the Denver Broncos is a privilege he does not take for granted. Jonathon Cooper released a statement on his IG after being removed from the Commissioners Exempt List pic.twitter.com/5sLSpIV40t — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) October 16, 2026 With Cooper’s trial date now in March during the offseason, it seems like any additional punishment/suspension would come after that is finalized. As we know, Cooper was arrested twice this offseason and is facing felony assault charges. The Broncos expressed their disappointment in Cooper, but after he completed a 40-day inpatient counseling, therapy, mental health, and overall wellness program, they backed their team leader. He participated in training camp and the preseason before missing the first six games due to being on the exempt list. Speaking strictly on the field, this will be a big boost to a Denver Broncos defense that is coming off their best overall performance during their victory over the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday Night Football. Cooper will provide some veteran leadership and solidify the edge rusher position opposite Nik Bonitto. Jonah Elliss and Que Robinson have played well while he was sidelined, but the addition of Cooper should strengthen the Denver Broncos’ run defense, which has struggled at times this season. This is still a developing story, but Jonathon Cooper is off the Commissioner’s Exempt List and will be eligible to play vs. the Cardinals in Week 7.
