title: Broncos Stock Up, Stock Down: Takeaways from the Week 6 Win Over the Seahawks
summary: The Broncos entered Thursday night as home underdogs vs. the defending champion Seattle Seahawks, but ended the night with a hard-fought victory and a 4-2 record. It wasn’t pretty, but it was a defensive slugfest between two of the best defenses in the NFL, and at the end of the night, the Broncos’ defense did […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - OCTOBER 15: Denver Broncos cornerback Ja'quan McMillian (29) and linebacker Que Robinson (51) celebrate after a sack in the first quarter during a game between the Seattle Seahawks and the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Broncos entered Thursday night as home underdogs vs. the defending champion Seattle Seahawks, but ended the night with a hard-fought victory and a 4-2 record. It wasn’t pretty, but it was a defensive slugfest between two of the best defenses in the NFL, and at the end of the night, the Broncos’ defense did enough to win the game. While the Broncos’ defense dominated, the Broncos’ offense struggled. However, they were always going to struggle. It was a short week, and they were going against Mike Macdonald’s top-ranked Seattle Seahawks defense. Still, Nix led the Broncos to two touchdown drives in the first half while the defense held the lead until the final seconds of the 4th quarter, when the Seahawks tied it. However, the Broncos’ defense called game in overtime with a Ja’Quan McMillian INT that set up the game-winning field goal. Stock up and stock down is a weekly series where I go through the Denver Broncos’ 53-man roster and tell you which Broncos players’ stock is going up, down, or remains unchanged. After yet another ugly win vs. the Seahawks on Thursday, we have a good mix of stock-ups and stock-downs today. Quarterback Bo Nix – Stock down: Nix hot takes are everywhere today. I am going with stock down but also saying it’s not time to hit the panic button just yet. This game was never going to be a get-right offensive showcase by the Broncos. Mike Macdonald’s defense is among the best in the NFL and very well coached. Add in the short week/TNF aspect of it, and you had the makings of a defensive slugfest between two of the top units in the NFL. Still, Nix and the offense need to be better. We saw similar struggles last year (An arguably worse showing on TNF last year vs. the Raiders) before seeing them turn it around and play pretty well late in the year. They have had a brutal stretch to start the year and came out of it 4-2 despite their obvious issues. Things get easier from here on out, on paper at least, and the offense will need to turn it around. You CANNOT have these same struggles vs. the Cardinals next week, coming off a mini-bye week. Jarrett Stidham – Unchanged: Some fans want Bo benched, but Stiddy remains the veteran backup. Sam Ehlinger – Unchanged: Emergency third-string QB Running Back JK Dobbins – Stock down: 2.4 yards per carry. Dobbins finished the game with 17 carries for 41 yards, and outside of one 16-yard scamper, he was mostly ineffective on Thursday Night. Take away that 16-yard run, and Dobbins had 16 carries for 25 yards, which comes out to be an ugly 1.6 yards per carry. The Broncos NEED better production from their run game. Dobbins has not shown much at all this season, and unless things change quickly, he should not be getting 17 carries a game. Rookie Jonah Coleman is eligible to come off the short-term IR this week and should be inserted into the Broncos’ offense immediately. RJ Harvey – Stock up: Harvey has been the Broncos’ best playmaker this season. He had 6 carries for 25 yards (4.2 YPC) and 3 receptions for 31 yards. That is 9 touches for 56 total yards from scrimmage. He has the explosion and burst that Dobbins does not have and is running hard through contact. I wanted to see more of Harvey on Thursday Night. Tyler Badie – Stock down: Badie has been making a few good plays a game, but unfortunately, left last night’s game with a thumb injury and was late ruled out. With Coleman coming off the IR next week, Badie will likely return to being inactive and may miss some time with this thumb injury. Adam Prentice – Unchanged: Played 5 offensive snaps and mostly contributed to special teams. Wide Receiver Jaylen Waddle – Stock down: 7 targets for 4 catches for 24 yards. Tough defense and the passing offense struggling. The Broncos need to get Waddle going. Courtland Sutton – Stock down: Thought he showed some life last week, but he only had 3 targets and 2 catches for 19 yards. Troy Franklin – Unchanged: 1 target and 1 catch for 2 yards. The passing offense was non-existent. Marvin Mims Jr. – Stock down: I am going stock down because he’s having a poor start to his contract year. Injuries, nothing of note on offense, and hasn’t been great as a returner. Mims also played just 16 snaps of offense, which was one less than Lil’Jordan Humphrey. Lil’Jordan Humphrey – Unchanged: Depth player who knows his role on offense. Tight End Evan Engram – Stock down: He was playing more than Trautman, but was 50/50 with him on Sunday and played two fewer than him on Thursday Night. With Payton taking over playcalling and running the ball more, Engram’s playing time has taken a hit. He also only had 2 catches for 13 yards. Adam Trautman – Unchanged: He is who he is. Nate Adkins – Unchanged : Played 22 snaps but did not see a target and was primarily used as a run blocker. Dallen Bentley – Unchanged: Remained a healthy scratch. Offensive Line Garett Bolles – Unchanged: Remains a consistent presence on the left side of the Broncos OL. Ben Powers – Stock down: He had a rough night against the Seahawks’ talented interior defensive line. A lot of pressure came from his area, and he had issues with run blocking. Luke Wattenberg – Stock down: His snaps are consistently wide, and he’s struggling in the same areas that Powers is. Quinn Meinerz – Stock up: Stud. Mike McGlinchey – Unchanged: Has had his ups and downs at right tackle but has been mostly consistent. Alex Palczewski – Stock up: Only played 1 offensive snap, but I wouldn’t mind seeing him get some reps at left guard. Matt Peart – Unchanged: 0 snaps on offense and played on special teams. Alex Forsyth – Unchanged: 0 snaps on offense and played on special teams. Kage Casey – Unchanged: Remained inactive Defensive Line Zach Allen – Stock up: Has been playing damn good football and continued that on Thursday Night. DJ Jones – Stock up: Was that the best game DJ Jones played as a Bronco? I go through games without really noticing him, but that was not the case last night. Multiple pressures, some TFLs, and he was consistently in the backfield disrupting the play. Malcolm Roach – Stock up: Played solid last night but did see Enyi Uwazurike play a few more snaps than he did. Some of that had to do with Roach going into the blue tent during the game, but still, a solid overall showing by Roach. He finished the night with a team-high 4 QB hits. Eyioma Uwazurike – Unchanged: Played 53% of the snaps and remains a big rotational presence along the Broncos defensive line. Sai’vion Jones – Stock up: He saw 22 snaps and made a few plays. Had a big hit on Sam Darnold late in the game and a PBU late in the game as well. He was active ahead of Jordan Jackson again and seems to be earning some more trust. Jordan Jackson – Unchanged: Inactive Tyler Onyedim – Unchanged: Redshirt rookie year Edge Rushers Nik Bonitto – Stock up: Bonitto has had back-to-back really good games and had his best game of the season last night vs. the Seahawks. Forced a fumble, had a sack, and was pressuring Darnold throughout the night. Jonah Elliss – Stock down: Jonah showed some life last night and had a sack, but a late-game knee injury that did not look good potentially derailed his season. No word on the severity, but he was carted off, and it did not look good on the replay. Que Robinson – Stock way up: I am a big Que Robinson fan, and he continues to flash talent each week. He has the size/speed off the edge as a pass rusher and could be on the verge of a big run here if he sees more playing time. He needs to improve against the run, but overall, he’s looking like an ascending player for the Broncos. Dondrea Tillman – Stock…

title: Game balls for the Broncos impressive defensive win over Seahawks
summary: The Denver Broncos defense dominated the Seattle Seahawks all night and were the sole reason they came out with a victory on Thursday Night Football as the offense stumbled in the second half with six three-and-outs and even the game-winning field goal drive didn’t generate a single first down. The offense wasn’t totally abysmal. In […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - OCTOBER 15: Alex Singleton #49 and Malcolm Roach #97 of the Denver Broncos pump up the crowd against the Seattle Seahawks during the third quarter of the game at Empower Field At Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos defense dominated the Seattle Seahawks all night and were the sole reason they came out with a victory on Thursday Night Football as the offense stumbled in the second half with six three-and-outs and even the game-winning field goal drive didn’t generate a single first down. Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: Fewer ads Create community posts Comment on articles, community posts Rec comments, community posts New, improved notifications system! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . The offense wasn’t totally abysmal. In the second quarter, they put together their two longest drives of the season in back-to-back possessions. First was a 16-play, 74 yard drive and the second a 9-play, 79 yard drive and both resulted in touchdowns. That gave us hope of a blowout, but the Seahawks defense brought the heat the rest of the game and shut them all the way down. Fortunately, the Broncos defense also brought the heat and while they gave up a few late scores to send the game into overtime, two timely interceptions sealed the victory and setup the game-winning field goal by Wil Lutz. Whatever issues the defense had in that Week 1 disaster have certainly been fixed now by Week 6. Here’s who we’re giving our game balls to: Defensive Front One guy that has been the center of ridicule early has been Alex Singleton and my game ball was originally going to go to him for how passionate and well he played in this game. He finished with 13 total tackles and two quarterback hits. He seemed like he was in on every play last night. However, I had to go with the whole front seven. They absolutely terrorized Sam Darnold all night long. The defense ended up with 17 total quarterback hits and TWELVE different players on defense had a QB hit. TWELVE! Have a game ball every one of you guys! – Tim Lynch The Broncos had 12 DIFFERENT players get a QB hit against the Seahawks. That's the most in the NFL since 2006. — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) October 16, 2026 Wil Lutz You always hold your breath when the Denver kicker attempts a field goal. And all of Broncos Country did that at the end of Thursday night’s game. Thankfully, it was an exhale of celebration and relief after Lutz nailed the game-winning 53-yard field goal against Seattle. On this day, he was big nuts Lutz, and absolutely clutch Lutz. Helluva kick. – Ian St. Clair BRONCOS WIN!!!!! 4-2 pic.twitter.com/Mcl3IEM4Lk — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) October 16, 2026 Ja’Quan McMillian Ja’Quan McMillian is a play-making monster. He had a big sack early and a game-winning interception. He deserves my game ball this week and all the love in the world from Broncos Country. – Sadaraine J-MAC INT!!!! pic.twitter.com/b2KORAVxiG — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) October 16, 2026 Kris Abrams-Draine Kris Abrams-Draine gets my gameball. He was forced into the spotlight with the absence of both Moss (who only played 20 snaps) and PS2 and he turned in what may be his best game as a pro. He finished the game with 6 tackles (4 solo), 3 passes defended, 1 huge INT, and 1 forced fumble. His career high in passes defended prior to this game was one. The fumble he forced was the first of his career. He did this while facing arguably the best WR in the NFL at this moment, JSN. Did I mention that this was only his 4th career start? Some of this credit has to be given to the pass rush which was harrying Darnold all night (17 pressures on 58 dropbacks) until they got gassed by the criminally inept offense, but he still played the best game of his career. He came into the game with 4 career passes defended and almost doubled that. – Joe Mahoney I still can't believe this play didn't end the game pic.twitter.com/ggjqRTTQlj — ThatsGoodSports (@BrandonPerna) October 16, 2026 Nik Bonitto This gameball is going to one BAMF, Nik Bonitto. He spent almost the entire game pressuring Sam Darnold. He only had half a sack and 4 tackles, but his forced fumble as the Seahawks were driving at the end of the first half was huge. His pressure rate was 22%, and he had 4 quick pressures (less than 2.5 seconds). He’s just a nightmare for opposing offenses. The whole pass rush was stellar, and Bonitto was phenomenal all night. – Adam Malnati Bonitto taking a page out of Von Miller's playbook pic.twitter.com/PpTLXPndSX — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) October 16, 2026 Vance Joseph Just give my ball to Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph. I give it to him a lot, but the defense is the only part of the team that shows up to play on a weekly basis. Even without Patrick Surtain II and Talanoa Hufanga, he was able to come up with a great gameplan to limit Seattle’s offense. Without their three turnovers and five sacks, the Broncos wouldn’t have had a shot to win the game. Kudos to the players for executing as well. Just think of how good the defense could be if the offense actually showed signs of life. A tip of the hat to Vance and his players. – Chris Hart Who gets your game ball for the Broncos-Seahawks game? Share in the comments section below.

title: Bo Nix doesn’t know why the Broncos are unable to push the ball downfield
summary: Have we had enough time to overreact to the Denver Broncos impressive defensive battle and win over the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks? I feel like I have… The commentary out there continues to be centered around Bo Nix and the offense and for good reason. We all had incredibly high expectations for this […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - OCTOBER 15: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos reacts against the Seattle Seahawks during the third quarter of the game at Empower Field At Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Andrew Wevers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Have we had enough time to overreact to the Denver Broncos impressive defensive battle and win over the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks? I feel like I have… The commentary out there continues to be centered around Bo Nix and the offense and for good reason. We all had incredibly high expectations for this offense coming into the season and they have really come up short. As bad as its been at times, there are some signs of life — just no consistency to go with it. “I think you can take the first half probably, really the second quarter, and that was a good example of what we could be.” Bo Nix One of those signs came through a 25 play stretch of dominance over back-to-back drives that the Broncos scored their only two touchdowns of the game during the second quarter. Nix was asked about if he felt the offense was close to finding its identity and he pointed to those two drives as evidence of that. “I think you can take the first half probably, really the second quarter, and that was a good example of what we could be,” Nix said after the game. “Running the football, getting to manageable spots, completing third downs, and competing on third downs and managing those drives and scoring with touchdowns. The game would have been different obviously had we settled for a field goal or two in those red zones, which they do a really good job keeping you out of the red zone. It was good to score when we did, and then our defense just held on. I do think there are some ways that we obviously will continue to improve. At the end of the day, the win is the most important.” That 16-play, 74 yard drive and 9-play, 79 yard drive showed a bit of everything we hoped to see this season. From successful screen passes to consistent rushing attacks and Bo checking out of a run to take an end zone shot that resulted in a defensive pass interference call. It was fun and raised our expectations for the game. “I don’t understand why we can’t really push the ball vertically right now. Defenses are just sitting back there hanging out” Bo Nix They then had six three-and-outs and needed the defense to generate turnovers to get the game-winning field goal in overtime. Not ideal… Then came a question about letting it rip more and Nix was shockingly frank about how it went down and admitted he doesn’t know why they can’t push the ball vertically right now. “I thought I saw the field really well, especially early when we were given opportunities to sort of be aggressive,” Nix said. “Then as the game went on, it felt a little bit like just third downs were the key. Then every once in a while, we had an opportunity to throw it deep again. Then they were in a short Cover-2 shell, covering it deep and we had outlets with 10 yards of space. So it’s just… I don’t understand why we can’t really push the ball vertically right now. Defenses are just sitting back there hanging out. We’re just going to keep running the football. Hopefully you have to find ways to get more out of it.” If the tape matches, then its just Bo taking care of the football and not putting throws in danger of being intercepted. It’ll be interesting to see how Tim Jenkins breaks this game down. What are you thoughts on Bo Nix and the Broncos offense right now?

title: Magical defensive performance earns Broncos key victory over Seahawks in primetime
summary: Another week, another Denver Broncos victory. Thanks to another top-notch defensive effort, the Broncos were able to take down the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks on Thursday Night Football. Denver didn’t play their best game. Though they battled hard enough to get the job done. In front of a sellout crowd, they rose to […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - OCTOBER 15: Head Coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos stands on the field prior to an NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Empower Field at Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Another week, another Denver Broncos victory. Thanks to another top-notch defensive effort, the Broncos were able to take down the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks on Thursday Night Football . Denver didn’t play their best game. Though they battled hard enough to get the job done. In front of a sellout crowd, they rose to the occasion in overtime to earn their fourth victory of a season. Moving forward, the team has a lot of work to do, especially on offense. Yet being 4-2 after a tough slate of opponents to start the season is a good spot to be in all things considered. After the game, Head Coach Sean Payton had high praise for the defense, his kicker, and how the offense was able to reel off two key scoring drives in the first half after enduring another three-and-out to start the game. “Real quick, a huge team win. Defensively, we were magnificent. I don’t know how many times we hit the quarterback, we got three takeaways. We felt like that was going to be a big deal in this game, being smart with the football,” stated Payton. “Offensively, we got going early and then obviously it was a battle. I’m happy for Wil Lutz. He really hit that last kick and it’s a good team we beat. Two years in a row, we beat the Super Bowl team and that’s not easy to do.” The Broncos were able to limit the impact of Seattle’s offense by holding them to just 14 points. That’s quite impressive considering they were down Patrick Surtain II, Talanoa Hufagna, and had Riley Moss on a limited snap count throughout the evening. With the offense struggling to do much of anything in the second half, Denver’s defense was on the field a lot. Through four quarters, they had a whopping 85 defensive snaps. In the second half, the defense did give up some yards, but they were absolute dominant taking the ball away. That was the major difference maker in last night’s victory. Forcing turnovers was one of the team’s biggest points of emphasis this offseason. With another three against the Seahawks, Denver now has ten on the season. That makes them one of the top-ranked teams in that respect. Last year, they were one of the worst in the NFL. Second-year edge rusher Que Robinson had a big performance against the Seahawks. He had four tackles, two quarterback hits, and one sack on Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold. After the game, the second-year player discussed how Denver’s defense has been able to embark on such a transformation. “I think it’s just the mindset we have. We know we’re a very destructive defensive line and defense, and the plan was to just go out there and play our ball. We definitely did that tonight,” stated Robinson. “We preach being dominant every day. ‘VJ’ does a great job calling it and we do a great job executing it. Like I said, it starts with ‘VJ.’ When he shows that emotion before the game and at practices, when he shows that emotion to us, we feed off that and we go out there and play our best for him.” There’s no doubt the defense is the bright spot of the team a third of the way through the regular season. They’re a well-coached unit that plays with passion and intensity. Without question, they have come a long way since struggling in the season opener against the Kansas City Chiefs. This year’s team is starting to remind me of the 2015 squad that eventually wound up winning Super Bowl 50. They weren’t the greatest on offense and Peyton Manning certainly struggled. Nevertheless, they were able to grind out tough victories due to their prowess on the defensive side of the ball. Hopefully, with extended prep time before their Week 7 matchup versus the Arizona Cardinals, Denver can find a way to be more productive on offense. It’s hard to have faith in that, especially with all the issues, but we have seen the light turn on, and things click the past two seasons after getting a little rest and having more time to prepare. If that happens? You could certainly call the Broncos a contender. If not? Fans across Broncos Country will just have to see how far the defense can carry them.
author: Christopher Hart

title: 8 Things we learned from the Broncos 17-14 OT win over Seattle
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! Another week, another stress-inducing game for the Denver Broncos. It wasn’t pretty, especially in the second half for Bo Nix and the Denver offense. But the team gritted out another win. All that matters is the Broncos beat the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks 17-14 in overtime. Denver now sits […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - OCTOBER 15: Jonah Elliss #52 of the Denver Broncos celebrates after sacking Sam Darnold #14 of the Seattle Seahawks during the third quarter of the game at Empower Field At Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Andrew Wevers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! Another week, another stress-inducing game for the Denver Broncos. It wasn’t pretty, especially in the second half for Bo Nix and the Denver offense. But the team gritted out another win. All that matters is the Broncos beat the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks 17-14 in overtime. Denver now sits at 4-2 after a brutal six-game stretch to start the season. Now the Broncos get a mini-bye before heading to the desert to face the Arizona Cardinals. Wil Lutz with the clutch kick You always hold your breath when the Denver kicker attempts a field goal. And all of Broncos Country did that at the end of the game. Thankfully, it was an exhale of celebration after Lutz nailed the game-winning 53-yard field goal. On this day, he was big nuts Lutz, and absolutely clutch Lutz. Helluva kick. Give Denver’s defense its flowers Down the best cornerback in the NFL in Patrick Surtain II, the team’s best safety in Talanoa Hufanga, and the Broncos hold Jaxon Smith-Njigba and the Seattle offense to 14 points? Damn impressive showing by Denver’s defense. On top of that, the Broncos forced three turnovers, got five sacks, five tackles for loss, and nine passes defended. Perhaps the stat of the night, Denver got 17 quarterback hits on Sam Darnold. In a defensive battle, the Broncos outshone one of the best defenses in the league. The Broncos secondary was fantastic Without the two best players in the unit, and Riley Moss limited most of the night, Denver’s secondary played an unreal game. Yes, JSN got his yards, but when the Broncos needed a play, the guys stepped up. Two of the biggest plays coming from Kris Abrams-Draine and Ja’Quan McMillian forcing huge turnovers, the latter getting the game-winning interception. McMillian is making a habit of this for Denver in clutch moments. He also got a sack. McMillian finished with five tackles (five sol0), one sack, one tackle for loss, two passes defended, and one quarterback hit. Abrams-Draine had six tackles (four solo) and three passes defended. All without PSs and Hufanga. Bo Nix must get better What we saw from the Broncos quarterback in the second half will not cut it. He must play better. What’s perplexing is how good the offense looked on back-to-back touchdown drives in the first half. Why does it have to be one or the other? Obviously, some of the credit goes to the Seattle defense. The Seahawks rank at the top or near the top for each statistical category. But Nix is going to have to start playing with more consistency because what he’s putting on the field is not good enough. It no doubt helps to sit at 4-2, having faced five of the best teams in the NFL, but figure it out. Denver’s running game is terrible The Broncos finished with 74 yards rushing on Thursday night. How the heck did they get that many? I don’t know if it’s J.K. Dobbins or the offensive line suddenly being terrible at run blocking, but this is bad. Perhaps rookie Jonah Coleman is the savior, and he’ll be back in Week 7 against the Cardinals. But similar to Nix, the running game issues have to get fixed. It’s brutal to watch Denver attempt to run the football right now. Dominance at home continues The Mile High Magic has returned. The Broncos improved to 3-0 at home this season after going 9-2 if you include the postseason. Denver has always been one of the best, if not the best, home-field advantages in the NFL. To see the success at home return like this is great to see. Throwback jerseys shine again There is no better throwback jersey in the NFL than the Broncos. And to have Seattle rock their throwbacks gave us veteran fans flashbacks to the old AFC West days. Just like at home, the Broncos remain unbeaten when they rock the snot rocket. Sitting at 4-2 is quite the feat As noted at the top, Denver just faced a brutal six-game stretch to start the season, and they sit at 4-2. When the schedule was released, every single person in Broncos Country would take that record. What should give fans hope is that the Broncos haven’t played their best yet. Similar to last season, we didn’t see the team start putting it all together until the calendar turned to November. Yet despite ugly games and performances, Nix and the offense being a disaster, they’ve beaten four of the best teams in football. That’s reason enough to feel good about this team.
author: Ian St. Clair

title: Inside the Grit Index: 7 NFL Draft prospects to watch
summary: With the Detroit Lions on their bye week, it is a great time to catch up on the college football action and continue tracking which 2027 NFL Draft prospects could be the best fits for the Lions. Unlike most NFL Draft-centric college football previews, the primary focus here is not to tell you which players […]

Unlike most NFL Draft-centric college football previews, the primary focus here is not to tell you which players are the top, most athletically gifted prospects. This is the Grit Index. For more information on what the Grit Index is and how it has evolved, check out the preseason version of this series . Below is a breakdown of the Intangible Qualities (IQs) used to determine a player’s Grit Index score. It’s the midseason check-in; it’s time to start looking at the next group of prospects. Local Spotlight Western Michigan vs. Central Michigan Saturday, Oct. 17 at 1:30 p.m. ET on ESPN+ Jalen Buckley , running back, Western Michigan In the battle for the Victory Cannon Trophy, Buckley is a former walk-on running back turned team captain for the Broncos. Beyond the work ethic to ascend from his walk-on status, Buckley has demonstrated passion and toughness playing through injuries. He played most of the 2025 season with a fractured wrist and proceeded to win 2025 MAC Championship Offensive Player of the Game honors. Jalen Buckley finished with 193 yards and two touchdowns on 19 carries to earn MAC Football Championship Offensive Player of the Game honors. @WMU_Football | #MACtion pic.twitter.com/yVSPV5rJFv — MACtion (@MACSports) December 6, 2025 Draft projection: Day 3 National Spotlight Indiana (5) vs. Ohio State (4) Saturday, Oct. 17 at 12:00 p.m. ET on FOX Carter Smith , offensive line, Indiana Smith, a team captain, returned to Indiana for another season as their starting left tackle despite being highly regarded by NFL Draft analysts . Although he entered the 2026 season with 41 straight starts at tackle, Smith is frequently viewed as having guard/tackle versatility at the next level. Unique for an offensive lineman, Smith has a background playing volleyball in high school. “He’s a great kid, high-character guy, good leader on this team,” Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti said of Smith. #Indiana LT Carter Smith did a nice job moving Alabama defenders in the run game and showcasing his upper body strength and strain ability. Always driving his legs and rooting out defenders to create running lanes. pic.twitter.com/lMrIHILqRS — Devin Jackson (@RealD_Jackson) January 3, 2026 Draft projection: Day 1-2 Jaylen McClain , safety, Ohio State McClain enters his junior year named a team captain with two Iron Buckeye honors to his name, an award given for effort demonstrated in the team’s strength and conditioning program. Off the field, McClain is also a 2026 AFCA Good Works Team Nominee and on the Wuerffel Trophy Watch List (academic Heisman) for founding the Everyday Legends Foundation, a nonprofit dedicated to empowering youth and strengthening underserved communities. Ohio State FS Jaylen McClain has true CF range w/ the trigger timing to turn big plays into incompletions. All 4 of his PBUs vs. Illinois 👇 pic.twitter.com/nHxSdaY40m — Dane Brugler (@dpbrugler) September 28, 2026 Draft projection: Day 2 Alabama (6) vs. Tennessee (14) Saturday, Oct. 17 at 3:30 p.m. ET on ESPN DeSean Bishop , running back, Tennessee Growing up , Bishop was the oldest of five with a single mother, instilling a never-quit mindset leading to his walk-on-to-team-captain story. On the field, 1,407 of his 2,209 yards have come after contact with 67 missed tackles forced, finishing as a semifinalist for the 2025 Burlsworth Trophy (nation’s best former walk-on). Despite playing as the bellcow back in the Vols’ win over Auburn on Oct. 3, setting career highs in rushing attempts (34), rushing yards (220) and rushing touchdowns (3), his passion for the game manifests even without the ball in his hands as a blocker. full_text: Jan 5, 2025; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs (26) and teammates pose for the cameras after his touchdown against the Minnesota Vikings during the second half at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: David Reginek-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con On Friday night, the Detroit Lions’ social media dropped a not-so-subtle hint about their next uniform combination. On Twitter, the Lions not only tweeted out a photo of a black Lions logo with a bright blue outline, but they also changed their Twitter logo to the same image. Detroit has done this several times in the past, and it means only one thing: the black uniforms are coming out this upcoming week. If you’re unfamiliar, the black Lions uniforms—dropped in 2024 and officially called Motor City Muscle—feature a black jersey, black pants, and a popping blue helmet with the black Lions logo. You can see it used in action below. Assuming all the hint dropping is true, the Lions will wear these for their home Week 7 game against the Green Bay Packers next week. The following week, the Lions host the Minnesota Vikings, and they’ve already announced that they will be wearing their new Rivalry Uniforms for that Week 8 divisional matchup . This offseason, the NFL announced and debuted the Rivalry design for all of the NFC North and AFC South teams. The Lions’ uniforms feature an all-grey look with black and blue stripes on the shoulder pads designed to mimic the eyes of a Lion. In Detroit’s debut photoshoot of the Rivalry uniforms , the jerseys and pants were paired with the same blue helmet from the Motor City Muscle uniforms. So we’ve got a couple of weeks of non-traditional Lions uniforms for what will be a pivotal two-game stretch of divisional games out of Detroit’s Week 6 bye.

title: Detroit Lions free up roster spots; place 3 injured players on IR
summary: On Friday of the Detroit Lions’ bye week, the team announced that they have placed three players on injured reserve: wide receiver/returner Tom Kennedy, offensive lineman Ben Bartch, and linebacker Devin White. All three players must miss a minimum of the next four weeks but may be out longer due to their injuries. Kennedy, the […]
full_text: DETROIT, MI - SEPTEMBER 13: Detroit Lions wide receiver Tom Kennedy (85) waits to receive a punt during a regular season NFL football game between the New Orleans Saints and the Detroit Lions on September 13, 2026 at Ford Field in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Scott W. Grau/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images On Friday of the Detroit Lions’ bye week, the team announced that they have placed three players on injured reserve: wide receiver/returner Tom Kennedy, offensive lineman Ben Bartch, and linebacker Devin White. All three players must miss a minimum of the next four weeks but may be out longer due to their injuries. Kennedy, the Lions’ starting punt and kick returner, injured his MCL in Week 5 and will require season-ending surgery . Detroit was originally hopeful Kennedy could return this season, but further testing showed he would not be able to return before the end of the season. The Lions are now on the hunt for a new returner, although they do have some intriguing options on the practice squad , including recently signed DeAndre Carter . All four practice squad wide receivers are expected to be in the mix for the role and could claim one of the three spots freed up by these transactions. Bartch started the Lions’ Week 2 game against the Buffalo Bills, filling in for left guard Christian Mahogany, but he suffered a foot injury that would keep him out of the next three weeks of practices and games. With Bartch needing to miss at least four more games, the oft-injured lineman is in for another season where he is sidelined by injury. This move could open the door for starting center Cade Mays to return to the active roster, as he is currently practicing within his injury evaluation window , and could potentially be ready to play against the Green Bay Packers in Week 7. White suffered a broken forearm in Week 5, and like Kennedy, will require surgery. However, White could recover in time to return to the field, as broken bones typically take eight to 12 weeks to heal. With six linebackers already on the active roster, the Lions will not need to add another player to his position group, and his spot will most likely go to safety Brian Branch, who is also within his injury evaluation window and could return to the active roster in Week 7. Because the Lions are on their bye week, they’re in no rush to fill any of these open spots if they deem a player hasn’t done enough to win a role on the active roster—like at returner—or if a player is not healthy enough to return, such as Branch and Mays. It’s also worth keeping an eye on veteran safety Jalen Mills, who was released from the practice squad this past week after exhausting all three of his roster elevations. If the Lions feel they need more depth, they could look to bring him back as well.

title: Which Week 6 game are you most looking forward to?
summary: After a nice bounce-back performance in the desert in Week 5, where the Detroit Lions rolled over the Arizona Cardinals to the tune of 45-21, the team now heads into their bye week on a high note. And while having a Week 6 bye isn’t the most ideal in terms of where it falls during […]
full_text: After a nice bounce-back performance in the desert in Week 5, where the Detroit Lions rolled over the Arizona Cardinals to the tune of 45-21, the team now heads into their bye week on a high note. And while having a Week 6 bye isn’t the most ideal in terms of where it falls during the course of the regular season, it comes at a decent time for Detroit. They are 3-2 through five weeks of play, firmly in contention in what figures to be a highly competitive NFC North race, and will likely be getting some reinforcements after the bye week is over. Now with the players enjoying their bye week and most of the coaches likely hunkered down at 222 Republic Drive preparing for the Week 7 matchup against the Green Bay Packers, we get to enjoy a weekend of stress-free football. That brings us to today’s question of the day—which game from the Week 6 slate are you most looking forward to watching? My answer: Naturally, I am going with the Sunday Night Football game between the Packers and the Dallas Cowboys. Green Bay has had some major ups-and-downs so far this year, while the Cowboys feature one of the more high-powered offenses in the game. Could this be a primetime shootout at Lambeau Field? Either way, it will be a chance for Lions fans to get one last look at the Packers before Week 7 rolls around. What about you? Which game from the Week 6 slate are you most looking forward to watching? Let us know in the comments below.

Mandatory Credit: Matt Kartozian-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Detroit Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Shepard has drawn a lot of criticism for how his defense has performed through the first month of the 2026 season. But following a Week 5 win in Arizona, the Cardinals coaching staff praised Shepard for his defensive game plan, calling it “unique” and “fascinating.” “That was pretty unique,” Cardinals offensive coordinator Nathaniel Hackett said of the Lions bracketing both WR Michael Wilson and TE Trey McBride. “I’ve been doing this a while— and it’s funny, the closest thing I ever saw was, we were playing the Ravens with Davante Adams, and I think there were, like, two to three guys on him the whole time. We were working on all these things we thought were going to happen, but they said, ‘nope, we’re going to take him away.’ […] But yeah, it was fascinating.” Here’s a clip of Hackett discussing Sheppard’s approach, via Ari Meirov: #Cardinals OC Nathaniel Hackett on teams double-teaming both Trey McBride and Michael Wilson: “That was pretty unique. The closest thing I ever saw was vs. the Ravens with Davante Adams, and I think there were, like, two to three guys on him the whole time. We just have to keep… https://t.co/8ovBWnO8XG pic.twitter.com/Qpi7Vhk8MH — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) October 15, 2026 The Cardinals entered this game with McBride and Wilson as their primary offensive weapons, with McBride accounting for 38% of the Cardinals’ offensive targets this season and Wilson right behind at 30%. No other Cardinals offensive player accounts for more than 9.5%. When the Cardinals got into third-and-long situations, Sheppard countered by running bracket coverage on both McBride and Wilson, forcing quarterback Jacoby Brissett to beat them another way, and outside of the first drive, this strategy was highly effective. Here’s a look at the Cardinals’ second possession of the game near the end of the first quarter on third-and-7. As you can see in the screenshots below, Lions LB Jack Campbell lines up in press vs. McBride (Yellow), and safety Chuck Clark has over-the-top and inside responsibilities. On the opposite side of the field, Wilson (orange) is bracketed by CB D.J. Reed on the outside and safety Keith Abney with over-the-top and inside coverage: On the next third down, the Cardinals need 12 yards, so the Lions play a deeper zone, but on the following two third-down plays the Lions use bracket coverage again and again: In the end, the Lions’ bracket coverage on the Cardinals’ two primary weapons forced the Cardinals to look elsewhere, and they couldn’t convert on 10 of their 18 third-down attempts, including five straight three-and-outs. While Sheppard has certainly deserved some criticism for how the defense has performed through five weeks, he also deserves his share of praise for his defensive strategy against the Cardinals, given how effective it was.

full_text: Detroit Lions executive vice president and general manager Brad Holmes speaks during media availability at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Thursday, Jan. 8, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Earlier this week, we checked in on the popularity of Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell . As of Friday morning, Campbell had an approval rating just over 91 percent among Lions fans. Now, let’s turn our attention to general manager Brad Holmes. Without a doubt, Holmes has faced more scrutiny than just about anyone in the Lions organization these days, save perhaps defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard. Upset fans point to the fruitlessness of Detroit’s 2024 NFL Draft class—particularly with the first three picks: Terrion Arnold (cut), Ennis Rakestraw (0 starts, 11 games), and Giovanni Manu (four games, one start). Lately, fans have been frustrated about his insistence prior to the season that they liked the players in their cornerback room (not sure what else he was supposed to say), only to see cornerback clearly be the team’s biggest issue through the first month of the season. And while Holmes certainly deserves plenty of criticism for how the secondary has turned out this year, it’s also important to point out the clear improvements he’s made on the roster this season. The Lions’ offensive line has made a significant turnaround thanks to the recent investments in Blake Miller, Tate Ratledge, Juice Scruggs, and Christian Mahogany—and we haven’t even seen what Detroit has in Cade Mays yet. Similarly, the defensive line is finally producing at a top-tier level. Thanks to draft investments in Aidan Hutchinson, Alim McNeill, and Tyleik Williams—along with free agent/waiver adds DJ Wonnum and Tyler Lacy—Detroit has an impressive pass rush and strong run defense presence up the middle. Holmes even found an unlikely contributor in sixth-round rookie Skyler Gill-Howard. And, again, we haven’t even seen the full potential of second-round pick Derrick Moore. And if you look at most of the players Detroit opted to move on from this offseason, they have not been producing on par with the contracts they signed elsewhere . Still, you have to consider the entire outlook before you vote. Before you do, here’s a look at Holmes’ approval ratings throughout the years. title: ESPN: Josh Jacobs has spoken to the NFL in their investigation
summary: According to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler, the NFL has had a discussion with Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs, which is an important piece of information now that he’s been reinstated by the league and removed from the commisioner exempt list. Here is Fowler’s relevant quote on the subject and the corresponding video, which touches […]
full_text: (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler , the NFL has had a discussion with Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs, which is an important piece of information now that he’s been reinstated by the league and removed from the commisioner exempt list . Here is Fowler’s relevant quote on the subject and the corresponding video, which touches on multiple league-wide topics beyond just Jacobs’ standing with the NFL: They ruled that he is off the commisioner exempt list starting on Monday. So, to start Week 7, he can go back to the team facility with the Packers, work his way back into the lineup for Week 7. Now that doesn’t mean that the investigation into his domestic incident is over. I’m told that is ongoing, but I talked to the attorney of the woman in the case, who said she has not participated in the investigation part. She has not been interviewed, due to privacy concerns. Josh Jacobs, I heard, has talked to the NFL. So a lot of legwork is done. They key here, Kevin, is the video that does exist, parties involved are trying to keep the video from being released. The police locally are trying to get it released. Does it ever come to light is the question? If it does, the league could step back in and create a longer suspension. Running through QBs ailments (Penix, Caleb, Hurts) as well as the latest on Josh Jacobs @SportsCenter with @KevinNegandhi pic.twitter.com/VHmPG3G2nM — Jeremy Fowler (@JFowlerESPN) October 16, 2026 This is the first time that it’s been reported that Jacobs has been interviewed as part of the league’s investigation. Previously, reports stated that Jacobs had not talked with the NFL — at those points in time. Here is why Jacobs’ talk with the league is a pretty important piece of information: When Ray Rice was suspended in 2014, the league initially suspended Rice for two games, after he had his discussion with the league about his domestic incident. When the video of Rice’s domestic violence incident was released to the public, the NFL punished Rice further, giving him an indefinite suspension. When Rice appealed the second suspension, on the grounds that he was already punished once for the same personal conduct violation, a judge ruled in Rice’s favor , stating that the league had to reinstate Rice back into the league and pay him out for games missed because he never misled the league during his interview during the NFL’s investigation. In short, Rice was truthful with the league, so the league had no basis to punish Rice more severely, just because a video caused a public reaction that the NFL did not want to deal with. In the eyes of the judge, the video did not change whether or not the league had all the information they needed to make their initial suspension of Rice, even if the NFL wanted to escalate the suspension due to the public’s reaction to the video. Because of the lessons learned in the Rice case, the league has taken a different approach with the Jacobs case. Instead of suspending Jacobs initially, they allowed him to spend six weeks on the commisioner exempt list — which is technically not a suspension, as Jacobs continued to get paid while he was unavailable for the Packers. The NFL only gets to press the suspension button once for the same personal conduct violation, as long as they aren’t misled during their investigation, but the league appears to be maneuvering in a way to reserve its right to suspend Jacobs in case the video in this dispute causes a negative public reaction — even if Jacobs was being truthful with them in their investigation up to his return in Week 7. Their one chance to hit the suspension button is still preserved. Financially, Jacobs has not been punished directly by the league in any way up to this point, but the NFL will likely announce an official suspension for the running back when the dust finally settles on the fate of the video. As a reminder, time on the exempt list will count as time served toward a suspension. Both Jacobs and the victim in the case are suing the Hobart-Lawrence Police Department to keep the video sealed , and the filing claims that the police department has 20 days to respond from October 14th. — Update: I have received an email from Brian Glicklich, the CEO of Digital Strategy Ltd., a self-described crisis communications and reputation management firm , who sent the following statement on behalf of attorneys Clarence F. Duchac III, David Z. Chesnoff and Richard A. Schonfeld — Jacobs’ representation: Josh has dedicated the last several months to bettering himself, and he accepts responsibility for his actions. He is excited to get back to work and on the field with his teammates. Josh is grateful for the support he is receiving from his teammates, coaches, the Packers organization, and the greatest fans in the world. Since there are ongoing legal matters, he will not have any further comment.

title: How the Packers’ defense is pressuring into interceptions
summary: The Green Bay Packers defense is climbing out of the bottom of the NFL’s worst defenses after a lopsided Week 3 loss to the Falcons, turning in a five-turnover performance in Week 5. They ranked 26th in EPA per play after Week 3 and now rank 14th after Week 5. While their run defense EPA […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers defense is climbing out of the bottom of the NFL’s worst defenses after a lopsided Week 3 loss to the Falcons, turning in a five-turnover performance in Week 5. They ranked 26th in EPA per play after Week 3 and now rank 14th after Week 5. While their run defense EPA per play and run defense success rate allowed remain below league average, the Packers defense is surviving on the strength of their pass defense. In week five, they forced Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum into three interceptions. The quality of quarterbacks faced might not be anything but below average, but the pass coverage unit shows on tape that they are sound in their assignments regardless, meaning they don’t give up ground or space easily within their play calls. First interception The first interception came with 5:39 remaining in the first quarter on a 2nd-and-10. Tyson Bagent was the Bears starter this game until Keenum took over late in the game. Bagent brought the offense out in an 11 personnel shotgun formation to run a 3×1 dagger concept Ben Johnson has used to carve up opposing teams in the secondary. The Packers are playing cover-8 “trix” once the formation motions to a 3×1. In cover-8, the coverage plays cover-2 to the trips passing strength while the backside safety keys in on the final #3 receiver or the deepest crossing route. Luther Burden is the receiver sent in motion running the dig route from behind the bunch receivers who are running deeper crossing routes across the field. Bagent is looking for the dig route and tried to rip the pass over Javon Bullard gaining depth in the vertical hook under the dig. Bullard tipped the pass up, allowing safety Xavier McKinney to run under the tipped ball from his deep half safety zone. Second interception Bagent’s second interception came with 41 seconds left in the third quarter and down 23-7 on a pass intended for Colston Loveland. The pass was intercepted by McKinney again. The Bears started in an empty 3×2 formation with trips to the right. Bagent is targeting Loveland running the dig route on a two receiver wrap concept with a short curl route under the dig. The intent is to pull up the curl flat player to the curl route and hit the dig in the window between the curl flat and weak hook defender. The Packers are playing cover-3 strong buzz rotation with the safety buzzing down to the strong hook toward the nickel, what Gannon would “Ralph” rotation (rotation to the right to the nickel). McKinney, as the strong hook defender, reads Bagent’s eyes the whole way and with no one threatening his zone, McKinney works to the middle of the field to play the pass to Loveland. Bagent is late on the throw, has to try to fit the pass over the hook defender, and throws it too far in front of Loveland and right into the hands of McKinney, who started from the far hash. Third interception The third interception came with 12:58 left in the 4th quarter. Case Keenum was in for Bagent, who drove the offense into the red zone before turning it over on a hurried throw with pressure in his face. The Bears were in an empty 3×2 formation again here on 4th and goal from the 9-yard line. Keenum tried to hit Rome Odunze on a double move over the middle but Ty’Ron Hopper came racing over from his quarter/flat zone to intercept the pass. The defense is in red zone quarters where they first show pressure and a cover-0 look. Hopper and Zaire Franklin back out of the blitz but Keenum is already changing the protection to slide right in case he gets a free runner off his right edge. The result is disastrous, though. The protection slide away from Lukas Van Ness proved to be costly. Van Ness came off the offense’s left edge untouched as the left tackle took his block inside to the inside rusher. Van Ness forced Keenum to drift away from the pocket and throw across his body to Odunze. Hopper read his eyes the whole way and came over from his zone to make the interception at the goal line where he eventually returned it out to the 20-yard line. The Packers coverage will be tested on Sunday night as the Cowboys come into Green Bay eager to get back on track after a brutal loss to the Buccaneers in week 5. The Cowboys like to throw deep, and the combination of CeeDee Lamb and Dak Prescott is nothing to scoff at.

title: Packers Injury Report: Green Bay rules out 4 vs. Dallas Cowboys
summary: The Green Bay Packers ruled out defensive lineman Jonathan Ford (calf), defensive lineman Javon Hargrave (Achilles), receiver Skyy Moore (ankle) and cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring) on Friday. None of these players will suit up against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, and the Packers will likely need to make roster moves to backfill for these injured […]
full_text: (Photo by Rich Graessle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Green Bay Packers ruled out defensive lineman Jonathan Ford (calf), defensive lineman Javon Hargrave (Achilles), receiver Skyy Moore (ankle) and cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring) on Friday. None of these players will suit up against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, and the Packers will likely need to make roster moves to backfill for these injured players. Beyond the players ruled out, offensive lineman Aaron Banks (knee/toe), defensive lineman Anthony Campbell (ankle), cornerback Brandon Cisse (hip) and offensive lineman Jacob Monk (quadricep) are listed as questionable for Week 6. Receiver Savion Williams (ankle), whose IR practice window has opened up, is questionable, while defensive lineman Jordon Riley (Achilles), whose PUP practice window has opened up, is doubtful. With so many moving parts, let’s just lay out the Packers’ full roster (including players’ injury statuses) going into Sunday Night Football . Quarterback Jordan Love Tyrod Taylor Nothing is concerning here. Running Back MarShawn Lloyd Pierre Strong Jr. Kaleb Johnson Nothing is concerning here. Receiver Christian Watson Matthew Golden Skyy Moore (out) Bo Melton J. Michael Sturdivant The Packers almost always have five or more receivers on the 48-man game-day roster, so expect to see a move here with Moore already ruled out — be it the activation of Williams to the 53-man roster or a call-up for receiver Isaiah Neyor from the practice squad. It’s also possible that Green Bay places Moore on the injured reserve to free up a roster spot. Tight End Tucker Kraft Mark Redman Jonnu Smith Josh Whyle Nothing is concerning here. Offensive Line Jordan Morgan Laken Tomlinson Sean Rhyan Travis Glover Anthony Belton Aaron Banks (questionable) Kevin Zeitler Jager Burton Jacob Monk (questionable) Donovan Jennings Nothing is concerning here, considering the Packers will need to scratch three at the position anyway. Even if Banks and Monk can’t go, Green Bay will still need a healthy scratch at the position. Defensive Line Karl Brooks Devonte Wyatt Javon Hargrave (out) Chris McClellan Jonathan Ford (out) Anthony Campbell (questionable) This is red alert/it could cost the team the game levels of concern. The Packers need five interior defensive linemen to be able to keep guys fresh, but they only have three players on the 53-man roster who are absolutely 100 percent going to play on Sunday. Green Bay is going to need two of the following players to give them reps: Campbell (questionable), Riley (PUP, doubtful) and/or a practice squad player David Blay Jr. Edge Defender Lukas Van Ness Barryn Sorrell Brenton Cox Jr. Dani Dennis-Sutton Nothing is concerning here, unless the team gets the bright idea to move Lukas Van Ness to the interior defensive line to help their numbers issue there…which would leave the Packers with just three edge defenders for the entire game against Dallas. That’s one issue about moving LVN around. Off-Ball Linebacker Zaire Franklin Isaiah McDuffie Ty’Ron Hopper Nick Niemann Kristian Welch Nothing is concerning here. Cornerback Keisean Nixon Brandon Cisse (questionable) Carrington Valentine Benjamin St-Juste (out) Kamal Hadden The Packers probably want to keep five players at cornerback on the 48-man game-day roster this week, not because of defense but because Bo Melton is having to play more offense as Skyy Moore’s replacement, meaning a similar body type (likely a cornerback) will have to backfill for Melton on special teams. Thankfully, Keisean Nixon was cleared from his injury, but now Cisse could potentially miss action and St-Juste is guaranteed to miss action. At minimum, assume that rookie practice squad cornerback Domani Jackson gets activated for his first NFL game. Safety Xavier McKinney Evan Williams Javon Bullard Kitan Oladapo Specialists K Trey Smack P Daniel Whelan LS Matt Orzech — So what do the Packers need to add this weekend? One receiver IR: Savon Williams PS: Isaiah Neyor, Quincy Skinner Jr. and/or Coleman Owen One or two defensive linemen PUP: Jordon Riley PS: David Blay Jr. If the team can’t carry five defensive linemen without moving Lukas Van Ness over, look for practice squad edge rushers Nyjalik Kelly or Arron Mosby to potentially be called up. One or two cornerbacks PS: Domani Jackson and/or Elijah Culp Look for the team to make a decent number of moves on Saturday. Remember, Hargrave and Moore are IR candidates, the team already has an open roster spot on the 53 and the team has the option to use two practice squad elevations, too. There’s a bunch of different buttons they can press to get to a 48-man game-day roster. Brandon Cisse added to the injury report and is questionable. pic.twitter.com/ByPqPtKkwm — Rob Demovsky (@RobDemovsky) October 16, 2026

title: NFL to reinstate Josh Jacobs to Packers’ active roster on Monday, per report
summary: The Green Bay Packers got the Friday afternoon news dump treatment this week, with a big breaking news item coming on the heels of the Milwaukee Brewers’ clinching win in the NLCS on Thursday night. According to veteran NFL reporter Tom Pelissero, running back Josh Jacobs will be removed from the Commissioner’s Exempt list on […]
full_text: ASHWAUBENON, WISCONSIN - JUNE 09: Josh Jacobs #8 of the Green Bay Packers participates in drills during the Green Bay Packers mandatory minicamp at Don Hutson Center on June 09, 2026 in Ashwaubenon, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers got the Friday afternoon news dump treatment this week, with a big breaking news item coming on the heels of the Milwaukee Brewers’ clinching win in the NLCS on Thursday night. According to veteran NFL reporter Tom Pelissero, running back Josh Jacobs will be removed from the Commissioner’s Exempt list on Monday. The move will make him eligible to play in the Packers’ week 7 game against the Detroit Lions. The NFL will remove Packers RB Josh Jacobs from the commissioner exempt list Monday, sources tell @ringer @netflixsports . pic.twitter.com/GeeF5MXBUE — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) October 16, 2026 The move will effectively leave Jacobs as having served a six-game suspension on the list while his legal case worked its way through the court system. After initially being charged with five charges related to domestic abuse (including one felony charge), Jacobs eventually pled no contest to two misdemeanor charges: battery and criminal damage to property. The reason for his impending removal from the exempt list is likely related to a recent filing by both Jacobs and the victim in the case, his former girlfriend. The victim had previously filed suit to block a surveillance video of the incident from being released to the public, and on Thursday, Jacobs joined that lawsuit in support of the request to seal the evidence permanently sealed . With the NFL unlikely to get access to the video and Jacobs having already served what is effectively a six-week suspension, the league evidently felt that it had no further justification to keep Jacobs from playing. In Jacobs’ absence, the Packers’ run game has sputtered with MarShawn Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson, Chris Brooks, and Pierre Strong, Jr. running the football. The Packers as an organization have generally spoken in support of Jacobs, though whether Jacobs would return to the lineup immediately in Week 7 is unclear as players on the Exempt list are barred from practicing with the team. In all likelihood, he would need at least another week of ramping up before being ready for game action, which could delay his season debut until Week 8 (Thursday Night Football vs. Carolina) or Week 9 (Sunday at New England).

title: NFL predictions: Expecting lots of points and a Packers win over the Cowboys
summary: Sunday night’s game should be a fun one. The Green Bay Packers host the Dallas Cowboys in a matchup of high-powered offenses, something that Packers fans weren’t so confident in just a few weeks ago. But last weekend, the Packers scored more than 30 points for the first time since last Thanksgiving, and they were […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 28: Jordan Love #10 of the Green Bay Packers celebrates a touchdown against the Dallas Cowboys during the fourth quarter in the game at AT&T Stadium on September 28, 2025 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images Sunday night’s game should be a fun one. The Green Bay Packers host the Dallas Cowboys in a matchup of high-powered offenses, something that Packers fans weren’t so confident in just a few weeks ago. But last weekend, the Packers scored more than 30 points for the first time since last Thanksgiving, and they were giving thanks to Jordan Love and the deep ball as the quarterback threw for more than 350 yards in a 31-7 win over the Chicago Bears. Meanwhile, the Cowboys have a high-powered offense of their own, with an excellent receiver tandem of their own in CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. Those two wideouts are catching passes from Dak Prescott, and before last Thursday’s surprising 24-16 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the Cowboys had put up at least 31 points in each of their previous three games. It’s no surprise then that the Cowboys and Packers are expected to load up on points when the two teams meet on Sunday Night Football in Week 6. Furthermore, Dallas has allowed at least 20 points in each of their five games so far and 28 or more in three of their five games. The Packers are a bit more inconsistent, with two games of 35+ allowed but three with 17 or fewer. All of those results combined have this week’s expected point total at 52.5, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . What do APC’s writers think? We’re all taking the over this week. The Packers and Cowboys combined for a whopping 80 points in last year’s tie game in Texas, and there aren’t a whole lot of reasons to expect them to play a low-scoring game this week. But who will win the game? We’re sticking with the home team here and expecting Green Bay to put up big numbers against a Cowboys defense that ranks in the bottom five of nearly every major statistical category. title: Packers offensive line should move forward without Aaron Banks
summary: Packers guard Aaron Banks was a limited participant in practice on Thursday, the second time this week he’s practiced on a limited basis. “Limited participant” is a pretty good description of Banks’ season to this point. He was out of much of training camp with a knee injury, which also cost him an appearance in […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NJ - SEPTEMBER 20: Aaron Banks #65 of the Green Bay Packers during the game against the New York Jets on September 20, 2026 at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Rich Graessle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Packers guard Aaron Banks was a limited participant in practice on Thursday, the second time this week he’s practiced on a limited basis. “Limited participant” is a pretty good description of Banks’ season to this point. He was out of much of training camp with a knee injury, which also cost him an appearance in the Packers’ Week 1 loss to the Vikings. Then, a toe injury knocked him out of the Packers’ Week 2 game against the Jets after just 22 snaps and he hasn’t been seen since. Now, with Banks on the way back, the natural question is if and when he gets his left guard job back. Asked about that possibility this week, head coach Matt LaFleur was diplomatic. “[The offensive line situation] is going to be pretty fluid,” he said. “We have to see where [Banks] is at. He hasn’t practiced in a long time, and those other guys have come in and done a really good job.” But I’m free to say what LaFleur wouldn’t. There’s no reason to put Banks back in the lineup, and the Packers should functionally move on from their 2025 free agent signing. For starters, replacement left guard Laken Tomlinson has been perfectly adequate. Nabbed from the Cowboys’ practice squad after extended auditions for Donovan Jennings and Jager Burton yielded little, he’s played every snap of the last two games. Nobody on the Packers’ line has been much help in the ground game, but Tomlinson has more than held up his end of the bargain as a pass rusher, allowing just two pressures over the Packers’ last two games. Tomlinson’s performance is, I think, a big reason we’ve seen Sean Rhyan improve over the past couple of weeks, too. With Donovan Jennings, Jager Burton, and Jacob Monk at the guard spots next to him during the Packers’ first three games, Rhyan looked constantly frazzled, careening from disaster to disaster as the pass protection crumbled around him. He could barely shift his attention to helping one beleaguered backup before the other would find himself in a terrible mess. I don’t think it’s a coincidence that Rhyan’s best two graded games of the year, per Pro Football Focus, have come with Tomlinson to his left and the surprisingly solid Travis Glover to his right. Furthermore, inserting Banks back into the lineup would just be repeating the same mistake that got the Packers into this mess. Banks’ limited reliability is a big reason the Packers found themselves in a pit of offensive line despair early this year. That shouldn’t have been a surprise. Banks was consistently injured for the 49ers and was consistently injured in 2025. That he would be battling the injury bug again this year is only a shock if you haven’t been paying attention. The Packers should resign themselves to Banks playing out the role of an expensive backup. That’s certainly not ideal, but it seems like the best way forward. They’ve found stability on the offensive line and there’s no reason to tinker with it. Laken Tomlinson has put in admirable work at left guard, as has Travis Glover at right guard, and he’s about to yield his role to Kevin Zeitler. A Morgan-Tomlinson-Rhyan-Zeitler-Belton offensive line is more than good enough to get the job done going forward. There’s no doubt that the finances would sting. Banks counts more than $12 million against the Packers cap this year. The Packers’ projected starting lineup without him only counts about $14.7 million against the cap. Those are some bad optics, financially! It’s never good to have a big chunk of salary cap riding the pine. But optics don’t win games, and it’s hard to make a compelling case that Banks will help the Packers do that at this point. The Packers should move forward with a non-Banks offensive line. Unless and until they need him in the lineup, they’ll be more than fine doing what they can with what they have.

title: NFL Predictions: Houston Texans Lay the Smackdown on the London Jaguars
summary: Not long ago, the Houston Texans were a pall over the conscience of Texans faithful, a tremendous disappointment of a start to the regular season, and bordering on franchise infamy. Today, following their first win of the season and a blockbuster trade that reunites QB C.J. Stroud with collegiate teammate WR Marvin Harrison Jr., the […]
full_text: Not long ago, the Houston Texans were a pall over the conscience of Texans faithful, a tremendous disappointment of a start to the regular season, and bordering on franchise infamy. Today, following their first win of the season and a blockbuster trade that reunites QB C.J. Stroud with collegiate teammate WR Marvin Harrison Jr., the Texans are the HOT once again! Oh yeah! @fox26houston MARVIN IS GOING TO LONDON! 🏈 Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans officially confirmed that newly acquired wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. WILL play this Sunday against the Jacksonville Jaguars across the pond! After joining the team via trade from the Arizona Cardinals, Harrison jumped straight into late-night playbook grinding with assistant WR coach Tyron Carrier. Coach DeMeco says his work ethic made the transition seamless at practice—and now C.J. Stroud gets his college target back on the field! Drop a 🤘 in the comments if you’re hyped to see MHJ in Steel Blue! ♬ original sound – FOX 26 Houston – FOX 26 Houston On top of that, the Texans released an encouraging injury report on Wednesday that detailed multiple players return to participation: S Ja’Marcus Ingram (limited), LB Henry To’oTo’o (limited), and WR Tank Dell (full) , who may be nearing a return to the field for the first time in nearly two years. S M.J. Stewart and RT Braden Smith also returned to practice last week, meaning the Texans will be significantly closer to full strength for their week six game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. While the Texans will still be missing some key pieces come Sunday (RB David Montgomery and S Jalen Pitre), they’ll appreciate the extra roster depth that joined them on the flight into the United Kingdom on Thursday, where they’ll face off against the Jags at Wembley Stadium in London at 8:30AM CST Sunday morning. The Texans are currently listed as 2.5-point underdogs on FanDuel. Honestly, considering the Jaguars’ excellent start to the regular season, these odds paint a favorable picture for Houston. The bookies are expecting this game to be a close one, and if any of the several Texans players returning from injury can contribute right away, they may just pull an upset in the Jaguars’ “home away from home” in London. Though, despite the general optimism surrounding Houston’s offense, FanDuel still expects Houston’s first drive to end in a punt. That won’t stop me from placing some lofty predictions on the Texans offense, though! Prediction 1: Texans WR Marvin Harrison Jr. will have not one, but TWO touchdown receptions ! While the trade for Harrison was very exciting, the reality of it all has left the Texans fanbase split. Some are in love with this trade and think this will launch the Texans back into playoff contention, and others think this was a waste of 2027 draft capital that won’t solve any of Houston’s most pressing issues. I personally am still a bit on the fence on the decision overall, but as for right now, I am ALL IN on Marvin Harrison Jr. lighting up this Jaguars defense in the red zone. One of Harrison’s best traits coming out of college was his ability to get seperation in the endzone, using his footwork and length to find a way open at the perfect time for his quarterback. Texans QB C.J. Stroud even spoke of Harrison’s abilities during the 2024 NFL Draft when he was selected fourth overall by the Arizona Cardinals: ”…I’m telling you, [Harrison] like, does this thing, where like…before the ball gets to him, he’ll like, move his body suddenly, and a dude will like…the DBs will go to his inside hip and he’ll shake out. Like he feels guys behind him…My big challenge…is the offensive coordinator…just find some ways to get him one-on-one. Find ways to get him to show his route-running. And not even show it, but just dominate in it.” – C.J. Stroud CJ Stroud had plenty to say about Marvin Harrison Jr. during Bleacher Report’s 2024 NFL Draft show, shortly after Harrison was selected by the Cardinals. On Harrison’s route running and awareness: “I’ve seen Marv in practice, and that’s where you see guys who are great be great… pic.twitter.com/rAyMnaogNL — Houston Stressans (@TexansCommenter) October 11, 2026 Something tells me Stroud’s opinion on Harrison is just as high now as it was during this 2024 NFL Draft clip, and is currently pounding the table for Nick Caley to scheme up some one-on-one opportunities for Harrison Jr. for his Texans debut. The Jaguars will do what they can to give Stroud muddy looks in coverage, but with three of their top four cornerbacks nursing injuries and listed as questionable as of Thursday, I expect their defense to find it difficult to cover a savvy receiver like Harrison Jr. Prediction 2: Will Anderson Jr. will have another three-sack game ! A few weeks ago, Battle Red Blog writer Mike Bullock predicted Will Anderson Jr. would get three sacks on Dak Prescott and the Dallas Cowboys in week four. While that prediction did not end up coming true that Sunday, it very much did the following week, so Mike can credit himself for not necessarily being wrong, but just ahead of the curve. Well, I’m going to take a note from him, and I’ll also predict a three-sack performance from Will Anderson Jr.! Anderson has firmly entrenched himself as one the very best pass-rushers in the NFL, but this year, he seems to be breaching even further into exceptional territory. Five games into the season and he’s already tallied 7.5 sacks, 10 TFLs, 27 tackles, a forced fumble, a pass deflection, and a seemingly infinite number of pressures. Some of his best work came late in Houston’s victory last week against the Tennessee Titans, where he tallied 3.0 sacks in the second half and practically slammed the door on the Tennessee Titans as he kicked them down into the AFC South’s cellar. When he’s on, he is truly a game-wrecking defender. Will Anderson Jr’s 7th entry to his DPOY campaign. pic.twitter.com/SoDE3P3gFa https://t.co/dfc1EGDVum — Chancellor Johnson (@ChancellorTV) October 11, 2026 Will Anderson’s dominance alone isn’t why I expect him to have another great game, though. Another reason for my bullish stance on him entering this game in particular is because of the Jaguars situation as tackle. Starting LT Anton Harrison departed the Jaguars vs. Eagles game last Sunday in the third quarter with a right knee injury, which will require arthroscopic knee surgery. While it is still unknown if this surgery will be season-ending or not, it will certainly be knocking Harrison out of the starting lineup this Sunday, which means the Jaguars starting tackles will likely be Walker Little on the left side and Cole Van Lanen on the right side. Both players are still good tackles that have plenty of recent starting experience with the Jaguars, so it won’t be easy pickings for Will Anderson, but that’s what will make his three-sack game even more impressive! I think this will be the game where Anderson’s inner super saiyan emerges and just dominates the game from start to finish. He and DE Danielle Hunter combined for 4.5 sacks and 2 forced fumbles on Jaguars’ QB Trevor Lawrence in their last meeting – the remarkable 36-29 comeback victory led by QB Davis Mills – and I expect both to do a similar amount of damage this time around. Will Anderson is already FanDuel’s betting favorite to win Defensive Player of the Year this season at +120, but another three-sack performance here would push him to over 10 sacks and possibly into MVP discussion. Prediction 3: Texans 27, Jaguars 24 I’m a little nervous with this prediction considering Houston’s recent track record in one-score games, but I’m going out on a limb here and predicting that the Texans will overcome the Jaguars by chewing the clock on the last drive of the game and then by kicking a long game-winning field goal as time expires, not unlike Jaguars’ kicker Cam Little’s heroic field goal in the final seconds of Jacksonville’s win over the Philadelphia Eagles. This time, however, the Jaguars will be on the losing…
