title: Mansoor Delane and Nohl Williams tandem a ‘pleasant surprise’ for Chiefs
summary: The 2026 Kansas City Chiefs feature a largely retooled defense after multiple key contributors departed in free agency last offseason. The unit currently ranks seventh in the league, allowing 19.3 points per game. Much of that falls on a secondary that features rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane — the sixth overall selection from April’s draft. Speaking […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2026 Kansas City Chiefs feature a largely retooled defense after multiple key contributors departed in free agency last offseason. The unit currently ranks seventh in the league, allowing 19.3 points per game. Much of that falls on a secondary that features rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane — the sixth overall selection from April’s draft. Speaking before Thursday’s practice, defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo looked back on Delane’s strong game in Week 4 against the Las Vegas Raiders and lauded the job the rookie is doing opposite second-year pro Nohl Williams. “[Delane] is on a progression upward,” remarked the coach. “I’m a little hard on corners. I would like more. I think he would tell you that. He’s tackled really well — although there was one play against Vegas where he let it get outside. Those are the ones I remember. “He’s coming along really good,” Spags continued. “I think him and Nohl together have been a pleasant surprise. I really didn’t know how that was going to go because you have a rookie and then you have a second-year guy. They’re playing aggressive like we want. “There’s been some things there that we need to iron out,” Spagnuolo pointed out. “We can’t get as many penalties. There’s some leverage things. There were a couple at the end of the game that I thought Mansoor should have taken away. We talked about it. We’re going to live with some rookie mistakes and some second-year veteran mistakes. All in all, I think those guys have been pretty solid for us.” Delane was limited in training camp due to a shoulder injury that he then aggravated in Week 1. Spagnuolo believes the rookie has the ailment out of his mind, as shown by his willingness to come up in run support. “I think, instinctively, he wants to,” Spagnuolo observed. “He was a physical guy at LSU. We harp on that here. We guilt those guys into being physical because when they’re not, we put it on tape. And I just think that’s him, he plays that way. Whatever the shoulder and everything, I think he’s kind of put it out of his mind, which is a good thing. You want to play like that.” Before leaving in Week 1, Delane made a spectacular interception on the play that injured his shoulder. Spagnuolo remarked on Delane’s natural ability, but the coach also had some advice for avoiding future injury. “That was a little more of an instinctive thing,” he recalled. “The down took a little while. I think he undercut it. He has a knack for that. He undercut one at practice yesterday that he was not supposed to. So we’ve got to make sure that he does it when the coverage says that you can do that. That was a good play that he made. I told him ‘Don’t fall the ground anymore so you don’t get hurt.’” THE @Chiefs GET THE WIN! pic.twitter.com/Kga49Yb0FG — NFL (@NFL) October 4, 2026 The Chiefs have actually had two interceptions by rookie defensive backs. Undrafted safety Xavier Nwankpa — who has taken only two defensive snaps over four games — snagged a pass on the Raiders’ final drive in Week 4 to seal the win. Spagnuolo explained how a depth player, largely on the roster for special teams, made the key play. “In that situation at the end of the game,” the coach said, “sometimes we put in a lot of DBs. He’s one of those I think seven — I forget which personnel we were in. That situation called for us putting those guys in. That’s what put him out there. If we get into that situation again, he’s part of that package. So you may see him again in there.” As the team moves forward, Spagnuolo knows depth in the secondary matters. He is happy to have veteran Chamarri Conner back from a knee injury to round out a safety rotation with Chris Roland-Wallace, Jaden Hicks, and Alohi Gilman. He is also high on how cornerback Kristian Fulton performed in Delane’s absence and is happy to have another boundary option when needed. “I’m glad we got back, is Chamarri,” Spagnuolo declared. “I’m sure you’ve watched the tape just like we have. Physically, I thought he played really good and had some really physical hits. Over on the sideline, he caused an incomplete pass, but I’d like to have him there more. And the guy that just seems to be a constant stabilizing guy is Chris Roland-Wallace. He’s a jack-of-all-trades for us. We can put him in at different spots.” With Conner, a fourth-year player in the system, back in the lineup, the Chiefs will tweak the safety rotation to keep Hicks and Gilman involved. “You can see now, so Chamarri’s back, but I think Jaden and A.G. still deserve to play. We rolled them through. I think Kristian Fulton has had some good downs. So, you see him rolling in there, and we’re going into the fifth game of the season for us. And I think the more you can do that in the first half of the season, I think the better off you’re going to be. Because somewhere along the way, we’re going to get nicked up and it’d be good for those guys to have some reps on their belt.”

Mahomes is 8-for-37 targeting Worthy on deep balls, the worst completion rate (21.6%) among 38 duos with 25+ targets since 2024. A quick-game passing attack isn’t fun for anyone and, more importantly, it leaves infinitely less margin for error. Just ask the 2024 and 2025 Chiefs. And part of it for me is Bo Nix is not playing competitively. It’s almost disrespectful to the quarterback position how he’s playing football right now.” Texans RB Montgomery, S Pitre out for London affair vs. Jaguars | ESPN The Texans will travel to London to face the Jacksonville Jaguars without at least a pair of starters. Olsen, who has won multiple Emmys (including the most recent one, from his spot on the Fox “B” team) seems destined to land with a No. 1 team, somewhere. Morgan Engel/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Chargers are facing off against the Kansas City Chiefss in Week 6 at Arrowhead Stadium hoping to secure their first win of the season. That came in Week 4 against the Seattle Seahawks, but against an offense like the Chiefs, which has the potential to break out on any given Sunday, this number could hit. That said, based on how the Chargers’ offense has performed and the Chiefs’ desire to make it more of a defensive game, I like the under in this one. Prediction: Under Chargers +7.5 FanDuel is giving the Chargers 7.5 points to start the game. The Chargers lost by more than a score in each of their first two weeks, but have kept things close in the last three. Their 23-17 loss against the Denver Broncos in Week 5 was the closest margin in a game this season. That being said, playing on the road against the Chiefs is an incredibly daunting task, especially for a team that is dealing with as many injuries as Los Angeles is. The line is fair, and I believe the Chargers will still have a tough time beating the spread. Prediction: Chiefs -7.5 Final Score The Chargers are massive underdogs here for good reason. They are one of the three winless teams in the league, going up against one of the three undefeated teams. They also have to do this on the road while Kansas City is coming off a bye week. title: Chargers-Chiefs Game Preview: 5 Questions with Arrowhead Pride
summary: This week we were joined by Maurice Elston of our Chiefs sister community, Arrowhead Pride, to help us preview this week’s matchup with Kansas City. With these two teams on two completely different trajectories this season, this game may not be appointment watching for most, but anyone who follows the AFC West knows it’s still […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - OCTOBER 04: Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs reacts prior to the game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Steve Marcus/Getty Images) | Getty Images This week we were joined by Maurice Elston of our Chiefs sister community, Arrowhead Pride, to help us preview this week’s matchup with Kansas City. With these two teams on two completely different trajectories this season, this game may not be appointment watching for most, but anyone who follows the AFC West knows it’s still likely to be a surprisingly competitive game between divisional rivals. Let’s go ahead and dive right in! 1.) The Chiefs are back. I don’t think anyone can say otherwise. Can you give us a TL/DR explanation on what happened last season and what the Chiefs did to quickly get back into the NFL’s elite? Last year, the Chiefs lacked discipline across the board. There were costly penalties, turnovers and dropped passes at unfortunate times, and those mistakes completely changed their fortunes in close games. Kansas City went 12-0 in one-score games in 2024, including the playoffs, before going 1-9 in those situations last season. That was probably the biggest difference between the two years. You pair that with Xavier Worthy’s shoulder injury, Rashee Rice’s six-game suspension and several injuries along the offensive line, and it became one of those seasons where everything seemed to go wrong. I also think all those extended playoff runs and trips to the Super Bowl finally caught up with them. The Chiefs turned it around quickly because they identified their problems and made the necessary changes. They reshuffled the coaching staff, bringing back Eric Bieniemy as offensive coordinator and hiring a demanding wide receivers coach in Chad O’Shea. Those moves restored some of the discipline, energy and accountability that were missing. They also understood that their style of play needed to change. Defenses had adjusted to Kansas City by taking away the big plays, generating pressure with four rushers and dropping seven into coverage. The addition of Kenneth Walker III and a renewed commitment to the running game have given the offense a different identity. With the dominant interior offensive linemen the Chiefs already had, that change has helped them return to the NFL’s elite quickly. 2.) Signing Kenneth Walker may end up being the most-impactful free agent signed this offseason. How was that signing first received by the Chiefs fan base and how much has he met or surpassed expectations? The signing was received extremely well by Chiefs fans. Walker was the running back many fans wanted, but I don’t think most people believed Brett Veach would spend the money necessary to get him. His three-year deal initially looked like a significant investment at a position where the Chiefs traditionally haven’t spent much money. However, after Jahmyr Gibbs and Bijan Robinson helped reset the running back market, Walker’s contract began looking like an excellent value. I think he has already surpassed expectations. You knew the Chiefs were getting a great player and a reigning Super Bowl MVP, but 537 rushing yards and 621 yards from scrimmage through four games is beyond what anyone reasonably could have expected. He has completely changed the identity of the offense, given the Chiefs a home-run threat in the backfield and made defenses respect the run on every play. 3.) If you were Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, how would you go about attacking this Chiefs defense? Which players/matchups would you attempt to exploit? If I’m Mike McDaniel, I’m attacking the Chiefs similarly to how the Raiders did. The best opportunity is in the middle of the field, where you can force Kansas City’s linebackers and safeties to defend in space. I would use running backs and tight ends on quick passes, option routes and crossing concepts designed to create favorable matchups against the linebackers. I would also test L’Jarius Sneed in the slot. Teams have had some success targeting him with quick passes this season, particularly when they can prevent Kansas City’s pass rush from getting home. If the Chargers can get the ball out quickly, attack Sneed in the slot and force the Chiefs’ linebackers and safeties into difficult coverage assignments, they should be able to move the football. 4.) If you were Chargers defensive coordinator Chris O’Leary, how are you attempting to put a lid on this Chiefs offense? How should teams prepare for Kansas City when they now have such a strong rushing attack to go with Patrick Mahomes? This is where it becomes much more difficult. Defenses can no longer sit back with light boxes, put extra defenders into coverage and dare the Chiefs to run. Kansas City has proven it will remain committed to the running game, and Kenneth Walker has shown he can handle a heavy workload while also breaking explosive plays. If I’m Chris O’Leary, I’m devoting extra resources to stopping Walker and challenging Kansas City’s wide receivers with man-to-man coverage. The Chiefs’ receivers haven’t consistently beaten man coverage this season, and the group is now depleted. Tyquan Thornton is sidelined with an ankle injury, while Rashee Rice is dealing with a hamstring injury and might not be 100% even if he plays. I would make the Chiefs’ available wide receivers prove they can consistently separate against man coverage. That comes with the obvious risk of leaving your defensive backs exposed against Patrick Mahomes, but allowing Walker to control the game would make Kansas City almost impossible to stop. 5.) Let’s go ahead and top this off with a final score prediction and few lines on how you see this game shaking out. Are the Chiefs going to win in a blowout? Will it be close? The Chargers should enter this game in desperation mode. They are 0-5 and badly need a victory, while the Chiefs are 4-0, coming off their bye week and probably feeling very confident. That creates the ingredients for a potential trap game. On paper, Kansas City is clearly the better team, especially considering the number of injuries the Chargers are dealing with. However, this is still an AFC West rivalry, and these games are normally competitive regardless of the teams’ records. I expect the Chargers to keep it close through the first three quarters before the Chiefs begin to separate late. Kansas City’s running game and fresh defensive front should eventually wear Los Angeles down. Chiefs 30, Chargers 20.

title: Rams Reacts: Fans blame Sean McVay for special teams problems
summary: The Los Angeles Rams have had problems on their specials teams for years, and fans are blaming Sean McVay as the reason. Nearly 57% of fans surveyed are putting the heat on McVay for the special teams woes. According to the data below McVay is taking more of the blame than Bubba Ventrone, and more […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams have had problems on their specials teams for years, and fans are blaming Sean McVay as the reason. Nearly 57% of fans surveyed are putting the heat on McVay for the special teams woes. According to the data below McVay is taking more of the blame than Bubba Ventrone, and more blame than Harrison Mevis. The Rams are one of if not the worst special teams units across the board. The unit most recently cost them on Monday Night Football against the Buffalo Bills with a poor opening kickoff leading to three points for Buffalo. Later, a missed Harrison Mevis kick and finally a blocked kick to basically end the game in Buffalo’s favor. McVay’s done plenty right , but if you ask the fans, they are burned-out on McVay getting the special teams so wrong. When it comes to betting at FanDuel , if the Rams are favored by 3 points or less, maybe bet on the other team. The Rams can’t guarantee three points to win a game, cover the spread or save their season. Are the Rams the best tw0-win team in the NFL? 65% of fans surveyed seem to think L.A. is the strongest 2-win team with the most potential. The data says expect the Rams to end the season with the best record out of all the other two-win teams across the league. Whereas, the Rams may be the best two-win team in the league, L.A. had much bigger dreams than being the strongest two-win franchise five weeks into their season. The Rams want to make the playoffs; they want to win the Super Bowl. The Rams still can do this, but they are falling well behind the San Francisco 49ers. Whereas you may want to check FanDuel and bet on the Rams winning more games than not, you also may want to avoid placing any bets on L.A. winning the whole thing, for now. Are you confident the Rams are headed in the right direction? The football season be like a pendulum with big swings back and forth. Last week ,after a win, fan confidence was above 70% , This week, after a loss, fan confidence sits at 33%. The Rams are favored to beat the Arizona Cardinals this week, but imagine if L.A. drops this game? Where will fan confidence be then? It’s been an uphill battle for the team that was expected to be the best in the NFL in 2026. The Rams haven’t looked like the best team in the NFL, their own conference, or their division. They look like a team that’s 2-3. They also look like a team that could be 4-1, or 3-2, but their 2-3. Might be no better time to bet the over on wins for L.A. at FanDuel. May have been the right time to bet the under from the start, or to bet the under again. Bet responsibly.

The All-Pro cornerback has quickly established himself as a cornerstone of Los Angeles’ secondary since arriving from Kansas City this offseason. If he cannot suit up, the Rams could need Josh Wallace and Emmanuel Forbes Jr. to take on larger roles alongside Jaylen Watson. With McDuffie sidelined, Los Angeles would lose its most reliable option in coverage at a time when containing opposing receivers remains critical. Pro Football Focus also ranks him third among 104 qualified cornerbacks with an 85.2 overall defensive grade and second with an 88.7 coverage grade. Those numbers illustrate just how difficult McDuffie has been to attack. Losing him against Arizona could force the Rams to rethink their defensive approach, making his status a must watch heading into Sunday’s game.

title: Will Sam Darnold be the starter when Rams face Seahawks?
summary: The Seattle Seahawks may be questioning if Super Bowl winner Sam Darnold is still the right man for the job, just six weeks into his second season with the team. When the Los Angeles Rams face the Seahawks twice in the final three weeks of the season, will they be facing Darnold, backup Drew Lock, […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks may be questioning if Super Bowl winner Sam Darnold is still the right man for the job, just six weeks into his second season with the team. When the Los Angeles Rams face the Seahawks twice in the final three weeks of the season, will they be facing Darnold, backup Drew Lock, or someone entirely different? Darnold threw two more interceptions during Thursday night’s loss to the Denver Broncos, giving him seven touchdowns and seven picks in four games this season; he missed the majority of Week 1, as well as Week 2 with a hip injury. Darnold’s rapid fire pace of interceptions has many Seahawks fans asking to see Lock — who had four touchdowns and no picks in his two games — when Seattle returns to face the Chiefs next Sunday night. Sam Darnold this season (4 games): 7 TDs 7 INTs pic.twitter.com/4a35GqhFpM — Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) October 16, 2026 However, Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald addressed the “controversy” on Friday after the loss, stating that the team had no intention of making a change at quarterback any time soon. Do we believe him? Coach Mike Macdonald with us #Seahawks beat writers doubles down on Sam Darnold being his starting quarterback going forward. Says he firmly believes Darnold is the solution. Says Anthony Bradford has a strong chance to return off IR to start vs Kansas City in 9 days. @933KJR — Gregg Bell (@gbellseattle) October 16, 2026 Darnold revived his career After a stint with Kyle Shanahan as a backup in 2023, Darnold went 14-3 with the Vikings in 2024, prior to losing to the Rams in the playoffs and getting sacked nine times in that game. Minnesota opted to let Darnold walk despite his career season and he signed a three-year, $100 million deal with Seattle. The move paid immediate dividends as Darnold won the Super Bowl in 2025 with the Seahawks. Darnold threw 14 interceptions and still had a turnover problem. However, Darnold didn’t throw any picks in the playoffs and he was exactly what the Seahawks needed for their Super Bowl winning campaign. It didn’t hurt that Seattle had a Super Bowl MVP running back in Kenneth Walker — who Seattle let walk in free agency — and arguably the best defense in the NFL, as well as the best special teams. Walker is gone, special teams has been shaky at best, and the Seahawks have fumbled the ball 11 times in six games, including nine by running backs and Rashid Shaheed. Seattle is 3-3 and staring at the same long road to the playoffs as the Rams. It’s early enough in the year that the Seahawks can turn this around, but will Darnold be a part of that turnaround? I believe that’s 9 sacks on Sam Darnold over the last two games. Just rough for Seattle offense right now. pic.twitter.com/ihLlO3GARV — Dugar, Michael-Shawn (@MikeDugar) October 16, 2026 Would the Seahawks benching Darnold actually allow for the turnaround they are looking for? That turnaround being less interceptions, less turnovers. Turnovers can be a part of Darnold’s game, he has 89 regular season interceptions in 105 games played. You could say the same about Matthew Stafford and plenty of great quarterbacks, interceptions can be a part of their process. You take the bad with the good. However, Darnold isn’t making up for his picks with production. He’s thrown for over 1,000 yards, but his seven touchdowns match his seven interceptions. Not ideal. While Darnold hasn’t been outplaying his mistakes in 2026, Drew Lock has four passing touchdowns with zero picks. Is Lock better than Darnold? Like anything, you can debate it, but probably not. Yet, Lock has been more efficient in 2026 than Darnold. The clearest change for Seattle to better their team after six weeks? Whether it’s Darnold or Lock, get better quarterback play. And if Darnold can’t clean up his act, then Mike Macdonald and Seattle may have no choice but to go another direction. Will that happen before Week 16? Darnold should be given every chance to get right. Macdonald should do what all the best coaches do, and that’s whatever is best for his team. At a certain point, Macdonald won’t be able to sit back and let Darnold figure it out. The Rams don’t face the Seahawks until December 25, then they play Seattle again two weeks later in the finale. If Darnold’s poor play keeps up, it’ll be fair to wonder who will be starting for the Seahawks by then, and what the future of Darnold and Seahawks looks like going forward. Until then, Darnold will have to play better, or he’ll face whatever the consequences are if he doesn’t. Including not playing the Rams on Christmas.

title: 3 things I think ahead of Rams-Cardinals
summary: Good teams keep losing teams losing. While the Los Angeles Rams are one of the NFL’s best teams on paper, their 2-3 start to the season is a major disappointment. There remains plenty of time to course correct and find footing in the NFC playoff picture; however, the jury is still out—are the Rams good? […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 12: Kyren Williams #23 of the Los Angeles Rams takes the field prior to the game against the Buffalo Bills at SoFi Stadium on October 12, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good teams keep losing teams losing. While the Los Angeles Rams are one of the NFL’s best teams on paper, their 2-3 start to the season is a major disappointment. There remains plenty of time to course correct and find footing in the NFC playoff picture; however, the jury is still out—are the Rams good? Sunday’s Week 6 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals isn’t certain to bring us more answers. How far does the needle swing if the Rams trounce the bottom-dwelling Cardinals? What can we really glean from this game in terms of LA’s place in the standings? The answer is not much, and the same goes for their earlier game this season against the New York Giants. Sunday is not a resume builder. It’s a requirement in order to keep pace with the San Francisco 49ers in the NFC West divisional race. So with that in mind, what could spell trouble for the Rams in Week 6? There a few items I can’t seem to shake out of my head. 1 – David Quessenberry at LT against Josh Sweat Alaric Jackson was initially suspended for two games following a post-game altercation against a Bills player. The league reduced his time missed to a single game . David Quessenberry will earn the start at left tackle in replacement. In wake of Alaric Jackson's suspension, Sean McVay says David Quessenberry will start at LT for Rams. Team will also open OL Keagen Trost's 21-day practice window this week, per McVay — Stu Jackson (@StuJRams) October 14, 2026 Quessenberry last started in 2023 for the Vikings. While he’s been a reliable spot contributor over his career, we have not seen him play much meaningful football during his LA tenure. At age 36, Quessenberry may not still be the same player he once was. We have no way of knowing whether that is the case. Sunday will be our first answer on this front. The fortunate news is that the Cardinals have very little pass rushing talent outside of Josh Sweat. The bad news is that Sweat will likely align across from Quessenberry most of the time. It’s best on complete unknown—if not best versus worst. No player on the Cardinals has more than nine pressures this season. Interior defensive lineman Dante Stills leads Arizona. Josh Sweat is second with eight. For comparison, Rams EDGE rusher Byron Young has two games with seven pressures. The Cardinals get most of their pass rushing production from the interior, including Walter Nolen and Darius Robinson. Sweat is the only individual you must worry about on the edge. 2 – The Arizona defense is a mess The Cardinals have lacked premier defensive talent for years. Former head coach Jonathan Gannon made up for this with creative defensive play calling. Gannon’s defensive coordinator, Nick Rallis, is still in place. It’s too early to say whether the same extent of creativity remains; however, we have enough information to conclude that his defense is one of the worst in football. Arizona ranks 30th in EPA per play. They are 25th in success rate and 29th in allowing explosive plays. The Cardinals are 25th in missed tackle frequency and allow the most points in the NFL on a per drive basis. You can look for a silver lining. There isn’t one. This was the Cardinals' 40th loss under Monti Ossenfort. Four years into his rebuild, Ossenfort now has: A 16-40 record No quarterback A squandered #4 pick A bad offensive line Few, if any, clear foundational pieces on defense — Theo Mackie (@theo_mackie) October 11, 2026 And that is good news for a Rams offense that is putting up a ton of yards but not necessarily efficient. Matthew Stafford is performing closer to average rather than at the MVP level we saw from him a year ago. Last week against the Bills should have been a “get right” game. It wasn’t. This is the weakest defense the Rams have faced yet. If they can’t light up the scoreboard against Arizona, it may be time to sound the alarm. 3 – Is Blake Grupe really an upgrade? The Rams just signed Blake Grupe off the Jets practice squad. He's been a bit below average on short field goals, about average from 50+, and reliable on extra points (98%). Last year he went 11/11 with the Colts, including a 60-yard field goal. pic.twitter.com/VOZtMJor4f — Josh (@JoshiosTweets) October 13, 2026 The Rams released kicker Harrison Mevis this week and signed Blake Grupe in replacement . Grupe certainly is more capable from longer range. Whether he’s consistently accurate is an open question . Because LA signed Grupe from the New York Jets’ practice squad, he must remain on the 53-man roster for at least three games. The Rams aren’t likely to lose to the Cardinals because of a missed field goal—hopefully it doesn’t come down to that. But LA does need to leave Sunday with earned confidence that Grupe is their kicker for the rest of the season. The Rams have invited volatility. Have they stopped the bleeding?

Aaron Donald records 3 sacks I think the Rams legend finally gets on the board in Week 6. title: Andrew Whitworth irritated with Harrison Mevis after Rams’ loss
summary: Andrew Whitworth explained on Fitz and Whit that he was a bit salty with Harrison Mevis after the Los Angeles Rams lost to the Buffalo Bills, and it wasn’t only because Mevis missed crucial kicks. It was because Mevis was laughing with Bills players after the loss. Whitworth said that laughing after a loss doesn’t […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - OCTOBER 04: Los Angeles Rams place kicker Harrison Mevis #92 watches his kick during the game between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Los Angeles Rams on October 4th, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Andrew Whitworth explained on Fitz and Whit that he was a bit salty with Harrison Mevis after the Los Angeles Rams lost to the Buffalo Bills, and it wasn’t only because Mevis missed crucial kicks. It was because Mevis was laughing with Bills players after the loss. Whitworth said that laughing after a loss doesn’t line up with how the Rams feel as a team, and it doesn’t line up with head coach Sean McVay. Odds are that Mevis would’ve been released after that game regardless of how Mevis acted, but Whitworth alludes it may have been a nail in the coffin for Mevis’s time with the Rams. Whitworth could be speaking for himself; he could be speaking for some players and coaches on the team. It’s an interesting take by “Big Whit”. The end of a football game is an emotional time typically for both teams as one is elated from their victory, the other gutted from a loss, or it’s a tie in which case no one knows how to feel. Players handle those emotions and outcomes differently. When players laugh after a loss, I see both sides. On the one hand you lost, what’s funny? On the other hand, these guys are playing in some cases their brothers, best friends, family, college teammates, high school teammates and longtime rivals and more. I can understand how a player can be gutted from a loss, but still excited to see someone they care about. I don’t disagree with what Whit is saying because it’s his opinion. What I will say is whether Mevis was laughing or not after the loss if he was the best kicker in the league, he’d still be on the team. Mevis wasn’t the best kicker in the league, and his laughing after a loss didn’t help his case with the Rams. It will be interesting to see if Mevis gets another shot elsewhere. It’ll be interesting to see if the Rams can find a kicker. Whit has some thoughts on Mevis and the end of Monday Night Football: “The biggest thing that irritates me… If you are in the mood to laugh with some Bills players after the game… when you see that after the game, it’s like hey man maybe it’s not a fit” pic.twitter.com/lEUM8ELui6 — Fitz & Whit (@fitzandwhit) October 15, 2026 Andrew Whitworth calls out Harrison Mevis for laughing after Rams’ loss (ramswire) “The identity and the mentality of football teams that are really good usually match up. Like, when you go look at the teams that lose a lot, I can show you a lot of guys that don’t always show they care the most. But like, if you are in the mood to go laugh and keekee with some Bills players after the game, you don’t match up to the head coach’s mentality because I know that dude. Like, the whole world stops when he doesn’t perform. When Matthew Stafford, at this point in his career, what he’s trying to accomplish, what Davante Adams wants, what Aaron Donald came back for, right? Like, there is no answer other than winning. You see, Mevis gets released. It’s exactly what I’m saying. There’s an identity and mentality to our football team.” LA Rams EDGE Myles Garrett will not return in Week 6 vs. Arizona Cardinals (cardswire) “The Arizona Cardinals will face the Los Angeles Rams , but they do get a little bit of a break. Pass rusher Myles Garrett will not return this week. Garrett, on injured reserve with a knee injury, was eligible to have his practice window opened this week. That didn’t happen. Head coach Sean McVay told reporters Tuesday that Garrett would not practice this week. He could potentially in Week 7, but the Cardinals will miss him. However, while Garrett won’t play, the Cardinals will still have to face pass rusher Byron Young, who leads the Rams with 3.5 sacks through five games.“ McVay faces former offensive coordinator LaFleur for first time when Rams host Cardinals (pinalcentral) “The Rams (2-3) are trying to get on track after an erratic start to the season, while the Cardinals (1-4) are seeking to recapture the success of their surprising season-opening visit to SoFi Stadium, when they knocked off the building’s other tenant, the Chargers. In short, there is a lot more for both sides to worry about rather than friendships and returning to one’s former place of employment. “As much as I love Sean, I haven’t really thought of him too much,” LaFleur said. “I’m sure he’s kind of feeling the same way about me right now.” Rams Midweek Report: Favorable Schedule Ahead, Myles Garrett Update, Sean McVay Concerns (si.com) “Given the issues on special teams, it’s hard to put a lot of faith in this team. They continuously invent new ways to lose. For the first time this season, the Rams are no longer Super Bowl favorites as that belongs to the San Francisco 49ers. At the same time, if the Rams can figure it out, there is the potential for them to go on a serious run. Here is their schedule before the bye week in Week 11: Week 6 vs. Arizona Cardinals 1-4 Week 7 @ Las Vegas Raiders 3-2 Week 8 vs. Los Angeles Chargers 0-5 Week 9 @ Washington Commanders 1-3-1 Week 10 @ Arizona Cardinals 1-4 The combined record for those teams is 6-18-1. That’s the lowest strength of schedule over the next five games in the NFL.It’s important not to look too far ahead in the NFL, but those are five very winnable games. The Rams could easily go into their bye week with a 7-3 record. At that point, the Rams may only be one or two games back in the NFC West behind the 49ers.“ Arizona Cardinals vs Los Angeles Rams Betting Preview: Week 6 Odds, Tips and Prediction (compare.bet) “Twelve and a half points is the biggest handicap on the Week 6 board, and it is being laid by a team with a losing record. The Rams are 2-3. Their point difference is minus one . The case for the number is that the matchup is brutal. Los Angeles lead the NFL in passing at 310.4 yards a game and are second in passing yards allowed at 163.4. They throw it better than anyone and stop it better than almost anyone. Arizona concede 32.4 points a game, the most in the league .“ Sean McVay, Matthew Stafford, Davante Adams, Aaron Donald & Puka Nacua preview Week 6 vs. the Cardinals (therams.com) “Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay, quarterback Matthew Stafford, wide receivers Davante Adams & Puka Nacua, and defensive end Aaron Donald speak with the media on Thursday. Watch them reflect on lessons from Monday’s matchup vs. the Buffalo Bills, preview Week 6 against the Arizona Cardinals, and more.” Matthew Stafford reveals the Rams’ biggest problem — and it’s not the kicker (nypost) “The problem isn’t necessarily how the Rams finish games or what the offense does when its backs are against the wall and it needs a score. They’ve been excellent when urgency is required, especially in two-minute situations. It’s more about the opportunities they miss before they reach the finish line. “There’s chances all over the place in games to snatch the momentum, or go pile on a lead, or claw back a little closer, so it’s not just about one possession at the end of the game, or whatever that is,” Stafford said. Over their last three games, the Rams have mastered the art of playing with their backs against the wall. Now they need to figure out how to play with that same sense of desperation before their opponent puts it there.“ Best Los Angeles Rams fantasy performances so far this season (keyt.com) “Every season in the NFL produces performances that feel less like a single game and more like statistical outliers — explosive outings where quarterbacks pile up passing yards, running backs break off long scoring runs, and receivers turn routine targets into multi-touchdown afternoons. These are the kinds of games that separate good fantasy weeks from historic ones. Stacker compiled a ranking of the best Los Angeles Rams fantasy…

title: Las Vegas Raiders-Buffalo Bills FEED topic: How will offensive line respond?
summary: Heading into their Week 6 matchup against the Buffalo Bills, the 2026 version of the Las Vegas Raiders’ offensive line hasn’t looked very different than last season. The Raiders are averaging just 3.0 yards per carry as a team and, according to Pro Football Focus, 240 of Ashton Jeanty’s 291 rushing yards (82.5%) have come […]
full_text: (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Heading into their Week 6 matchup against the Buffalo Bills , the 2026 version of the Las Vegas Raiders’ offensive line hasn’t looked very different than last season. The Raiders are averaging just 3.0 yards per carry as a team and, according to Pro Football Focus , 240 of Ashton Jeanty’s 291 rushing yards (82.5%) have come after contact. Additionally, quarterback Kirk Cousins has been under pressure on 41.0% of his dropbacks in Las Vegas’ last two games, per PFF . As a result, head coach Klint Kubiak suggested some changes to the Raiders’ trenches could be coming during his press conference on Monday after the team’s 45-17 loss to the New England Patriots. “We have to look at everything,” Kubiak replied when asked about a potential shuffle to the offensive line, via Silver & Black Sports Network’s Jesse Merrick . “We have to improve there. It’s something I’ve been saying for multiple weeks now that’s not getting done, and so, as a coaching staff, it falls on me. It falls on me to get it fixed.” The Athletic’s Sam Warren added that Kubiak confirmed other linemen will get more opportunities moving forward. In other words, the coach is publicly calling the position group out, and it’s up to them to respond. No one should feel like their spot is safe at this stage, leading to questions about what changes could be in store for Sunday’s game against the Bills. Left guard Spencer Burford seems like the most logical choice to get replaced. Burford has really struggled in pass protection, giving up the most pressures (18) of any guard this season, per PFF . Additionally, his 56.6 run-blocking grade doesn’t inspire much confidence and is tied for 56th out of 81 qualifiers (minimum 85 snaps). Then again, the other guard, Jackson Powers-Johnson, has a case to get replaced, too. Powers-Johnson has been stingier in pass protection with just nine pressures surrendered in four games. However, he’s been a problem in the running game with the fifth-worst run-blocking grade (43.8) at his position. The third-year pro has struggled with consistency throughout his career and had to fend off second-year pro Caleb Rogers during training camp to remain in the starting lineup. That sets up another potential swap. On top of that, Kolton Miller and Tyler Linderbaum were viewed as steadying presences on Las Vegas’ offensive line heading into the campaign. However, both have left something to be desired. Miller has been charged with 12 pressures over the last two weeks, and Linderbaum’s 63.1 PFF grade for the season ranks 19th among centers. The latter isn’t “bad” per se, but it isn’t what the organization bargained for when it made him the highest-paid interior offensive lineman in NFL history, and by a wide margin at that. Granted, it’s highly unlikely that those two are in danger of losing their respective spots at this stage. But there is certainly room for improvement. Long story short, the only Raiders offensive lineman who has met or exceeded expectations so far this season is right tackle DJ Glaze. The 2024 third-round pick has been solid in the run game with a 62.8 mark and has made tremendous strides in pass protection, yielding just seven pressures. That gives the Silver and Black a silver lining in the trenches, but the rest of the group has some work to do and, as noted above, changes could be coming. Rogers had a rough showing in his one start this year, filling in for an injured Powers-Johnson against the Kansas City Chiefs. But that’s a small sample size, and it isn’t like the current first-string guards are getting the job done. The Texas Tech product has exclusively played right guard under Kubiak, but he did get run on the left side during the preseason a year ago. Also, JPJ and Burford have experience playing on both sides of the line to expand the combinations that the Raiders can deploy in the trenches. Meanwhile, rookie Trey Zuhn III was cross-trained at just about every offensive line position during training camp but has only been used as an extra lineman/jumbo tight end for 12 snaps during the regular season. He could factor into the mix at guard too, and maybe even left tackle if need be, since that was his primary college position. Granted, Zuhn missed last week’s game with a knee injury and was limited in this Wednesday’s practice. Also waiting in the balance is second-year offensive tackle Charles Grant, whose only significant regular-season action came in last year’s Week 18 contest against the Chiefs. So, for this week’s game day discussion on The FEED , we’ll be keeping tabs on the Raiders’ offensive line, starting with who is on the field. The game kicks off at 1:25 p.m. PST and will air on CBS (check your local listings). I look forward to talkin’ some ball with y’all!
author: Matt Holder

title: Raiders Week 6: Bills a supreme challenge for leaky red zone defense
summary: The sixth-best red zone offense versus the fourth-worst red zone defense. That’s the high-level tale of the tape when Joe Brady’s Buffalo Bills (4-1 overall) offense clashes with Rob Leonard’s Las Vegas Raiders (3-2) defense this Sunday inside Allegiant Stadium. Brady, a 37-year-old wunderkind of an offensive-minded head coach, is the architect of Buffalo’s top-ranked […]
full_text: Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) | Getty Images The sixth-best red zone offense versus the fourth-worst red zone defense. That’s the high-level tale of the tape when Joe Brady’s Buffalo Bills (4-1 overall) offense clashes with Rob Leonard’s Las Vegas Raiders (3-2) defense this Sunday inside Allegiant Stadium. Brady, a 37-year-old wunderkind of an offensive-minded head coach, is the architect of Buffalo’s top-ranked scoring offense (164 total points) — the team also has the fourth-highest yardage output at 1,981 yards — and the red zone has been quite bountiful for the Bills. On 21 trips to the money zone between the opponent’s 20-yard line and goal line, Buffalo made 15 end zone visits giving them a 71.4 red zone percentage which is sixth-best in the NFL. The biggest benefactor of that domineering performance in a contested area of the football field is quarterback Josh Allen who is equal parts passer and scrambler as he leads the NFL with eight rushing touchdowns (239 yards rushing on 43 carries). The signal caller is bolstered by talented running back James Cook (95 carries, 523 yards, five touchdowns rushing). Talent certainly is a big boost but not bad for a rookie head coach. Quelling or stopping that is on the shoulders of Leonard and his defenders. “He’s a really good player and somebody you got to account for. But it’s not something you don’t have to deal with in other weeks of the season, but yes, definitely have to be aware of him as a rusher,” Leonard said of Allen. “He’s really good at extended plays, whether he scrambles to run, or scrambles to throw.” “It is,” Leonard added when asked how crucial it is for Las Vegas to improve the run defense against Allen and Cook. “Again, it’s not about the Bills. We just got to stack good plays. Right now, we’ve had good play, bad play, good play, bad play. Just got to keep improving.” Josh Allen has scored a touchdown in each of Buffalo's first 4 games this season 🦬 No quarterback in NFL history has ever scored a rushing touchdown in each of his team's first 5 games of a season 👀 h/t @BuffaloBillsPR pic.twitter.com/2xCiU6Bqy6 — The Commish (@CommishFilmRoom) October 13, 2026 Leonard, the 41-year-old defensive coordinator that orchestrates the Raiders defense, is in charge of the 22nd-ranked unit in points allowed (129) and 27th in yards yielded (1,885). The rookie defensive boss is at the helm of one of the worst red zone defenses in the NFL, however. Opponents have visited that area 18 times and on 14 of those occasions, scored a touchdown giving Las Vegas an unflattering 77.8 red zone percentage which ranks 29th out of the 32 teams. On paper, being pitted against a Joe Brady’s Buffalo offense score 15 red zone touchdowns on 21 trips is a mismatch. Games, however, aren’t played on paper. Leonard must have his defense disciplined and executing throughout Sunday’s clash against the Bills and that means communications and fundamentals — both severely lacking in the Week 5 drubbing at New England — must be present. The defensive line, linebackers, and secondary must not over-persue, maintain gap discipline, and be physical in the red zone — and anywhere on the field Buffalo’s offense has possession of the ball. Elite edge rusher Maxx Crosby must be his disruptive self and fellow defensive linemen Malcolm Koonce and Kwity Paye (who has been a non-factor since a Week 1 debut for the Raiders) must provide complementary defenders off the edge. Linebackers Nakobe Dean and Quay Walker need to be ready and willing to attack or drop in coverage and the defensive backs need to be all on the same page. Of course, it’d be grand if the Raiders defense can take the ball away from the Bills — Las Vegas is ranked second with 10 takeaways on the season but the total dwindled drastically over the course of the first five games. “It’s always the same. That’s why it’s called takeaways; you have to take it away. It’s not going to happen by accident,” Leonard said while adding “no”, the amount of takeaways Las Vegas racked up didn’t mask his defense’s defeciencies when asked. “I’d really like to move on. It wasn’t our best performance from that game. We just didn’t do well. We got to improve,” Leonard responded when asked if he was surprised Las Vegas couldn’t get to Patriots quarterback Drake Maye last week. The Bills now have the 3rd worst defense in the league and they give up .141 EPA per play ABOVE LEAGUE AVERAGE. That's an additional 8.46 expected points over 60 plays. Since 1999, not a single team sporting a defense with numbers this bad went 4-1 in their first 5 games. pic.twitter.com/QeOVP4JKAc — Adam (@adampensel) October 13, 2026 But here’s another intriguing aspect of the Raiders-Bills matchup: Buffalo’s red zone defense is lacking, too. Defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard (pronounced Leonard like the Raiders’ defensive boss) captains the 27th-ranked red zone defense. And the Bills defense overall is statistically worse than the Raiders ranking 28th in points allowed (141) and 30th in yards yielded (1,943). Buffalo gives up the second most passing yards (1,402) and fourth-highest passing touchdowns (13) and has just two interceptions (25th in the league). If there’s ample time for Klint Kubiak’s Raiders offense to click once more, it’s against Buffalo. Las Vegas has the eighth-most passing yards (1,268) and second most passing touchdowns (12) to just four interceptions thrown (fourth best). But getting the ground game going (ranked 28th in yards gained at 410; dead last in yards per carry average at 3.0) is vital, too. Buffalo is likely going to replicate what other defenses have done: Load the box with eight defenders to stymie the run game and dare Kubiak and quarterback Kirk Cousins to beat them over the top — which Las Vegas hasn’t done well, at all. “Yeah, we have our calls and we have the different ways that we want to attack different defenses. Every defense gives a unique approach, and we have to have a solution for the different things that they present to us,” Raiders offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko said. “So, whether it’s loading the box, light box, different stuff, we really try to give the players the best answer. But it really comes down to us putting the players in their best situations and the guys executing their techniques and playing fast.” Head-to-Head Sunday’s clash marks the 44th time the Raiders and Bill will meet. Buffalo leads the all-time series 22-21 (2-0 in playoff action) and currently holds a three-game win streak over the Silver & Black, dating back to 2017 (Buffalo dropped Oakland 34-14 at home that game). The most recent outing between the two teams was in September of 2023, which the Bills won 38-10. The Raiders’ posted back-to-back wins in 2014 and 2016 (26-24 and 38-24, respectively). The Silver & Black own the longest win streak of the series at six from 1967 to 1972. Quote of Note “I think that you do what you got to do to win the game, man. Your weaknesses come out, and what the numbers say that they are, and we’re just trying to go win the game. So, we’re trying to improve all of our weaknesses. That’s offensive, defense, special teams, and the other side of the ball, they’re going to come after what you’re good at. They’re going harp on, ‘Hey, this team, they’ve taken the ball away,’ so they’re going protect it better. So, we’ve got to continue to take the ball away and just continue to improve as a team.” —Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak when asked if the team’s ability to create turnovers through first three weeks of season hid some of the defense’s weaknesses
author: Ray Aspuria

title: What’s the defense needs to beat the Buffalo Bills
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders face a stiff challenge on Sunday as the Buffalo Bills come into Allegiant Stadium for a Week 6 matchup. After being completely dominated by the New England Patriots, few expect them to rise to the challenge and overcome. However, it is not impossible but getting back to what was successful is […]
full_text: (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) The Las Vegas Raiders face a stiff challenge on Sunday as the Buffalo Bills come into Allegiant Stadium for a Week 6 matchup. After being completely dominated by the New England Patriots, few expect them to rise to the challenge and overcome. However, it is not impossible but getting back to what was successful is imperative. Run defense that works When the defense and especially the defensive line, is playing their best football, it is with a nose tackle and two 5-techs. Lately, the defensive line trio of Folorunso Fatukasi, Adam Butler, and Tonka Hemingway has been coming alive. None of the aforementioned players are 3-techs, which means that whenever the alignment is in a 4-man front, problems ensue. Furthrmore, Hemingway being in concussion protocol and not practicing doesn’t bode well for the front either. Fatukasi is the unsung hero of the defense; he has been since he first took the field in the preseason. When aligned as the nose, his push on the center completely disrupts nearly every run or pass play. Against the reigning rushing champion James Cook and Josh Allen, surrendering yards due to alignment is a luxury the Raiders defense can’t afford. Allowing linebackers Nakobe Dean and Quay Walker to position themselves where they feel most comfortable. They can plug holes faster, blitz more successfully and flow sideline to sideline more freely. Against the Bills, they need to cover the flats as well as the areas in between the hashes and numbers. Dalton Kincaid and Dawson Knox will be problems for the Raiders. Watch and learn from film Defensive coordinator Rob Leonard had a great opening three-game set to the season. However, the play-callers have increasing levels of experience with each opponent; he has put tendencies on film and gotten exposed. What’s worse is that Leonard has become so down-and-distance predictable that offensive coordinators are able to anticipate his blitzes and take advantage of them. Cover-zero (man coverage with no safety help), typically used when blitzing, is getting his corners eaten alive. Rub routes from twins and bunch formations are generating early wins for opposing wide receivers in short-yardage situations. High-low criss-crossing route combinations are hitting for explosive plays and in-breaking routes from the tight ends are keeping the chains moving in the intermediate. Eric Stokes got paid in the offseason and is struggling. Whether wide receivers are running away from him towards the middle of the field, or cooking his 8-yard cushions he hasn’t been the same. Darian Porter was an opening day starter until he got hurt. When Hezekiah Masses’ struggles got too pronounced, Porter got on the field and proved why he deserves his job back. Taron Johnson gets beat early on short routes and is usually outmanned by the player he’s covering. Masses has been susceptible to the double move and have been getting beat in man coverage. Treydan Stukes is fighting for his life against tight ends and is placed in some damned if you do, damned if you don’t positions. Whether he takes the crosser in front of him or the one behind him, he keeps getting stung. The truth is, Leonard is scheming around a very young secondary. While they have proven to be playmakers when opportunity knocks, inexperience is beginning to poke through. Show them something new Leonard is creative and has excellent play designs. What is needed is to get back to the drawing board and put together something no one has seen yet. Zone blitzes and simulated pressures, mixed with some variations to his double-mug looks can help get the pass rush home. Maybe even activating the blitz from the third level. Whatever he does, it must devise a way to attack while saving a defender to spy on Allen. Primarily, to keep him from running all over the place and being the playmaker that Allen is. Leonard must also continue to develop his young defensive backfield. Coach his guys up and realize they all have to learn on the fly and don’t lose hope or patience with them. Focusing on details and practicing the time-honored tradition of tackling are things that can help the Raiders hold the Bills offense down. Offering them their best chance to do the unthinkable and pull out the win on Sunday.
author: Philip Robinson

summary: There are no surprises on the Las Vegas Raiders’ injury front as they head into Sunday’s home game against the Buffalo Bills. All of the injury details relayed by head coach Klint Kubiak Friday was expected. Starting defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway will not play. He missed all week of practice with a concussion he suffered […]
full_text: (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images There are no surprises on the Las Vegas Raiders’ injury front as they head into Sunday’s home game against the Buffalo Bills. All of the injury details relayed by head coach Klint Kubiak Friday was expected. Starting defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway will not play. He missed all week of practice with a concussion he suffered last week at New England. Hemingway could have a chance to return next week. Hemingway has been the Raiders’ snap leader in the defensive tackle rotation. Expect Adam Butler, who is a team captain this week, and Jonah Laulu to get more playing time with Hemingway out against the Bills’ potent offense. Meanwhile, starting wide receiver Jalen Nailor will play after missing last week’s game with a concussion. Backup rookie offensive lineman Trey Zuhn is questionable with a knee injury that kept him out last week. Kubiak said neither wide receiver Dont’e Thornton nor tight end Carter Runyon will be activated from the injured reserve this week. Meanwhile, for Buffalo, wide receiver DJ Moore and defensive lineman Ed Oliver are listed as questionable to play.

title: Raiders wide receivers Week 5 snap and production review
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders fell to 3-2 in a 45-17 loss at the New England Patriots on Sunday. Let’s review how their wide receivers fared: Tre Tucker Tucker played 75 percent of the snaps, which led the team Sunday and was a season high for him. He had four catches for 41 yards on five […]
full_text: (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders fell to 3-2 in a 45-17 loss at the New England Patriots on Sunday. Let’s review how their wide receivers fared: Tre Tucker Tucker played 75 percent of the snaps, which led the team Sunday and was a season high for him. He had four catches for 41 yards on five targets. Tucker has had 49 receiving yards or less in 15 of his past 16 games.. Cody White: White played 37 snaps after playing a career-high 52 snaps in Week 4. White had two catches two catches for 44 yards on four targets. Malik Benson The rookie sixth-round pick played a career-high 16 snaps. He had one catch for six yards. He has two catches on eight targets for 12 yards this season. Deven Thompkins: Elevated from the practice squad for the game, Thompkins played 13 offensive snaps. He had one catch for eight yards on one target. Dareke Young: He played 11 offensive snaps after playing 12 in the previous three games. He didn’t have any catches. Conclusion: The Raiders threw 22 passes to tight ends and running backs in Week 5. The number was 34 the week prior. At New England, the Raiders’ receivers caught a combined eight catches 99 yards on 14 targets. The team could have Jalen Nailor and Dont’e Thornton back this week to try to spark some more production. And yes, star tight end Brock Bowers does line up as a receiver often.

title: Raiders-Bills Week 6: 5 things to watch
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders will try to bounce back from two straight losses as they host the Buffalo Bills on Sunday. Kickoff is at 1:25 p.m. PT. Here are five keys to victory for the Raiders: Play better defense: The Raiders defense has been in the dumps after a strong start to the season. They […]
full_text: (Photo by Edward Monigan IV/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders will try to bounce back from two straight losses as they host the Buffalo Bills on Sunday. Kickoff is at 1:25 p.m. PT. Here are five keys to victory for the Raiders: Play better defense: The Raiders defense has been in the dumps after a strong start to the season. They have allowed 102 points in the past three games. New England has 536 yards of offense in Week 5 and they had 387 yards on explosive plays through three quarters. That can’t happen against this offense. Turnovers: The Raiders had nine takeaways in their three wins to start the season. They had one in the past two games both losses. If you’re going to beat this offense, creating turnovers is a great way to do it. The Raiders need to revert to their early-season takeaway magic. Cut down penalties: The Raiders’ had just 120 penalty yards un the first four games. They had 101 in Week 5. They need to clean that act up quickly. Better offensive line play: The Raiders’ offensive line has stalled in recent weeks. Kirk Cousins has been getting pressured often and the run game has been lacking badly. This unit needs to pick it up. Start fast: There will probably be a lot of blue in the Allegiant Stadium stands. This will be the Bills’ first game in Las Vegas with fans in the stands. Bills Mafia travels well. This could be another fan takeover. So, the Raiders need to start fast and get their fans in it ASAP.

summary: The Minnesota Vikings are 5-0, but can Kevin O’Connell’s ball-control offense sustain a Super Bowl run with Kyler Murray? full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 4: Kevin O'Connell head coach of the Minnesota Vikings speaks with Kyler Murray #1 before the game against the Miami Dolphins at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings are 5-0 , but can Kevin O’Connell’s ball-control offense sustain a Super Bowl run with Kyler Murray? Tyler Forness and Dave Stefano break down why the offense is trending up despite an incomplete picture on The Real Forno Show . Through five weeks, the Vikings have had just 18 snaps where Kyler Murray, Justin Jefferson, and Jordan Addison were all healthy. Tyler acknowledges the challenge: “We still don’t have a clear picture of what that will look like.” But he pushes back on national media doubting the defense: “We are already seeing people in the national media move the goalpost and said, ‘Well, what if Brian Flores’ defense isn’t good for one game? And can Kyler Murray shoulder the load?’ I think that conceptual idea is kind of bullshit.” The episode centers on O’Connell’s evolving relationship with Murray. Tyler offers a memorable analogy: “This is essentially a boyfriend and girlfriend trying to build a foundation for future success.” He adds, “You’re getting engaged. You’re getting married. You’re buying a house. You’re having kids. We need to start seeing some of that coming out of the bye.” Tyler dismantles the idea that O’Connell won’t adapt: “This narrative that O’Connell doesn’t cater to his quarterbacks is a load of crap.” He traces evidence from Kirk Cousins to Sam Darnold, J.J. McCarthy, Carson Wentz, Max Brosmer, Josh Dobbs, and now Murray. Key Points: Vikings defense is historically good; offense is built to complement it — “the less you can keep your defense on the field, the better they’re going to be long term” Minnesota ranks 2nd in time of possession, averaging 32.9 seconds per play, giving the defense just 42 snaps per game vs. the total of 1,025 last season Run game is 28th in EPA per rush, but O’Connell’s commitment is a growth point: “He’s decided, ‘I’m not going to give up on the run game'” Jordan Mason’s return should boost zone concepts; Aaron Jones excels in gap schemes (duo, counter, pin pull) Short passes function as run game — Tyler credits chat member John Moscrip: “short passes are run game” Brandon Staley’s Saints defense is “not exactly a good coach” “We haven’t seen them unlocked” — Tyler’s most exciting takeaway Kevin O’Connell’s tendency to chase shots remains a concern: “That’s always been in his DNA” Stefano adds: “If the offense ticks up and we get positive EPAs like we did last weekend, that will go into the number one special teams and the number one defense. full_text: The New England Patriots offense will have one of its best players back against the New York Jets. Wide receiver A.J. Brown, who spent the last four weeks on injured reserve, will be activated to the 53-man roster on Saturday. The expectation is that he will line up against the Jets on Sunday, according to a report by Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. Brown, 29, was moved to IR following the Patriots’ season opener against the Seattle Seahawks. After catching three passes for 26 yards in his debut with the team, he suffered an ankle injury in the third quarter. The issue was later diagnosed as a high ankle sprain, prompting New England to move him to injured reserve. After the requisite four weeks on IR, Brown returned to practice on Wednesday to open his 21-day activation window. Despite being a limited participant throughout the week, he has progressed enough to rejoin the active team this week. “I think he looks okay, like everybody,” head coach Mike Vrabel said about Brown on Friday. “Some good plays, some bad plays. We’re trying to see where his conditioning level is and see how he may feel here after practice today.” Apparently, he is feeling good. Brown now rejoins a receiving corps also featuring Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism. The Patriots will host the Jets at Gillette Stadium on Sunday, 1 p.m. ET.

title: Patriots vs. Jets series history ahead of Week 6 game
summary: The New England Patriots and New York Jets will meet on Sunday afternoon to add another chapter to a story going back more than six decades. Their game in Week 6 of the regular season will be the 134th overall in the series. Let’s take a look back at some of the most important moments […]
full_text: The New England Patriots and New York Jets will meet on Sunday afternoon to add another chapter to a story going back more than six decades. Their game in Week 6 of the regular season will be the 134th overall in the series. Let’s take a look back at some of the most important moments of the rivalry. Patriots vs. Jets series history Overall history: Especially in the late 60s and early 70s, the Jets got the better of the rivalry, at one point giong 14-of-15. However, the tide started to turn decisively in the 2000s and with Tom Brady and Bill Belichick leading the Patriots. As a result of their dominance — which included a 15-game win streak and a 13-year span in which the Jets never beat New England in 60 minutes — the Patriots now hold a 77-56-1 lead overall in the series. This includes a 2-1 edge in the playoffs, with them winning in 1985 (26-14) and 2006 (37-16), and the Jets celebrating a victory in 2011 (28-21). First game: Week 2 of the AFL’s inaugural 1960 season saw the Patriots visit the then-Titans at the Polo Grounds in New York. The game would end up as the first victory in Patriots franchise history, and it was a controversial one. The Titans took a 24-21 lead into the final seconds of the game, when they were unable to exercise a standard punt play resulting in a fumble. After players from both teams appeared to kick the ball forward, Boston defensive back Chuck Shonta recovered it and returned it 25 yards for the touchdown and a 28-24 Patriots victory. After the game, the Titans filed a complaint with the league, but the score was upheld and they later also lost the rematch in Boston. Most memorable game: There are two ways of looking at this. One could go with what is arguably the most entertaining game of the series, that even has its own Wikipedia entry and has become the butt — no pun intended — of jokes for more than a decade now. However, instead of picking the 2012 “Buttfumble” game, we are choosing the second path: NFL history being altered forever. If Drew Bledsoe had not been knocked out of the Week 2 game between the Patriots and Jets in 2001, after all, who knows how quickly Tom Brady would have gotten his shot and helped kick-start a two-decade dynasty. The game itself was not particularly thrilling — New England lost a defensive-dominated contest with a final score of 10-3 — but its impact on the league can be felt to this day. | Highlights Most recent game: While the Patriots were already gearing up for their return to the playoffs, the Jets continued to flounder through their season. The two teams’ Week 17 meeting last December looked the part: New England dominated from the get-go, jumping to a 35-3 halftime lead behind four Drake Maye passing touchdowns — to Austin Hooper, Rhamondre Stevenson, Stefon Diggs and Hunter Henry — as well as another score by Stevenson. Maye later added a fifth TD to Efton Chism, while the defense put undrafted rookie QB Brady Cook in a blender all day. The result was a 42-10 victory. | Highlights The Patriots and Jets will add to the series history on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET at Gillette Stadium.
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: Milton Williams embracing extra attention as Patriots’ defensive centerpiece
summary: When opposing offenses begin preparing for the New England Patriots’ defense, No. 97 is typically atop the scouting report. After signing a four-year, $104 million contract with the Patriots last offseason, Milton Williams went on to put together a career season. Despite missing six games due to injury, the 27-year-old recorded a career-high 59 pressures […]
full_text: When opposing offenses begin preparing for the New England Patriots’ defense, No. 97 is typically atop the scouting report. After signing a four-year, $104 million contract with the Patriots last offseason, Milton Williams went on to put together a career season. Despite missing six games due to injury, the 27-year-old recorded a career-high 59 pressures while adding 3.0 sacks in the playoffs alone. Other teams took notice, as Williams’ double-team rate has gone up to start this season. “I always say, ‘It costs to be the boss,’” he said. “That’s the price of doing business in the NFL, getting paid and being one of the guys that, you know, I’m probably either first, second, or third on a scouting report each and every week. You play the New England Patriots, it’s like, ‘Alright, we start with 97 and go from there.’” Defensive coordinator Zak Kuhr has seen the increased attention as well. “I would agree with you on that, of them sliding to him or double teaming him — wherever it may be,” Kuhr said. Although Williams has continued to find ways to impact games, the extra attention contributed to a slower start than he would have liked as he recorded just six pressures through the first four games. “I feel like the first couple weeks I was in my own head about it,” Williams said. “You know, making excuses instead of just going out there and just playing. So that’s what I’m focused on now, going out there playing and affecting the game anyway. If I got double team, three people whatever it is. Just figure out a way to make an impact and try to win.” As Kuhr and the defensive staff have worked to create more favorable matchups for Williams, the defensive tackle has searched for answers of his own. That has included studying fellow defensive tackles who consistently face double teams around the league, including star Aaron Donald. “Win quicker. Beat the first guy and then be ready to throw a second move when the next guy come,” Williams said. “It’s tough when they both get on you at once, but if one come, beat him. If they come on different levels, it’s a little easier.” That work began to pay off in last week’s win over the Las Vegas Raiders, when Williams recorded a season-high six pressures. Now, Williams will look to build on that performance and continue finding ways to be a disruptive force along the Patriots’ defensive line. “This is what I work for,” Williams said. “This is what I prayed for, the opportunity to be in this position. I just got to take advantage of it.”

title: ‘War daddy’ Dre’Mont Jones has taken charge of Patriots’ edge room
summary: Entering the 2026 season, no position on the New England Patriots’ roster was a bigger question mark than the defensive edge. And yet, with their first five regular season games in the books, those questions have been answered emphatically. Even with nominal starter Harold Landry remaining on the physically unable to perform list, the group […]
full_text: Entering the 2026 season, no position on the New England Patriots’ roster was a bigger question mark than the defensive edge. And yet, with their first five regular season games in the books, those questions have been answered emphatically. Even with nominal starter Harold Landry remaining on the physically unable to perform list, the group has played some quality football. Each player’s individual efforts play a role in that, but so does the leadership especially provided by one man: Dre’Mont Jones. A free agency signing back in march, Jones has taken charge of the room. “He is a war daddy. He is tough. He fits well in that room,” said outside linebackers coach Mike Smith. “You can’t have a better leader in a room than Dre’Mont Jones.” When Jones arrived in Foxborough on a three-year, $36.5 million contract, he joined a group in transition. K’Lavon Chaisson and Anfernee Jennings, who had ranked first and third in edge snaps in 2025, were both gone; Landry, who finished second on that list, was recovering from offseason knee surgery. The expectations for Jones were therefore clear: help the group find its new identity and provide veteran leadership. So far, he has been doing just that. “We talk about when you build a room they don’t know who the leader is from the outside in because we all play hard, play physical. But Dre is that guy,” said Smith. “He puts all the time in, and all the work in, and practices hard, does all the right things and never complains. He’s just the same person, consistent. Doesn’t have the ups and and downs. You know exactly what you’re going to get when Dre comes in this building. It’s huge to have a guy like him. Our room wouldn’t be where it is because of a guy like him.” Considering the preseason uncertainty, the Patriots’ edge trio of Jones, Elijah Ponder and Gabe Jacas has performed at a surprisingly high level so far. However, there is some uncertainty surrounding the group heading into the upcoming Week 6 game against the New York Jets. Jones sustained a shoulder injury in last week’s win over the Las Vegas Raiders and was a limited practice participant on Wednesday and Thursday. That said, his coach knows that the 29-year-old will do whatever he can to be available for the team on game day. “He pushes through it every day,” said Smith. “He won’t tell you how bad he hurts or what’s going on, he’s just going to do his job and make sure everybody else does their job. He’s very important not just to this room, but the team and this defense.”
