I also record a video version for Patreon, where I break down […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 04: Bryce Young #9 of the Carolina Panthers and Tetairoa McMillan #4 react after a touchdown during the second half of a football game against the Detroit Lions at Bank of America Stadium on October 04, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Each week, I’ll publish two film-room previews: one focusing on the offense and one on the defense. These are primarily film-based, focusing on the schemes, tendencies, and matchups that could shape Sunday’s game, with all statistics coming from the Fantasy Points Data Suite . I also record a video version for Patreon , where I break down the plays in greater detail and where you can further support my work. Yet another week watching an opponent’s offense and thinking, “Well, this looks quite fun.” The Panthers have a quarterback playing very good football, two talented receivers, and creative ways to get their best players favorable matchups. They also have an offensive line that can make the whole thing fall apart. Bryce Young is doing a lot to overcome that, but the Eagles’ defensive front has opportunities this week. Vic Fangio’s challenge is getting after Young without giving this passing game the isolated downfield matchups it wants. Pass Game Young is playing with real confidence. His release is excellent; he’s throwing with anticipation, and he’s placing the ball accurately enough to give his receivers opportunities to make plays after the catch. He’s also doing this without putting the football in harm’s way very often. Nine touchdowns and two interceptions through four games reflect the combination of aggression and control that shows up on film. This is absolutely a vertical passing offense. Young isn’t standing back there looking for a checkdown on every snap. He’s willing to attack outside the numbers, throw into tight windows, and give his receivers opportunities when the coverage leaves them isolated. Here, Jalen Coker wins downfield, and Young hits him in stride. If the Eagles are going to play single-high coverage, their corners had better be comfortable turning and running. Panthers' Offense All22 Thread. 1) Yet another quite fun offense I got to watch! Bryce Young is playing very well, and they funnel much of their passing game through two fun wide receivers & Darren Waller. Here is Jalen Coker winning downfield, and Young hitting him in stride.… pic.twitter.com/AadWEcpYAo — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 15, 2026 Coker deserves proper attention alongside Tetairoa McMillan. He has caught 18 of his 22 targets for 222 yards and two touchdowns, despite playing in only three games. He’s a big receiver who can win outside, contribute after the catch, and do some of the physical work this offense asks of its receivers. This isn’t a passing game where you can tilt everything toward McMillan. Darren Waller is the other receiving weapon who stood out, particularly in the red zone. The Panthers can spread the defense out and let him work against a linebacker or safety, and his option routes give Young an answer based on the defender’s leverage. They also use him on crossing concepts, where his size gives Young a target even in tight coverage. The Eagles’ linebackers and safeties will have some difficult coverage assignments if the rush doesn’t get home. I like the variety in this offense. You get the familiar under-center outside-zone action with a boot off it, but there are also boots and keepers from the gun, RPOs, empty formations, and spread passing concepts. They can condense the formation and threaten the run or spread everyone out and make the defense declare its intentions. Young looks comfortable operating within those different structures. It’s a fun offense to study. 2) As mentioned, Darren Waller is the other weapon to keep an eye on, especially in the red zone. The Panthers like to spread the defense out and can do a bit of everything on offense. You will see the standard outside zone under center boot action, but a lot of passing comes… pic.twitter.com/8gr8kuezFz — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 15, 2026 McMillan, though, is the player who can take over a game. He’s playing like a true WR1. He is strong at the catch point, can go up and get the football, and take over a game if you let him. The Panthers move him and Coker around to create favorable matchups rather than leaving them in the same positions all afternoon. Against single-high coverage, Young will give McMillan opportunities downfield. According to Fantasy Points Data, Young ranks fourth in attempts against single-high safety coverages, with 755 yards and six touchdowns, despite having played only four games. That matches what I saw. The Panthers see those outside opportunities and go after them. For the Eagles, I wouldn’t play a ton of single-high this week, which is where Young is at his most comfortable. 3) Tetairoa McMillan has made the leap and is playing like a true WR1. They move him and Coker around the field to create positive matchups. Coker is tall, but McMillan is very strong at the catch point and can go up and get it. Young will test defenses vertically with McMillan… pic.twitter.com/4vsXXNRoIm — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 15, 2026 However, the protection is a significant problem. There are plays where the Panthers look completely overwhelmed, including against pressure looks, and their willingness to keep attacking downfield can make those failures look particularly ugly. They don’t always take the immediate underneath answer. Sometimes they want the shot, and the protection simply doesn’t give Young enough time. Individual blitzes have caused some awful breakdowns, but Young has generally punished the blitz this season. The offense is averaging +0.35 EPA per dropback against blitzes, and only one of its ten sacks has come against a blitz. The other nine came against non-blitz looks. The Eagles should have opportunities to get home without constantly sending pressure. This is a week to trust the front 4. Young’s production drops from +0.41 EPA per dropback in a clean pocket to −0.02 under pressure. Make him operate under pressure while keeping enough defenders back to contest the throws he wants. I would play a ton of split-safety coverages while rushing 4. 4) However, the offense does have a clear issue, which is pass protection. They have struggled vs. the blitz, but also with just 4 pass rushers. This play might look a little familiar. They will take shots vs. pressure looks, rather than take the easy checkdown every time,… pic.twitter.com/62VixfCAfk — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) October 15, 2026 Their use of empty makes this offense particularly interesting. Young loves throwing from empty, and the Panthers are happy to attack vertically from it. Many offenses use empty to get the ball out quickly and spread out underneath defenders. The Panthers can do that, but they will also ask their receivers to win downfield with only five blockers protecting. Young’s use of empty has always been unique. The Eagles won’t face many similar challenges this year. Young is 17-of-22 for 237 yards from empty, averaging 10.77 yards per attempt, behind only Brock Purdy. It’s a small sample, but it supports how dangerous these plays look. And, once again, McMillan is a major part of it. Spreading the defense out can make it easier for Young to identify his best matchup, and he’s accurate enough to take advantage. Personally, I would want Fangio to show pressure against these formations and then change who actually rushes. Simulated pressures could test the protection while preserving seven defenders in coverage. The Eagles don’t have to send six just because the Panthers have emptied the backfield. They need those five blockers to sort out the rush correctly and give Young a less comfortable picture behind it. 5) However, what makes this offense really interesting is their use of empty. full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 09: Saquon Barkley #26 of the Philadelphia Eagles talks with Devonta Smith #6 during the second quarter of the game against the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium on October 09, 2025 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles issued their third and final official injury report of the week on Friday in advance of their Week 6 game against the Carolina Panthers. The Eagles ruled five players OUT: Jalen Hurts, Saquon Barkley, Will Shipley, Jalyx Hunt, and Michael Carter II. The Eagles already ruled Hurts out when they announced the starting quarterback is dealing with a “superficial blood clot.” It’s unclear how much time Hurts will miss; estimates seem to vary from as little as a couple weeks to as most as a season-ending issue. We all hope the best for Hurts’ health while he recovers. In the meantime, Tanner McKee will start at quarterback. It seems like Cole Payton will serve as the backup QB while new addition Joe Milton III could be the emergency third option, at least for Sunday’s game. Barkley is missing his second straight game due to a hamstring injury. With Barkley out and now both Tank Bigsby and Shipley on injured reserve, the Eagles have two health running backs on their roster: Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele. Look for Pierce to start while Steele could be mixed in. The Eagles also have Jaydon Blue and Ian Wheeler on the practice squad if they want to use a temporary elevation for more backfield depth. Hunt’s absence is no surprise since Vic Fangio said it would be “miraculous” if he played this week. It sounds like Hunt could avoid going on injured reserve, though. Hunt currently leads the Eagles in quarterback hits so losing him hurts a pass rush that already hasn’t been very productive. MC2 got banged up in Week 5. He was previously the starting safety next to Andrew Mukuba in nickel packages after Marcus Epps suffered an injury. But now Carter is sidelined The Eagles ruled one player DOUBTFUL: A.J. Epenesa. Epenesa was limited on Wednesday before being downgraded to not practicing on Thursday and Friday. With Hunt out and Epenesa likely not playing, the Eagles will be without two of their five edge rushers. The Eagles ruled five players QUESTIONABLE: Landon Dickerson, Drew Kendall, Eli Stowers, Grant Calcaterra, and Jakorian Bennett. Dickerson was limited in practice all week. I have a hard time believing the Eagles will activate him from injured to play before he’s able to fully participate in at least one practice. Kendall missed Wednesday’s practice before being limited on Thursday and Friday. Doesn’t seem conducive to him suiting up on Sunday. If neither Dickerson nor Kendall play, the Eagles will likely use their same starting offensive line from last week: LT Jordan Mailata, LG Willie Lampkin, C Jake Majors, RG Tyler Steen, RT Markel Bell. Continuity!!!!! Stowers was a full participant in practice but it doesn’t seem like the Eagles will be in a rush to activate him from injured reserve. Ditto for Calcaterra and Bennett. The Eagles have until 4:00 PM Eastern on Saturday to make any roster moves prior to Sunday’s kickoff. title: Eagles place Will Shipley on injured reserve
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are placing Will Shipley on injured reserve, according to an official team announcement. Shipley, who started on Sunday, reportedly suffered “a partial tear of his plantar fascia” during the Eagles’ Week 5 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. By going on IR, Shipley will automatically miss the Eagles’ next four games: The Eagles […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Will Shipley #28 of the Philadelphia Eagles warms up before a game against the Washington Commanders at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles are placing Will Shipley on injured reserve, according to an official team announcement. Shipley, who started on Sunday, reportedly suffered “ a partial tear of his plantar fascia ” during the Eagles’ Week 5 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. By going on IR, Shipley will automatically miss the Eagles’ next four games: Week 6 vs. Carolina Panthers Week 7 vs. Dallas Cowboys Week 8 at Washington Commanders Week 9 vs. New York Giants The Eagles then have their bye in Week 10 so the earliest we could see Shipley back is Week 11, when they host the Pittsburgh Steelers. With Saquon Barkley still nursing a hamstring injury and Tank Bigsby also on IR, the Eagles are currently without their top three running backs. Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele are the only healthy backfield options on the roster. The team also has Jaydon Blue and newly signed Ian Wheeler on the practice squad. Putting Shipley on IR frees up a roster spot for the Eagles signing Joe Milton III away from the Dallas Cowboys’ practice squad .

title: Eagles opposing player to stop, Week 6 edition
summary: The Eagles are an explicit mess right now. They have had 24 players on the injury report this week. Stars Jalen Hurts, out with a serious, though treatable issue with a superficial blood clot, and Saquon Barkley will not play Sunday against the visiting Carolina Panthers. Dontayvion Wicks, Jalyx Hunt, Michael Carter II, Will Shipley, […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 4: Bryce Young #9 of the Carolina Panthers celebrates after a touchdown against the Detroit Lions during an NFL football game at Bank of America Stadium on October 4, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Eagles are an explicit mess right now. They have had 24 players on the injury report this week. Stars Jalen Hurts, out with a serious, though treatable issue with a superficial blood clot, and Saquon Barkley will not play Sunday against the visiting Carolina Panthers. Dontayvion Wicks, Jalyx Hunt, Michael Carter II, Will Shipley, and A.J. Epenesa are questionable, along with offensive threat DeVonta Smith, Drew Kendall, Landon Dickerson, Tyler Steen, Marquise Brown, Jonathan Greenard, Grant Calcaterra, Eli Stowers, Jakorian Bennett, and E.J. Jenkins. What is certain is that the rising 2-2 Panthers will have Bryce Young, who has thrown for 1,268 passing yards in Carolina’s first four games, the second-most yardage thrown by a Panthers’ quarterback through four games since Cam Newton’s rookie season. Young is beginning to turn into the player everyone envisioned him to be when he was taken No. 1 overall out of Alabama in the 2023 NFL Draft. Young has thrown nine touchdown passes against two interceptions this season and averaging an NFL-high 317 yards passing a game, up considerably from 188.2 yards passing a game last season. “The quarterback has really progressed,” said Eagles’ defensive coordinator Vic Fangio about Young, when asked this week about what impressed him about the Panthers. “I think I coached against him when he was a rookie, and to see the progress that he’s made from then to now, kudos to him and their coaching staff. He really good processor, makes quick decisions, knows where to go with the ball. He’s elusive, he’s a scrambler, really good anticipation. Very, very impressed by him.” The Eagles will start Tanner McKee in place of Hurts this Sunday, further complicating a scrambled offensive that is not working under first-year offensive coordinator Sean Mannion. The Eagles are the worst second-half team in the NFL under Hurts, who single-handedly won their first two games, and walked off the field with a 17-16 lead against Jacksonville last week. Now they have McKee there, who has not looked good at all, in fact, he’s regressed since his rookie season. McKee inherits an offense that has converted 10 of 38 third downs in the second half. They have gone 18-straight possessions over the last six quarters in the second half without scoring a touchdown, and are last in scoring in the NFL, averaging 6.4 points in the second half. The Eagles are last in the NFL in the second half in yards per play (3.6), passing yards per play (60.6), and tied for 31st in red-zone efficiency (33.3%). In their five games this season in the second half, they scored 10 points and 149 yards against Washington, 10 points and 125 against Tennessee, 0 points and 54 yards against Chicago, 0 points and 66 yards against the Los Angeles Rams and 3 points and 84 yards against Jacksonville, which averages out to 95.6 yards and an NFL-low 4.6 points a game in the second half. Under Young, Carolina is No. 6 in the NFL in second-half scoring, averaging 14.5 points a game, up from 10.6 last year. Young has completed 101 of 162 passes (62.3%). His stature, generously listed at 5-foot-10, 204 pounds, was thought to be a hindrance. The Eagles will definitely have to play with hands up in his face, but Young moves well and throws well on the run. The Eagles may not have a chance to get hands in his face, considering that they are ranked No. 28 in team sacks with 6. The Eagles are a pulsating cesspool right now. Facing an improving Bryce Young and depending on a sinking Tanner McKee does not seem to be a cure.

title: Eagles-Panthers Game Preview: 5 questions and answers with the Week 6 enemy
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are returning to Lincoln Financial Field this weekend to host the Carolina Panthers. The Birds will be coming off a trip from London while their opponent is coming off a bye week. In order to preview this Week 6 matchup, I reached out to our enemies over at Cat Scratch Reader. The […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - DECEMBER 08: Bryce Young #9 of the Carolina Panthers throws a pass as Jalen Carter #98 of the Philadelphia Eagles dives toward him in the first quarter of a game at Lincoln Financial Field on December 08, 2024 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles are returning to Lincoln Financial Field this weekend to host the Carolina Panthers. The Birds will be coming off a trip from London while their opponent is coming off a bye week. In order to preview this Week 6 matchup, I reached out to our enemies over at Cat Scratch Reader . The witty Walker Clement kindly took the time to answer my questions about this upcoming battle. Let’s take a look at the answers. 1) Bryce Young seems to be playing well; three of his top seven games in terms of passer rating have taken place this season. How real is his improvement and what can it be attributed to? I’m scared to say it’s real but that’s mostly because we’ve been hurt before. Young was excusably atrocious (coaching dumpster fire) in his rookie year. He was worse to start his second season to the point that he got benched until an Andy Dalton broken thumb returned him to the line up. He was better, but not good. Last year, his third season, had ups and downs. The ups showed he was physically capable of playing well, a legitimate question up to that point. The downs proved he couldn’t (yet) play well consistently. This season he seems to be playing well consistently. His worst game was against the Cleveland Browns when he had a mild, nagging knee injury that has apparently persisted through the bye week. Otherwise he has been one of the best quarterbacks in the league. His statistical improvement alone has been so stellar that he remained a top 10 passing quarterback through Week 5 despite having a bye in Week 5. So, is it real? Why is it real? I truly don’t know but all of Panthers nation is what I would describe as cautiously giddy at this unexpected and welcome turnabout in Young’s fortunes. We’re also all fully braced for when the other shoe drops and knocks the wheels off of our clown car. 2 – Sounds like the Panthers could be getting some key players back for this game. Who are you expecting to return and what’s the impact? What about the absences that Carolina could be dealing with? There are three players who could return to the lineup and have a significant impact over what the team put together against the Lions in their last game. First is Taylor Moton. He has started nearly every game for the Panthers at right tackle since 2018. He is an excellent player who will elevate the Panthers struggling run game if he is ready to play. There is no guarantee he will be up to the task after recovering from blood clots in his lungs during the offseason. But with back up and rookie right tackle Monroe Freeling questionable-at-best with a knee injury, the Panthers need every man they can find. Similarly, Tershawn Wharton may be ready to step into the ailing defensive line rotation. He should provide some much needed fresh legs and pass rushing acumen. Don’t expect him to get a sack if he plays, but he should be contributing to pressure. The second most important returning player is wide receiver Jalen Coker. He is an incredibly talented guy and shares great chemistry with Bryce Young. He is a large part of Young’s statistical improvement this year. With him on the field, McMillan shouldn’t need to catch another 14 passes for 192 yards in a single game. 3 – The Eagles’ offense stinks but the Panthers haven’t exactly been one of the top defenses in the league. What are the strengths and weaknesses of that unit? The strengths entering Week 4 were the interior defensive line and the cornerbacks. Since then, defensive tackle Cam Jackson and cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson have landed on IR. Young corners Akayleb Evans and Will Lee III had rough outings against the Lions. Lee has promise, but he’s a rookie who is still adjusting to the speed of the game. They are expected to start again this week. That leaves Devin Lloyd, who has been amazing, and Jaelan Phillips, who is a one-man show thanks to injuries across the rest of the front seven, as the noticeable strengths of the defense. It sounds bleak, but they managed to hold Jahmyr Gibbs to 46 yards on 15 carries in their last game. Anything can happen. 4 – What’s the biggest matchup in the Panthers’ favor and the biggest matchup against their favor? Wide receiver Tetarioa McMillan, the Week 4 NFC offensive player of the Week, vs anybody you have is the biggest match up in favor of the Panthers. Conversely, DeVonta Smith versus anybody left standing in a Panthers uniform after the snap is a huge mismatch against Carolina. That suggests an explosive, high scoring game with lots of fast scores. Right? 5 – Who wins this game and why? With the Eagles currently listed as 1.5-point home favorites, what’s your score prediction? It a little bit depends on who they get back from injury, but I think these are two teams trending in opposite directions. The Panthers should ultimately win this one, but the idea of a shoot out decided by the performance of two star wide receivers will be wrong. I expect the Panthers to flip, or fumble, the script and end up narrowly winning a surprisingly defensive battle 17 – 14. I’d be comfortable widening the margin of victory if Young, Coker, and Moton are all fully cleared to play. I also wouldn’t be surprised to see them look completely new to the game of football and lose by three possessions or more. Such is the confidence bred by our recent years of, uh, success.

full_text: Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images | Getty Images Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts was ruled out for Sunday’s game due a blood clot they discovered in London. Unfortunately, the blood clot moved and Hurts could be looking at an extended absence. The team will move forward with Tanner McKee as the starting QB, and have rookie Cole Payton as the backup, but added more depth on Friday by signing Joe Milton off the Dallas Cowboys’ practice squad. Breaking: The #Eagles are signing QB Joe Milton off the #Cowboys practice squad and to their 53-man roster, per sources. pic.twitter.com/e4LVVD4ove — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) October 16, 2026 Milton has two seasons under his belt in Dallas, and played in five games during that time. He completed 37-of 53 pass attempts for 424 yards and two touchdowns, but he also threw two interceptions. It’s interesting that the Eagles didn’t bring back Andy Dalton, who they released just a week ago, but there were some internet rumors that other teams were interested in the veteran QB and maybe he didn’t want to return to Philly. Either way, the Eagles signing Milton means they don’t expect Jalen Hurts to be back soon, and will need at least an emergency QB3, if not someone to compete for the backup job.

title: Eagles News: Zack Baun says Tanner McKee has “got some sort of Tom Brady career arc to him”
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Is Tanner McKee going to be the Tom Brady to Jalen Hurts’ Drew Bledsoe?!?! I don’t think that’s what Zack Baun was suggesting here as much as he’s trying to hype up his teammate. I can’t say I’m feeling encouraged about […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Tanner McKee #16 of the Philadelphia Eagles runs off the field against the Washington Commanders following an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Is Tanner McKee going to be the Tom Brady to Jalen Hurts’ Drew Bledsoe?!?! I don’t think that’s what Zack Baun was suggesting here as much as he’s trying to hype up his teammate. I can’t say I’m feeling encouraged about McKee after watching him struggle this offseason and fail to initially beat out Andy Dalton in the team’s eyes. But based on the positive glimpses we’ve seen in the past, I’m not ready to totally be out on him. I’m holding out hope that he can still offer some good moments. Will be interesting to see. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Jalen Hurts’ blood clot next chapter in bizarre Eagles season — let’s get weird – PHLY Eagles “I love Tanner,” said Zack Baun, creating a triangle. “I love that guy so much. I told someone that it’s just seeming like he’s got some sort of Tom Brady career arc to him, because he’s totally capable, he’s tall, he knows where to go with the ball, he gets it out on time and he’s got a lot of confidence in these receivers.” Unsaid is that as dire as things may look for a team with about as many players listed on the injury report as first downs they’ve earned in the second half of games this season, it’s not like the offense can get worse. Maybe there’s some magic to be found in McKee shepherding a lineup likely to feature more backups than starters. He already knows those guys! “It’s hard to say because our offense hasn’t quite gotten rolling,” said Covey. “In an ideal world, I think he fits great in this offense. Now, we still gotta find ourselves a little bit. So in that process of finding yourself, you want a guy as confident as Tanner. I think he can help with us finding it.” Why Eagles players think Tanner McKee is ready for this moment – NBCSP A weird Eagles season took another unexpected turn on Thursday when we learned Jalen Hurts is out for Week 6 against the Panthers with a blood clot in his calf. All of a sudden, Tanner McKee is a starter “I think everybody’s got a lot of belief in Tanner,” tight end Dallas Goedert said. “When his number has been called upon, he has stepped in and done a good job for us. Obviously, you hate to lose Jalen like that, the leader of the offense. But it’s kind of what we’ve been dealing with all year. The next man has to step up.” Spadaro: Tanner McKee will be ready for his moment – PhiladelphiaEagles.com The moment is here for quarterback Tanner McKee, and he intends to maximize the opportunity. In the NFL, every player understands the responsibility: When the time comes, and it will for every player, it is imperative to be ready, to be prepared, to produce. Tanner McKee, starting quarterback. This isn’t a Week 18 game, where McKee has gained the only two starts of his four-year NFL career to date. This is Week 6, at Lincoln Financial Field against the Carolina Panthers defense with so much at stake. McKee, replacing Jalen Hurts – out with a blood clot in his calf as announced by the Eagles on Thursday, has prepared every day since the day the Eagles selected him with a sixth-round draft pick in the 2023 NFL Draft for this very scenario. “As a backup quarterback, that’s the mindset you have to have,” McKee said on Thursday at his locker in the Jefferson Health Training Complex. “At any moment, you have to be ready to play on a Sunday. It could be the first play, it could be the last play. It’s kind of a luxury for me to have the ‘1’ (starter) reps in practice and just running the meetings or whatever it is. It’s kind of a luxury for me as a backup to have a week to prepare like that.” Jalen Hurts is “out indefinitely” … now what for the Eagles? – BGN It’ll be interesting to see if there are any notable stylistic differences between Sean Mannion calling the game for Hurts versus McKee. But, again, I’m not expecting the results to suddenly be pretty. Though, if you’re looking for reason for optimism, the Panthers’ defense might be fairly gettable. They’re banged up at cornerback with starters Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson both on injured reserve. NFC East Mixtape Vol. 198: Time for someone to take charge – NFC East Mixtape This week is offering us four different NFC East games, two of which take place in primetime. Can the New York Giants keep things up against the New Orleans Saints? Will the Philadelphia Eagles stop their skid against the Carolina Panthers? Is there any way the Dallas Cowboys can get things back on track, at Lambeau Field of all places? Are the Washington Commanders doomed against San Francisco? Do they even know how football works?! RJ Ochoa and Brandon Lee Gowton discuss on the latest edition of the NFC East Mixtape! You can see that we have a BRAND NEW NFC East Mixtape YouTube Channel so make sure to subscribe as the show will live here exclusively in video format. AND you can also listen to the show! On Blogging The Boys and/or Bleeding Green Nation podcast feeds as well as the SB Nation NFL Show feed! Eagles QB Jalen Hurts’ ‘superficial blood clot’: A doctor weighs in – PhillyVoice “It’s probably going to be week by week. They’ll have to check that blood clot with another ultrasound to see if it’s moving, to see if it’s improving. If it’s not moving and it is improving, it starts to stabilize and resolve, he probably can play. But if it’s getting bigger or moving, then you start worrying about it going to the deep veins versus the superficial veins, and then eventually causing a deep vein thrombosis. Then you can have big problems with that if it gets thrown to the heart it blocks the lungs it’s called a pulmonary embolism, which can be life threatening. I’m not a vascular surgeon. That’s more of their specific field. But in terms of what I know in general is that if that clot starts to improve, whether it goes away, it gets reabsorbed or if it gets very stabilized — like it’s not moving or if it’s not getting larger — then hypothetically he can play, because he was playing on it and so they determined that he was safe to play. It’s a judgment call. But that’s what you would have to see, that the clot itself doesn’t get worse or continue to migrate.” The Hits Keep Coming – Iggles Blitz And for the Eagles. They need their star QB to return soon if they have any chance of turning the season around. Tanner McKee will start this week. It will be interesting to see how the offense looks with him running it. McKee struggled this summer. He’s had more time to learn the offense by now and will have a gameplan to study to get ready for Sunday. Maybe that will help him to play better. It will help that he is going against one of the worst defenses in the league (26th in points, 29th in yards). Brian Answers: Eagles woes, Panthers offensive gameplan, Bryce Young extension, and more! – Cat Scratch Reader I didn’t feel great about this game, but then Jalen Hurts was ruled out with a blood clot. Which, by the way, from one fan base to another, I hope he recovers in short order and has no complications. These types of things make you realize there’s more to life than the next week of football, and I hope Hurts gets all the treatment he needs and doesn’t have any negative impact on his life as a person. That said, this is definitely a game where the Panthers should have every chance to win it, in convincing fashion. And knowing their recent history as a franchise, they might drop the ball and lose this game. Cause Panthers fans can never have nice things. Who’s Tanner McKee? The Eagles turn to the ‘Mormon Missile’ to replace Jalen Hurts – The Athletic One might have been more skeptical of that statement two months ago, when McKee was adjusting to new…

title: NFL predictions: Favorite bets for Steelers vs. Buccaneers
summary: The Steelers are 3-2 heading into a Week 6 showdown with the 1-4 Buccaneers. If you like to place a few bets on the side to spice up your viewing experience, now’s a great time to check in with our friends over at FanDuel Sportsbook, with the game just a few days away. Here are […]
full_text: (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Steelers are 3-2 heading into a Week 6 showdown with the 1-4 Buccaneers. If you like to place a few bets on the side to spice up your viewing experience, now’s a great time to check in with our friends over at FanDuel Sportsbook , with the game just a few days away. Here are some of their offerings that caught my eye. Steelers first drive result: Offensive Touchdown +380 The Steelers have scored a touchdown on the first drive of the game in two of the past three games. This all kicked in against the Bengals when Mike McCarthy made the call to change up the right side of the offensive line, and to lean away from the zone-running schemes they were favoring during the first two weeks, and instead switch to a more man/duo heavy scheme. The Buccaneers are good at stopping the run, but their pass defense has been among the worst in the league, and the first drive of the game is often one where play callers like McCarthy come out looking strong since they are able to script the first series out before the defense has time to adjust. I like the Steelers to make it their third first-drive touchdown in four weeks, but if you’re less confident, FanDuel is offering a Field Goal attempt at +330, and a Punt at -105. To score 2+ touchdowns: Jaylen Warren +750, Pat Freiermuth +3300 Warren has been on fire lately and is a player I expect to be featured heavily in this game, even if it’s more as a pass catcher due to Tampa Bay’s stout run defense. Likewise, Pat Freiermuth leads the team in touchdowns with four on the season. Both are players I expect to have favorable matchups in the passing game this week and who could be leaned on heavily in the red zone. If two touchdowns feels a bit rich for you, however, I do like picking a half in which Freiermuth could score a single touchdown. He’s listed at +600 whether you think he scores in the first half or second half, though I favor the second half. One parlay involving Warren, Freiermuth, Bernard If none of the previous options excite you, or you’re the type who likes to make your own odds, a parlay is a way to add even more intrigue. I’ve cooked up a four-leg parlay that might intrigue you: Jaylen Warren over 3.5 receptions (-114) Jaylen Warren over 91.5 rushing + receiving yards (-114) Germie Bernard to record a 10+ yard reception (-750) Pat Freiermuth anytime touchdown scorer (+310) Parlay odds: +1080 And there you have it. Those are my favorite prop bets for this week’s game. Are there any that you have your eyes on for this week?

title: Steelers-Buccaneers preview: What to expect from Tampa Bay’s offense, defense in Week 6
summary: The 3-2 Steelers will travel to Tampa Bay in Week 6 to take on the Buccaneers, who sit at a disappointing 1-4 but are coming off their lone win of the season thus far — a 24-16 showing against the Cowboys in Week 5. It’s been a rough season for Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles […]
full_text: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images | Getty Images The 3-2 Steelers will travel to Tampa Bay in Week 6 to take on the Buccaneers, who sit at a disappointing 1-4 but are coming off their lone win of the season thus far — a 24-16 showing against the Cowboys in Week 5. It’s been a rough season for Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles and co., and the team’s recent three-year, $165 million extension for quarterback Baker Mayfield already isn’t aging that well: The veteran passer struggled in a winless start to the year before missing games with a dislocated thumb on this throwing hand. But coming off a Thursday Night Football win in Dallas, the Buccaneers have some momentum and extra prep time to prepare for the Steelers. What should Pittsburgh expect on Sunday? What to expect from the Bucs’ offense Rushing YPG: 133 (7th) Passing YPG: 173.4 (27th) PPG: 20 (25th) RB : The Buccaneers offense will be without starting quarterback Baker Mayfield for yet another game, meaning undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels will once again start under center for Tampa Bay against Pittsburgh. The good news is that Daniels is a rookie with just two starts under his belt. That can show in his play and the Steelers should be able to take advantage of some mistakes on Sunday. That said, Mayfield was having a rough start to 2026, and it was Daniels who helped lead the Buccaneers to their first win of the season last week. Like everything in the NFL, beating the Buccaneers won’t be slam dunk in Week 6. Daniels looked impressively poised and accurate against the Cowboys defense last week, passing for 189 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions with 76% completion. Of course, offensive coordinator Zac Robinson put together a game plan to help the young passer succeed, with an emphasis on the quick game and play action. Daniels is on the shorter side for an NFL passer (6’0), and his arm strength doesn’t leap off the screen, but he drives the ball well on short and intermediate passes and only had a few rough misses against the Cowboys (note this was against a struggling Dallas defense). His escapability is an upgrade over Mayfield’s, with Daniels already having 87 yards and four first downs on the ground this season. Jalon Daniels lowers the shoulder and picks up the 1st down 💪 @TBvsDAL on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/LG3l61JU0s — NFL (@NFL) October 9, 2026 While the Buccaneers are largely a short-game passing attack, Daniels still has moments where his processing slows down and he attempts to play hero ball. Tampa Bay has a strong offensive line but currently has the third-worst sack rate in the NFL (10.1%), with 17 sacks allowed this season. A number of those plays have been quarterback error — Tampa Bay has the NFL’s seventh-longest time to throw at 2.98 seconds — even if Daniels has been an improvement in that area over Mayfield. QB dropbacks to result in a scramble or sack this season Jayden Daniels and Jalon Daniels being right next to each other is just some good clean family fun pic.twitter.com/3DnKAd5quh — Ian Hartitz (@Ihartitz) October 13, 2026 If the Steelers can keep up with Daniels in the backfield, they should be able to log some sacks or at least a handful of pressures on Sunday. But Tampa Bay’s offensive line won’t make that task easy. Led by one of the league’s best tackles in Tristian Wirfs and a slew of other good players such as Graham Barton and Luke Goedeke, the Buccaneers can both pass protect well and maul in the run game. Lowest pressure rate allowed among OL this season Buccaneers 18.4% Chiefs 18.9% Falcons 19.1% Bengals 20.6% Vikings 21.2% pic.twitter.com/Gk1sLlhljy — PFF (@PFF) October 13, 2026 On the ground, the Tampa holds defenses to the sixth-lowest run stuff rate (12.5%) in the NFL. The Buccaneers are also second-best in yards before contact per attempt (2.16), per NFL Pro. The Buccaneers use a lot of motion to try to confuse defenses pre-snap, and it melds well with a rushing offense that favors gap concepts. At running back, the room has two solid names in starter Bucky Irving and former Steeler Kenny Gainwell. Both are slimmer running backs who can be a weapon in the passing game, with Irving showing off his phone-booth quickness with a long run against Dallas last week. Nasty jump cut and vision by Bucky Irving pic.twitter.com/fWUxwEQLtt — Billy M (@BillyM_91) October 9, 2026 If healthy, Sean Tucker is another name to keep an eye on in Tampa Bay’s backfield as a more hard-nosed, downhill runner. At pass catcher, the Buccaneers have a number of recognizable names, but still lack an established WR1. Emeka Egbuka leads the team in receiving yards with 192 through five games, averaging just 9.1 yards per reception as a primarily underneath target. Tight end Cade Otton, with 182 yards, has also been a steady contributor. Chris Godwin Jr. hasn’t had his pre-injury production, but has been another solid name in the short game with 129 of his 179 yards this season coming after the catch. On more downfield passes, 5’10 speed threat Tez Johnson averages 27.6 yards per catch on five receptions this season, while rookie Ted Hurst III, one of my favorite mid-round prospects this spring, has made some plays with eight grabs for 128 yards and a touchdown this season. Ted Hurst III's first career TD 🗣️ @MINvsTB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/vwmtGgBFFi — NFL (@NFL) September 27, 2026 Tampa Bay is one of the most 11 personnel-heavy offenses in the league, getting a wide range of receivers involved. Still, its running game ranks top 10 thanks to a competent offensive line. On paper, the Steelers’ defense certainly has the talent to shut down the Buccaneers’ offense, but Daniels is a bit of an X factor. Will an experienced pass rush with more film on the rookie dominate, or will Daniels continue to improve and clean up Tampa Bay’s sack rate with his mobility? Also complicating things is the tendency for offensive coordinators to mix up their tendencies more when playing with a reserve quarterback. However, if the Steelers can disrupt the Buccaneers’ quick passing game and run game and force Daniels to play out of rhythm and with more downfield shots, this game could bode well for the Pittsburgh defense. What to expect from the Bucs ’ defense Rushing YPG Allowed: 72.8 (2nd) Passing YPG Allowed: 226.6 (20th) PPG Allowed: 22.4 (T-14th) RP : The Buccaneers’ defense makes a fascinating matchup for the Steelers’ offense. This contest will pit strength against strength: Pittsburgh’s running game versus Tampa Bay’s run defense. But it will also feature weakness against weakness: the Steelers have struggled against man coverage, yet the Buccaneers run man concepts at a bottom-third rate in the league. In most metrics, the Buccaneers’ run defense is near the top of the league, and their overall strategy is pretty apparent. Tampa Bay has light boxes — six or fewer defenders — at the second-lowest rate (20.7%) in the NFL. They have stacked boxes — eight or more defenders — at the second-highest rate (41.4%) in the league. Put another way, 79.3% of the time, the Bucs have seven defenders or more in the box against the run, giving them a numbers advantage if the offense doesn’t answer with some combination of two tight ends, a fullback, or a condensed formation that hugs the receivers tight to their linemen. The results have followed. Not only are the Buccaneers allowing the second-fewest rushing yards per game, but they’re also top-seven or better in: Average yards after contact (1.72, 1st) Yards per carry (3.3, T-2nd) EPA/Rush (-0.18, 4th) Runs of 10+ yards allowed (9, T-4th) Run stuff rate (18.9%, 7th) While he doesn’t fill up the stat sheet, plenty of credit for the Buccaneers’ success against the run should be paid to nose tackle Vita Vea. As a nose tackle, Vita Vea doesn't often fill up the stat sheet, but he's still a disruptor against the run. First clip, takes on two blockers and closes a potential lane for the RB. Next two clips, shows…

full_text: (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Steelers fans and fans across the country. The Pittsburgh Steelers take on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday, but are limping in with the injuries to Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson. The Steelers look to notch their first win on the road while still perfect at home, but a critical stretch begins on Sunday as the AFC North will be tightly contested between all four teams. Following the Bucs, the Steelers take on another NFC South opponent, the New Orleans Saints, with back-to-back divisional matchups with the Bengals and Browns before an interstate battle with the Philadelphia Eagles. A realistic finish of 3-2 through the five games puts the Steelers at 6-4, but getting greedy isn’t a bad idea, and taking down one or both of their division matchups puts the Steelers in prime position to win the division. The offensive line has played well with bookend tackles Troy Fantanu and Max Iheanchor. Mason McCormick and Zach Frazier have been great on the interior. Jaylen Warren is on an absolute tear with eyes on a continued workhorse role even with the return of Rico Dowdle. Are you confident in the Steelers? As we do every week, we polled Steelers fans if they are confident in the direction the Steelers are heading. 49 percent of fans voted yes after their 34-22 win over the Colts. A win on Sunday against the Buccaneers would push Pittsburgh to 4-2, and likely push that 49 percent number even higher. title: Mike Macdonald sticking with Sam Darnold as Seahawks starting quarterback
summary: The Seattle Seahawks, for now, will stick with their Super Bowl winning quarterback amid ongoing struggles with turnovers and accuracy. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald told Seattle Sports 710 and later reporters on Friday that there won’t be a pivot to Drew Lock, who started and performed well against the Arizona Cardinals and otherwise doesn’t […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks, for now, will stick with their Super Bowl winning quarterback amid ongoing struggles with turnovers and accuracy. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald told Seattle Sports 710 and later reporters on Friday that there won’t be a pivot to Drew Lock, who started and performed well against the Arizona Cardinals and otherwise doesn’t have any turnovers through (essentially) two games played. “We have a great backup quarterback in Drew,” Macdonald told Seattle Sports. “Drew is a tremendous quarterback. He’s a starting-level quarterback, and [I understand] that we didn’t turn the ball over when Drew played, and then we’ve had takeaway issues [with Sam starting]. “But right now, I think these things we have to attack as if they’re in our control, and then we can move it forward. Sam’s played great football for us this year the majority of the time, and there’s other times where, and he’ll be the first to tell you, he needs to take care of the football.” Darnold acknowledged on Thursday night following his catastrophic two-interception showing against the Denver Broncos that the turnovers, of which he has a league-leading seven picks, are hurting the team. “I just think it’s ‘BS,’ you know, for me to keep turning the ball over,” Darnold said. “It’s not fair to our defense, not fair to our special teams’ group, not fair really to the entire team. So I have to be better that way.” “We have a lot of faith in Sam,” Macdonald said at his press conference. “Sam has played great football for us. He’s done a lot of great things this year. He’s obviously turned the ball over more than we want to. There are things on our end that can help him play better football and he’s part of the solution rather than the opposite.” It’s not surprising that Macdonald didn’t get off the plane and immediately declare Drew Lock the starter. We’ve sort of been here with Mike when Geno Smith had his turnover issues in the 2024 season, namely against the Los Angeles Rams in a 26-20 overtime loss. He never benched Geno for Sam Howell, and now we’ve got another conversation brewing with Darnold and Drew Lock. If Darnold continues to struggle against the Kansas City Chiefs, a QB change really should not be out of the question. It’s less of, “Is Drew Lock suddenly a franchise quarterback?” and more of, “Is Drew Lock going to be less of a liability than Sam Darnold?” at this point in what is on course to be a very disappointing season. A highly anticipated Sunday night showdown with Kansas City, in part because of Ken Walker’s return to Seattle, now has an even bigger storyline to watch.
author: Mookie Alexander

title: The cracks in the Seahawks offense last season are now chasms under Brian Fleury
summary: The Seattle Seahawks offense stinks. Ignore the points scored, which do not accurately reflect the underlying statistics, the Seahawks offense is bad. It may cost them a playoff berth, and it’s pretty much already cost them the NFC West title barring some humongous San Francisco 49ers collapse. Seattle sits at 3-3 after a brutal 17-14 […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks offense stinks. Ignore the points scored, which do not accurately reflect the underlying statistics, the Seahawks offense is bad. It may cost them a playoff berth, and it’s pretty much already cost them the NFC West title barring some humongous San Francisco 49ers collapse. Seattle sits at 3-3 after a brutal 17-14 overtime loss to the Denver Broncos. The Seahawks’ three losses are by a combined eight points, but the turnover margin in those games is a combined -7. That’s not going to get it done. Sam Darnold has played poorly enough to justify talks about benching him. The running game is both banged up and an absolute mess. If not for Jaxon Smith-Njigba, the Seahawks would look like an offense befitting of their 1990s throwbacks, because Seattle’s offenses for much of the early 1990s were an impossible watch. New offensive coordinator Brian Fleury is taking a lot of heat for the way this unit has cratered coming off a Super Bowl season. I’m not going to excuse Fleury whatsoever for this atrocious offensive slide, but I think there’s something bigger at play that stems from the tail-end of last season under Klint Kubiak. The warning signs for the Seahawks offense were there last year For those of you who are new to Field Gulls and/or don’t remember, I wrote a big article right before the season finale against the San Francisco 49ers . Seattle had won six consecutive games but the high-flying, high-scoring offense from the first half of the season noticeably dipped during the win streak. I’m not going to just quote myself in huge blocks and make this article a lot longer than it needs to be, so here are the CliffNotes (MookNotes?) of what I observed at the time: The passing game clearly declined in efficiency from the Los Angeles Rams loss onward . The run game improved, which was a relief, but Sam Darnold’s hot start noticeably cooled and it was more than just the four-interception disaster against LA. His sack rate would’ve been worse if you took the Rams game out, actually. They were also a much more explosive offense pre-Rams loss. Teams started blitzing Sam Darnold more and stacking the box less . Four of Darnold’s six highest blitz rates faced were from Week 11 onward, most notably the onslaught from Brian Flores’ Minnesota Vikings. Even the Carolina Panthers blitzed on over half of Darnold’s dropbacks. Darnold was one of the most blitzed QBs at the time (and generally performed well), but teams were sending extra heat more often. In terms of stacked boxes (8+ defenders in the box), the Seahawks went from facing stacked boxes north of 35 percent of the time to barely 30. Opposing teams stopped fretting about the running game and wanted Sam Darnold to beat them. Sam Darnold’s weaknesses were exposed in pure dropback situations . When Sam was slinging it, the Seahawks were the best play-action passing team in the NFL. Put him in a spot without the play-action and things get a whole lot worse. At the time of last year’s article, Darnold was 23rd in EPA/dropback on non-PA throws, with most of his interceptions coming in those scenarios. Seattle scored a lot of points by living off short fields. The Seahawks still scored at a healthy clip in part because they were getting defensive and special teams touchdowns, as well as really short fields that the offense couldn’t screw up. They led the NFL in touchdown drives starting at midfield or better from Week 12 onward. From Weeks 1-11, the Seahawks scored touchdowns on about 25% of their drives when starting inside their own 30. They scored touchdowns about 10% of the time from Week 11 onward, which ranked 28th. The running game showed signs of improvement . The rushing EPA was markedly better while the success rate was only moderately better. Seattle’s passing game dropped considerably but the rushing attack found some juice as the season progressed. A great sign for how they ended up performing in the Super Bowl. My buddy Griff (cmikesspinmove on Twitter and BlueSky, one half of the Seattle Overload podcast ), provided some more perspective on how flat the passing offense in particular was after Darnold’s torrid start. Can't let Kubiak off the hook (or Sam if that's how you want to look at it) SB run made it easy to gloss over that the pass EPA from weeks 11-18 2025 was 23rd. That Kubiak offense fell off hard. https://t.co/rN26dQTffM — under zone x (@cmikesspinmove) October 16, 2026 Things have only gotten worse for the Seahawks in 2026 The Seahawks offense is not good at virtually anything right now even though Jaxon Smith-Njigba is having a dominant season . They rank 25th in EPA/play, 18th in EPA/pass (almost certainly propped up by Drew Lock’s showing against the Arizona Cardinals), 31st in EPA/rush, 9th in sack rate, 16th in net yards/attempt, 28th in third-down conversion rate, 18th in red zone touchdown rate, and 16th in yards per play. Sam Darnold is playing like a bad quarterback in play-action or dropback . Darnold is 24th in EPA/play on play-action passes, heavily hampered by his three interceptions and no touchdown passes, and 25th in EPA/dropback on non-PA throws, right behind Bo Nix. So nothing is working for Darnold and his turnovers are absolute game-sinkers. Defenses are stacking the box even less than last year and Seattle can’t take advantage. While fully acknowledging the Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet injuries, Seattle cannot run the ball explosively. The stacked box rate is 23.6%, 15th in the NFL and nine percentage points lower than 2025. The Seahawks rank 25th in EPA/rush against light boxes, and their yards after contact against light boxes is 19th after being 11th in 2025. Over the past two games, the Seahawks faced stack boxes at a 15% clip, and the Seahawks running backs put up zero explosive runs against the San Francisco 49ers and three against the Broncos. Yes, Sam Darnold is still getting blitzed a lot , and he’s the literal worst QB when pressured . Darnold has been blitzed on almost 37% of his dropbacks, fifth-highest rate in the NFL. Last year is was 34.8%, so it was already high and now it’s even higher. When he’s pressured, he is essentially a non-functioning quarterback. This is his EPA/dropback. Dead last. Keep in mind that Darnold was 30th in this same stat last year, so this is a two-year trend of the same problem. When he’s under duress he is at his worst, and the offensive scheme and pass protection only exacerbates his chronic weakness. The Seahawks still cannot consistently score touchdowns without reasonably good field position . Seattle has now had 40 drives at or inside of its own 30-yard line this season. Only five of those have turned into touchdowns, which ranks 26th (via Stathead ). Their touchdown drives during this ugly three-game stretch have traveled 23, 65, 20, 68, 24, 23, and 67 yards. They’re average TD drive length from Week 4 onward is 41 yards. When Drew Lock started against the Cardinals, they did have 86-, 80-, and 70-yard touchdown drives, while Darnold had 90- and 80-yard TD possessions against the Washington Commanders. That’s it. But the pattern from late last year has bled into this year: Seattle’s offense is stuck when it isn’t starting possessions effectively a couple of first downs away from field goal range. You cannot live like that. The running game is horrendous . I’ve already given some stats earlier in this section, but when Kenneth Walker III and Zach Charbonnet (up until his injury) caught fire it saved the offense. That’s not happening with Emanuel Wilson and George Holani. So if the passing game structure is broken and there is no running game as a fallback option, you are screwed. We have to be honest with how much Klint Kubiak protected this offensive line . Hawkblogger had this great question and stat about Seattle’s max protect usage. Last year they were first, this year (prior to last night) they were 27th. That means a lot more responsibility belonging to the offensive line than previously…
author: Mookie Alexander

title: Seahawks make unwanted NFL history in loss vs. Broncos
summary: While it was the defense that kept the Seattle Seahawks within striking distance right until the end in their devastating 17-14 overtime loss to the Denver Broncos on Thursday night, it was ultimately Sam Darnold and the offense’s inability to string together scoring drives that helped their former AFC West rival make history. With just […]
full_text: While it was the defense that kept the Seattle Seahawks within striking distance right until the end in their devastating 17-14 overtime loss to the Denver Broncos on Thursday night, it was ultimately Sam Darnold and the offense’s inability to string together scoring drives that helped their former AFC West rival make history. With just 168 yards of offense, the Broncos now hold the record for the lowest yardage total in an overtime win in NFL history, breaking a record that stood for 22 years. Or, put another way, the Seahawks hold the record for fewest yards allowed in an overtime loss in NFL history . They surpassed the 2004 Chicago Bears who defeated the Tennessee Titans 19-17 in Week 9 with 176 yards. The Broncos' 168 total yards of offense is the lowest yardage total in an overtime victory in NFL history pic.twitter.com/f14gCsv3Sh — Benjamin Solak (@BenjaminSolak) October 16, 2026 It’s the second notable overtime win from a struggling offense this season, joining the Green Bay Packers Week 2 comeback win over the New York Jets, where they strung together just 199 total yards (5th lowest all time). Albeit, the game was played in rain and windy conditions, which likely contributed to the low scoring outcome. However, it wasn’t the weather that put Denver in a position to beat the defending Super Bowl champions, but rather a dominant performance from the defense, who racked up five sacks, two interceptions and two forced fumbles—one of which they recovered. Offensively, quarterback Bo Nix averaged an unfathomable 0.6 air yards per completion. Seattle struck first with a field goal at 8:29 in the opening frame, but after back-to-back second quarter touchdowns from running backs J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey put the Broncos up 14-3, their defense was able to hold it down. Wide receiver Rashid Shaheed fumbled on the ensuing drive, which resulted in a turnover and although Seattle’s defense forced a punt to give Darnold and company one more chance to put points up before halftime, nothing came of it. However, the Seahawks defense turned a corner in the second half. They forced punts on all Denver’s possessions but the offensive inconsistency continued, with a missed 47-yard field goal from kicker Jason Myers to open the third quarter followed by two consecutive punts. As a result, Nix and the Broncos remained in a position to control the clock and ultimately, they did. Even though they generated just two trips to the red zone all night, Sam Darnold’s costly interception in overtime set up Will Lutz’s game-winning field goal. The saying is defense wins championships and if last night was any indication, it sure does.
author: Michael Hapanovich

title: Seahawks injury update: Anthony Bradford could return vs. Chiefs
summary: The Seattle Seahawks offense is broken. While the disaster on Thursday night wasn’t all on the team’s offensive line, the Seahawks front certainly didn’t do their quarterback, Sam Darnold, any favors. Well, have no fear, Seahawks fans! Because help is on the way. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said that starting right guard Anthony Bradford […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks offense is broken. While the disaster on Thursday night wasn’t all on the team’s offensive line, the Seahawks front certainly didn’t do their quarterback, Sam Darnold, any favors. Well, have no fear, Seahawks fans! Because help is on the way. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said that starting right guard Anthony Bradford has a very good chance to return next Sunday in the team’s showdown with the Kansas City Chiefs. Bradford has been on injured reserve since Week 2 with hip and knee injuries. The three-year starter played against the New England Patriots and sat out of Seattle’s win over the Arizona Cardinals before being placed on IR. Mike Macdonald said there’s a very good chance injured RG Anthony Bradford will return next Sunday against the Kansas City Chiefs — Andrew Destin (@AndrewDestin1) October 16, 2026 A rotation of Christian Haynes and rookie Beau Stephens has replaced Bradford, with both guards being a mixed bag through four weeks. The Seahawks offensive line has struggled significantly in 2026, and Bradford’s return could be a boost, especially for right tackle Abraham Lucas. While Bradford has been much maligned by Seahawks fans during his tenure, he served as a key piece for Seattle down the stretch last season. The return comes at a time when the Seahawks are desperate for answers on offense as they fell to 3-3 in the midst of their toughest stretch of the season. Thanks to the Thursday night game, the Seahawks will have nine days before needing to make a decision on Bradford before they host the Chiefs on Sunday Night Football on Oct. 25 at 5:20 p.m.
author: Jack Freeman

title: Snap Reactions: Seahawks inconsistent offense dominates stat sheet, loses another game
summary: After hoisting the Lombardi Trophy in February and bringing back 20 of 22 starters, fans and analysts had high expectations for the Seattle Seahawks heading into the 2026 season. So far, those expectations are not being met, and following a disappointing 17-14 overtime loss to the Denver Broncos on Thursday Night Football, the Seahawks will […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - OCTOBER 15: Rashid Shaheed #22 of the Seattle Seahawks catches a two point conversion against the Denver Broncos during the fourth quarter of the game at Empower Field At Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images After hoisting the Lombardi Trophy in February and bringing back 20 of 22 starters, fans and analysts had high expectations for the Seattle Seahawks heading into the 2026 season. So far, those expectations are not being met, and following a disappointing 17-14 overtime loss to the Denver Broncos on Thursday Night Football , the Seahawks will have nine days to prepare for Week 7 when they will face one of three teams in the league that is currently undefeated in the Kansas City Chiefs. The first topic of note when it comes to snap counts on the offensive side of the ball is the rotation between Christian Haynes and Beau Stephens swung heavily in Haynes’ favor against the Broncos. After Haynes playing time had slowly decreased each week, he played more than double the snaps of Stephens in the loss to Denver. Of course, neither Haynes (5 pressures allowed) nor Stephens (3 pressures allowed) excelled in the loss to the Broncos, and whether it’s missed assignments due to playing in a new system or miscommunications from lineup changes, the line is not performing at the level it did in 2025. At receiver Rashid Shaheed saw the lowest percentage of offensive snaps of the season at 45.9% of snaps, while simultaneously tying his season high in snaps played at 39 simply due to the fact that the Seattle offense was on the field for a whopping 85 snaps. On the positive side, Shaheed and Sam Darnold finally teamed up for a couple of deep connections, though the refs overturned 32-yard completion and Shaheed was injured pulling in a 42-yard pass shortly after halftime. Following the injury, second year receiver Tory Horton took many of Shaheed’s snaps on both offense and special teams. Horton had a nice 13 yard return on a punt, and pulled in a 13 yard pass on 3rd & 8, but Darnold was off target on several other pass attempts that headed in Horton’s direction, including one pass that was batted down at the line, one that was off target and uncatchable and the very poorly thrown interception that Kirk Herbstreit somehow decided was all Horton’s fault. It’s true that Horton may have been in better position to catch the pass or even break the pass up with a flatter route or had he come back to the ball, but Darnold underthrew the ball on a pass delivered late and that’s where the finger should be pointed. At tight end, Elijah Arroyo’s night ended early due to a shoulder injury on just his fifth offensive snap, with Nick Kallerup getting Arroyo’s snaps the rest of the night. When Denver had the ball, the defense got pushed around some during the first half as Denver put 14 points on the board. Tyrice Knight played in place of the injured Drake Thomas, and while that may have played a role in the Broncos putting points on the board in the first half, the Seattle defense had Bo Nix and company on lockdown after halftime. Meanwhile, veteran offseason additions Trevon Diggs and Dante Fowler combined for just nine snaps, while the return to health of the starters in the secondary kept Nehemiah Pritchett on the sideline for all but nine defensive snaps. Just as every week, Brady Russell led the way on special teams with 24 snaps, while Patrick O’Connell and Jimmy Ciarlo were right behind at 21 snaps apiece. Eric Saubert played 20 special teams snaps, with Mike Morris and Rodney Thomas at 19 to round out the top six. Also noteworthy is that Irv Charles saw his first game action for the Seahawks after coming over from the New York Jets in an offseason trade, playing on the return and coverage units on both punts and kickoffs. And now it’s on to the mini bye before hosting the AFC West leading Kansas City Chiefs in Week 6.
author: John Gilbert

title: Seahawks-Broncos post-game analysis: Give it away, give it away, give it away now
summary: There was an extended moment on Thursday Night Football when the Seattle Seahawks looked like the defending Super Bowl champs. A good, healthy fourth quarter of game clock. Plus the first 2:49 of overtime. Outside of that? Not so much. I’m not ready to write this team’s obituary yet. But the formula they’ve followed in […]
full_text: There was an extended moment on Thursday Night Football when the Seattle Seahawks looked like the defending Super Bowl champs. A good, healthy fourth quarter of game clock. Plus the first 2:49 of overtime. Outside of that? Not so much. I’m not ready to write this team’s obituary yet. But the formula they’ve followed in 2026 is one for defeat, not victory. It’s the formula of an incomplete team, with some shiny pieces such as the best offensive player alive and two of most exciting young defenders in the league. Led by a defensive genius. However. Lose the turnover battle, give away points and possessions, count on your superhuman defense to cover for all your mistakes: this is the very model of a modern losing football team. It’s psychically hard to believe the team on the left lost this game. Those are numbers for a three-score romp, not an overtime heartbreaker. Unless you know the whole story. Giveaways included. Then it all makes sense. Lose the turnover battle by three and all your pretty stats are fool’s gold. And still, for literally the majority of the game, the Seahawks defense was nigh impenetrable and put the offense in position to go get the game. You can’t stop an NFL offense better than this. A) Give up 14 points in the second quarter, no other quarters; B) Then hold them to 24 total yards the rest of regulation, ending their drives thusly: Punt End of Half Punt Punt Punt Punt Punt Punt End of Half Through all this, the Seahawks defense is playing like a 6-0 team intent on repeating. The offense is playing like an 0-6 team intent on repeating the same mistakes week after week. It would all be quite a bit more tedious had they not just won a title in the calendar year we currently inhabit. (Although one could say, the offense’s Keystone Cops routine is even more tedious because they’re smack dab in the middle of a championship window and you don’t get those every decade. Wait. The Seahawks do get those. Nevertheless!) Focus, John. Be a JSN, not a running back. Clarifying, this third loss is on the offense entirely, although special teams made a special appearance. For all the coolness that Rashid Shaheed’s final punt return exuded, the game landed in OT in large part because Jason Myers doinked a 47-yarder. Then, in the extra period, the Broncos might not have been in field goal range to begin with without a mishandled kickoff and holding flag on the return. The sobbest part of the Seahawks’ sob story, besides its repetitiveness, is it wouldn’t take a completely clean game from Seattle to flip these losses into victories. Pick six in Washington was the margin of defeat. End zone fumble against the 49ers, same. Then two scoring chances were snuffed out with late interceptions in Denver. Seattle’s opponents know they can sit back, be patient, take zero risks and wait for party favors. That’s their best hope, and it works half the time. So when Darnold gift wrapped the victory for Denver by putting extra air under this pass — — it was another reminder that football is about all three phases. I joined the game in progress so we’ll save some Predators and Prey for the second half. Quick recap anyone, so we can forgive* and forget? *your forgiveness may vary Q1: Seahawks 3, Broncos 0 The score’s a bit deceptive, what with Denver ending the first quarter in the middle of a 16-play, 74-yard drive. It’s technically accurate though. Seattle punted, then pinned the hosts deep in their own end, turned the stop into favorable field position, earned exactly one first down, and sent Jason Myers out for a successful 55-yarder. 3-0 and everything looked very defensive-minded. As viewers expected from the first-and third-best scoring defenses from last year. The play of the game, until Sam’s overtime boo-boo, comes from an offense, however, and Denver’s at that, on fourth down from the Seattle 45. The Broncos have three yards to gain in that very particular part of the field where kicking makes little sense and the math says go for it. The interior linemen form a phalanx focused on Byron Murphy, who is pushed back, creating oodles of space for Tyler Badie to roam. He easily converts. A drive that would’ve been scoreless ends in seven points. These are the moments few will mention after another giveaway-infested performance by the offense. But Sean Payton took a chance and it paid off. Q2: Broncos 14, Seahawks 3 The Broncos would finish that drive in the end zone, force a punt, and march right back down again with the aid of a soft facemask call on third down (second drive extended past its expiration date), Denver’s longest run of the day (16 for J.K. Dobbins), questionable DPI in the end zone on Devon Witherspoon, and a gimmicky Wildcat touchdown. Denver was turning one positive play into seven points each time. But here’s the thing. They would net all of 24 yards between their second score and the end of regulation. In one half of football, 24 yards. They ran into the brickest of walls, the Seahawks defense made dang sure. All the Seattle offense had to do was slam the door shut with three scoring drives or so, and not give the Broncos any extra chances. Well. Instead, Rashid Shaheed fumbled, the Broncos defense stymied Jaxon Smith-Njigba long enough to keep points off the board, Shaheed came thiiiiiiiiiiiis close to hauling in a field-flipper, and the half ended 14-3. Q3: Broncos 14, Seahawks 3 (still) Predator: Nick Bonitto and friends Prey: Seattle pass protectors How: In the third quarter and the start of the fourth, not one, not two but three third-down sacks ended dangerous Seahawks drives. Sack 1 forced the key Myers miss, Sack 2 came at midfield, and Sack 3 took Seattle out of field goal range altogether. It was a poor night for the OL in pass pro, as we will cover later. Action : There was a lot of defense played in the third. Seattle’s deep passing game finally saw a sliver of daylight with a huge Shaheed 42-yarder. Only a sliver: that reception represented half the yardage gained in the period by both teams combined . And the only play over 20 yards to that point. Q4: Broncos 14, Seahawks 14 Predator: I got two for you on an otherwise bleak night. It’s gotta be JSN with that magnificent 6-83 line in the fourth quarter alone, including a fourth down conversion where he got blasted and the final seven-yarder to simplify Myers’ final kick. It’s also gotta be George Holani, who has not been the recipient of much respect in this space. He earned it on the Seahawks’ lone touchdown drive. Prey: JSN does not concern himself with the opinions or identity of the prey. Holani bounced off five dudes. When the Seahawks are making these plays on offense instead of coughing it up, they’re unbeatable. Much to ponder. How: These are real carries. By real men. Back to back plays even. Action: Holani’s exploits — and first score of the year! — were sandwiched between two three-and-outs from the otherworldly defense we are privileged to follow. Shaheed provided the cherry on top, a two-point feat (feet?) of concentration that helped make up for his earlier fumble. It almost did matter, too. So when Darnold threw his first interception of the night, inside the two-minute warning, Mike Macdonald’s non-Carrollian preservation of timeouts suddenly mattered. The defense stuffed two runs, Bo Nix threw right at Uchenna Nwosu on third down, allowing the Seahawks to field a punt with over a minute remaining, which Shaheed clutchily and casually brought back to the 46. And that’s when the actual value of Darnold materialized. I suspect there are some criticisms of the Seattle QB out there in the ether today, and he makes it easy on his detractors. He tried to lose the game once, he did lose it the second time, he’s been overall mediocre since his return, but in between the lowlights he showed us why you CAN win it all with him at the helm. Even if it never happens again, they did it once and could return to the same glory with this guy. Exhibit one: Darnold absorbed…
author: John Fraley

title: Seahawks Droppings: Seattle fights back vs. Broncos just to give the game away… again
summary: Seattle’s defense kept them in the game, but the offense turned the ball over too much and had untimely penalties in a 17-14 overtime loss to the Denver Broncos.  I missed my Milwaukee Brewers punching their ticket to just the second World Series in team history for that garbage? At this point, I could probably […]
full_text: Seattle’s defense kept them in the game, but the offense turned the ball over too much and had untimely penalties in a 17-14 overtime loss to the Denver Broncos. I missed my Milwaukee Brewers punching their ticket to just the second World Series in team history for that garbage? At this point, I could probably just copy and paste the same recap article every week. The Seahawks offense didn’t show up until the fourth quarter, finally finding the end zone with about five minutes left in the game. Seattle’s defense got them the ball back shortly and the Seahawks went back to work, getting near FG position. Then, Sam Darnold tried to end the game with an interception. The Seahawks defense, however, forced another three-and-out to allow their offense one more shot to tie the game, which they did, sending the game to overtime. In the extra frame Darnold succeeded in essentially ending the game, throwing another pick. The defense did their best, but Denver was already basically in scoring range and ended it with a long FG to send the Seahawks to .500 at 3-3. Seattle already has as many losses as last season, and any hope of them rekindling their fire of last season is dwindling. They look like a broken team on offense. Seahawks Droppings Simply put, you can’t lose the turnover battle and expect to win. Seattle is proving that this season with three more of them today. All of their losses have boiled down to coughing the ball up too much. Except that stretch at the end of last season, the team has actually turned the ball over quite a bit under Mike Macdonald. At this point, I don’t know if it’s fixable. Start the Sam Darnold conversation . Look, I’m not trying to run the guy out of town, he won a Super Bowl for us after all. However, I also don’t want to commit long term to him. John Schneider might be feeling that way as well. There are a lot of cheaper QBs that could turn the ball over just as much. I don’t know if there’s a disconnect with Brian Fleury or if Darnold is just regressing. Either way, I don’t like it. Jason Myers missed another FG, and the Seahawks had to scramble to get the game to overtime. There needs to be a competition at kicker this offseason at the very least. Jaxon Smith-Njigba is the only thing keeping this offense alive. He’ll still get his targets and catches even though the other team is keying on him. Rashid Shaheed made a few plays for basically the first time all season. I still don’t know where the tight ends are, and why they’re not a bigger part of this offense. Seattle’s defense had a couple rough early drives that were once again extended by penalties . After that, they shut everything down, especially in the second half. Holding a team to 30 yards in a half is ridiculous production. The offensive woes might be spoiling an elite stretch of defense. For the second week in a row, the offensive line basically sucked. Darnold was under constant duress, and the run game was pretty much nonexistent again. All of the OL took turns being awful, spreading the terrible play around. Abe Lucas was beaten like a drum. Charles Cross was getting toasted. Grey Zabel was getting called for penalties. When they weren’t giving up sacks, the OL was letting the Broncos DL knock down passes at the line of scrimmage. How many of those did they have, like five?? I really hate what I’m seeing with the Seahawks right now. If the defense wasn’t playing out of their mind, Seattle might only have one win. Honestly, this doesn’t even look like a playoff team. The worst part is, the main issues of turnovers, penalties, and special teams gaffes have been consistent going all the way back to preseason ball. The fact that the coaching staff hasn’t been able to correct these mistakes makes me think we’ll have to face a whole season of backbreaking turnovers and/or penalties when the game is there for the taking. I just don’t have faith in them turning this around right now, and that sucks to write.
