title: Ranking all eight NFL divisions this season by strength: NFC North at No. 1?
summary: Why do we have the NFC North at No. 1 in our annual division power ranking -- even ahead of the mighty NFC West? And is the NFC South at the bottom of our list ... again?
full_text:
Every year around this time, we like to rank the NFL's divisions against each other. We have a tool that does that -- ESPN's Football Power Index -- but the powers that be also ask me to do it, which I take as license to disagree with FPI.

 One of my quiet personal obsessions is the idea that, at some point, a division will send all four of its teams to the playoffs in a given year. This has been possible only since 2020, when the NFL expanded the playoff field to seven teams from each conference, and we are 0-for-6. We've had divisions in which every team finished with a winning record -- most recently last season's NFC North. But it hasn't been enough to put all four teams in the postseason.

 So far in 2026, we have two divisions in which all four teams have winning records. And if the season ended right now -- after the  Seahawks lost to the Broncos  on Thursday night to kick off Week 6 -- all four of the teams in the NFC North would hold playoff spots. So there's hope, even though at this point the other one of those divisions (AFC North) would have just one playoff team.

 Because I'm mildly obsessed with this idea, I use it as a gauge for this exercise. It's not the only qualification, but I do tend to rate a division higher if it's close and I believe one has the better chance of pulling off the all-four. That's a bit of an explanation about the madness behind my method. Here are the rankings for you all to get upset about. Enjoy. (Note: FPI rankings are through Week 5.)

 

 
 Jump to a division ... 
AFC: East | West | North | South 
NFC: East | West | North | South 

 
 

 

 1. NFC North 
 Combined FPI rating: 6.0 (No. 2 of eight) 

 
 Detroit Lions : 2.1 (10th in the NFL) 
 Chicago Bears : 1.7 (12th) 
 Minnesota Vikings : 1.5 (13th) 
 Green Bay Packers : 0.7 (16th) 
 
 It was a tough call between this division and the NFC West, which has three teams in the FPI's top six while this one has only one in the top 10. But the premise here is that we want to know which division has the best chance of landing all four of its teams in the playoffs, and with apologies to the Cardinals, I believe that puts the NFC North up top. This division features three teams (Detroit, Chicago, Green Bay) with high-end offenses but shaky defenses and one team (Minnesota) with the best defense in the league but an offense that's still putting things together.

 

 At 5-0, the Vikings are still ranked 13th by FPI because of their 26th-ranked offense. But their defensive and special teams FPI both rank No. 1 overall, and if you look at the injury issues they've had on offense, it's not difficult to imagine that unit improving. The Packers are 10th in offensive FPI despite massive offensive line issues and a complete lack of a run game. Those issues feel less likely to improve than Minnesota's weaknesses, but it's not out of the question. And the eventual return of edge rusher  Micah Parsons should boost Green Bay's 19th-ranked defense.

 Chicago ranks 12th in FPI offense and defense, and it could get quarterback Caleb Williams back from injury in Week 6. Detroit is fourth in offensive FPI and 30th in defensive, and the Lions' playoff hopes rest on their ability to outscore the teams on their fourth-place schedule. I like their chances.

 

 
 

 2. NFC West 
 Combined FPI rating: 8.8 (No. 1 of eight) 

 
 San Francisco 49ers : 6.7 (first in the NFL) 
 Los Angeles Rams : 4.5 (third) 
 Seattle Seahawks : 3.5 (sixth) 
 Arizona Cardinals : minus-5.9 (30th) 
 
 Like everyone else who has assumed since the Myles Garrett trade that the Rams are an unstoppable force, FPI continues to leave me alone on the "Shouldn't we wait to see it first?" island. There is no way anyone who has watched them play this season truly believes the 2-3 Rams are the third-best team in the NFL. Yet there they sit by being fifth in offensive FPI, sixth in defensive FPI and, of course, that pesky 32nd in special teams. With nearly 30% of the season complete, they've allowed more points than they've scored. They've lost to all three teams they've played that have a winning record, and if not for the Eagles gifting them a  Week 4 win , they'd be 1-4. I'm willing to believe the Rams have what it takes to be one of the best teams in the NFL, but right now they are absolutely not.

 

 Meanwhile, the 49ers look elite despite being riddled with injuries. They're 5-0, second in offensive FPI and 10th in defensive FPI. They beat the Rams handily in the season opener and just won a knock-down, drag-out game against the Super Bowl champion Seahawks . Seattle (now 3-3) went into Thursday night's game ranked second in FPI defense and special teams -- but a troubling 14th in offense. If the Seahawks want a shot at repeating, they need to get the run game figured out the way they did as last season went along.

 The Cardinals rank 23rd in FPI's offensive rankings, dead last in defense and 29th in special teams. They are the main reason this division can't dream of putting all four teams in the playoffs, but again, the Rams have yet to show us anything this season that should make us think this division could get three.

 

 
 

 3. AFC North 
 Combined FPI rating: minus-2.5 (No. 5 of eight) 

 
 Cincinnati Bengals : 2.4 (eighth in the NFL) 
 Baltimore Ravens : 0.9 (15th) 
 Pittsburgh Steelers : minus-1.1 (19th) 
 Cleveland Browns : minus-4.7 (27th) 
 
 This is one of two divisions, along with the NFC North, in which all four teams have winning records. FPI doesn't particularly love any of them. It has Cincinnati's offense ranked sixth, Baltimore's offense 11th (though  Lamar Jackson 's absence is woven in there), Pittsburgh's offense 19th and Cleveland's offense 31st. Defensively, FPI ranks the Ravens 14th, Steelers 15th, Browns 16th and Bengals 18th, which is about as mediocre and closely bunched as you can get.

 Cincinnati's offensive ranking, combined with FPI's assessment of the 3-2 Bengals' remaining schedule as the easiest in the league, offers hope for Joe Burrow 's return to the postseason. Baltimore has the 4-1 first-place record and has yet to play a division game, so opportunity is there for the Ravens to take control. Jackson's left ankle injury  isn't believed to be long term, and they just beat the Falcons with Tyler Huntley anyway.

 FPI (and history) identify the Browns as the weak link here. They've been outscored by an average of 3.8 points per game but still have a 3-2 record. That's a testament to the job first-year coach Todd Monken is doing, but it certainly offers license to wonder how sustainable it is over the rest of the season. And the Steelers? Well, quarterback  Aaron Rodgers is flinging it, running back  Jaylen Warren is on a hot streak, and the defense looks better than it did last season. They also have the head-to-head win over the Bengals in their pockets (though they also lost to the Browns ). The Steelers are hard to figure, but they're even harder to count out.

 This division always feels like it has a chance to put at least three teams in the playoffs each season, and if the Browns keep overachieving, the North could make history.

 

 

 
 

 4. AFC West 
 Combined FPI rating: 1.8 (No. 3 of eight) 

 
 Kansas City Chiefs : 4.3 (fourth in the NFL) 
 Denver Broncos : 1.5 (14th) 
 Los Angeles Chargers : minus-1.3 (20th) 
 Las Vegas Raiders : minus-2.7 (22nd) 
 
 The Chiefs are back! FPI has them seventh in offense and eighth in defense after their bye week. And Patrick Mahomes  seems to be feeling all the way recovered from last season's major knee injury . After reaching the AFC Championship Game seven years in a row and winning three Super Bowls along the way, the Chiefs watched as two other AFC West teams made the playoffs last season. But they look like a good bet to resume their postseason streak at 4-0.

 Last year's No. 1 seed in the AFC, the Broncos, are 4-2. FPI has them ranked third in defense but 17th in offense. Early-season regression from quarterback Bo Nix…

title: NFL Week 6 preview: Picks, predictions, schedule, betting odds, fantasy tips
summary: Patrick Mahomes vs. Justin Herbert? C.J. Stroud vs. Trevor Lawrence? There are 13 more games in Week 6, and we have picks, predictions and more for all of them.
full_text:
Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season is here. Will the Chiefs stay unbeaten -- or can the Chargers  finally get their first win? Could the Raiders get back on track against the feisty Bills? Which teams will come out on top in divisional showdowns, including Texans-Jaguars and Ravens-Browns? And what should we expect on Sunday night in Cowboys-Packers?

 We're here to get you ready for the action. First, our NFL Nation reporters take you inside the locker room with the best thing they heard this week, and ESPN Research provides a key stat to know. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder makes a bold prediction for each matchup, fantasy analyst Eric Moody shares fantasy football intel, and betting analyst Pamela Maldonado gives her  insights  for each contest. We also have Football Power Index (FPI) game projections, and Maldonado, Moody and Walder all give us final score picks for every game.

 Let's get into the full Week 6 slate, which culminates with the "Monday Night Football" matchup between the Commanders and 49ers on ESPN . (Game times are Sunday unless otherwise noted, and all odds are via DraftKings.)

 What we're hearing on the Texans: New WR  Marvin Harrison Jr . is playing , according to coach DeMeco Ryans. Harrison and QB  C.J. Stroud  will have an opportunity to re-create their fireworks from their college stint at Ohio State in 2021-22. Don't expect Harrison to play most of the offensive snaps, but there will be packages for him. -- DJ Bien-Aime 

 What we're hearing on the Jaguars: QB  Trevor Lawrence 's history against the Texans isn't great. They're the only division team against which he has thrown more interceptions (11) than touchdown passes (eight) and has a completion percentage below 60% (57.8%). One reason to be optimistic for Sunday is that Lawrence leads the NFL in off-target percentage at 8.8%, meaning he's rarely making bad passes or throws that should be intercepted. His previous best off-target percentage was 15% last season, when he had the best season of his career. -- Michael DiRocco 

 Stat to know: The Jaguars have given up 608 passing yards on throws of 15-plus yards downfield this season, second most in the NFL behind the Lions (633). Stroud is one of two QBs to attempt a pass of 15-plus yards downfield at least 45 times in 2026. -- ESPN Research 

 

 Bold prediction: Texans CB  Kamari Lassiter will record an interception. This is blind faith in a good player who has struggled mightily. But I think he turns it around and, as a result, leads Houston to an upset win. -- Walder 

 Injuries: Texans | Jaguars 

 Fantasy nugget: Stroud is a viable streaming option with four teams on a bye. The Jaguars have been tough on QBs, giving up only 14.0 fantasy points per game. But Stroud has scored at least 20 fantasy points in back-to-back games and averaged 19.9 fantasy points in five career games against Jacksonville. WR  Nico Collins remains his top target, and Stroud now has another familiar playmaker in Harrison. See Week 6 rankings . -- Moody 

 Betting insight: Since 2018, the under is 8-2 when the Jaguars play in London. Jacksonville's defense gives up only 2.9 yards per carry, giving Houston's struggling run game little room to improve. That forces Stroud to carry the offense behind protection that has given up 14 sacks. Meanwhile, Houston's 18 sacks and Jacksonville's injury at left tackle ( Anton Harrison ) could keep the Jaguars from efficient drives. Read more . -- Maldonado 

 Maldonado's pick: Texans 20, Jaguars 19 
 Moody's pick: Jaguars 24, Texans 20 
 Walder's pick: Texans 23, Jaguars 21 
 FPI prediction: JAX, 58.4% (by an average of 2.2 points)

 

 Matchup must-reads: WR Harrison will play for Texans on Sunday, coach says ... Jaguars WR Washington has the clutch gene  ... Harrison latest in Texans' quest to solve WR2 conundrum ... Jaguars' Coen to tweak playcalling after delay of game issues 

 
 

 Bears (3-2) at Falcons (2-3) 
 1 p.m. ET | Fox | CHI -1.5 (51.5 O/U) 

 What we're hearing on the Bears: QB Caleb Williams ' potential return from a hamstring injury would come with an injection of explosiveness and playmaking the Bears' offense has been lacking since Week 3. "He has tremendous talent, arm ability with his legs as well," WR Rome Odunze said. "So obviously, when you're missing a player like that on the field, you feel it." Chicago could benefit in a lot of areas from Williams' return, namely with his deep ball (12 passing touchdowns of 20-plus air yards, the most in the NFL since the start of 2025) and his play under duress. Including last season, Williams threw nine touchdowns to one interception when pressured. -- Courtney Cronin 

 What we're hearing on the Falcons: QB Michael Penix Jr . has the fourth-worst EPA per dropback (minus-0.7) in the league when pressured among QBs with at least 20 dropbacks. But with no pressure, Penix is fifth best in EPA per dropback (0.58). The Bears have generated only 52 pressures, the fifth-lowest total in the NFL despite blitzing at the seventh-highest rate (39.3%). -- Marc Raimondi 

 Stat to know:  Though the Bears (173.2) and Falcons (166.8) are the top two teams in average rushing yards per game, both teams also have stout run defenses. Atlanta ranks fourth in rushing yards allowed per game (80.2); Chicago ranks ninth (96.0). -- ESPN Research

title: Ravens believe Browns' Todd Monken wants 'to kick our tail'
summary: When Cleveland's coach takes the sideline Sunday, Baltimore players will face off against their fiery former OC.
full_text:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- Many in the Baltimore Ravens ' locker room believe Cleveland Browns coach Todd Monken is not being entirely truthful about Sunday's reunion.

 Monken, who was Baltimore's offensive coordinator the previous three seasons, insisted this week that there are no added emotions in facing his former team. But the Ravens feel they know exactly what this game means to the usually fiery Monken.

 "If I know Todd the way I think I know Todd, he will want to kick our tail," Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey said.

 Despite great success in 2023 and 2024, Monken exited Baltimore nine months ago amid conflicting reports about his relationship with players, especially with quarterback Lamar Jackson , who isn't expected to play Sunday because of an ankle injury. During the 2025 season, when the offense dropped to the middle of the NFL, there were anonymous sources who voiced the players' discontent with Monken's playcalling.

 

 In the offseason, Monken stressed there were no issues between him and Jackson. After Monken was hired by the Browns in January, he received congratulatory texts from Ravens players, including Jackson.

 Now, after leading the Browns (3-2) to their best start in five years, Monken is facing the Ravens (4-1) in an early-season battle for first place in the AFC North ( 1 p.m. ET, CBS ).

 "He might not say it in the media, but to the team he definitely talks a lot of trash and lets them know [that] he wants to beat us," Ravens running back Derrick Henry said.

 During his time in Baltimore, Monken elevated the Ravens' offense to new heights. In 2023, he helped Jackson to his second NFL Most Valuable Player award. The next season, Monken led the Ravens' offense to its first No. 1 ranking in the NFL.

 But in 2025, the Ravens unraveled in a disappointing 8-9 season. With Jackson struggling with injuries, Baltimore finished with 311.8 yards per game, which was its fewest in eight years.

 Ravens wide receiver Rashod Bateman said he felt Monken left on good terms, pointing out the impressive production and records set under him.

 "When you are a player, you have to make the choice whether you want to make this game about Todd Monken or do you want to make it about going to play football," Bateman said. "I am pretty sure Todd Monken is not worried about Rashod Bateman or what he has done in Baltimore. He is worried about getting the Cleveland Browns right to beat us. So, I think for both sides, the respect is mutual."

 Monken feels grateful for how the Ravens handled his final month with the team, and the Ravens can be thankful to Monken for how he helped them land his successor with an influential phone call to Declan Doyle.  

 In January, Monken was allowed to work at the Ravens' facility after John Harbaugh was fired as head coach. He had his initial virtual meeting with the Browns while sitting in his Ravens office.

 

 "I don't think it was awkward for them," Monken said of the Ravens. "We'd been around it for three years. I mean, there's a lot of appreciation of me for the people in the building, and I would think there's appreciation for the job that I did every day there."

 When the Ravens showed interest in Declan Doyle to become their next offensive coordinator, one of the calls that Doyle made was to Monken. They knew each other because Monken was a graduate assistant at Notre Dame with Doyle's father, Chris.

 Monken's advice to Doyle: Take the Ravens' offensive coordinator job, because the players are there to win.

 "He certainly had a big influence," Doyle said. "If he had said, 'Hey, don't touch that place,' I would have placed a lot of value in that. But that was not the case."

 Monken knows a lot of the strengths and weaknesses of Baltimore's offensive players. The Ravens are familiar with Monken's schemes and tendencies.

 Ravens coach Jesse Minter doesn't think either side has an advantage, saying the situation is "overblown."

 "There are so many of those things where it's like, 'Well, they know that we know that they know,'" Minter said. "[I] don't put a lot of stock into it."

 Likewise, Monken wants to make sure the focus is on the teams and not him.

 "Ultimately, I have a job to do," Monken said. "And the job is, what can I do today to help our team get better and keep taking strides to play winning football. And that's really all I think about."

full_text:
Throwback Thursday is coming to the NFL in Week 6 with a matchup for nostalgic eyes on "Thursday Night Football." The Denver Broncos and Seattle Seahawks will each wear their throwback uniforms in the game.

 

 Denver's look is a callback to the 1977 uniforms that honor the "Orange Crush" era. The orange jerseys include oversized white numbers in legacy blue trim, while white pants and legacy blue helmet complete the look. Featured on the lid is the iconic hissing Bronco and "D" on the side. The Broncos boast a 5-0 record since debuting the combination in the 2024 campaign.

 Seattle is throwing it back to the 1990s with its royal blue jerseys, and matching silver helmet and pants. Running on the uniform's sleeve is a classic Seahawks logo on top of green and blue stripes. Neatly, the old Kingdome appears on the inside collar. The matte silver helmet is similar to what the franchise wore in its early history. The Seahawks have a 4-3 record in the throwbacks since debuting them in 2023. 

 The alternate uniform space is well represented, too, as the New Orleans Saints are wearing their all-white color rush uniforms with a white helmet against the New York Giants . New Orleans unveiled the white lids in 2025 with a new tri-color stripe down the center and a black face mask for the first time in franchise history. A mini fleur-de-lis is subtly included on the tri-color stripe.

summary: The quarterback said there are several hurdles to clear before he would be able to face the Falcons on Sunday.
full_text:
LAKE FOREST, Ill. -- Quarterback  Caleb Williams was officially listed as questionable on the Chicago Bears ' final injury report ahead of their Week 6 game at the  Atlanta Falcons  ( Sunday, 1 p.m. ET, Fox ).

 Williams was a full participant during the Bears' Wednesday walk-through and practice sessions Thursday and Friday. The quarterback said he had to go through "a bunch of medical protocols" before being cleared by team trainers, which could happen before the team leaves for Atlanta.

 "I'm hopeful we'll have more clarity at the end of the day today," Bears coach Ben Johnson said Friday. "He looked good [Thursday] for one practice, but we've got to be able to stack a few back-to-back. He got some good work in on Wednesday, even though we walked through, he went through his own throwing session beforehand. Part of the plan, and he's on track right now."

 Williams missed three straight games while recovering from a hamstring injury sustained during the fourth quarter of a Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings . On Thursday, he took issue with the reporting around his injury , for which he claimed that "nothing that has come out that has been right about what it is and what it has been."

 

 Johnson did not sense that his quarterback was frustrated with anything other than not being able to play.

 "I, honestly, I didn't feel any frustration from him," Johnson said. "He was in this little bit of a no-man's land, 'Hey, what do I what do with myself? I've never been in this situation. I've never been in the training room this much. I've never been second or third fiddle in the quarterback room ever in my life.' Just like, 'I just need a little guidance on how I can best help and serve.'

 "He's a captain, he wants to do that desperately. 'How can I help us win in this different setting?' I don't know that I felt frustration, other than an eagerness to get back out there and help the guys on the field."

 While Williams' status is questionable, the Bears will be without running back Kyle Monangai for a second straight game. Monangai did not practice this week while recovering from thumb and toe injuries, the latter of which he visited a specialist for last week.

 "It wasn't one of those things we felt like we needed to put him on IR for," Johnson said. "So, it's still week-to-week, and as far as I know he's trending in the right direction."

 Chicago will also be down three starters on defense, with defensive end  Montez Sweat 's two-game suspension for violating the PED policy and injuries that are sidelining linebacker T.J. Edwards (hamstring) and Dayo Odeyingbo (quad) in Week 6.

title: What Cowboys-Packers' Micah Parsons trade means a year later
summary: We examine the fallout and lingering impact on both franchises more than a year after the blockbuster deal.
full_text:
If Sunday's game between the Green Bay Packers and the Dallas Cowboys at Lambeau Field were a made-for-TV movie, it would open like this: The home team's starters would be introduced, and Micah Parsons would run out last to a raucous ovation while his former team stood and watched.

 Instead, Parsons will be without a uniform, will come out unannounced and his play will have zero impact on who wins the game. Nearly 14 months after Parsons was traded from the Cowboys to the Packers, and a little more than nine months removed from left ACL surgery, the All-Pro edge rusher has yet to be cleared to return from last year's season-ending injury.

 Given everything that has happened for the two teams since that Aug. 28, 2025, blockbuster deal , Parsons' presence still looms large over both franchises as they try to build championship contenders. Both teams are off to bumpy starts this season as Green Bay awaits Parsons' return to action and Dallas' defense continues to struggle.

 

 Parsons might still be the one player the Packers need to get back to a Super Bowl, but it didn't happen in Year 1. The Packers were 9-3-1 when Parsons blew out his knee at the Denver Broncos in Week 15, and they didn't win another game -- including an opening-round playoff loss. They're off to a 3-2 start this year while they wait for Parsons' return, which could still be weeks away .

 Meanwhile, the Cowboys had arguably the worst defense in the NFL last season, and at 2-3 this season, they're still trying to remake their defense into what owner and general manager Jerry Jones envisioned when he shipped Parsons to the Packers.

 Just like last season's 40-40 tie -- when Parsons had a sack and three tackles in his first matchup against the Cowboys -- Sunday's game ( 8:20 p.m. ET, NBC ) will not reveal a winner in the trade, but what does it mean for both franchises a year later?

 Cowboys quarterback  Dak Prescott said he will miss being able to play against his former teammate.

 "Wishing him all the best and getting healthy," Prescott said. "Caught up with him a lot this offseason and here in Dallas while he was rehabbing, so he knows I support him in that.

 "But at the end of the day, it's the Cowboys versus the Packers. It's not me versus Micah, or the Cowboys versus Micah. It's about us going in and getting to win."

 

 How the Parsons trade has affected the Cowboys 

 Since the trade, the Cowboys dealt for defensive tackle Quinnen Williams . After signing him to a three-year, $105 million extension in August, Jones said the Parsons trade could not have worked out better, but he stopped short of saying the Cowboys won the deal.

 In addition to defensive tackle Kenny Clark , the Cowboys received the Packers' first-round picks in 2026 and 2027.

 Last season, the Cowboys flipped the better of the 2027 first-rounders to the New York Jets for Williams and their 2026 second-round pick. With the No. 26 pick in this year's draft, the Cowboys added pass rusher Malachi Lawrence , who has only one sack, one tackle for loss and seven quarterback pressures but is expected to see more playing time Sunday.

 Jones went so far as to compare the Parsons trade to the 1989 trade of running back Herschel Walker to the Minnesota Vikings that helped the Cowboys win three Super Bowls in a four-year span in the 1990s.

 "You could say those picks got us key players, but the main thing that the Herschel Walker trade did, it caused me to be more aggressive and caused us to, if you will, take more risk because we had more picks," Jones said in August. "It's like going to Las Vegas with some extra money in your pocket.

 "In a way this actually created a mental part to us and to my role in it, to step out and make the moves and take, if you will, risks that are involved to be where we are today with a complete makeover of the defense."

 

 But the makeover, to be kind, remains a work in progress.

 Last season, the Cowboys allowed a franchise-record 511 points and were 30th in yards allowed per game. After the season, defensive coordinator Matt Eberflus was fired, and only one defensive coach remains from last year's staff (assistant linebackers coach J.J. Clark).

 Defensive coordinator Christian Parker came from the Philadelphia Eagles , where he was the passing game coordinator and defensive backs coach in 2024 and 2025. He brought a new scheme that has had some strong moments -- among them two fourth-and-1 stops of Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry in Week 3 and improved third-down work at times -- but has not been consistent.

 Through five games, the Cowboys have allowed 395.4 yards per game, which ranks 31st in the league. Four of their five opponents have had a season high in yardage. They are allowing 168.4 rushing yards per game (32nd) and 27.2 points per game (26th). Dating back to last season, the Cowboys have allowed 20 or more points in each of their past 12 games, matching a team record.

 This week, Dallas added longtime NFL coach Mike Pettine , a former Packers defensive coordinator, as a senior defensive assistant to help Parker.

 "We have to play better all across the boards," coach Brian Schottenheimer said. "I think [Parsons is] a terrific player. I'm looking forward to seeing him, but I like the picks that we got from Micah. I think we've done some really great things getting those picks. 

 "And I hope that when it's all said and done, it goes to show that that made a big difference because I do feel that way when you look at the guys who we were able to add to our roster."

 Yet that difference hasn't been reflected in takeaways or sacks. 

 During Parsons' tenure in Dallas after being drafted No. 12 in 2021, the Cowboys averaged 1.72 takeaways per game. Since the trade, they have averaged .64. With Parsons on the roster, the Cowboys had three or more sacks 33 times (48.5%), but in the 22 games since the trade, the Cowboys have reached that mark seven times (31.8%). With Parsons in Dallas, the Cowboys were held to one sack or fewer 29.4% of the time. Without him, that figure is 52.3%.

 

 How the Parsons trade has affected the Packers 

 In Green Bay, the jolt that Parsons' arrival gave to the locker room was unlike anything many of the players had ever felt.

 "S---, his presence," Packers All-Pro safety Xavier McKinney said at the time. "Just being Micah Parsons. When you get a guy like that, of that talent, you can put him out there and tell him to just stand there. And before the play is snapped, they're going to be looking for him because if you're not prepared for him, it's not going to be good for you."

 Or as Packers coach Matt LaFleur said: "He definitely has an aura about him."

 Parsons delivered on the promise initially. He recorded 12.5 sacks before his left knee buckled in the 14th game of the season. Despite missing the last three games, he still led the NFL with 64 quarterback pressures, according to ESPN Analytics. The problem was, the Packers didn't win another game, including the deflating playoff loss to the Chicago Bears in the wild-card round, when they allowed 25 fourth-quarter points.

 

 The trade meant the Packers went into this past offseason without a first-round pick. But general manager Brian Gutekunst believed he had a roster that wasn't in need of many players, as evidenced by him trading away more picks and drafting six players -- his smallest class since taking over in 2018. He used his first three picks on defensive players -- cornerback Brandon Cisse (Round 2), defensive tackle Chris McClellan (Round 3) and edge rusher Dani Dennis-Sutton (Round 4). All three have been significant contributors so far.

 The Packers also lost defensive coordinator Jeff Hafley, who became the Miami Dolphins ' head coach in January. He was replaced by former Arizona Cardinals coach Jonathan Gannon, who has kept his plans for how he intends to use Parsons mostly under wraps.

 Gannon, however, said Parsons has made an impact despite not…

Fantasy football is all about fun, competition and camaraderie, but it's also another way to appreciate the best of the best in the NFL. For more than three decades, ESPN Fantasy has been here with you, celebrating peak performers and magical moments.

 Class of 2026 Week 6 Inductee: Terrell Owens 
 3,624.5 fantasy points 
1,078 receptions, 15,934 receiving yards, 156 total TDs 

 A prolific, big-play receiver whose NFL career spanned 15 seasons for five different teams, "T.O." scored the second-most fantasy points among wide receivers during the ESPN era. He managed six seasons as a top-10 overall and top-five wide receiver in fantasy points (1998, 2000-02, 2006-07). During his 2000-02 peak, Owens scored at least 300 fantasy points in three straight years, making him one of only eight wide receivers in history with a streak at least that long. title: NFL Week 6 betting guide: Analysis, best bets and TD predictions
summary: Our experts dive into the odds and player props for Week 6 and offer their betting tips and favorite plays.
full_text:
Value is value, no matter where -- or how -- you find it. And that's what we'll aim to do each week in this space: find betting value.

 Ben Solak, Seth Walder and Matt Bowen bring different perspectives into how they approach sports betting. Solak leans on his expertise in player evaluation and the X's and O's to find edges, while Walder relies on statistical models to pick out plus-expected value bets, focusing mainly on defense. Bowen, a former NFL safety, predicts positive matchups and game winners from tape study and his understanding of the league. Also included are fantasy projection creator Mike Clay's top predicted anytime TD scorers for Week 6.

 From spreads and moneylines to totals and defensive player props, a good price might be found anywhere. Results will be tracked throughout the season, with flat one-unit wagers for each listed bet. With that, let's dive into our best bets, the top game to bet, favorite defensive props to play and the top predicted TD scorers.

 Note: Odds by DraftKings   and subject to change. 

 Jump to: 
 Bowen's Game of the Week 
 Solak's plays  | Walder's props 
 Clay's TD projections 

 

 

 Bowen's Game of the Week 

 Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-2.5, 42.5) 
9:30 a.m. ET on NFL Network, Wembley Stadium, London

 

 It's a tough week to pick games. However, we are going to make some plays here, starting with my picks for the Texans and Jaguars in London. Here's how I see Sunday's matchup playing out ...

 

 When the Texans have the ball: Quarterback C.J. Stroud has played really good football over the past two games, coinciding with Nico Collins ' return from a hamstring injury. Collins is the difference-maker on in-breakers, isolation throws and red zone targets. During that two-game stretch, versus Dallas and Tennessee, Stroud completed 72.3% of his throws and had three touchdown passes. The Texans also traded for Marvin Harrison Jr . this past week, so let's see how many snaps he gets Sunday and how he is deployed in the route tree versus a Jaguars defense that has given up 266.2 passing yards per game (third most).

 Houston's run game remains an issue. The Texans have averaged only 79 rushing yards per game (second fewest), and with David Montgomery down with a groin injury, Woody Marks will get the start. Marks gives the Texans more upside as a receiver, but it will be tough to create daylight against a Jaguars defense allowing a league-low 2.9 yards per carry. This feels like a pass-heavy script for Houston on Sunday.

 When the Jaguars have the ball: Coach Liam Coen should have a game plan focused on attacking the Houston zone coverages. The Texans play the second-most zone in the league (77% of coverage snaps), mixing both single-high and split-field schemes. The Texans will use play-action and leveled concepts to carve out windows for Trevor Lawrence , who has thrown 10 touchdown passes on the season, compared to only three interceptions. I also expect Lawrence will have to use his legs more on second-reaction scrambles versus Texans edge rushers  Will Anderson Jr . and Danielle Hunter .

 The Jags are in the same spot as the Texans when it comes to creating production on the ground. Bhayshul Tuten is averaging just under 70 yards a game, but this Texans front seven is allowing only 3.3 YPC, which is tied for the third fewest. Yes, Coen and the Jaguars will work to create run-pass balance, but this game comes down to Lawrence's ability to make plays on third downs.

 I'm on the under in the London games. And with two divisional opponents who have the defensive personnel to win critical situations, I feel it will be tough for both offenses. For the game pick? It's the Jaguars on the moneyline (-142) and to cover the 2.5 points .

 Other looks from around the league 
 

 Pittsburgh Steelers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers total points UNDER 39.5 (-105) 

 Rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels played good football in Week 5 versus a subpar Dallas defense, but Pittsburgh will have more answers to counter the defined pass game we are seeing from the Buccaneers. Plus, Tampa Bay owns a top-five blitz rate (40.4%), and its run defense is allowing only 3.3 YPC (second fewest). With Aaron Rodgers ' limited mobility, plus the wide receiver injuries in Pittsburgh, this game could be a grind.

 Bijan Robinson longest rush OVER 18.5 yards (-118) 

 Robinson's explosive run rate (rushes of 10-plus yards) is 12.7%, which is lower than expected. However, Robinson has six rushes of 20 or more yards this season. I'll take Robinson to rip off a big play once he gets to the edges versus the Chicago defense.

 Cam Skattebo rushing yards OVER 58.5 (-109) 

 Take the anticipated rushing volume and the matchup here. Skattebo is averaging 16.2 carries per game, and he has rushed for 59 or more yards in three of five games played. That total feels low too against a Saints defense allowing 148.8 rushing yards per game (third most).

 

 

 
 Solak's plays 
 

 C.J. Stroud passing yards OVER 257.5 (-111) 

 The Jacksonville Jaguars have a generally strong defense, but it has some vulnerabilities. They're second in points per drive allowed and third in EPA per play allowed -- but dead last in explosive pass rate allowed, with 17.2% of the pass attempts against them going for at least a 16-yard gain. Specifically, throws to the intermediate area of the field have been easily accessible. The Jaguars allow a completion percentage of 64% on intermediate throws (seventh highest) and a whopping 76% completion rate on all in-breaking routes (fourth highest).

 

 Guess what the entire Texans passing attack is built around? Stroud has thrown an in-breaker on 41.1% of his pass attempts this season (fifth-highest rate) and has thrown intermediate on 26% of his dropbacks (seventh most). You see where my head is at with this one.

 I think there are two ways to get into this angle here: Stroud passing yards and Nico Collins receiving yards. Collins has five straight games of 100-plus receiving yards against the Jaguars and is looking to tie the NFL record for consecutive games of 100-plus yards against the same opponent. I expect a heavy diet of Collins, given his strength at these specific vulnerabilities.

 I will lean to Stroud for the potential of big explosives to Kayshon Boutte , Jaylin Noel or the newly acquired Marvin Harrison Jr . I'll be on Collins receiving overs and Stroud passing overs when building out my bet card this week.

 Matthew Stafford passing yards UNDER 283.5 (-113) 

 The Los Angeles Rams are 12.5-point favorites against the Arizona Cardinals this week. They ran the ball with impunity against Arizona last season. Running backs had 253 yards on 33 carries in the Rams' Week 14 win and 119 on 25 carries in a Week 18 win. That kept Stafford from totaling big days through the air. In fact, Stafford has gone below this number in seven straight games against the Cardinals, last clearing it in 2021.

 Though the Rams had a tougher day running the football than expected last week against the Buffalo Bills , their running game remains one of the league's best by success rate. The Bills have allowed only 3.7 yards per carry to running backs this season, the seventh-lowest figure through five weeks; the Cardinals, at 4.2 allowed, are more around league average. With OL Alaric Jackson  suspended, the Rams seem less likely to pass it and risk big hits on Stafford in what should be a quiet divisional win.

title: Decked-out, diehard Jaguars fans swarm London for pub takeover
summary: Jaguars fans roll deep in the United Kingdom, and the fandom showed up big at London's briefly renamed ''Tealwood'' pub Thursday night.
full_text:
LONDON -- For three hours Thursday night, the Greenwood sports pub and kitchen on Victoria Street in Central London ceased to exist. In its place: Tealwood.

 An apt renaming, as Greenwood was hosting one of three pub takeover events sponsored by the Jacksonville Jaguars ' U.K. branch for Jaguars fans who live in the United Kingdom or made the trip to London for the team's annual home game at Wembley Stadium this Sunday.

 There will be another Friday night and Saturday afternoon, and there was one the previous Friday night in advance of the Jaguars' home game at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last week, which they won 19-17 on Cam Little 's 57-yard field goal as time expired.

 Those events are part of the NFL franchise's movement to continue to build its international fanbase, a push that began back in 2013 when the team played the first of what is now 15 games in London. The Jaguars also have their own U.K. fan club (Union Jax), have been heavily involved in helping to build interest in flag football with clinics, have appearances with current and former players throughout the year, run a year-round junior cheerleading program and send hundreds of students annually to the London games as part of a Reward Rows program.

 "Even if you knew nothing about the NFL, you were like, 'Oh, but the Jags are our team,'" said Phoebe Schecter, a former Buffalo Bills coaching intern, one of the first members of the Great Britain national American football team and now an NFL analyst for Sky Sports. "And so I think there's always going to be that really great association.

 

 "The Jags really do have a presence [in the U.K.], and the fans are truly bought in, and you get superfans. I mean, something as silly as somebody's on social, it's like a Mr. and Mrs. Jaxson de Ville, but they're superfans here in the U.K. and they're bought into the costumes and this whole persona. It's who they are. And you see that in the States, and now that's kind of creeping in over here in a great way."

 Jamie Phillips and Francis Sweeney are two of those fans. Sweeney -- decked out in an oversized Jaguars hat, jersey and jacket and carrying a Jags-themed wrestling belt over his shoulder -- has attended the team's games in London for the past five years. He's not the only Jags fan in his family, though.

 "My wife doesn't like any sports, and she's obsessed with the Jaguars," he said.

 Phillips, who was at Thursday night's pub takeover, wore a Jaguars mascot fuzzy hat on the 59-degree day at the Jaguars' practice at The Grove resort, the team's headquarters since it arrived Oct. 9. He was the team's 2024 nominee for the NFL's International Fan of the Year and has been a Jaguars fan for 15 years.

 That began two years before the Jaguars started making annual trips overseas, but Phillips latched on to the franchise even though it had just three winning seasons since the 2000s began.

 "I want to take after the underdog as most Brits do," he said. "A bit of an obsession, really, is what it's become."

 

 Phillips and Sweeney were among the 200 fans who had tickets to attend Friday's practice. There were also dozens of students from multiple primary and secondary schools across the London area, all of whom participate in JagTag. That's the Jaguars U.K. -- an arm of the franchise based in the U.K. -- flag football program for people ages 8-18. As practice wound down, the students were getting ready to get onto the field, receive tips and run drills with the 16 members of the Jaguars' practice squad.

 The program involves 360 schools in six major cities and 12 towns around London. It began in 2016 with roughly 1,200 participants and in 2024 had reached 100,000, said Andy Scott, the U.K. grassroots manager of JagTag.

 "We started in about six schools in West London in Fulham because of our connection with [Jaguars] ownership," Scott said. "Obviously, our owner [Shad Khan] owns the Fulham Football Club, so we ran it out of the foundation to try and gain that footprint across there. So yeah, it was small steps to a big finish."

 Ben Conway and Joel Neumann also were at Friday's practice. The two run the social media account "Endzone Near You" on Instagram, TikTok and Facebook and produce daily NFL content. They're also huge Jaguars fans -- both were at the Jaguars' 19-17 victory over Philadelphia at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Sunday, and they'll be at Sunday's game against the Houston Texans at Wembley Stadium.

 Their most notable post from the last game summarized the final 12 seconds: The reaction of Eagles fans around them after Jake Elliott's 48-yard field goal gave Philadelphia a 17-16 lead, followed by their reaction after Little's winning field goal as time expired.

 The final play of that game was among the season highlights playing on 17 television screens at Greenwood/Tealwood during Thursday night's pub takeover. The three-hour event included appearances by Jaguars cheerleaders and Jaxson de Ville. Schecter, along with former NFL cornerback and current Sky Sports NFL analyst Jason Bell and Jay Lawrence of Absolute Radio, a British national radio station, emceed the event.

 Fans in the two-story pub were decked out in assorted Jaguars gear, including the jerseys of cornerback Travis Hunter , quarterback Trevor Lawrence , tight end Brenton Strange and defensive end Josh Hines-Allen , as well as those of former players Fred Taylor and Keenan McCardell.

 The highlight of the night was a Jaguars trivia contest. Among the questions:

 What color jerseys did the Jaguars wear in their first appearance in London in 2013?

 Answer: Black.

 How many teams have the Jaguars played in London?

 Answer: 13 ( San Francisco , Dallas , Indianapolis , Baltimore , Houston , Denver , Atlanta , New England , the Los Angeles Rams , Miami and Chicago once, and Buffalo and Philadelphia twice).

 How long was the longest TD scored in international game history, and who scored it?

 Answer: Parker Washington on a 97-yard punt return.

 Schecter called the takeover, which has become a regular occurrence in London when the team is in town, a success. She hopes it will result in more people becoming Jaguars fans.

 "People want to be a part of something," she said. "They want to feel like they're part of a team. And I think the 'Duuuval' chant, the Jags, that's something that they feel like they can own."

title: Why is Chargers RB Omarion Hampton's snap count decreasing?
summary: Coach Jim Harbaugh and OC Mike McDaniel on why RB Omarion Hampton is being used differently.
full_text:
For all intents and purposes, when the Los Angeles Chargers selected running back Omarion Hampton with the No. 22 pick in the 2025 NFL draft, it seemed a perfect fit.

 Hampton provided the physical, bruising style of running so often associated with coach Jim Harbaugh's teams. He was the type of three- or even four-down back that the front office envisioned pairing with quarterback Justin Herbert .

 But less than two seasons in, it's been more flashes than a surefire bet.

 

 A fractured left ankle early in the season and a right ankle injury late hampered his rookie campaign, but Hampton produced when on the field with 545 yards and a team-high four touchdowns. With offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel hired in January, Hampton's role seemingly neared a breakout in a new wide-zone-heavy run scheme.

 The former Miami Dolphins coach compared Hampton to Hall of Fame running back Terrell Davis. And after a week of training camp, McDaniel highlighted Hampton as a player with as much growth as, if not more than, any player.

 The proof hasn't been in the pudding so far.

 This season, Hampton's snap count has decreased since having 40 in Week 2 against the Las Vegas Raiders . Hampton also had a career-high 23 carries in that game. Since then, his numbers have dropped, going to 20 snaps against the Denver Broncos in Week 5 -- the fewest offensive snaps among the running back room of Kimani Vidal (26) and Keaton Mitchell (21).

 However, that isn't hindering Harbaugh's confidence in Hampton. Harbaugh said that Hampton is "playing extremely well in all phases." But, if that is true, then why the decrease in usage?

 "Yeah, hard to predict how many [snaps] a player is going to get but yeah, every time Omarion is in the game, I'm fired up," Harbaugh said Wednesday. "Kimani played really really good football too. And Keaton as well. There's three outstanding backs, but love them, love them all."

 Following a Week 4 loss to the Seattle Seahawks , Harbaugh didn't explain why the running back share changed in Week 3.

 

 Hampton had a costly fumble against the Raiders, his second of the season. Then in Week 3, he dropped to 27 snaps against the  Buffalo Bills . Then, he played 22 snaps versus Seattle. Harbaugh said the rotation is what they thought was best for the team and wanted to utilize the skills of three running backs who are "all playing good."

 From a statistical standpoint, Hampton's numbers aren't far off through five games this season compared to last. He currently has a team-high 73 carries for 271 yards as opposed to 66 carries for 314 yards last year. His runs have been deemed a "rush success" 37% of the time so far, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. That figure was at 42% in 2025.

 McDaniel finally broke the usage change down the week after Seattle. He said that depending on how the game plays out, he has had plenty of times when three running backs are involved on game day. According to him, the running back room is a "strength" and there's an advantage to having defenses prepare to tackle three different players with "various skill sets."

 "I'm assessing each week what our players are good at because I'm getting new information, and it's new in a season. So, trying to find the right balance, trying to give guys opportunities," McDaniel said. "It's very fluid, but it's not an attack on any one individual. It's my job to do better, score more points and utilize all the assets we have. And there's only one ball."

 

 Hampton is still listed as the starter in the depth chart. However, McDaniel felt he was "underutilizing a strength" -- in the RB room as a whole -- which might explain the carry distribution changing as this season has progressed.

 The issue with the distribution is that the Chargers spent a high pick on Hampton. Vidal was a 2024 sixth-rounder, and Mitchell arrived as a free agent in March. The investment in Hampton is more costly if it fails.

 "I can't make the statement more emphatic. It's not because I've lost any faith in [Omarion] at all. I thought he was a very hard tackle and made plays with his opportunities, and that's what I was looking to do in the game," McDaniel said after Week 4. "I didn't go into the game thinking of a touch ratio. It just was the way it played out based on what was happening in the game."

 Three days later, Hampton played the fewest snaps of his career. Meanwhile, Vidal and Mitchell's roles have been on the uptick. McDaniel said Thursday that "there's a lot of things from a matchmaking and game-planning perspective about what you're doing as an offense," before pointing out that Hampton had the most carries (14) of anyone on the team.

 So far, the running back room -- which McDaniel saw as a strength going into the season -- has been safe from the injuries that have decimated the offense. That leads to McDaniel diversifying the back involvement rather than running the game plan "through guys that got here in the last couple weeks."

 "The running back room is a very important piece of our team, and because it's a really strong, really good room by all NFL standards. For instance, I think there was a couple third downs that Keaton picked up for us that were crucial, and Kimani had a great touchdown run on the play after a turnover," McDaniel said Thursday. "So we'll continue to utilize those guys for their playmaking ability, particularly when you see lineup changes like we did [against Denver]."

 Each of them have had their productive stretches, offering a different look for defenses. Vidal specifically has seen his offensive snap count rise from four in Week 1 to 26 in Week 5, when he rumbled for a 42-yard touchdown run that changed the game's momentum. Mitchell has steadily played at least 15 snaps each game.

 

 Those three are "a little different" but each does a great job, Herbert said. But as for Hampton, he said he has seen him grow into someone the team can trust to put the ball in his hands.

 "He's just such a physical runner. A guy that's able to break so many tackles and he's great in pass protection too," Herbert said. "So, a guy that you just get the ball whether he's running over a guy or running around him with his speed, he's a great guy to get the ball to."

 Hampton was once viewed as the future of the Chargers' back field alongside Herbert and a dominant rushing attack. One new offensive coordinator later, his role is decreasing -- just like the Chargers' playoff hopes.

title: Rams can't seem to fix their special teams
summary: Special teams have played a significant role in five of the Rams' nine losses since the start of last season, including the playoffs.
full_text:
LOS ANGELES -- The Rams entered this season as Super Bowl favorites, but their special teams unit has been a big part of what has kept Los Angeles' "superteam" from having success.

 As Rams head coach Sean McVay tries to fix the issues for the unit in-season, he said he has leaned on a lesson from former Rams defensive coordinator Wade Phillips.

 "If it's important enough to you, you'll get it done." 

 The Rams enter Week 6 with a minus-15.3% special teams DVOA, which would be the worst in history over a full season.

 One of the first attempts to fix the unit came Oct. 2 when the Rams cut returner Xavier Smith . The second came Tuesday, when the Rams released kicker Harrison Mevis .

 The previous day, Mevis missed a 50-yard field goal attempt in the first quarter of the Rams' loss to the Buffalo Bills and had a potential winning field goal blocked in overtime. The kicks were the fourth and fifth failed kicks by Mevis this season, giving him a 56% field goal rate (5-of-9). That is the lowest field goal percentage in the NFL.

 The Rams replaced Mevis with Blake Grupe , whom they signed off of the New York Jets ' practice squad.

 "Ultimately, we need better production, and that's what we're hoping to get [from] Blake," McVay said.

 

 Grupe split his 2025 season with the New Orleans Saints and the Indianapolis Colts . Grupe, who spent the first 45 games of his career with the Saints, was cut after going 18-of-26 on field goals with New Orleans in 2025.

 He spent the final five games with the Colts, where he made all 11 of his field goal attempts and all 10 extra points.

 Grupe called that time in Indianapolis "a big stint in my career," saying he was able to show what he could do.

 "I hit the ground running," Grupe said. "We had a rainy game in Jacksonville, so it definitely wasn't an easy first one, but we got out there, we got to work, got the ball rolling. 
 
"Those five weeks in Indy were seriously big for me, big for my career."

 The kicking woes are not an issue isolated to this season. The Rams have a 77.2 field goal percentage over the past four seasons, the second worst in NFL over that span, according to ESPN Research.

 "There's a lot that goes into special teams," Grupe said. "Guys got to cover. We got to put the ball where it's supposed to be. You've got to have elite specialists play to be elite on special teams. So I feel like I can do that.

 "There's a lot of things that we can do on kickoff and bring some consistency in the field goal game."

 Special teams have played a significant role in five of the Rams' nine losses since the start of last season, including the playoffs. After the Rams allowed a 58-yard punt return touchdown that sparked a 16-point comeback by the Seattle Seahawks in Week 16, McVay fired special teams coordinator Chase Blackburn.

 "There are so many different things that you're trying to be able to fix, and then sometimes other problems open up," McVay said. "I felt like that field goal operation was trending in the right direction after all the work. I think we did some good things. I liked the way that we were protecting. Obviously, we can't give up the 'swim sea' area against a player like [Bills outside linebacker Greg] Rousseau in that moment [Monday] night.

 "You just have to lean in, and you have to be able to identify what are the problems? Let's provide some tangible solutions, and let's ultimately be able to bring it to life for the players." 

 And although the Rams are 2-3 through their first five games of the season, four of their games (and all three of their losses) came to 2025 playoff teams.

 Now, they face a stretch that should be easier: In the Rams' next five games, they play the 1-4 Arizona Cardinals  twice, the 3-2 Las Vegas Raiders , 0-5 Los Angeles Chargers and the 1-3-1 Washington Commanders . According to ESPN Analytics, their Week 6 through 10 schedule is the easiest five-game span of any team this season.

 "This isn't the first time that we've had adversity and the first time that we've had some different things that I have to do a better job of," McVay said of the special teams unit. "We'll lean in. We'll go back to work. We'll use these as growth opportunities."

title: Five takeaways from five weeks of the Raiders' season
summary: What should be taken away from the first five weeks of the Raiders' 2026 season?
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev. -- The  Las Vegas Raiders ' 45-17 loss  in Week 5 to the New England Patriots was bad. They were outplayed in all three phases. But the team is not hanging their heads and letting a brutal afternoon in Foxborough, Massachusetts, take away from all the strides they have made under first-time coach Klint Kubiak .

 Through five games, the Raiders are in a better situation than most would've expected entering the season. They are 3-2 ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Buffalo Bills  ( 4:25 ET on CBS ), and would be in the playoffs if the season ended today.

 They have scored 25-plus points in four of five games. Meanwhile, the defense has recorded the second-most takeaways in the NFL (10).

 "It was a bad game overall. Everyone knows that, from coaches to players," defensive end Maxx Crosby said Wednesday. "I think this team is resilient. We love being around each other, and we expect to be a lot better this week."

 If the Raiders want to make sure last week's performance was an outlier instead of a sign of what's to come, they have to make significant improvements on both sides of the ball. With that said, here are five takeaways from five weeks of the Raiders' season, including potential changes needed at offensive line and inconsistent production in the run game.

 

 Kirk Cousins is beating Father Time. But for how much longer? 

 Cousins, 38, has played well. He has thrown for 1,269 yards, 12 touchdowns and four interceptions. The 15-year veteran quarterback also has a 65.1% completion rate and a passer rating of 100.7. Cousins' touchdown total is the second-most through the first five weeks in his career. (He threw 13 touchdowns between Weeks 1-5 for the Minnesota Vikings in 2023.)

 

 Cousins wasn't the sole reason for the Raiders being steamrolled by the Patriots in Week 5. But he didn't have his finest outing. Sure, his numbers looked fine. Cousins completed 19 of 28 passes for 243 yards and a touchdown despite being under duress throughout the game. However, Cousins missed open targets because he either stared down tight end Brock Bowers or held the ball too long.

 And when rookie  Fernando Mendoza replaced him late in the fourth quarter, the 2026 No. 1 pick showed off the mobility that Cousins lacks. Still, the Raiders are far from making a change at quarterback. The team has been satisfied with Cousins' performance thus far.

 "That's why [Cousins is] here. We have a lot of confidence in him," Kubiak said. "Kirk's the starter, and if Fernando's called upon, he'll be ready to go just like he was [last week]."

 Yes, he doesn't have the arm strength, and it's harder for him to extend plays with his legs. But Cousins is the reason the Raiders have a winning record.

 Las Vegas ranks ninth in points per game (26) despite relying heavily on the passing game due to struggles to run the ball. His relationship with Kubiak and knowledge of the offense have been invaluable. More importantly, he has made smart decisions with the ball.

 If the Raiders' losing streak continues, and Cousins has similar performances to the one he had against New England, there would likely be conversations about giving Mendoza a chance to start. But for now, the team is fine with Cousins remaining the commander of the offense.

 

 

 Growing pains kicking in for the Raiders' young secondary. 

 When relying on a secondary that consists of young players who are still adjusting to the pro level, growing pains are expected to occur. That's what Las Vegas has dealt with in recent weeks.

 Rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses made a strong impression when he recorded two interceptions and earned AFC Defensive Player of the Week honors in Week 2. Since then, Masses has faced stronger competition and has been getting picked on in coverage. In the past three games, he has allowed nine catches for 155 yards, two touchdowns, a passer rating of 106.9 and a 60% completion rate.

 Against the Patriots, Masses had to alternate reps with second-year cornerback Darien Porter , who also was inconsistent in coverage. He allowed a 49-yard reception to wide receiver Kyle Williams . Meanwhile, starting rookie safety Treydan Stukes gave up three catches for 59 yards and a touchdown. Stukes' performance featured moments when he looked lost in coverage and whiffed on tackles.

 There's no reason to lose faith in the Raiders' young core in the secondary, including rookie cornerback Jermod McCoy , who has only played in 30 defensive snaps in four games. But patience will be required.

 

 Will the run game ever get fixed? 

 Kubiak being tied to one of the league's worst rushing attacks -- 28th in yards per game (82) -- is a bit surprising. He's known for orchestrating a strong run game, which is why there was optimism that he could fix the Raiders' rushing woes from previous seasons. Instead, the Raiders are still searching for answers.

 

 It's hard to pinpoint one specific thing that has led to the Raiders' struggles running the ball. It's been a byproduct of a multitude of issues. For starters, running back Ashton Jeanty hasn't been 100% healthy, dealing with an ankle and foot injury. Kubiak, however, said on Wednesday that Jeanty is feeling "a lot better" physically. Whenever Jeanty returns to full strength, he still has to improve his vision and take advantage of open lanes when it appears. The thing is, those open lanes have come in spurts since the offensive line has struggled in run blocking.

 The Raiders could improve their rushing numbers by getting rookie running back Mike Washington Jr . involved. On 25 carries, Washington has posted a team-high five yards per attempt. Washington's issues in pass protection and pass catching have prevented him from fully taking on the role of RB2. He only had one carry for five yards in the loss to the Patriots.

 Another element could be the lack of a vertical threat at wide receiver who can keep opposing defenses honest and not have them stack the box.

 A consistent run game will allow the Raiders to reach their full offensive potential. They will be able to control the time of possession and be even more effective in the pass-action game. Until then, the Raiders figure things out, they will continue to be one-dimensional as an offense.

 

 

 What has happened to Kwity Paye ? 

 The Raiders signed Paye to a three-year, $48 million deal with the hope that he could improve their pass rush and be a reliable running mate to Crosby. His performance in the season-opening win over the Dolphins suggested as much. Paye recorded two sacks and five pressures.

 Since then, Paye's production has declined drastically. In 154 defensive snaps over the past four games, Paye has six tackles, four run stops, three quarterback pressures and no sacks. Paye has been nonexistent to the point where Malcolm Koonce has made a strong case for more playing time.

 In 110 defensive snaps during this stretch, Koonce has totaled eight tackles, eight run stops, 12 quarterback pressures and three sacks. Koonce's pressure total of 17 is second on the team.

 The Raiders need Paye to step up, especially since opponents are chipping and double-teaming Crosby -- who has a team-high 25 pressures -- frequently. Crosby has been chipped 36 times -- fifth-most in the league. He has faced double teams on 10.1% of his pass rush snaps.

 

 Changes within the offensive line could be on the horizon. 

 The Raiders might need to evaluate the left guard spot. Their decision to name Spencer Burford a starter to begin the season was understandable. He has experience playing in a West Coast offense, going back to his time with the San Francisco 49ers .

 But he has been a liability as a pass and run blocker. In 189 pass-blocking snaps, Burford has allowed two sacks and 23 pressures -- the most among left guards in the league. He allowed seven quick quarterback pressures -- the number of pressures allowed by a blocker in less than 2.5 seconds after the snap.

title: Pop quizzes from Aaron Rodgers?! How Steelers QB preps his pass catchers
summary: The 42-year-old veteran acts more like Simon Cowell than Ken Jennings as he builds trust with his teammates.
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- Days before making his first career start, Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Germie Bernard stood in front of a meeting room at the team practice facility and addressed his offensive teammates.

 From a seat facing Bernard, quarterback Aaron Rodgers began peppering the rookie with questions. Rodgers asked about hand signals, route-running details, the Steelers' playbook and the Indianapolis Colts ' defensive tendencies. Anything and everything was on the table.

 One at a time, Bernard answered the veteran's questions. When Bernard got one right, Rodgers moved on to the next. When Bernard answered incorrectly, the wide receiver and quarterback went over the correct answer. Afterward, Rodgers and his three fellow quarterbacks met with their position coach, Tom Arth, and gave a glowing assessment of Bernard. He was ready.

 

 "They were just going on and on about how well Germie knows the plan," Arth said. "Basically, they're like, he can call the plays just like a quarterback would."

 This wasn't Bernard's first time being put on the spot by Rodgers -- and it won't be the last. A second-round draft pick out of Alabama, Bernard is one of the many young pass catchers regularly called to the front of the room and quizzed by Rodgers as a unique way to build trust and test the knowledge of his teammates.

 "What I've learned from Aaron is like, OK, I know that the reason why he's doing this, because he wants us to be prepared all-around," Bernard said. "He wants to make sure that we know what we're doing when we're out there playing with him.

 "... I love the challenges, man. It makes me grow. It makes me a better football player. It makes me a better person because it makes you look at things a lot different. So, I'm just grateful that he does that because whether I get an answer right or I get an answer wrong, I'm able to learn from the things that I don't know."

 Since becoming the Green Bay Packers ' starter in 2009, Rodgers has quizzed his offensive skill teammates in players-only meetings as a way of making sure they see the game the same way. Jordan Love , his successor in Green Bay, continued Rodgers' tradition.

 "It's pretty eye-opening to see who knows the plan, see who knows who we're playing and who their personnel is," Rodgers said. "I just think it's important to keep those guys on their toes and keep those guys studying and making sure they're watching film and knowing what's in the plan. There's always going to be those quizzes, and hopefully, they get a little bit better."

 And in a week in which the Steelers are missing three of their top five wide receivers , Rodgers, 42, will have to rely on an array of young, under-the-radar pass catchers. Before they face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers ' defense Sunday ( 1 p.m. ET, CBS ), they have to pass Rodgers' quizzes during the week.

 

 "It's a method of accountability, but also it's an opportunity to talk football and specifics of football," Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said. "And it's an opportunity to engage with him even further."

 Bernard passed both of Rodgers' weekday quizzes, administered in a window after practice and before coach-led meetings, and Sunday's Week 5 test against the Colts. Bernard, who finished with a team-high nine targets, was already poised to have a bigger role against the Colts with veteran Michael Pittman Jr . on injured reserve because of a foot injury, but Roman Wilson  suffered an injury during the game, creating an even bigger opportunity for the rookie. Bernard finished the win with six catches for 80 yards, including a 25-yard catch-and-run on a broken play to convert a third down in the fourth quarter. Leading by just two points, the Steelers' conversion kept the drive going and eventually ended with a touchdown to go up two possessions.

 "He's been getting better," Rodgers said, adding that Bernard doesn't repeat mistakes. "He asked the right questions, and I think he's becoming a little bit more prepared and dialed in. It's just confidence. When a young player starts playing with confidence, you see the potential of a player. And I thought last week was a good step in that direction."

 Rodgers, a "Jeopardy" superfan and guest host in 2021 , doesn't channel Alex Trebek or Ken Jennings in the quizzes for his teammates. Instead, he embodies another larger-than-life TV personality when he starts testing his teammates: Simon Cowell, who exploded in popularity as the tough-love judge of the early iteration of "American Idol."

 "I've been young and up there in front of everyone, and now it's awesome to be sitting next to him and asking some questions," said Steelers tight end Robert Tonyan , who first played with Rodgers in Green Bay when Tonyan was a rookie in 2018. "We were joking about it. He's like the Simon Cowell. I'll be Randy Jackson."

 

 Wide receiver Ben Skowronek , Tonyan added, is Paula Abdul.

 "All of those guys are really, really, really smart, and they know everything about the offense," said Steelers wide receiver Brandon Smith , who first got quizzed by Rodgers when the two played for the New York Jets  in 2024. "They know about the linemen movements, and they know about where the running back's going. They know about protections, they know everything. That's where I aspire to be in my own game."

 A practice squad wide receiver, Smith was elevated to the game-day roster against the Colts because of Pittman's injury. Similar to Bernard, Smith was put on the spot in the days leading up to the game against Indianapolis so Rodgers could make sure he could trust the receiver. Smith said his palms got a little sweaty at that moment, but when his opportunity arrived, he was calm and collected because of his preparation.

 With Wilson and Skowronek sidelined by injury against the Buccaneers, Smith's expanded role will likely continue for at least another week.

 "I have a lot of trust in him, knows the plan every week, even when he's been down [on practice squad]," Rodgers said. "And so I expect B. Smith to be able to step in and play as well as he possibly can."

 It's not necessarily unheard of for a quarterback -- and some of the more veteran players -- to test the younger players. Wide receiver DK Metcalf said Russell Wilson previously quizzed his receivers in Seattle, but Rodgers' method of calling his teammates to the front of the room still makes his approach somewhat unique.

 "I think that's a pretty normal thing for quarterbacks -- maybe not in front of the team," said Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Davante Adams , who was teammates with Rodgers in Green Bay and New York. "... Different guys have different ways of doing it. I'm grateful for it to be honest, though, because you feel like you're being picked on in the moment.

 

 "When it's happening, you may be nervous because you're a young player or whatever the case may be, but at the end of the day, he's almost simulating what the game will be like. [You're] just reacting and finding a way to respond in the moment. To answer in a team setting in an impromptu type of way, it obviously shows that you know what you're doing. It's a good way to get guys ready."

 Rather than putting his teammates on the spot in a meeting, Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes prefers to talk through routes with his pass catchers one-on-one during practices and training camp. It's a method Mahomes developed through his experience with tight end Travis Kelce early in Mahomes' career. When Mahomes took over as the team's starter in 2019, Kelce, a six-year veteran at that point, began approaching the young quarterback after plays in practice and talked through what he was seeing. That left an impression on Mahomes.

 "He would always just talk to me after every play, so when we got to games, I would know what he was thinking," Mahomes said. "Obviously, that's kind of blossomed to what it's blossomed to, so I try to keep that going. I've done it with Rashee [Rice] now and a lot of these guys…
